title: Constraint Qualifications and Regularity Conditions for Nonlinear Constraint Systems
abstract: Constraint qualifications (CQs) and regularity conditions (RCs) play a fundamental role in establishing global iteration and oracle complexity results for first-order methods on solving functional constrained optimization problems. Various conditions have been proposed and employed in the literature, with their validity established for different classes of applications. However, the use of different conditions across existing studies makes it difficult to directly compare their theoretical results and underlying assumptions. In this report, we systematically review several widely used CQs and RCs and investigate their relationships. In particular, we establish implications among these conditions and identify cases in which the implications are strict, thereby clarifying their relative strengths. Our results provide a unified perspective on existing regularity assumptions and offer guidance for selecting appropriate conditions in the complexity analysis of first-order methods.

title: Counterexamples to torsion-freeness in the $K$-theory of crystallographic group $C^*$-algebras
abstract: We give a negative answer to a question of Sánchez Saldaña--Velásquez and Lück asking whether the topological K-theory of the reduced group C*-algebra of a split crystallographic group with finite cyclic holonomy is always torsion-free. For two explicit split crystallographic groups with translation subgroup of rank four and holonomy of order four, we compute the equivariant K-theory of the classifying space for proper actions and find nontrivial two-torsion. The equivariant universal coefficient theorem transfers this torsion to proper equivariant K-homology, and the Baum--Connes conjecture identifies the resulting groups with the topological K-theory of the corresponding reduced group C*-algebras.

title: Bilinear Strichartz Estimates and Linear Morawetz Estimates for Schrödinger Operators with Potentials
abstract: In dimensions three and above, we establish bilinear Strichartz estimates for Schrödinger operators with potentials using perturbative arguments and Morawetz estimates. Our approach does not require smallness of the potential. As part of the analysis, we also establish endpoint versions of the bilinear Christ-Kiselev lemma.

title: Order continuity of induced homomorphisms between free Banach lattices
abstract: Let $T\colon F\to E$ be a bounded operator between Banach spaces and let $\overline T\colon FBL^{(p)}[F]\to FBL^{(p)}[E]$ be the lattice homomorphism induced by $T$ between the corresponding free $p$-convex Banach lattices generated by $F$ and $E$. We show that $\overline T$ is order continuous if and only if it is either zero or a lattice isomorphic embedding. For $p=\infty$, this holds precisely when $T$ is zero or an isomorphic embedding, while for $1\leq p<\infty$, apart from the zero operator, $T$ must be an embedding and the pair $(T(F),E)$ must have the operator-extension property POE-$p$. In addition, we study when $FBL^{(p)}[E]$ is order dense or majorizing in $FBL^{(q)}[E]$ for $p<q$.

title: On the properties of the potential and the spherical harmonic expansions for general planets
abstract:
The convergence of spherical harmonic expansions (SHEs) of gravitational potentials below the Brillouin sphere has been a long-standing problem in potential theory and geodesy. In previous work, some of the present authors gave a necessary and sufficient condition for convergence along a fixed ray, formulated in terms of analyticity of a longitudinal average of the balayage density. In the present paper, we extend these results to arbitrary physical solid planets, assuming only that the planet is a compact subset of $\mathbb R^3$ and that its density belongs to $L^\infty$. We establish sharp regularity properties of the gravitational potential at the Brillouin sphere. The potential and its first derivative extend continuously to the sphere, the first derivative is locally Hölder continuous with exponent $1/2$, and the second derivative satisfies the optimal bound $V''(z)=O\bigl(\operatorname{dist}(z,\partial\mathbb D)^{-1/2}\bigr)$ under nontangential approach from the exterior.
  We also obtain sharp estimates for the spherical harmonic coefficients: $a_\ell=O(\ell^{-3/2}).$ If, for almost every latitude, the Brillouin sphere is a one-sided Lebesgue point from the interior of the longitudinally averaged density, then $a_\ell=o(\ell^{-3/2}).$ Both estimates are optimal. We explicitly recover the balayage density on the Brillouin sphere from the exterior gravitational potential, and its circular averages from the potential along a single radial line. Finally, we give a physical characterization of convergence of the SHE below the Brillouin sphere. If the SHE converges at such a point, then, after truncating the planet at any suitable intermediate radius, the gravitational potential of the removed outer part is completely determined by that of the remaining truncated planet. This provides a direct interpretation of the strong constraint imposed by convergence below the Brillouin sphere.

title: Phase-space dynamics and multicomponent wave-packet structures in the Dunkl anharmonic oscillator
abstract: We study the phase-space dynamics and multicomponent wave-packet structures of the Dunkl anharmonic oscillator (Kerr medium). Starting from the time-evolved state, we derive analytical expressions for the Dunkl-Husimi $Q$-function and a normalized angular Husimi profile. The Dunkl parameter modifies the coherent-state excitation weights and the parity-dependent phase accumulation, producing angular anisotropy and asymmetric phase-space separation. For the half-integer deformation $μ=0.5$, the dynamics generate asymmetric multicomponent Husimi patterns with unequal peak heights and an early reconstruction at $t=π/λ$. For the deformation $μ=1.0$, the Husimi distribution exhibits broadening while retaining its multimodal structure and unitary evolution. At the fundamental nonlinear revival time, the wave packet is reconstructed for the selected parameter ratio. The standard Kerr dynamics are recovered in the limit $μ\rightarrow 0$.

title: Stein's method for negative binomial and hyper-negative-binomial laws, with applications
abstract: We develop Stein's method for the negative binomial law and for the hyper-negative-binomial law, the law of the smallest row total of an array of independent geometric variables given the differences of the row totals, with every constant explicit. The main instrument is a comparison of two biasings of the approximated variable, which cancels the rate term exactly at the matched parameter. We provide total variation bounds for sums of independent geometric variables at drifting parameters, for sums of dependent geometric variables (the Arratia-Goldstein-Gordon theorem with geometric summands and the Poisson law as an endpoint), and for Poisson mixtures; the exact conditional law of negative-binomial counts given their differences, with the Bessel law as its Poisson limit; and a dependency expansion for the column direction of a contingency table. A final section verifies every bound numerically, with one script per result.

title: Modeling and Analysis of Cooling Induced Isotropic Nematic Transitions in Pharmaceutical Liquid Crystals
abstract: This paper studies the phase transition from an isotropic to a nematic liquid crystal driven by controlled cooling, motivated by the manufacturing of next-generation pharmaceutical drugs. Using the non-isothermal Ericksen model for liquid crystals with a variable degree of orientation, we formulate the problem as a stiff, quasilinear system of parabolic partial differential equations. We establish a consistent thermodynamic framework, prove the well-posedness of the system, and conduct a rigorous asymptotic and numerical scaling analysis of the moving phase boundary in a cylindrical cell subjected to bottom-wall convective cooling. Our analysis identifies a critical sample thickness that separates two distinct physical regimes. Below this threshold, the transition follows the cooling dynamics and the material remains quasi-isothermal. Above the thickness threshold, bulk thermal diffusion governs the dynamics, imposing a dominant thermal delay characterized by a concave quadratic propagation front. These results demonstrate that scaling from laboratory characterization to industrial production fundamentally alters the spatial thermal history of the material, providing a predictive mathematical framework to optimize cooling protocols for kinetic arrest.

title: Noncritical multi-bubbles and hyperbolic double bubbles
abstract: We prove that standard $k$-bubbles uniquely minimize perimeter in $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbb S^n$ for $n\ge2$ and $1\le k\le n$, and that standard double bubbles uniquely minimize perimeter in $\mathbb H^n$ for $n\ge3$. For nonnegative curvature, the proof combines the structure and spectral theory of Milman--Neeman with a uniform semialgebraic exceptional set, an almost-everywhere profile comparison, and localized variational arguments. A curvature-variable lift gives a uniformly elliptic comparison at the Euclidean limit. The independent hyperbolic argument uses the rotational structure of Cotton--Freeman, a scalar meridian force potential, and a transverse conformal variation. The critical range $k=n+1$ in $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbb S^n$, and hyperbolic clusters with more than two finite cells, are not covered.

title: Inference in an interactive multi-type branching network
abstract: We study statistical inference for a high-dimensional stochastic interaction model observed only through low-dimensional aggregate data. The model describes pairwise communication between $d$ individuals as a collection of mutually interacting branching processes with immigration, where activity on one directed pair may trigger subsequent activity in the reverse direction. The latent interaction counts are not observed. Instead, for each individual, only the total number of messages sent and received in each time slot is available. This aggregation gives rise to an inverse problem in which the parameters governing the latent pairwise dynamics must be recovered from substantially compressed observations.

title: The sum of sizes of nontrivial cross-intersecting families
abstract:
Families $\mathcal A_1,\ldots,\mathcal A_m\subseteq\binom{[n]}k$ are cross-intersecting if every member of one family meets every member of each other family. A family is nontrivial if its members have no common element.
  For $n>2k$ and $m\ge3$, we determine the maximum sum of the sizes of $m$ nonempty, nontrivial cross-intersecting families. We prove the sharp bound \[ \sum_{i=1}^{m}|\mathcal A_i| \le \max\bigl\{m\,h(n,k,1),\ g(n,k)+3(m-1)\bigr\}, \] where \[ h(n,k,1)=\binom{n-1}{k-1}-\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}+1 \] and \[ g(n,k)=\binom nk-2\binom{n-k}k
  -\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}+\binom{n-2k+1}k. \] We also characterize all equality cases. Two types of extremal configurations arise: copies of a maximum nontrivial intersecting family, and copies of a specific three-member nontrivial intersecting family together with its full cross-intersecting companion. The proof applies a known restricted lexicographic comparison to obtain the weighted bound for shifted families, and uses local generator reductions for critically shifted families. These reductions exploit shiftedness after removing the common core of a section, while preserving nontriviality and the required shadow relations between sections.

title: Graphs with three distinct distance eigenvalues, one of which is zero
abstract: Koolen, Hayat and Iqbal asked for the connected graphs whose distance matrix has exactly three distinct eigenvalues, the middle one being $0$. The examples they gave, namely the Johnson graphs, the Hamming graphs and the halved cubes, are distance-regular. In this note, we show that the distance spectrum of such a graph is $\{ρ,0,-c\}$ with integers $c\ge2$ and $c\midρ$. For $c=2$ the graphs are exactly the cocktail party graphs, and for $c=3$ they are exactly the Cartesian product $K_3\,\square\,K_3$ of two triangles, the Petersen graph and its complement. We also show that such a graph need not be transmission-regular: Seidel switching the lattice graph $K_6\,\square\,K_6$ with respect to a line and the triangular graph $T(11)$ with respect to a maximal clique of size $10$ gives graphs on $36$ and $55$ vertices with distance spectra $\{54,0^{(26)},(-6)^{(9)}\}$ and $\{81,0^{(45)},(-9)^{(9)}\}$. Among the graphs of diameter $2$ obtained by switching a strongly regular graph with smallest eigenvalue $-2$ with respect to one part of an equitable partition, these two are the only ones that have exactly three distance eigenvalues and are not transmission-regular. We also observe that the transmission-regular graphs with exactly three distinct distance eigenvalues, the smallest one being $-3$, are exactly the complements of the strongly regular graphs with smallest eigenvalue $-2$ other than the cocktail party graphs.

title: Letter to a Young Black Mathematician: History, Storytelling, and Belonging in Mathematics
abstract: What does it mean to tell the story of a mathematician? Written as a letter to a young Black mathematician, this article reflects on how stories shape our understanding of mathematics and our sense of belonging within the mathematical community. Through the lens of Hidden Figures Revealed, a project documenting Black mathematicians at The Ohio State University, I discuss humanity, mathematics, and context as three guiding principles for mathematical storytelling. In particular, I reflect on how this framework emerged through archival research, shaped historical narratives, and informed mathematical learning experiences.

title: The optimal four-dimensional lattice quantizer and bounds from Voronoi facets
abstract: We prove that the root lattice $D_4$ uniquely minimizes the normalized second moment among four-dimensional lattices, up to similarity. The computer-assisted proof combines the classification of secondary cones with integration over Voronoi cells and weighted sums of squares. In dimensions at least two, comparison with circular cones gives a lower bound in terms of the number of Voronoi facets, improving the sphere bound and recovering the hexagonal value in dimension two. We prove Ajjanagadde's circular-cone concavity conjecture and deduce the lattice case of his conjectured quantization bound.

title: The covering radius of RM(1,9) is precisely 242
abstract: Let $\text{RM}(r,n)$ be the $r$th order Reed-Mullet code of length $2^n$, and let $ρ(r,n)$ denote its covering radius. It is known that $242\leρ(1,9)\le 244$, and the determination of $ρ(1,9)$ is a long-standing open question. We give a computer-assisted proof that $ρ(1,9)=242$, leveraging the classification of the $349$ orbits in $\text{RM}(3,9)/\text{RM}(2,9)$ under $\text{GL}(9,2)$ [1,3]. The notebook to verify the computer search portion, Verify_RM(1,9).ipynb, contains all data and recomputes each check, and may be found in the repository https://github.com/FreemanSlaughter/Covering-Radius.

title: Unconstrained support points can leave a convex support
abstract: Support points provide a practical and effective way to approximate a probability distribution by a small set of equally weighted representatives through energy-distance minimization. In many applications, the variables satisfy convex constraints that the representatives should also respect. We investigate whether unconstrained support points automatically satisfy such constraints and show that this is not guaranteed. We construct counterexamples using three planar observations, a density with full triangular support, and positive-definite matrix data admitting an indefinite optimal representative under the Frobenius norm. We also identify cases in which containment holds, establish stability under distributional perturbations, and quantify the objective cost of imposing a convex-hull constraint. For a fixed number of representatives and a positive population constraint gap, empirical configurations with vanishing global objective error eventually leave the sample convex hull almost surely.

title: The symbolic pfaffian method I: A generalization of the Gallucio-Loebl-Tesler Theorem
abstract:
The pfaffian number of a graph $G$, denoted by $\mathrm{pf}(G)$, is the minimum integer $k$ such that the generating function of perfect matchings of $G$ can be written as a linear combination of $k$ pfaffians of signed adjacency matrices. The Galluccio-Loebl-Tesler Theorem states that $\mathrm{pf}(G) \leq 4^g$, where $g$ is the orientable genus of $G$. We generalize this theorem by relating the pfaffian number of a graph to another graph parameter: the symbolic pfaffian number, denoted by $\mathrm{spf}(G)$. Namely, we prove that $\mathrm{pf}(G) \leq 2^{\mathrm{spf}(G)}$. Our proof is based on linear algebra arguments and does not depend on topological properties of graphs.
  As a consequence of our generalization, we conclude that $\mathrm{pf}(K_{2n}) = 2^{\mathcal{O}(n \log n)}$, an improvement on the previous upper bound of $4^{\mathcal{O}(n^2)}$ based on the genus. We also consider lower bounds for $\mathrm{pf}(G)$ related to $\mathrm{spf}(G)$. In particular, we show that the graphs with $\mathrm{pf}(G) = 4$ are the graphs with $\mathrm{spf}(G) = 2$. On the other hand, we show that our main result is strictly more general than a previous generalization by Norine.

title: Bilateral Christoffel-Geronimus-Uvarov formulas for mixed-type orthogonality on algebraic supports
abstract: Christoffel-type determinant formulas construct both normalized polynomial families and their reproducing kernel for mixed-type orthogonality in several variables after independent rational matrix transformations on the two arguments. The pairing may have a rectangular matrix of functionals, with separate degree bounds on each component, and may be supported on an algebraic variety. The reduced matrices are calculated from the original biorthogonal polynomials, rational moments, polynomial division and the masses left free by division; their nonvanishing determinants characterize existence and uniqueness. For measure pairings the rational data are expressed by Cauchy and multivariate Fantappie transforms. Exact dimension counts incorporate the four matrix factors and the relations of the support. For normal degree-ordered original families and fixed factors, when the component degrees on each side differ by a bounded amount and the normalization dimension grows at most like one degree layer, the resulting orders are bounded on curves and grow at most linearly on surfaces. For pairings allowing scalar factors to move between arguments, called balanced pairings, an exact obstruction determines whether a bilateral mass decomposes into unilateral masses when the denominators act injectively. Residue duality provides coordinates for division and mass quotients on integral curves, including singular points, and on the finite surface quotients specified here. Explicit singular-curve families retain nondegenerate residue pairings as denominator zeros coalesce. Positive congruences admit a further reduction by orthogonal projection, while balanced pairings give simultaneous intertwining identities for all coordinate multiplication matrices.

title: Multivariate analogues of Ruijsenaars' hypergeometric function
abstract: We construct multivariate analogues of Ruijsenaars' hypergeometric function as nested products of overlap coefficients between eigenfunctions of twisted primitive elements in representations of the modular double of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$. The construction is a hyperbolic counterpart of the nested multivariate Askey--Wilson polynomials and functions. Using iterated coproducts, we derive four systems of difference equations for which these multivariate functions are joint eigenfunctions. The four systems correspond to the two sets of variables and the two step sizes $iw_1$ and $iw_2$, which are interchanged by modular duality. We also prove that Ruijsenaars' one-variable transform is unitary in the parameter regime required for the construction, for positive as well as complex conjugate $w_1,w_2$. A two-sided normalization of the kernel separates the input and output weights, so that iterating one-variable transforms yields unitary multivariate transforms with explicit inverse and Plancherel formulas.

title: Universality of Large-Scale Geometry For Critical Random-Cluster Models
abstract: The understanding of the behaviour of critical lattice models in two dimensions has made immense progress in the past couple of decades, with conformal invariance as its conjectured end goal. We consider here the critical random-cluster model (or FK-percolation) on a large class of graphs --- namely bi-periodic isoradial graphs --- with cluster-weight~$q \in [1,4]$. Following up on the establishment of rotational invariance at criticality in \cite{Rotation}, we prove that the large scale behaviour of these models is asymptotically the same on all such graphs. These include the critical homogeneous models on the square, triangular and hexagonal lattices.

title: Metastability of the Meissner state in the three-dimensional Ginzburg--Landau model with pinning
abstract: We study the persistence of the Meissner state in the three-dimensional magnetic Ginzburg--Landau model with a spatially dependent pinning term. Factoring out the equilibrium profile associated with the pinning term reduces the problem to the analysis of a weighted Ginzburg--Landau functional. In the extreme type-II regime, we construct locally minimizing vortexless configurations for applied fields extending far beyond the first critical field. We obtain quantitative estimates showing that these configurations remain close, up to gauge transformations, to a Meissner-type state determined by a weighted London problem. We also prove the uniqueness, up to gauge transformations, of the locally minimizing Meissner-type branch within a quantitatively controlled class of local minimizers. A central difficulty is to derive elliptic estimates that remain uniform in the Ginzburg--Landau parameter in the presence of the resulting spatially dependent weight. Under a small-BMO assumption on this weight, we obtain the required regularity and extend to the three-dimensional pinned setting the metastability picture previously established for the homogeneous model.

title: Krzyż's conjecture for the seventh coefficient
abstract: A holomorphic function bounded in modulus by one in the unit disk has Taylor coefficients of modulus at most one. If the function has no zeros, Krzyż's conjecture predicts the stronger bound $2/e$ for every coefficient of positive order. We establish this bound for the seventh coefficient: $|a_7|\leq2/e$, with equality precisely for the functions $η\exp[-(1-ξz^7)/(1+ξz^7)]$, where $|η|=|ξ|=1$. Thus the largest possible value of $|f^{(7)}(0)|$ in this class is $7!\,2/e$, and the extremal functions are uniquely determined up to rotations of the variable and multiplication by a constant of modulus one.

title: Second order Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle for solenoidal fields: sharp constants, optimizers and sharp stability
abstract:
The second order Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle of Cazacu, Flynn and Lam is the uncertainty principle for the gradient of a function. Motivated by the question of Maz'ya on the uncertainty principle for divergence-free vector fields, solved by Cazacu, Flynn and Lam for $N=2$ and by Hamamoto for $N\ge3$, we study the second order principle for divergence-free fields $\mathbf{U}$ on $\mathbb{R}^N$. We prove that $\int|Δ\mathbf{U}|^2dx\int|x|^2|
abla\mathbf{U}|^2dx\ge C_N^2(\int|
abla\mathbf{U}|^2dx)^2$, where $C_N=1+ rac12\sqrt{N^2+8}$ for $N\ge3$ and $C_2=1+\sqrt2$. For the velocity of an incompressible flow, $\int|
abla\mathbf{U}|^2$ and $\int|Δ\mathbf{U}|^2$ are, up to constant factors, the enstrophy and the palinstrophy, so the inequality bounds the palinstrophy from below in terms of the enstrophy and the spatial spread of the velocity gradient. The constant $C_N$ is sharp and larger than the constant $ rac{N+2}{2}$ for general fields, and all the optimizers are explicit fields with Kummer function profiles. We also obtain the sharp constants on the poloidal and the toroidal fields of each degree. Then we prove the sharp stability of the inequality. In sum form, the deficit controls a chain of squared distances to explicit families of poloidal and toroidal fields, with all the constants sharp. In product form, we find the sharp stability constant in all dimensions. For $N\ge4$ it is $ rac12(\sqrt{N^2+4N-4}-\sqrt{N^2+8})$, and it is attained by swirling flows, the toroidal fields of degree one. On the Fourier side, the sixth order poloidal problem becomes a first order Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality for radial functions, and its stability follows from weighted Poincaré inequalities with Gaussian type measures.

title: The recognition problem for 4-manifolds and the unknotting problem for 2-spheres in 4-manifolds
abstract: We show that there is no algorithm to decide whether or not a given 4-manifold is PL homeomorphic to the connected sum of 7 copies of S 2 x S 2 . We also show that the TOP and PL unknotting problems for all surfaces in the connected sum of 7 copies of S 2 x S 2 are unsolvable.

title: Painlevé VI superintegrability and Heun-Racah algebras
abstract: We study the two fourth-order quantum superintegrable systems in the Euclidean plane that separate in polar coordinates and whose angular potentials are determined by the general four-parameter sixth Painlevé transcendent. One system has an oscillator radial term and the other an extended-Coulomb radial term. For both systems we give the fourth-order quantum integral explicitly, derive the cubic symmetry algebra and its Casimir, and construct a deformed-oscillator realization. At fixed energy the two algebras are specializations of the Heun--Racah algebra. Their structure functions contain the same quartic angular factor, determined by the Painlevé~VI parameters, while different radial factors distinguish oscillator and Coulomb dynamics. The Coulomb integral is obtained by transforming the Cartesian Hermitian symmetry at the operator level. The lower-order terms generated by the polar coordinate change are essential for commutation with the Hamiltonian. The two quantum systems are also related by the Levi-Civita transformation and coupling-constant metamorphosis, which gives a direct correspondence between their Painlevé parameters, algebras, Casimirs and representations. Earlier exceptional-Jacobi models arise at special rational parameter values, whereas the results here apply to the full four-parameter Painlevé~VI family. We also compare the quantum results with the corresponding classical Poisson algebras.

title: Isomorphism classes and geometric classification of three-dimensional Jordan algebras and the length function
abstract: We investigate the algebraic classification of Jordan algebras of dimensions at most three over arbitrary fields with more than two elements. Our approach combines the theory of nilalgebras and radicals with Peirce, Wedderburn decompositions and the length function. In characteristic two, we adapt the Peirce decomposition to organize the classification, including the field-dependent isomorphism conditions among parametrized families. We also study the varieties of Jordan algebra structures up to dimension three over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two. Besides explicit degenerations and standard arguments, we introduce the alicyclic and characteristic conditions as geometric obstructions to degeneration. We determine the rigid algebras and irreducible components in both dimensions. In dimension three, one component is the nine-dimensional affine space of square-zero products; unlike the other three components, it contains no open orbit.

title: Fourier analysis on a class of Schwartz spaces and applications
abstract: The study of regularity and solvability of partial differential operators on non-compact manifolds requires the construction of adapted functional spaces. In this work we introduce $\mathcal{S}(\mathfrak{M}\times\mathbb{R}^n)$, the Schwartz space on the product of a homogeneous space $\mathfrak{M}$ and the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$. We characterize $\mathcal{S}(\mathfrak{M}\times\mathbb{R}^n)$ and its topological dual by employing discrete Fourier analysis in terms of eigenfunction expansions associated with a class of anisotropic elliptic operators on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We provide a characterization via partial Fourier coefficients and via full coefficients, that is, with respect to both components of $\mathfrak{M} \times \mathbb{R}^n$ simultaneously, which is achieved by studying the Fourier analysis on $\mathfrak{M}$. Our results provide new tools for the analysis of operators in this broader setting. As an application, we investigate the global existence and regularity of solutions for a class of partial differential equations on $\mathfrak{M}\times \mathbb{R}^n$.

title: A nonarithmetic lattice from a mirror in the Couwenberg-Heckman-Looijenga construction
abstract: We prove that the stabilizer of a reflection mirror of the Couwenberg-Heckman-Looijenga lattice $\mathcal{C}(G_{29},3)$ induces a nonarithmetic lattice in $\operatorname{PU}(2,1)$. This lattice is not commensurable with any Deligne-Mostow lattice in $\operatorname{PU}(2,1)$ or any lattice in the twenty-two nonarithmetic classes listed by Deraux, Parker and Paupert.

title: Cuspidal sheaves on the stack of L-parameters
abstract: We introduce the notion of cuspidal coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of local L-parameters. We give a complete classification and relate them to Lusztig's cuspidal local systems (or character sheaves). Under the categorical local Langlands conjecture, these sheaves are expected to correspond to supercuspidal representations supported at basic points. We also construct semiorthogonal decompositions of the category of coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of L-parameters that conjecturally match the semiorthogonal decompositions of sheaves on $\mathrm{Bun}_G$ coming from the stratification by the Kottwitz set and Bernstein decomposition of representation categories.

title: Ad-conditions for higher-order recurrences: Dunkl and matrix-valued settings
abstract: The ad-conditions of Duistermaat and Grünbaum characterize bispectrality for a pair of differential operators. M.~Reach observed that a sequence of functions which is simultaneously an eigenfunction of a second-order differential operator and satisfies a recurrence relation of arbitrary order must satisfy a different kind of ad-conditions. We prove that the Reach ad-conditions are also sufficient, by an argument which is purely algebraic. This motivated us to explore ad-conditions in two new directions: to Dunkl differential-difference operators, where the coefficients of the ad-condition become elements of the Dunkl algebra and the reflection enters as a coefficient, and to matrix-valued orthogonal polynomials, where we exhibit ad-conditions for several families of exceptional matrix-valued polynomials satisfying five- and seven-term recurrence relations.

title: Beyond Typical Strings: Sampling the Complexity Landscape
abstract: Uniform random sampling of strings is overwhelmingly dominated by high-complexity strings, leaving the much smaller set of low- and intermediate-complexity strings largely unexplored. Here, we adapt the nested neutral set estimator (NNSE), a Monte Carlo rare-event sampling method, to estimate the distribution P(K) of complexity values for binary strings of fixed length. NNSE allows us to explore the full complexity landscape, including exponentially rare low-complexity regions that are inaccessible to direct sampling, for string lengths up to several hundred. We apply the method to several widely used complexity measures: Lempel-Ziv 76 (LZ76), Lempel-Ziv 78 (LZ78), context tree weighting (CTW), the block decomposition method (BDM), and block entropy. We further introduce uniform complexity weighting (UCW), which gives equal weight to different complexity levels rather than to individual strings. This approach provides a dataset-independent framework for comparing complexity measures across their full range and reveals substantial differences between measures for low- and intermediate-complexity strings that are largely hidden by conventional uniform sampling. Using the NNSE to perform UCW sampling allows us to compare complexity measures across their full range in a dataset-independent way. This reveals differences in their behavior for low- and intermediate-complexity strings that are practically inaccessible to conventional uniform sampling.

title: Erratum to "Linear representations of 3-manifold groups over rings"
abstract: The fundamental groups of compact $3$-manifolds are known to be residually finite. Feng Luo conjectured that a stronger statement is true, by allowing only finite groups of the form $\mathrm{PGL}_2(R),$ where $R$ is a finite commutative ring with identity. In a prior paper, "Linear representations of $3$-manifold groups over rings", we, together with two co-authors, gave an equivalent formulation of Luo's conjecture via faithful representations, investigated variants of the conjecture where the target group is of type $\mathrm{SL}_2, \mathrm{GL}_2, \mathrm{PSL}_2$, or $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ as in the original conjecture, and claimed to provide a $3$-manifold group which violated all four variants of the conjecture. We have discovered a flaw in the work, such that the existing proof is valid only for $\mathrm{SL}_2$ and $\mathrm{GL}_2$. Here, we provide a modified argument for the $\mathrm{PSL}_2$ and $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ cases.

title: Partial $C^{2,α}$ and $W^{2, VMO}$ regularity for nondifferentiable fully nonlinear elliptic equations and Isaacs equations
abstract:
We investigate the partial regularity of viscosity solutions to fully nonlinear elliptic equations of the form $F(D^2u, x) = f(x)$ in previously unexplored settings:
  (i) When $F$ is non-differentiable with respect to $D^2u$. (ii) When either $F$ or $f$ lacks Dini continuity in $x$.
  In the first scenario, we introduce a tangent operator property for $F$ such that, for a fixed point $x_0$ and a given matrix $M_0$, $F(M, x_0)$ is tangential to a convex or concave operator at $M_0$. We establish partial $C^{2,α}$ regularity for equations exhibiting this property.
  In the second scenario, we establish new partial $W^{2, \text{VMO}}$ regularity provided that the oscillation of $F$ in $x$ under the $L^n$-norm is of order $o(\log^{-1}(1/r))$.
  We address the Hausdorff dimensions of the singular sets of solutions for equations of the form $F(D^2u)=f(x)$ with data $f$ in $W^{1,n}$.
  Additionally, we demonstrate that the tangent operator property holds for various classes of equations, including nondifferentiable twisted elliptic equations, infimum of $C^1$ equations, semiconvex equations, and piecewise differentiable equations.
  Finally, we tackle the issue of smooth enveloping and obtain partial regularity of solutions for three subclasses of Isaacs equations.

title: On the lower bound of the refined Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture: proof of the cases S_{6,3} and S_{7,3} for 3x3 matrices
abstract: For Hermitian matrices $α,β$ let $\A_{n,m}(e^α,e^β)$ be the average of the traces of all words with $n$ letters $e^α$ and $m$ letters $e^β$. The refined Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture contains the lower bound $\A_{n,m}(e^α,e^β)\ge\Tr e^{nα+mβ}$ (Tr denotes the trace), which for $n=m=1$ is the Golden--Thompson inequality. We prove this lower bound for all $n+m\le7$ when the matrices have size at most three, and for $\min(n,m)\le2$ in every dimension. In all these cases we prove the stronger inequality $\A_{n,m}(A,B)\ge\Tr(A^{n/m}B)^m$ for positive semidefinite $A,B$, or its mirror image with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged; the lower bound of the refined conjecture follows from the Araki--Lieb--Thirring inequality. The cases with three letters $B$ in dimension three, $(n,m)=(3,3)$ and $(4,3)$, are reduced by an exact identity and the inequality of arithmetic and geometric means to a polynomial inequality in two variables, which is certified in exact rational arithmetic by Bernstein expansion on three boxes. The certificate is a short program in the ancillary files.

title: Classification of three-dimensional Leibniz dialgebras with two-dimensional annihilator
abstract: A Leibniz dialgebra is a vector space with two bilinear products $\dashv$ and $\vdash$ satisfying the dialgebra analogue of the right Leibniz identity. This notion is obtained by the same standard procedure that turns the associative identity into the axioms of Loday's associative dialgebras. In particular, $(\mathcal{DL},\dashv)$ is a right Leibniz algebra, so a Leibniz dialgebra is a Leibniz algebra together with a second, compatible product. This paper recalls the definition of Leibniz dialgebras and continue the algebraic classification of three-dimensional complex Leibniz dialgebras. This paper describes up to isomorphism all Leibniz dialgebras $(\mathcal{DL},\dashv,\vdash)$ for which the Leibniz algebra $(\mathcal{DL},\dashv)$ is isomorphic to one of the algebras $\mathcal{L}_{8}(α)$, $\mathcal{L}_9$, $\mathcal{L}_{10}$, $\mathcal{L}_{11}$ of the classification of three-dimensional complex Leibniz algebras. The result consists 18 families of pairwise non-isomorphic Leibniz dialgebras, nine of which depend on a complex parameter.

title: Complete Bernstein functions and real powers of P-matrices
abstract: We classify the nonzero complete Bernstein functions whose matrix functions preserve every real P-matrix in every order. They are precisely $f(z)=a+bz$, with $a,b\ge0$ and $a+b>0$, and $f(z)=a+cz/(z+s)$, with $a\ge0$ and $c,s>0$. For each fixed order $n\ge4$, the preservers vanishing at zero are exactly $cz$ and $cz/(z+s)$; every other such function admits a strictly totally positive counterexample. For a finite positive measure $μ$ on $(0,\infty)$, put $g(z)=\int z/(z+s)\,μ(ds)$ and $M_t=\int s^t\,μ(ds)$. In every fixed order $n\ge4$, a finite constant shift restores preservation on all real P-matrices if and only if $M_{r_n}$ and $M_{-r_n}$ are finite, where $r_n=\lfloor n/2\rfloor-1$. Every $a>c_n\sqrt{M_{r_n}M_{-r_n}}$ is sufficient, with $c_n$ depending only on $n$. A complete Bernstein function vanishing at zero admits a possibly different repairing constant in every order exactly when it is linear, or is a pure kernel mixture with all positive and negative integer moments finite. For principal real powers, the preserving exponents are $\mathbb R$ in order one, $[-1,1]$ in orders two and three, and $\{-1,0,1\}$ in every higher order. An explicit rational determinant-one totally positive family gives negative principal minors uniformly on prescribed compact subsets of $(-1,0)\cup(0,1)$.

title: Diagram of Geodesic Intervals in $C'(1/8)$-Groups
abstract: Let $Γ$ be a group characterized by a small cancellation $C'(1/8)$-presentation. We study the structure of its Cayley graph, specifically geodesic intervals and digons. We prove that all geodesic segments $[x,y]$ of length $n$ can be covered by finitely many simple geodesic digons with pairwise $C'(1/8)$-short lower intersections whose lower sides lie on a common geodesic segment $[x,y]$. This is a generalization of a proposition of Kharlampovich-Sklinos (arXiv:2106.05461) for random groups. We then bound this resulting diagram of digons, showing that the total perimeter of its cells and its edge count is bounded by $n$, and the cycle rank is equal to the number of distinct cell contours. Thus, although there may be many different geodesics, the size of their union is bounded linearly in the distance between their endpoints. The constant is independent of the number and lengths of the defining relators. In particular, the estimate applies to infinite presentations with unbounded relator lengths. From this we get a consequence for growth, allowing us to compare the number of geodesic words with the number of group elements of the same length.

title: Primary components and large prime factors of cyclotomic values
abstract: Let $Φ_r(a,b)$ denote the homogeneous cyclotomic value. For sufficiently large $A$, uniformly for $1/2\leq B\leq A$, $r\geq3$ and $Z\geq2$, the number of coprime pairs in $(A,2A]\times(B,2B]$ whose greatest prime factor $P(Φ_r(a,b))$ is at most $Z$ is $O(AB/\varphi(r)+\sqrt{r/\varphi(r)}\,π(Z;r,1))$, where $π(Z;r,1)$ counts primes at most $Z$ congruent to $1$ modulo $r$. If $n=n(A)\to\infty$ through positive integers and $1\leq H(A)=o(\log A)$, then $P(a^{2^n}+1)>2^nAH(A)$ for almost all $a\in(A,2A]$, and $P(a^{2^n}+b^{2^n})>2^nA^2H(A)$ for almost all coprime pairs in $(A,2A]^2$, with no further restriction on $n$. For every fixed $α>0$ and every $r\geq A^α$, pairwise distinct primitive prime divisors of $Φ_r(a)$ can be selected for all but $O_α(A^{1-c_α})$ bases in $(A,2A]$, where $c_α>0$. For coprime positive integers $a,b$ with $\max(a,b)\geq2$ and $r\geq3$, put $C=Φ_r(a,b)$ and $S=\varphi(r)^2\log\max(a,b)$. Uniformly as $S\to\infty$, $\max_{p\mid C}p^{v_p(C)}\geq(5/16-o(1))S$. For every positive function $h(S)\to\infty$, $\sum_{p\mid C,\;p^{v_p(C)}>S/h(S)}v_p(C)\log p =(1-o(1))\log C$ uniformly in the same limit.

title: A closed formula for the Poisson cohomology of scalar Dubrovin-Novikov brackets in arbitrary dimension
abstract: The structure of the Poisson cohomology groups for scalar Poisson brackets of Dubrovin-Novikov type with $D$ independent variables has been first described in arXiv:1512.05744 ; in that work, a complete dimensional counting was provided for $D=2$, and some numerical results exhibited for $D=3$, $D=4$. Here, we prove a formula for the dimensional counting of the Poisson cohomology for arbitrary $D$. Moreover, we show how to obtain canonical representatives for each cohomology class.

title: Ground States of a Coupled Fractional Schrödinger System under a Total-Mass Constraint: Complete Classification and Concentration Behavior
abstract: We consider a coupled fractional Schrödinger system with trapping potentials under a total-mass constraint, in which both the intraspecies and the interspecies interactions are attractive. For every fractional order $s\in(0,1)$ and dimension $N\ge1$, we obtain a complete classification of the existence and non-existence of minimizers: minimizers exist if and only if both intraspecies coefficients lie below the single-component critical mass and the interspecies coupling coefficient lies below an explicit critical threshold $β^*$, and no minimizer exists otherwise. The threshold $β^*$ is characterized by means of an auxiliary intensity function, which yields a lower bound for the energy functional without invoking a new coupled Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality. As the coupling coefficient approaches $β^*$, we analyze the concentration behavior. In the one-dimensional half-Laplacian case, the two components are shown to blow up at a common zero of the trapping potentials and, after rescaling, to converge to the same fractional ground-state profile, with the mass ratio determined explicitly by the intraspecies coefficients and the critical mass. For polynomial trapping potentials whose flattest common zero has order $q_0\in(0,1)$, the sharp blow-up rate is established, and both components concentrate simultaneously at the flattest common minimum.

title: A block-encoding approach to the Segawa-Suzuki spectral mapping theorem
abstract: We revisit the Segawa--Suzuki spectral mapping theorem for abstract Szegedy-type quantum walks from a block-encoding viewpoint. Retaining both eigenspaces of the involution underlying the chiral symmetry yields a natural two-by-two block representation in which the usual discriminant operator and its counterpart form the diagonal blocks. The non-endpoint spectral mapping theorem then follows from an elementary Schur decomposition, substantially simplifying the original proof by avoiding its invariant-subspace decomposition and approximate-eigenvector arguments. The same framework establishes the result for the spectrum, point spectrum, and Fredholm essential spectrum and gives a direct block-theoretic description of the endpoint inherited and birth eigenspaces. We illustrate the construction with a one-dimensional split-step quantum walk.

title: On the Distribution of Prime Squares and Its Applications
abstract:
We prove that, for every \(A>0\), all but \(O_A(X(\log X)^{-A})\) integers \(n<X\) satisfying \(n\equiv11\pmod{24}\) admit a representation \[
  n=a^2+b^2+p^2, \] where \(p\) and \(a^2+b^2+1\) are prime and \((a,b)=1\). For ergodic averages along prime squares, we prove a universal divergence result for integrable functions, while establishing almost-everywhere convergence for near-integrable functions. We also quantify how the bounds used to establish convergence behave as one approaches integrability. Moreover, we prove endpoint improving and sparse bounds for the corresponding discrete averages, with an explicit Orlicz loss.

title: Two-point concentration for graph classes admitting sparse vertex deletion
abstract: For fixed $p\in(0,1)$, we prove that the maximum number of vertices in an induced subgraph of $G(n,p)$ from a given class is concentrated on two consecutive integers, unifying and extending several earlier results. We require that the class contain arbitrarily large graphs and that every sufficiently large $k$-vertex member have a vertex of degree $o(k)$ whose deletion leaves a graph in the same class. This condition holds for empty graphs, trees, forests, planar graphs, graphs of bounded maximum degree, degeneracy or treewidth, graphs excluding a fixed complete bipartite subgraph (including graphs containing no cycle of length four), and many other graph classes.

title: Beyond the reduced Landau--Lifshitz--Bloch equation: Singular potential, global well-posedness, and micromagnetic limits
abstract: We study the full nonlinear mean-field Landau--Lifshitz--Bloch equation in micromagnetics arising from Garanin's spin-polarisation model [D. Garanin. Fokker-Planck and Landau-Lifshitz-Bloch equations for classical ferromagnets. Phys. Rev. B, 55 (1997)] prior to the usual near-equilibrium reduction. The equation combines a singular inverse-Langevin potential with a mobility whose longitudinal component degenerates at saturation, together with exchange, anisotropy, and the nonlocal whole-space stray field. The natural state space is the closed unit ball $|m|\leq 1$. For any $H^1$ initial data satisfying $|m_0|\leq1$, including saturated data of infinite free energy, we construct global weak solutions and derive instantaneous separation from saturation $|m|=1$. This restores uniform parabolicity and yields the thermodynamic formulation and exact energy identity for positive times. We further establish a quantitative low-temperature limit to the Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation and prove convergence of global trajectories to a single equilibrium. A spectral Curie-type threshold characterises the stability of the paramagnetic state and yields exponential relaxation above the threshold. Finally, for uniformly separated data we prove strong well-posedness, including global strong solutions in one- and two-dimensional domains, and exponential stability of non-degenerate equilibria, with a small-data global theory in three dimensions.

title: Stability, discretization, and optimality of continuous-time causal optimal transport
abstract: We prove stability of continuous-time causal and bicausal optimal transport problems when both marginals converge in adapted Wasserstein distance along common vanishing time shifts. The marginal laws, filtrations, and costs may all vary, while the limit remains the original causal or bicausal transport problem. This allows for time discretization and the approximation of transport problems between non-degenerate scalar fractional stochastic differential equations by their Wong--Zakai schemes. We further establish sufficient conditions so that the synchronous coupling is optimal for the bicausal transport problem between scalar fractional stochastic differential equations under continuous, nonnegative submodular costs of polynomial growth. This result covers all Hurst parameters \(H\in(0,1)\) up to an additional order-preserving commutator condition on the corresponding coefficients for the rough regime \(H\in(0,1/2)\).

title: A Koszul-Type Splitting Theorem for Complex Supermanifolds
abstract:
We study the splitting problem for complex supermanifolds using formal exponential maps and Ehresmann connections. We show that every formal exponential map induces a splitting of the underlying supermanifold. Furthermore, we establish that every Ehresmann connection determines a linearization of the infinite jet space, extending the corresponding construction for ordinary manifolds to supermanifolds.
  For Ehresmann connections preserving the zero section, we construct a formal exponential map in two ways: via the linearization of the infinite jet space and directly from the connection operator. We prove that both constructions yield the same map and induce the same splitting, thereby generalizing Koszul's splitting theorem from linear connections to zero-section-preserving Ehresmann connections. Finally, we provide examples showing that, without this assumption, the two constructions may yield different splittings, or one or both of them may fail to induce a splitting.

title: Spherical Schubert varieties in $GL_n / P$
abstract: Let a general linear group act on a partial flag variety transitively, and consider the induced action of a Levi subgroup $L$. A Schubert variety is $\textit{$L$-spherical}$ if it is stable under the $L$-action and contains a dense open orbit of a Borel subgroup of $L$. It is $\textit{toric}$ if, in addition, $L$ is a torus. In this paper, we give a combinatorial classification of $L$-spherical Schubert varieties in partial flag varieties. This is achieved by applying Lakshmibai-Seshadri paths forming crystal graphs of Demazure modules. Previously, Hodges and Lakshmibai classified $L$-spherical Schubert varieties in Grassmannians. $L$-spherical Schubert varieties in complete flag varieties were treated independently by Gao-Hodges-Yong and Can-Saha. Our classification generalizes and unifies these results.

title: Quasi-polynomial valuations of lattice polytopes
abstract: We prove that for any valuation $\varphi$ of lattice polytopes in ${\mathbb R}^m$, which is quasi-polynomial with respect to ${\mathbb Z}^m$-translations, and any lattice polytope $P$, the function $\varphi(nP)$ is quasi-polynomial in $n$.

title: Spectral unions of intervals with few rational relation tile the real line
abstract: We prove that every spectral finite union of pairwise disjoint bounded intervals whose lengths satisfy at most four linearly independent rational relations tiles the real line, and that each of its spectra has at most five cosets modulo its least period. This includes every spectral union of at most five bounded intervals. The proof combines specialization preserving subset-sum equalities with rigidity of exchanges between finite spectral fibers. We also obtain common tiling complements for all spectra of primitive sets of at most seven elements in finite cyclic groups, and establish the sharp eleven-point range in which consecutive pairs force periodicity of the dual set.

title: Distortion of Random Max Filters over Reflection Groups
abstract:
A max filter with Gaussian templates $a_1,\dots,a_D$ is a
  $G$-invariant map $\R^d\to\R^D$, where $G$ is a finite reflection group. As
  $D\to\infty$ its distortion converges a.s to the condition number of
  $M_G^{1/2}$, where $M_G$ is the second-moment matrix of a standard Gaussian
  vector moved into a fundamental chamber of $G$. We compute this limit exactly
  for the sign and dihedral groups, and show it grows as $Θ(\sqrt d)$,
  $Θ(d^{3/2})$ and $Θ(k)$ for the sign, symmetric and dihedral groups of order $2k$. The
  symmetric case bound uses a lower bound on the covariance of order
  statistics. For any finite $G$ we also show that the infimum defining the optimal lower Lipschitz
  constant of a piecewise-linear $G$-invariant map is a minimum.

title: Parameter-Free First-Order Method for Constrained Variational Inequalities
abstract:
Constrained variational inequalities (VIs) provide a general framework for modeling and solving complementarity and equilibrium problems with functional constraints. In this paper, we propose a parameter-free accelerated operator sliding (PFAOS) method for solving monotone VIs with convex smooth constraints. For a single constraint, PFAOS achieves an operator evaluation complexity of $\mathcal{O}(1/\varepsilon)$ and a constraint gradient evaluation complexity of $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{\varepsilon})$, without requiring prior knowledge of the Lipschitz constant of the VI operator or the smoothness constant of the constraint function. We further extend PFAOS to multiple constraints by incorporating a primal-dual hybrid gradient update, yielding a multi-constrained PFAOS (MC-PFAOS) method that preserves the same evaluation complexities.
  Finally, numerical experiments are conducted on large-scale games with coupling constraints to validate the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

title: A new upper bound for $A(19,6,8)$
abstract: We compute Polak's bound $A_4(19,6,8)$ for binary constant weight codes, obtaining the numerical value $673.04001$. An exact rational certificate gives $A_4(19,6,8)\le 673.0400143064802474039375132665301315202504$, and hence $A(19,6,8)\le 673$. This improves the upper bound $693$ listed in Brouwer's table. The certificate is verified by a separate program using exact rational arithmetic.

title: Blowdowns along Ricci flow in dimension four
abstract:
We show that the blowdown shrinking Ricci soliton of Feldman, Ilmanen and Knopf is strictly dynamically stable in the following strong local sense:
  (1) The Ricci flow from every metric on a closed 4-manifold containing a region close to a rescaling of a sufficiently large compact subset of the soliton in either orientation and with controlled geometry elsewhere develops a singularity with unique tangent flow modeled on the soliton.
  (2) The singular time slice has an isolated conical singularity, and by Gianniotis-Schulze the flow can be continued by blowing down a sphere of self-intersection $\pm1$.
  (3) On a closed 4-manifold, the set of metrics whose Ricci flows have their first singularity modeled on the soliton is $C^{14}$-open. It is nonempty if and only if the manifold contains a sphere of self-intersection $\pm1$.
  (4) The soliton is strongly rigid among shrinking Ricci solitons.
  As applications, we construct $C^{14}$-open sets of initial data whose Ricci flows perform any prescribed ordered sequence of blowdowns.
  (1) Every closed simply connected smooth 4-manifold, including spin and exotic examples, can be reached by Ricci flow from a standard $k\mathbb{CP}^2\#\ell\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2$, through finitely many blowdown singularities.
  (2) On the standard $2\mathbb{CP}^{2}\#9\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^{2}$, there are infinitely many open sets of initial metrics whose Ricci flows, after a single blowdown, reach pairwise nondiffeomorphic manifolds.
  The proof uses the spectral analysis of Naff and the second author and deals with the gauge-fixing problem along Ricci flow through a Ważewski argument inspired by Stolarski. We also use Bamler-Lai's PDE-ODI principle. Except for continuation (requiring nonnegative curvature of the asymptotic cone), all results apply to linearly stable nonflat asymptotically conical shrinkers in all dimensions.

title: On the second smallest ideal right-angled hyperbolic four-polytope
abstract: The regular ideal right-angled 24-cell has volume $4 π^2/3$ and is the unique minimum-volume entirely ideal right-angled hyperbolic four-polytope. We prove that the next distinct volume is $8 π^2/3$ and that its unique equality case is the reflection double of the 24-cell across one octahedral facet. We also show that an entirely ideal right-angled four-polytope whose facets are regular ideal octahedra or their doubles across triangular faces decomposes into a chain of regular 24-cells, with opposite cutting facets in each intermediate cell.

title: Applying Changes to LDPC Codes by Using 3-Induced Matchings and Eigenvalues
abstract: The 2-switch operation for reducing the number of short cycles in Tanner graphs of LDPC codes has been utilized in some works. If this operation is appropriately applied to a 2-induced matching in a bipartite graph, then it surely preserves the bipartiteness of the graph. With a 2-induced matching, we have only one choice for applying this type of change to the graph. Using 3-induced matchings creates more potential and flexibility to apply certain changes to the Tanner graph. We present a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a 3-induced matching in bipartite graphs with girth at least 6. A 3-induced matching helps us to have more choices for applying a change to a bipartite graph while surely preserving the bipartiteness of the graph and keeping the degree sequences unchanged. Among all changes that we consider, we select the best change for reducing the number of cycles of length 6. The eigenvalues of subgraphs are used to reach a 3-induced matching, and a condition in some steps can be checked to ensure that the subgraph has at least one 3-induced matching. We present some numerical results regarding the steps at which the condition that guarantees the existence of a 3-induced matching is checked.

title: Uniform duplication-divergence random graphs I: Degrees and Local Limits
abstract: We study a growing random graph in which each new vertex chooses a uniformly random parent, joins that parent with probability $r\in(0,1]$, and independently joins each of the parent's current neighbors with probability $p\in(0,1)$. Let $p_c$ be the unique solution of $p_c e^{p_c}=1$. For $0<p<p_c$, we prove that the empirical degree distribution converges in probability to the stationary distribution $π$ of an explicit reset-and-growth Markov chain. Its upper tail satisfies $π((y,\infty))\sim C_{p,r}y^{-κ}$, where $C_{p,r}>0$ and $κ>0$ solves $p^κ+pκ=1$. This confirms predictions from physics (Lambiotte, Krapivsky, Bhat and Redner, \textit{Physical Review Letters}, 2016). We further show that for every fixed radius $\ell$ and $p<p_c$, the empirical distribution of induced rooted $\ell$-neighborhoods converges to the invariant law of a graph-valued reset-and-growth Markov process. We give an explicit construction of the limiting graph using a marked ancestral genealogy. Its root component is almost surely finite for $r<1$, and infinite with exactly one end for $r=1$. Moreover, for every $0<p<1$, both the fixed-vertex degrees and the maximum degree grow on the scale $t^p$, and the vertex of maximum degree is eventually unique and persistent.

title: Four-Dimensional Semi-Homogeneous Convex Cones: A Complete Classification
abstract: We classify all four-dimensional semi-homogeneous convex cones, i.e., closed, pointed, full-dimensional cones whose connected automorphism group has principal orbits of codimension at most one. On such cones, the Monge-Ampère equation defining the canonical barrier reduces to an ordinary differential equation. This makes this barrier computationally accessible. The semi-homogeneous cones can then be used in modeling by conic programs. An obvious subset of such cones are the homogeneous cones. The key point allowing the classification is that for all other cones, the automorphism group has a three-dimensional subgroup acting locally faithfully on the principal orbits. This subgroup must have a Lie algebra which is either abelian or a direct product of a 1-dimensional algebra and a two-dimensional algebra generated by $A,B$ satisfying $[A,B]=B$. In both cases we classify all 4-dimensional representations up to isomorphism, and for each representation all invariant convex cones. For every cone an orbit invariant is computed.

title: Sedentariness in Cayley graphs
abstract: Let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of a finite graph $Γ$. We say that vertex $u$ of $Γ$ is sedentary if for some constant $C>0$, $|\exp(itA)_{u,u}|\geq C$ for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$. In this paper, we investigate vertex sedentariness in walk-regular graphs with a focus on Cayley graphs and, more generally, vertex-transitive graphs. In particular, we define the necklace polynomial of an integral graph and use this notion to characterize sedentariness in integral walk-regular graphs. As an application, we use basic tools from algebraic number theory to show that an integral Cayley graph on a group of odd order is sedentary and provide a lower bound on its sedentariness. We also give sufficient conditions such that a unitary Cayley graph over a finite ring is sedentary. Furthermore, we characterize the existence of twin vertices in Cayley graphs and vertex-transitive graphs, and completely determine the occurrence of sedentariness, perfect state transfer and pretty good state transfer in vertex-transitive graphs with twins. Finally, we prove that if $Γ(G,S)$ is a nonempty, integral, normal Cayley graph, then for any prime $p$ with $\gcd(p, |G|)=1$, there is at least one eigenvalue of $Γ(G,S)$ which is not a multiple of $p$. This generalizes a result of Arnadottir and Godsil, which states that an integral normal Cayley graph of odd order possesses an odd eigenvalue.

title: A power-saving asymptotic for a Möbius-weighted GCD quadratic form
abstract: For the Möbius-weighted quadratic form $T(N)=\sum_{m,n\leq N}μ(m)μ(n)(m,n)^2/(mn)$, we prove that $T(N)=cN+O_{\varepsilon}(N^{2/3+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, where $c>0$ is given by an absolutely convergent series of finite Möbius sums multiplied by a convergent Euler product. The proof combines the classical Jordan-totient decomposition of the GCD kernel with a mean-value estimate that is uniform in a coprimality parameter. Grouping the resulting squares according to $\lfloor N/d\rfloor$ gives the error term and a nonnegative series for $c$.

title: The Continuum Limit of the Deep Linear Network
abstract: The Deep Linear Network (DLN) is a simple version of a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) in which the activation function is the identity and the bias vector is the zero vector. We examine the behavior of the model when the number of weight matrices, which is finite in the original model, goes to infinity. We show that a plausible continuum limit is a dimensionally reduced version of the Yang-Mills equation on the torus, revealing an unexpected geometric interpretation of infinite-depth DLNs. While we do not prove this rigorously, it is a very pretty calculation. It also gives some insight into several features of the construction. We note that the choices of boundary conditions on the ends of the discrete series survive better in the continuum limit. Also, the regularizing functional which uses the moment map survives nicely in the continuum limit, whereas the regularizing functional using the size of approximating terms has no sensible limit. This surely is useful information for the choices we make in the finite-dimensional theory, and might also be useful in the more complicated MLP setting.

title: A Hierarchical direct solver for Lippmann-Schwinger equations based on boundary traces
abstract: A high-order hierarchical direct solver for variable-media scattering in two dimensions is presented. Standard discretizations for these problems produce dense linear systems that are commonly solved iteratively, requiring a new global solve for each incident field. The method proposed here instead constructs a reusable scattering operator for the inhomogeneous medium, based on a hierarchical subdivision of the computational domain. First, high-accuracy leaf scattering operators are built from discretized local integral equations. Up the hierarchy, neighboring boxes are merged to build the scattering operators for successively larger boxes. A key feature of the method is that each scattering operator is represented as a map of incoming traces to outgoing traces. Consequently, volume unknowns appear only in the leaf computations; all higher levels of the hierarchy operate entirely on boundary traces. The hierarchical solver is presented first at the continuum level and discretized only afterward using high-order local volume quadrature, polynomial trace representations, and boundary integral techniques. For a discretization involving $N$ degrees of freedom, the method requires $O(N^{3/2})$ work and $O(N\log N)$ storage to build all scattering operators. Once these are available, any incoming field can be processed at cost $O(N)$ if only the outgoing field is required, and cost $O(N\log N)$ if the full field is required. Numerical experiments demonstrate high-order accuracy on a range of challenging scattering problems including cavities, back-scattering, limited regularity, and high wavenumber, that pose significant challenges to iterative methods.

title: Some Remarks on the Asymptotic Behavior of Mean Field Games of Controls
abstract: We analyze the asymptotic behavior of several mean field games of controls. First, in the time-dependent case, we examine the behavior of solutions to discounted mean field games of controls as the discount factor $λ$ tends to infinity. Next, we study three stationary models of mean field games of controls, finding that solutions to the first-order discounted problem and the second-order ergodic problem can be obtained from solutions to the second-order discounted problem by taking $ν\to 0$ and $λ\to 0$, respectively. Finally, we investigate the long-time average behavior of solutions to the time-dependent system with no discount, finding that solutions converge to the solution to the second-order ergodic problem as $T \to \infty$.

title: Clarkson--McCarthy type inequalities, part II: refinements, unitary orbits, unitarily invariant norms and $\ell_s$--$\ell_s$ estimates
abstract: In previous work \cite{Zha26a}, the author established Clarkson--McCarthy type inequalities for several classes of operator families, including $\ell_p$--$\ell_p$ estimates and mixed $\ell_q$--$\ell_p$ estimates, by means of operator square-sum identities. The present paper has two main aims. First, using the tracial joint spectral measures recently introduced by O.~Heinävaara \cite{Hei25}, we obtain several refinements of the McCarthy--Clarkson inequalities, one of which confirms a conjecture of Audenaert \cite{AK17}. Second, combining tools from matrix analysis with complex interpolation theory, we establish Clarkson--McCarthy type inequalities for unitary orbits, unitarily invariant norms, and $\ell_s$--$\ell_s$ estimates, again in the framework of operator square-sum identities.

title: Spectral Fields and Unitary Descent: Local splitting, simultaneous norms, and transcendental obstructions
abstract: Spectral fields can recover matrix coefficients without standardizing the invariant Hermitian form. Over an algebraic subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ stable under nontrivial complex conjugation, we prove that every Zariski-dense subgroup in a normalized Hermitian model of dimension $m\ge4$ and signature $(m-1,1)$ at the fixed embedding contains a loxodromic element whose spectrum makes all diagonal coefficients norms. The element can be chosen so that every positive power is regular and generates the same splitting field. For an arbitrary initial Hermitian model over such a field, two spectra suffice for standard unitary descent over an extension of relative degree at most $(m!)^2$. Over every quadratic extension $F/k$ of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic zero, a four-dimensional quasi-split unitary group of Witt index two contains a discrete, Zariski-dense free subgroup whose spectra all split over $F$. Over intrinsic fields of positive transcendence degree, we construct a single convex cocompact, Zariski-dense free subgroup of $\mathrm{SU}(3,1)$ for which, for every initial regular element and every normalized extraction, the Hermitian obstruction persists after adjoining any finite family of spectra and over the total spectral field.

title: Excedances and Deficiencies of Integer Partitions
abstract: The notion of a fixed point, applied by Blecher and Knopfmacher to integer partitions, can be considered as a permutation statistic. Here we apply two related permutation statistics, excedance and deficiency, to integer partitions. Using analytic and combinatorial techniques, we establish several generating functions and make connections to partition concepts including Dyson's crank statistic, overpartitions, and the Rogers--Ramanujan partitions.

title: Absorption Probabilities for Brownian Convex Hulls in Arbitrary Dimension
abstract:
For every dimension $d\ge1$, we determine the probability that a prescribed point in $\mathbb R^d$ belongs to the convex hull over $[0,1]$ of a standard Brownian motion starting at the origin or of a Brownian bridge from $0$ to $0$. We obtain explicit one-dimensional integral formulas involving only standard special functions. For example, in dimension three the Brownian-motion absorption probability $p_3^B(r)$ for a prescribed point at distance $r>0$ from the origin is \[ p_3^B(r) =\frac{r}{\sqrt2\,π^{3/2}} \int_0^\infty \left(\fracπ{2\sqrt{1+v^2}}-1\right) \mathrm{e}^{-r^2(1+v^2)/4} (K_1-K_0)\!\left(\frac{r^2(1+v^2)}4\right)\,\mathrm{d} v, \] where $K_ν$ denotes the modified Bessel function of the second kind. For each fixed dimension $d\ge1$ and each prescribed nonzero point in $\mathbb R^d$, we derive precise asymptotics of the non-absorption probabilities for the convex hulls of Brownian motion on $[0,T]$ and a Brownian bridge from $0$ to $0$ over the same interval, as $T\to\infty$. The corresponding probabilities are asymptotic to explicit positive constants times $T^{-1/2}(\log T)^{d-1}$ and $T^{-1}(\log T)^{d-1}$, respectively.
  We also consider the first time $τ_d$ at which the growing convex hull of a standard Brownian motion in $\mathbb R^d$ absorbs a prescribed point at distance one from the origin. We determine the Mellin and Laplace transforms of $τ_d$ explicitly. Although $\mathbb E[τ_d]=\infty$ in every dimension, we prove \[ \frac{\logτ_d-2d}{2\sqrt d} \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}N(0,1), \qquad d\to\infty. \] In particular, $τ_d^{1/d}\to\mathrm{e}^2$ in probability, as $d\to\infty$. Surprisingly, the same limit holds for $S_d^{1/d}$, where $S_d$ is the first time at which the Brownian convex hull contains the entire unit ball.

title: A sharp plank theorem for cube annuli
abstract: We prove a conjecture of András Bezdek on plank coverings of square annuli. A plank in a Euclidean space is the closed region between two distinct parallel hyperplanes, and its width is the distance between them. Let $Q$ be a unit square and let $H$ be a square of side length $1/2$ whose sides are parallel to those of $Q$. Then every finite family of planks covering $Q\setminus H$ has total width at least $1$. More generally, if an axis-parallel box with side lengths $h_1,\ldots,h_d$ is removed from the unit cube in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\sum_jh_j = d-1$, then every finite plank covering of the remaining set has total width at least one. The bounds are sharp.

title: Some Constructions in the Category of Topological Partial Actions
abstract: We present some theoretical aspects of the categories of global and partial group actions of topological groups on topological spaces, denoted by G-ActTop and G-pActTop, respectively. We construct topological partial actions on products and disjoint unions of topological spaces, and G-pinvariant subspaces. Furthermore, we provide an adequate definition of congruence (G-pcongruence), which enables the construction of quotient objects in the category of topological partial actions. In addition, we associate a special G-pcongruence to each pair of strong G-pmorphisms. Then, we study products, co-products, equalizers, co-equalizers, pullbacks, and pushouts in the category G-pActTop. We find that the category of topological partial actions is finitely complete and contains a co-complete subcategory. Finally, we show that the relationship between a topological partial action and its enveloping action is functorial. As a consequence, we obtain that the categorical product in G-ActTop coincides with the categorical product in G-pActTop. Moreover, the envelope of a co-product in G-pActTop is given by the co-product of the respective envelopes.

title: Stability of Solitons in the Parametrically Driven and Damped Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation in Arbitrary Dimension
abstract: We study the spectral stability of soliton solutions of the parametrically driven and damped nonlinear Schrödinger (PDDNLS) equation with power-law nonlinearity $|Ψ|^{2κ}Ψ$ in $N$ dimensions. We identify two families of stationary solutions, $Ψ_\pm$, whose existence is determined by two conditions: one involving the nonlinearity exponent~$κ$ and the spatial dimension~$N$, and another involving the forcing amplitude~$r$ and the damping coefficient~$ρ$. By linearising around these solutions and introducing a convenient parametrisation through~$\varepsilon$, we reduce the stability problem to a dissipationless eigenvalue problem for two Schrödinger-type operators, $L_0$ and $L_1$. We prove that $Ψ_-$ is always unstable, while for $Ψ_+$, we carry out a complete spectral analysis by decomposing the problem into angular momentum sectors $\mathcal{S}_l$. We show that modes with $l \geq 2$ generate no instabilities and that no complex quadruplets arise on~$\mathcal{S}_1$. We also derive an analytical instability criterion on $\mathcal{S}_l$ by combining a Vakhitov--Kolokolov-type argument with a local analysis that determines the direction of the eigenvalue splitting near the origin. In addition, we uncover new phenomena at both small and large values of $κ$ that were not investigated in earlier one-dimensional studies. Numerical stability diagrams for $N = 1, 2, 3$ are presented.

title: Optimistic Gradient Algorithms with Randomized Coordinate and Variance Reduction Strategies for Composite Inclusions
abstract: In this paper, we consider a class of possibly nonmonotone finite-sum composite inclusions in which evaluating all components or updating all coordinates at every iteration can be computationally expensive. We develop two optimistic gradient frameworks that combine variance reduction with randomized block-coordinate updates. The first framework applies under a blockwise average Lipschitz continuity condition and the existence of a weak-Minty solution. It achieves an $\mathcal{O}(1/k)$ convergence rate for the expected squared residual, and its iterates converge almost surely under mild additional conditions. The second framework relies on a backward-forward reformulation under average co-coercivity and co-hypomonotonicity. It achieves faster $\mathcal{O}(1/k^2)$ and $o(1/k^2)$ rates for the expected squared residual, as well as $o(1/k^2)$ almost-sure rates. For both frameworks, we provide a generic condition on the stochastic estimator that covers mini-batch, loopless SVRG, and a generalized JacSketch-type estimator, and we derive the corresponding oracle complexities under importance-based block sampling. In particular, in highly heterogeneous regimes, the L-SVRG and JacSketch variants attain $\mathcal{O}\big(n + n^{2/3}ε^{-2}\big)$ and $\mathcal{O}\big(n + n^{2/3}ε^{-1}\big)$ oracle complexities for the nonaccelerated and accelerated methods, respectively. Numerical experiments illustrate the effects of variance reduction and block-coordinate sampling, and compare the proposed methods with existing baselines.

title: On potential density of rational points on hyperkahler varieties
abstract: In this paper, we prove that the rational points on hyperkähler varieties in each of the four known deformation families admitting a rational Lagrangian fibration are potentially dense. Furthermore, we give several applications and construct examples of hyperkähler varieties beyond these families satisfying the potential density property. Our approach is first to prove that rational points on hyperkähler varieties admitting two rational Lagrangian fibrations with distinct associated isotropic rays are potentially dense. We then construct a projective Shafarevich--Tate twist admitting two such fibrations, together with a dominant rational map from the twist to the original variety.

title: A Directed Cubical Framework for k-critical Bipersistence Modules
abstract: In topological data analysis, multiparameter persistence modules (MPMs) are used to analyze data with multiple parameters. Summarizing topological information for MPMs is a non-trivial task; one useful summary of bipersistence modules is the fibered barcode \cite{lesnick2015interactive,lesnick2025fast}. In this paper, we use a directed topological construction of the parameter space of a bifiltration to extend the fibered barcode. Specifically, given a $k$-critical bifiltration $F$, we build an associated directed Euclidean cubical complex $C$ whose directed paths each correspond to a one-parameter subfiltration of $F$. The path space of $C$, $\di{C}$, is used to define the \emph{extended fibered barcode}, which contains all possible monotonically increasing paths in $C$. We show that there can be paths in $\di{C}$ which generate filtrations not obtainable along a line with positive slope, and that all lines with positive slope have a path in $\di{C}$ that generate an equivalent barcode. We introduce two types of equivalence for these restricted modules: combinatorial equivalence of diagrams, and simplicial equivalence of the filtrations generating the modules. We show that removing certain cubes from $C$ yields a subcomplex on which dihomotopic paths induce simplicially equivalent filtrations, and hence combinatorially equivalent diagrams.

title: Costate Estimation and Covector Mapping for Bernstein Polynomial Direct Methods in Optimal Control
abstract: Bernstein polynomial approximation of continuous functions has a slower rate of convergence as compared to other approximation methods. ``The fact seems to have precluded any numerical application of Bernstein polynomials from having been made. Perhaps they will find application when the properties of the approximant in the large are of more importance than the closeness of the approximation.'' -- has remarked P.J. Davis in his 1963 book Interpolation and Approximation. This paper presents a direct approximation method for nonlinear optimal control problems with mixed input and state constraints based on Bernstein polynomial approximation, in which the dynamic and path constraints are imposed at the Bernstein coefficients (control points). We provide a rigorous analysis showing that, under convergence assumptions on the control polygons, the proposed method yields consistent approximations of time continuous optimal control problems and can be used for costate estimation of the optimal control problems.
