In particular, multipliers satisfying a relaxed Karush Kuhn Tucker system of the resulting nonlinear program, scaled by the quadrature weight, approximate the costate and the multipliers of the optimal control problem. Owing to the structure of the Bernstein differentiation matrix, the discrete transversality conditions are contained in the relaxed Karush Kuhn Tucker system, and no additional closure conditions need to be added to it. This result leads to the formulation of the Covector Mapping Theorem for Bernstein polynomial approximation.

title: Yet another approach to measuring distance in some hyperspaces
abstract: In this article, we define a new partial distance on hyperspaces consisting of closed balls, which is a partial metric in the sense of Matthews. We prove that these partial metric spaces are complete if and only if the metric spaces from which the corresponding ball spaces arise are complete. Finally, we compare the topology induced by the new partial distance with that induced by the classical Hausdorff distance.

title: The Dilate Rollercoaster
abstract:
Given a finite subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$ and a multiset of non-zero integers $Λ=\{λ_1, \ldots, λ_k\}$, the dilate sum \[Λ\cdot A:=λ_1\cdot A+λ_2\cdot A+\cdots+λ_k\cdot A =\{λ_1a_1+\cdots+λ_ka_k: a_1, \ldots, a_k\in A\}.\] For a non-zero real number $r$, say that $Λ_2$ $r$-dominates $Λ_1$ if we can partition some of the elements of $Λ_2$ into blocks summing to the elements of $r\cdotΛ_1$. Then for all finite subsets $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$, $Λ_2\cdot A$ contains a translate of $r\cdot(Λ_1\cdot A)$, and hence $|Λ_1\cdot A|\le|Λ_2\cdot A|$ for all $A$. In a recent paper, Kravitz (arXiv:2606.27087) proves the converse: if $Λ_2$ does not $r$-dominate $Λ_1$ for any $r$, then there exists a finite set $A$ satisfying $|Λ_1\cdot A|>|Λ_2\cdot A|$. For example, $\{2, 3, 5, 7\}$ does not contain two disjoint subsets with a sum ratio of 7, and so there exists a finite $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$ for which $|A+7\cdot A|>|2\cdot A+3\cdot A+5\cdot A+7\cdot A|$.
  We extend Kravitz's method to apply it to multiple inequalities and multiple sets, showing that for multisets $Λ_{i,j}$ with $1\le i\le k$ and $1\le j\le\ell$, there exist finite sets $A_1, \ldots, A_\ell\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$ such that for all $1\le i<k$ \[|Λ_{i,1}\cdot A_1+\cdots+Λ_{i,\ell}\cdot A_\ell| >|Λ_{i+1,1}\cdot A_1+\cdots+Λ_{i+1,\ell}\cdot A_\ell|\] provided there do not exist indices $1\le i_1<i_2\le k$ and a non-zero scalar $r$ such that $Λ_{i_2,j}$ $r$-dominates $Λ_{i_1,j}$ for all $1\le j\le\ell$.
  Along the way, we resolve the analogue of Nathanson's Problem 1 for his Theorem 4 (arXiv:1604.08940), as well as the problems in Section 1.4.3 of Kravitz's paper.

title: Loss of Monotonicity in the Vector Play Model and Consequences for Newton-Type Solvers
abstract: The vector play model (VPM) replaces the implicit minimization of the energy-based hysteresis model (EBM) by an explicit update. Its tangent contains the product of the Hessians of two unrelated potentials and is unsymmetric. Hence, the VPM has no co-energy density at frozen memory, and the skew part makes $\boldsymbol{H}\mapsto\boldsymbol{B}$ lose monotonicity in a band just outside the pinning circle, into which small time steps drive the sliding states. In composite models, the determinant of the tangent can change sign, which explains published failures of the local inversion $\boldsymbol{B}\mapsto\boldsymbol{H}$, and where it is negative, $\boldsymbol{H}\mapsto\boldsymbol{B}$ is not injective. In the scalar potential formulation, the exact tangent keeps a descent guarantee, whereas symmetric surrogates of the tangent, such as the symmetrized tangent or Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (BFGS) updates, lose it and become ascent directions where the skew part dominates, as computations of TEAM Problem 32 confirm. It is therefore recommended to use solvers with an unsymmetric tangent.

title: Large Maximal Intersecting Families with Covering Number Three
abstract: Let $n>2k$ and $k\ge4$. The largest size of an intersecting family of $k$-subsets of $[n]$ with covering number at least three is \[ g_1(n,k)=\binom{n-1}{k-1}-3\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}+\binom{n-k-2}{k-1}+\binom{n-2k}{k-1}+3, \] attained by a unique family up to isomorphism. We prove that every other maximal intersecting family $\mathcal F$ with covering number three satisfies \[ |\mathcal F|\le M(n,k)=\max\{q(n,k),g_2(n,k)\}, \] where \begin{align*} q(n,k)&=\binom{n-1}{k-1}-3\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}+\binom{n-k-3}{k-1}+\binom{n-2k+1}{k-1}+3,\\ g_2(n,k)&=g_1(n,k)-\binom{n-k-3}{k-3}+1. \end{align*} This bound is attained for every $n>2k$ and $k\ge4$, so $M(n,k)$ is the second largest distinct size. For $k=4$, $g_1(n,4)=13n-69$ and $M(n,4)=12n-61$. For $k\ge5$, we have $M(n,k)=q(n,k)$ when $2k<n\le3k-2$ and $M(n,k)=g_2(n,k)$ when $n\ge3k-2$; the two terms coincide only at $n=3k-2$. We also classify all families attaining $M(n,k)$ that admit a critically shifted labeling, including additional nonisomorphic families at $n=2k+1$. The proof combines local replacements with an inverse-shift estimate and gives a new proof of the known maximum and its uniqueness.

title: Strongly Pseudoconvex Domains with Finite Dimensional $p$-Bergman Spaces
abstract: We show that for every $n\ge2$, $p>2$, and positive integer $m$, there exists a finite-volume pseudoconvex domain $D\subset\mathbb C^n$ with real-analytic strongly pseudoconvex boundary whose $p$-Bergman space $A^p(D)$ has dimension $m$. These domains admit smooth strictly plurisubharmonic exhaustions and satisfy $H^\infty(D)=\mathbb C$ and $\dim A^s(D)=\infty$ for every $0<s\le2$. Moreover, for every finite $s\ge p$, we have $\dim A^s(D)=\lceil pm/s\rceil$. As an application, we show that the Bergman projection fails to map $\mathcal{C}_c^\infty(D)$ into $A^p(D)$ and admits no bounded extension to $L^s(D)$ or $L^{s/(s-1)}(D)$ for any finite $s\ge p$.

title: Porosity in Diophantine approximation
abstract:
We provide a general framework for obtaining upper bounds on the packing dimension of certain sets arising from Diophantine approximation using the notion of porosity from geometric measure theory. In particular, the framework relies on showing that such sets are mean porous, as introduced by Koskela and Rohde (Math. Ann., 1997). As applications of our framework we show that:
  For $\varepsilon>0$ sufficiently small, the set of $d$-dimensional $\varepsilon$-badly approximable points has packing codimension comparable to $\varepsilon^{d}$ up to multiplicative constant.
  Any $C^{2}$ submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ with bounded first and second partial derivatives intersected with the set of $d$-dimensional $\varepsilon$-badly approximable points has packing dimension strictly less than the dimension of the submanifold.
  For any matrix $A\in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ satisfying certain Diophantine conditions, the set of points that avoid the $\varepsilon \|\mathbf{q}\|_{\infty}^{-\frac{n}{m}}$-neighbourhood of the orbit $\{A\mathbf{q} \mod \mathbb{Z}^{m}:\mathbf{q} \in \mathbb{Z}^{n}\}$ has packing codimension greater than $C_{A} \varepsilon^{m}$ for $C_{A}$ a constant depending on $A$ and $m$ only. \end{itemize}

title: Exact Asymptotics for the Harmonic Descent Chain and Extended Convergence Bounds for Recursive Statistics
abstract: We give an exact asymptotic expansion of the occupation probabilities $a(n,k)$ of the harmonic descent chain, introduced by D. Aldous, as $n\rightarrow\infty$ with $k\in\mathrm{o}(\sqrt{n})$. In addition, we extend the recent results of Brandenberger et al. by giving a bound on the rate of convergence of sequences defined recursively by $x_n = \frac{1}{H_{n-1}}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\frac{x_i}{n-i}$ for more general initial conditions. This result enables the application of an existing central limit theorem, also by Brandenberger et al., to statistics of the critical beta-splitting tree which satisfy our more general initial conditions.

title: Variance-reduced First-order Methods for Finite-sum Function Constrained Convex Optimization
abstract: This paper studies finite-sum convex optimization with convex function constraints, where both the objective $f(x)=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)$ and the constraint mapping $g(x)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n g_j(x)$ may have a large number of components. We propose a variance-reduced anchored constraint extrapolation method (VaRAn-ConEx), which combines stochastic component sampling with primal--dual extrapolation for nonlinear function constraints. Relative to stochastic approximation schemes such as ConEx, VaRAn-ConEx~method reduces gradient complexity by using epoch-wise full-gradient correction and variance-reduced estimators for both the objective and constraint components. In the semi-finite case where $n=1$, the method attains gradient complexities $O(\sqrt m/ε)$ under constant steps and $O(m/ε^{1/2}+1/ε^{3/2})$ under nonconstant steps. In the fully finite-sum case, we establish boundedness of the Lagrange multiplier sequence and derive convergence and gradient-complexity bounds for constant and nonconstant step-size policies. Under these policies, we then prove similar gradient complexity with $m$ replaced by $\max\{m,n\}$. We also show acceleration when the finite-sum objective $f$ is strongly convex, irrespective of components $f_i$.

title: Quantitative spectral rigidity for negatively curved manifolds and Outer Space
abstract: Let $M$ be a closed manifold with fundamental group $G$. A subset of conjugacy classes $E \subset \text{conj}(G)$ is said to be spectrally rigid if when two negatively curved Riemannian metrics have the same marked length spectra on $E$, then their length spectra agree on all conjugacy classes. In this work we study spectrally rigid subsets from a quantitative perspective. We show that, if the density of $E \subset \text{conj}(G)$, measured with respect to a fixed reference metric, decays more slowly than $T^{-1/2}$ then $E$ is spectrally rigid. We establish analogous rigidity results for Culler-Vogtmann Outer Space and show that the $T^{-1/2}$ threshold is sharp in this setting.

title: Two moments suffice for Bessel approximation: conditioned differences, contingency tables, and probabilistic divide-and-conquer
abstract: We develop Stein's method, with explicit constants throughout, for the discrete Bessel distribution: the law of a Poisson variable given its difference from an independent Poisson variable. The Bessel family is characterized by a birth-death operator with quadratic death rate $n(n+k)$ and as the exact fixed-point set of a centered quadratic-bias transform, and we prove a dependency expansion of Arratia-Goldstein-Gordon type: two joint moments of a column array control the total-variation distance from the conditioned row sum to a matched Bessel law. Applied to the row-constrained Fisher-Yates ensemble on $2\times c$ contingency tables -- independent Bernoulli or capped-Poisson entries conditioned on the row-sum difference, column sums free -- this yields a limit theorem -- which upgrades to the entire conditioned table at the same two-moment error -- a completely explicit enumeration estimate, and an exact divide-and-conquer sampler with certified acceptance. The entire apparatus -- operator, expansion, enumeration, sampler -- generalizes to $r\times c$ tables, where conditioning on all successive row differences produces a hyper-Bessel law. Verification scripts are included as ancillary files.

title: Porteous Meets Walsh: Counting Critical Points for $\mathcal{H}_2$-Norm Model Order Reduction Using Algebraic Geometry Behind Multiparameter Eigenvalue Problems
abstract: Several polynomial systems arising in systems and control have been shown to exhibit a partially linear structure, which allows them to be reformulated as a multiparameter eigenvalue problem (MEP). In this work, we show how such MEP formulations can be leveraged to obtain refined information about the solution set of the polynomial system. We demonstrate, in the setting of single-input single-output $\mathcal{H}_2$-norm model order reduction, how the Thom--Porteous formula can be used to derive an exact count of the complex solutions of the critical equations derived from Walsh's theorem. We prove, under suitable genericity assumptions, that their set of complex solutions is finite and that all solutions occur without multiplicity. Moreover, we derive an explicit formula for the total number of complex solutions as a function of the model orders. Throughout, we provide a self-contained and application-oriented exposition of the algebro-geometric tools required for our analysis, with the aim of making them accessible to the broader engineering community.

title: Generic Linear Momentum Escape for Twist Maps
abstract: We prove that linear momentum escape is generic in the $C^{1,α}$ topology for smooth potential perturbations of exact symplectic twist maps, for every $0<α<1$. We assume a $C^2$ generating function, a uniform twist condition, and uniform upper bounds on $D_{11}S$ and $D_{22}S$. For an open dense set of potentials, every sufficiently small momentum drift is realized by an orbit. This genericity result does not extend in general to the $C^2$ topology. We give examples with no nonzero linear drift under $C^2$-small perturbations in every dimension. In dimension one, a second example has bounded momentum along every orbit under $C^2$-small perturbations.

title: Upper bounds for packings of cylinders around the unit sphere
abstract: In this note we study the problem of packing infinite circular cylinders tangent to the unit sphere. For a given number of cylinders $N$, $N\geq 3$, the maximal common cylinder radius $R_N$ is the maximum $R$ for which there exist $N$ circular cylinders of radius $R$ with non-overlapping interiors, all tangent to the unit sphere. In 1990, Kuperberg conjectured that there does not exist a packing of more than 6 cylinders of radius one tangent to the unit sphere, that is, $R_7<1$. This conjecture was recently confirmed by an exhaustive computer-assisted case analysis. Here we prove new bounds for $R_N$ for small $N$ by considering an auxiliary configuration of spherical quadrilaterals. In particular, we provide a short geometric proof of Kuperberg's conjecture and show that $R_7<0.9978$.

title: A Preconditioned Semismooth Newton Method for Box-Constrained Elliptic Optimal Control Problems with Random Coefficients
abstract: We consider the optimal control problem of an elliptic PDE with random diffusion under pointwise box constraints on the control. The constraints make the optimality conditions nonsmooth, with an active set that is not known in advance, and the random diffusion couples the state and the adjoint across all stochastic modes. To design a solution algorithm for this problem, we rely on the Fenchel duality viewpoint. Fenchel duality absorbs the box constraint into the objective and yields an exact reduced problem in the elliptic adjoint variable alone. After a stochastic Galerkin--finite element discretization, eliminating the state leaves a strongly monotone, piecewise smooth equation, which we solve directly by a matrix-free semismooth Newton method with the box projection retained exactly and with no outer iteration, penalty or smoothing parameter. Next, we introduce and analyze a current-set preconditioner, which adds the active-set correction of the current Newton step to a mean-diffusion reference operator and is inverted exactly by a rank-1 update. For implementation, we use a cheaper preconditioner that keeps only a fraction of free control values. Numerical experiments show second-order convergence of the state, and Newton and PCG counts that stay bounded under mesh refinement and growth of the stochastic dimension.

title: Coinduction in Grounded Arithmetic
abstract: A grounded arithmetic counts a sentence as true only when a terminating process establishes it; a sentence no such process settles has no value. Such a logic can state that an event happens, but not that it never happens under unbounded choice. This paper extends such a logic so that it can. The base is Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) with Inductive Grounded Arithmetic (IGA)'s least-fixed-point reading and ground induction. It adds a separate greatest-fixed-point former $ν$ with Park's coinduction rule, proves that one former cannot carry both ground induction and coinduction, and adds a dichotomy rule: the classical disjunction between a least-fixed-point atom and the greatest-fixed-point atom of its dual, under a derivable premise that the body's leaves are decided. The systems are sound for an explicit model reading every $ν$-body at its greatest fixed point, hence consistent; they agree with the least model wherever it has a value and prove sentences it leaves without one. The dichotomy replaces the underivable hypothesis that an order is well-founded by the derivable one that its steps are decided; the change of model pays for the move. With ground induction the dichotomy derives the omniscience rule of the sibling arithmetic OGA, so the system has no semantics whose certificates for universals are its own proofs. The systems prove, as single sentences, that every decided tree is well-founded or has an infinite branch given by a term, total in the new model; that random assignment terminates while its divergent twin runs forever; that a fair loop terminates and the alternating-bit protocol delivers every message; that open games are determined; that the termination gap in Nakata and Uustalu's trace semantics closes; and that Cinderella wins the bucket game at capacity three. Isabelle/HOL checks every result.

title: Hopf Algebra of Graphs for Operator Splitting Methods
abstract: Motivated by combinatorial identities arising in the study of operator splitting methods and their description in terms of bipartite rooted trees, we establish a connection between operator splitting methods and the theory of combinatorial Hopf algebras. We show that the inclusion-exclusion expansion of the elementary weight of a rooted tree over its rooted subforests can be interpreted as the antipode of Schmitt's Hopf algebra of graphs. This interpretation recovers known identities for operator splitting and partitioned Runge-Kutta methods from general properties of the antipode. We further show that adjoint operator splitting methods can be described algebraically through the antipode and the canonical involution of the original method. The resulting framework also yields new combinatorial identities and connects the analysis of geometric numerical integrators with the theory of incidence Hopf algebras.

title: A comparison of parallel iterative methods for ILU triangular solves
abstract: Exact triangular solves parallelise poorly, limited by the size and number of the level sets, so on GPUs the factors from incomplete LU (ILU) factorisations are often solved approximately with parallel iterative methods. We compare four such methods: a Jacobi method, an Incomplete Sparse Approximate Inverse (ISAI), GMRES polynomials, and AIRG, a reduction multigrid built on GMRES polynomials, for which we introduce a parallel coarse/fine splitting that bounds the diagonal dominance ratio of the fine-fine block. We test them with ILU(0) and ILU(1) factors of canonical PDE problems and 91 SuiteSparse/Matrix Market matrices, the latter on a single GPU. AIRG is the most robust on the PDE factors, with nearly flat iteration counts under refinement and no per-problem tuning, but has the largest setup and memory costs. GMRES polynomials are more robust than the Jacobi method at a similar cost. As the inner solve of an ILU preconditioner with tuned inner iteration counts, ISAI gives the largest median speedups over a hipSPARSE exact triangular solve (4.5$\times$ and 6.8$\times$ for ILU(0) and ILU(1)), though this was dominated by smaller problems; on the largest ILU(1) problems all four methods give similar median speedups of 2.1-2.6$\times$.

title: Dynamic programming principle for controlled systems driven by fractional Brownian motions and related backward stochastic Riccati equations
abstract: This work aims to study the stochastic optimal control problems of controlled stochastic differential systems driven by both Brownian motions and fractional Brownian motions via dynamic programming principle. The stochastic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation is obtained. Different from the classical case, the obtained stochastic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation is a backward stochastic partial differential equation driven by both fractional Brownian motions and standard Brownian motions, whose solution is a pair of random fields. For linear quadratic optimal control problem this backward stochastic partial differential equation is explicitly solved by relating it to a backward stochastic Riccati equation.

title: A Note on the NP-Hardness on Quadratic Optimization over Doubly Stochastic Matrices and the Gromov-Wasserstein Problem
abstract: The Gromov-Wasserstein problem is an extension of the regular optimal transport problem that is adapted for pairs of distributions residing in incomparable spaces. Broadly speaking, given a pair of metric measure spaces, the Gromov-Wasserstein problem seeks couplings between these spaces that minimize the distortion between the metric evaluations. In this note we record the fact that the Gromov-Wasserstein distance between finite metric spaces is NP-Hard to compute. Our argument relies on a reduction from the Hamiltonian Cycle Problem, and it builds on ideas in Vayer's thesis and Ryner et. al's work that draw connections between the 2-Gromov-Wasserstein and the Quadratic Assignment Problem. During the preparation of this manuscript we learned of the appearance of Breitung et. al's work, whose result essentially supersedes ours. We hope this note serves as a useful companion whose proof is, hopefully, more elementary and easier to understand.

title: Mutual Information Estimation via Triangular Transport Maps: Finite Sample Guarantees and Sample Allocation
abstract: We study finite sample guarantees for transport based mutual information estimation. Mutual information can be estimated by first learning the conditional and marginal densities and then evaluating their log-density ratio by Monte Carlo. Given training samples, we use triangular transport maps to learn these densities and then compute the mutual information estimate on an independent batch of evaluation samples. For conditional density estimation using triangular transport maps, we establish non-asymptotic guarantees over realizable Hölder classes by viewing the conditional density as an ordinary density with respect to the product of the law of the conditioning variable and Lebesgue measure. This allows standard density estimation techniques to be applied directly to the conditional density estimation. These results yield finite sample guarantees for the resulting mutual information estimator and characterize how a fixed sample budget should be allocated between training and evaluation in order to minimize the mean squared error. Numerical experiments support the predicted training and evaluation error rates and illustrate the resulting sample allocation tradeoff.

title: Invariant mean on weakly almost periodic functionals over a Hopf-von Neumann algebra
abstract: Let \(M\) be a Hopf--von Neumann algebra with predual \(M_*\). Using minimal weak*-closed left ideals, we obtain an idempotent state \(\varphi\in\operatorname{WAP}(M_*)^*\) satisfying \(\varphi\star ω\star\varphi=\varphi\) for every state \(ω\) on \(\operatorname{WAP}(M_*)\). This state determines the largest closed introverted subspace \(X_\varphi\subseteq\operatorname{WAP}(M_*)\) containing the identity and admitting a two-sided invariant mean. We also characterize the existence of a unique two-sided invariant mean on introverted operator systems in \(\operatorname{WAP}(M_*)\) by a symmetry condition on their left and right state orbits. The criterion recovers the classical results for locally compact groups and their Fourier algebras, and gives a unified treatment of cocommutative Hopf--von Neumann algebras, compact quantum groups, unital \(C^*\)-Eberlein algebras, and \(\operatorname{WAP}(M(G))\) for every locally compact group \(G\).

title: Coisotropy-one homogeneous spacetimes I: (3,2)-Kinematical Lie algebras with $d\geq 3$
abstract: This is the first of several papers devoted to the classification of coisotropy-one homogeneous spacetimes. It is the first step in extending the classification of spatially isotropic homogeneous spacetimes of kinematical Lie groups to the much vaster context of homogeneous spacetimes that are not spatially isotropic; that is, where the rotations no longer act transitively on the space of directions in each tangent space. In this first paper we classify (up to isomorphisms preserving the rotational subalgebra) a class of the relevant transitive Lie algebras, the so-called (3,2)-kinematical Lie algebras, for the coisotropy-one case in spatial dimension at least 4. As a by-product of this classification, we classify two-dimensional real representations of Bianchi Lie algebras up to a suitable notion of equivalence.

title: Comments on "Multidimensional Costas Arrays and Their Periodicity"
abstract: Rubio and Torres conjectured that a multidimensional Costas array, defined by a bijection between two boxes of integer points whose domain has at least as many dimensions as its image, can stay Costas in every window of its periodic extension only if its order is a power of two fixed by the dimension of the domain. We give a four-dimensional periodic Costas array of order $6$, with a two-dimensional domain and a two-dimensional image, so the conjecture is false. The verification reduces to $36$ windows. It has been confirmed by computer and in the Lean proof assistant. The array also meets with equality the pigeonhole bound that Rubio and Torres use for their non-existence results, so that bound is tight.

title: Energy-Efficient UAV Covert Communications via Metaheuristic Optimization
abstract: Wireless communication systems increasingly require not only confidentiality but also transmission undetectability, motivating covert communications. This paper studies an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) enabled covert communication system where a UAV serves a legitimate receiver in the presence of multiple active and colluding wardens with imperfect location information. We maximize covert energy efficiency (CEE) by jointly optimizing the UAV's 3D trajectory and transmit power while accounting for energy. To address the resulting non-convex problem with robust covertness constraints, we develop Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO)-based metaheuristic algorithms and compare them with a Block Coordinate Descent with Successive Convex Approximation (BCD-SCA) benchmark. Numerical results show that the proposed methods improve CEE while satisfying covertness constraints.

title: HideOut - User Protection Against Localization with Throughput Guarantees in Mobile Networks
abstract: Channel state information (CSI) in cellular networks is primarily used to maintain quality of service (QoS), yet it leaks privacy-sensitive information, in particular the user equipment's (UE) location. CSI is reported in plaintext on a publicly available schedule; thus, capturing it on the air and using a well trained AI model to localize the UE is straightforward. This simplicity in the attack execution makes it a serious privacy vulnerability. Using conventional privacy enhancing techniques, such as additive perturbation from differential privacy, to protect location data can potentially degrade the downlink communication quality. We present HideOut, a client-side defense mechanism that preserves the user's location from neural-based localization methods, while maintaining their downlink Spectral Efficiency (SE). Unlike generic adversarial attacks, HideOut treats downlink SE as a strict constraint in an optimization setting. Under maximum ratio transmission (MRT) beamforming, we show that a user-selected SE loss budget can be converted into an angular rate-feasible constraint on the reported channel vector. HideOut then performs gradient-based localization obfuscation while projecting each update onto this rate-feasible set. We evaluate HideOut against four CSI-based localization architectures under both white-box and black-box assumptions. Across models, HideOut increases localization ambiguity (error) from approximately $1--2$ m to $72--85$ m while keeping downlink SE loss within a $1\%$ budget. These results show that CSI-based localization can be substantially degraded at negligible communication quality loss when adversarial perturbations are made aware of the wireless link.

title: A Counterexample to the Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa Conjecture
abstract: We provide a counterexample to the non-abelian Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa conjecture. The construction comes from an equivalent maximal-coupling entropy inequality, for which a counterexample can be found in a lower-dimensional group. We give an explicit cardinality counterexample in $D_4^{14}$, the fourteenth direct power of the dihedral group of order $8$.

title: Analog and hybrid computing in the 21st century
abstract: Analog computers solve problems through physical representations of mathematical variables and relations, often using the dynamics of electronic circuits and their associated signals. Many analog computers directly represent nonlinear dynamical systems; they encode their solutions in the signals that they generate. Although most modern scientific computing relies on digital architectures with inherently discrete-valued representations and algorithmic approaches, the design constraints of such architectures increasingly limit both performance and energy efficiency. Analog systems can circumvent some of these constraints; they execute specific computations very efficiently by mapping them directly onto physical processes using smaller and simpler computing elements than the ones in digital architectures. In this article, we provide an interdisciplinary perspective on modern analog and hybrid (i.e., analog-digital) computing. We discuss how modern scientific computing workflows can leverage analog approaches in various applications, such as in simulating dynamical systems, performing optimization, and enabling more energy-efficient implementations of artificial intelligence.

title: Completing the classification of Hopf superalgebras of dimension up to 10
abstract: We introduce a family of semisimple Hopf superalgebras obtained from abelian extensions. Using this family and bosonization, we complete the classification of Hopf superalgebras of dimension up to 10 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We also determine the duals of the semisimple classes with nonzero odd part and give tables of the complete classification.

title: Multivariate diagonal harmonics: character polynomials and proofs of two conjectures of Bergeron
abstract:
We prove Bergeron's Hook-Components and Coefficient-Length conjectures for the Vandermonde polarization module and full diagonal harmonics in every rank and number of alphabets. Hook-label characters are elementary skewings of the alternating character, and the maximal Schur length in label $μ$ is $n-μ_1$. We compute character and dimension polynomials of diagonal coinvariants in every bosonic--fermionic superspace for $D\ge3$, $n\ge\max\{D,2D-6\}$, answering Church--Ellenberg--Farb's character and dimension questions.
  For augmented commutative algebras in characteristic zero, we construct natural two-Schur presentations and filtered free resolutions with one Schur generator in each homological degree. For polynomial algebras, specialization to orthogonal idempotents identifies the first unstable correction for every nonempty tail $τ$ and degree $D>|τ|$. The stable threshold $n\ge D+τ_1$ is sharp when the row dimension is at least $\ell(τ)$. First parabolic algebras recover finite jets, their multiplication and their maps.
  Selected-label lifts give uniform Vandermonde generation through degree $D$ for $D\ge3$, $n\ge2D-3$, and disjoint-label products generate every first occurrence for positive integral row weights. Constructive degree reflection determines all two-column moment homology and generates its first syzygies from degree $n+1$; two-column Vandermonde generation reduces to degree $n-1$. Invariants and harmonics separate through the character range and through degree $n$ in two alphabets. The hook identities also give the fully graded sign component of the $t=0$, $(1,2)$-superspace Theta conjecture.

title: Total dominating sets and four-colorings of planar triangulations
abstract:
In 2018, Goddard and Henning conjectured that every planar triangulation on at least four vertices has two disjoint total dominating sets. It was proved by Francis, Illickan, Jose, and Rajendraprasad in 2024. As a strengthening of this result, Goddard and Henning also conjectured that every planar triangulation with at least four vertices has a proper $4$-coloring with color classes $C_1,C_2,C_3,C_4$ such that $C_1\cup C_2$ and $C_3\cup C_4$ are total dominating sets. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture: for every $n\ge 36$ there is a planar triangulation with $n$ vertices without such a coloring.
  As another strengthening of the result by Francis, Illickan, Jose, and Rajendraprasad, they conjectured that every near-triangulation has a $4$-coloring, not necessarily proper, in which every vertex $v$ sees at least $\min \{ \operatorname{deg}(v),3 \}$ colors on its neighbors. We prove this conjecture for all planar triangulations.

title: Unconditional optimal convergence of a relaxation Crank-Nicolson difference scheme for 2D space-fractional NLS
abstract: In this paper, we develop a linearly implicit relaxation Crank-Nicolson difference scheme for the two-dimensional space-fractional nonlinear Schrödinger (SFNS) equation, where the fractional Laplacian is approximated by a simple fractional central difference scheme. The proposed scheme is uniquely solvable and conserves discrete mass for general real-valued nonlinear coefficients, and a modified discrete energy in the cubic case. By introducing a modified error system employing a cut-off technique, we establish the optimal-order error estimates without mesh-ratio restriction. Specifically, the primary variable achieves second-order temporal and spatial convergence in the discrete $H_h^{α/2}$-norm, and the relaxation variable satisfies the same convergence in the discrete $L^2$-norm. Some numerical experiments confirm the relevant theoretical results.

title: A new perspective on Riemann surfaces and von Neumann algebras via thin Blaschke products
abstract:
In 2014, K.Guo and the second author constructed the first example of an infinite Blaschke product
  $B$ (a thin Blaschke product), for which the associated multiplication operator $M_B$ is irreducible
  on the Bergman space $L_a^2(\mathbb{D})$ over the unit disk $\mathbb D$. We take a substantial step forward toward characterizing
  the irreducibility of the operator $M_B$ on
  $L_a^2(\mathbb{D})$, or equivalently, the trivialness of the von Neumann algebra
  $\{M_B,M_B^*\}'$. This characterization indicates a close connection with the primeness of $B$ and with
  the two-component property of the Riemann surface $\mathcal{S}_B$ associated with $B$. The approach is built upon
  a nested family of connected components of the sublevel set
  $\{z\in \mathbb{D}:|B(z)|<t\}$ for $0<t<1$, which captures the function-theoretic and geometric feature of $B$.

title: A Clustered Equivalent-Source Method with Local Response Compression and Group-Symmetry Reduction for Antenna-Array Analysis
abstract: Full-wave analysis of finite antenna arrays is computationally demanding because detailed element responses must be resolved and coupled across the entire array. To reduce this cost, this paper presents a clustered equivalent-source method that combines local response compression with group-symmetry reduction. Local responses are represented in compressed equivalent-surface bases or coordinates inherited from child clusters. Symmetry constraints associated with the cluster partition and excitation reduce the coupled system, while the corresponding group transformations recover the complete response in the retained coordinates. To assess overall efficiency, we evaluate the costs of local construction, propagation, global solution, and recovery. Numerical examples involving layered and finite annular patch arrays show close agreement between the computed and reference complex far fields and shorter complete-run times than those of the corresponding symmetry-reduced direct solvers. Among the three equivalent-source implementations for the layered array, the one with the smallest coupled system has the longest runtime because local construction and propagation dominate the cost. These findings highlight the need to consider local construction and coupling costs when assessing the benefit of reducing the global system dimension.

title: Consumption and Investment with Multiple Job-Switching Opportunities
abstract: We study finite-horizon optimal switching with affine rewards in a consumption-investment model with finitely many occupational regimes. Directed shortest-path costs yield the exact natural borrowing limit. A dual transformation reduces the control problem to a one-dimensional system of variational inequalities with interconnected obstacles. Convexity and a distributional waiting inequality give local spatial $C^{1,1}$ regularity and smooth fit, including destination ties. These estimates establish strong duality and recover optimal consumption, investment, and switching strategies. A reflected backward stochastic differential equation representation yields a set-based integral formula without prescribed boundary geometry. Every connected component of the spatially regular locus is a maximal smooth graph over time. Exact examples exhibit disconnected contact sets, temporal boundaries under strict triangle costs, and a corner in an individual boundary component under additive route costs. A convergent time discretisation completes the analysis.

title: A Telescopic Method with Guaranteed B-Stationarity for Partitioned Cardinality and Complementarity Constraints
abstract: We consider the minimization of a smooth function subject to box constraints and partitioned cardinality constraints (PCC): the variables are divided into groups and, within each group, at most a prescribed number of variables may be non-zero. This class contains bound-constrained minimization, cardinality-constrained minimization and bound-constrained mathematical programs with complementarity constraints. We introduce the Telescopic Method, which alternates iterations of a bound-constrained method on the faces of the feasible set with inexpensive one-dimensional "escaping" tests that exchange a variable of the current face by a currently null one within the same group. We prove, without constraint qualifications and without requiring global solutions of subproblems, that every limit point of the generated sequence is B-stationary, i.e., it satisfies the first-order condition defined by the tangent cone of the feasible set. This guarantee is obtained with exchanges of a single variable, whatever the number of non-null entries of the limit point, because B-stationarity for this class of problems decomposes into conditions on single variables. On the 60 bound-constrained mathematical programs with complementarity constraints of the test set of Kirches, Larson, Leyffer and Manns, the method found approximately B-stationary points in all the problems. Applications to separable regression, sparse polynomial approximation and portfolio selection are described and tested numerically.

title: The covering radius of the first-order Reed-Muller code in nine variables is 242
abstract: We prove that the covering radius of the binary first-order Reed-Muller code RM(1,9) is exactly 242. Equivalently, the maximum nonlinearity of a Boolean function in nine variables is 242. Our proof combines a one-point rigidity theorem with a spectral and computational exclusion of the two larger candidate nonlinearities. We first show that every nine-variable Boolean function of nonlinearity 243 admits a unique one-point modification that raises its nonlinearity to 244: the point to be changed is the vector sum of its support. This part uses exact Walsh-update identities, integer interpolation, rigidity of a quadratic residue, and a sharp Walsh l1 estimate for cubic Boolean functions. To exclude nonlinearity 244, we use Parseval's identity and congruences of integral Walsh coefficients to force an exceptionally restricted spectrum. An associated cubic residue phase must attain the extremal Walsh l1 bound 10240. We eliminate one equality spectrum by hyperplane slicing; the other forces the original Boolean function from the signs of the cubic phase and yields a double-complement-pairing identity for its cubic top part. The classification of alternating trilinear forms over F2, an exact filter of their representatives, and two exhaustive enumerations of 218 quadratic supplements then rule out every remaining candidate. Together with the known construction attaining nonlinearity 242, these arguments establish the asserted covering radius.

title: Continuous, locally Lipschitz and Lipschitz selections for intuitionistic fuzzy sets, with applications to expert voting
abstract: This paper studies continuous selections in the framework of intuitionistic fuzzy sets. To each intuitionistic fuzzy set $A=(μ,ν)$ on a topological space $X$ we associate the interval-valued map $F_{A}(x)=[μ(x),1-ν(x)]$, whose width is the hesitation degree. Hence, in this setting, a selection of $F_{A}$ is an ordinary fuzzy membership function compatible with the intuitionistic information, and every selection is the membership function of Atanassov's operator $D_{\vartheta}$ for a suitable pointwise parameter $\vartheta$. When $X$ is normal and $μ$, $ν$ are upper semi-continuous, a continuous selection exists by the Katětov--Tong insertion theorem. We show that upper semi-continuity arises naturally in a voting model, in which a panel of experts divides a metric universe into closed regions of acceptance and rejection, and for this model we construct an explicit continuous selection, the consensus selection, illustrated by a non-compact example in the plane. On metric spaces we characterise the intuitionistic fuzzy sets that admit an $L$-Lipschitz selection through a non-local version of the condition $μ+ν\leq 1$, and we give the largest and the smallest such selections in closed form. Finally, we prove that the set of continuous selections depends in a $1$-Lipschitz way on the intuitionistic fuzzy set, with respect to the Hausdorff-type distance of Grzegorzewski. We also characterise the intuitionistic fuzzy sets admitting locally Lipschitz selections.

title: SAWs, trails, kites, patterns
abstract: A self-avoiding walk (SAW) on a vertex-transitive graph $G$ is a path that visits no vertex more than once; a trail is a path that traverses no edge more than once. The number of $n$-step self-avoiding walks (respectively, trails) starting at a given vertex has order $μ(G)^n$ (respectively, $μ_{\text{T}}(G)^n$), where $μ(G)$ is called the connective constant and $μ_{\text{T}}(G)$ is the trail constant. It is immediate that $μ=μ_{\text{T}}$ if $G$ either has degree $3$ or less, or is a tree. We prove a necessary and sufficient condition for the strict inequality $μ< μ_{\text{T}}$ if $G$ has degree $4$ or more and is not a tree, and in addition $G$ possesses a so-called height function. This condition is satisfied whenever the height function is transitive. The core of the proof is a pattern theorem for graphs possessing height functions, and this is achieved using an unpublished argument for ${\Bbb Z}^d$ by Hammersley, reported by Janse van Rensburg et al. (J. Stat. Phys. 85, 1996, 103--130). Some ancillary results are included concerning SAWs on the line graph of $G$.

title: Agent4FreeFem: A Verification-Guided Framework for Autonomous Topology Optimization
abstract: Topology optimization has become an indispensable design tool in the aerospace, automotive, and mechanical engineering industries. Yet bringing a new problem from its description to an optimized result remains slow, expert-dependent, and unreliable: the workflow spans many manually connected stages, each new problem requires solver code to be written and debugged manually, and such code often fails or yields incorrect results. We present Agent4FreeFem, a pipeline driven by a large language model that turns a natural-language problem description into a set of verified optimization results without manual solver-code development or debugging. The pipeline keeps the problem definition unmodified, localizes errors using independent sources of evidence, and completes constrained repairs automatically, thereby providing efficient end-to-end automation, autonomous execution, and verifiable results. We evaluated Agent4FreeFem on a suite of single-physics and coupled multiphysics problems. Every case passed runtime verification and finished within the repair budget of each stage.

title: A Second-Order Stochastic Dynamic Mode Decomposition by Richardson Extrapolation
abstract: Stochastic dynamic mode decomposition (SDMD) approximates the Koopman semigroup of an Itô diffusion by a Galerkin generator matrix on a dictionary of observables, computed from samples of the invariant law and evaluations of the generator, and advances observables with a first-order stochastic Taylor step (SDMD-1). The second-order Taylor step (SDMD-2) also needs the matrix of second generator actions, hence a dictionary with four derivatives, evaluations of a fourth-order differential operator at every sample, and a third matrix. We show that the Richardson extrapolation of two SDMD-1 half steps (SDMD-R) is second-order accurate with the data, the matrices, and the regularity of SDMD-1. One error bound covers exact and empirical Galerkin matrices. It consists of the Galerkin error of the dictionary, which is common to all schemes, a time-stepping term, and a data term of order $m^{-1/2}$ in the sample size $m$. The time-stepping term is $O(\dt^2)$ for SDMD-R and $O(Θ_N\dt+\dt^2)$ for SDMD-2, where $Θ_N$ is the norm of the second-order Galerkin residual $\Proj_N\cA(I-\Proj_N)\cA|_{\cV_N}$. The first-order term is attained and, for self-adjoint generators, vanishes only for generator-invariant dictionaries. For reversible periodic diffusions and trigonometric dictionaries with cutoff $K$, the step restriction $\dt\lesssim K^{-2}$ makes all three schemes contractions, and the error against the Koopman semigroup on $H^\ell$ observables is $O(K^{-(\ell-2)}+\dt^p)$ plus a sampling term of order $K^{d+2}m^{-1/2}$ in dimension $d$, with $p=1$ for SDMD-1 and $p=2$ for SDMD-R and SDMD-2. Numerical experiments confirm that SDMD-R matches or improves on the accuracy of SDMD-2 at the cost of SDMD-1.

title: A proof of the Zariski closure conjecture and quasi-Frobenius exponential algebras
abstract: Let $G=\exp(\g)$ be an exponential solvable Lie group, $π\in\widehat G$, and $Ω_π$ the coadjoint orbit attached to $π$ by the orbit method. The Zariski closure conjecture asserts that the Poisson characteristic variety $\VA(π_ν)$ of the deformed representation coincides with the Zariski closure of $Ω_π$ in $\g^*$. Known until now only in special situations, including the nilpotent case, it is proved here in full generality. Since the Hilbert space of $π$ is a quantization of the symplectic manifold $Ω_π$, the statement says that the passage back from the representation to the orbit, a dequantization, loses nothing: the orbit is recovered, up to Zariski closure, from the algebra alone. We also characterize the quasi-Frobenius exponential Lie algebras, those whose dual vector space is a Zariski-dense coadjoint orbit, through the triviality of the annihilator of an irreducible representation.

title: On the Local Regularity of Homogeneous Complex Monge-Ampère Equations
abstract:
We establish a local higher regularity theorem for the homogeneous complex Monge-Ampere equation on $X\times D$, where $X$ is a complete, possibly noncompact Kahler manifold and $D\subset\mathbb C$ is the unit disc. For a bounded weak solution given by the Perron envelope, we prove higher regularity on a smaller spatial domain when the smooth boundary data are locally small. The geometric hypotheses require uniformly convex local Kahler potentials and a local barrier threshold sufficiently large relative to the global $L^\infty$ bound of the solution. We also obtain quantitative local Holder estimates.
  The proof combines a perturbative construction of local holomorphic disc foliations with a construction of global subsolutions using convexity and barriers. A key analytic difficulty is the loss of Holder regularity in the construction of holomorphic disc families, which we address using BMO estimates and Nash-Moser-Zehnder theorems. Comparison along the discs identifies the local smooth solution by holomorphic discs foliation with the global weak solution.
  We apply the theorem and its proof to compact Kahler manifolds and to ALE, ALF, and asymptotically complex hyperbolic (ACH) ends. Under the stated geometric and decay assumptions, we obtain higher regularity of each prescribed order sufficiently far out, together with weighted Holder estimates preserving the boundary decay.

title: Spatial Token Interleaving and Two-Pass BP Decoding for Semantic Image Transmission
abstract: Semantic error control coding (SECC) can correct the residual errors of a standard channel code with a foundation model that supplies a prior on the source content, but existing SECC schemes are designed for text. In this paper, we develop SECC for image transmission with spatial token interleaving and a two-pass belief propagation (BP) schedule. At the transmitter, a vector-quantized (VQ) tokenizer converts an image into tokens, which are transmitted in multiple low-density parity-check (LDPC) code blocks of fifth-generation New Radio (5G NR). In raster order, a block that BP fails to decode corrupts consecutive token rows, so the interleaver reorders the tokens such that adjacent tokens are carried by different blocks, without additional transmitted bits. At the receiver, after the first BP pass, token recovery fuses the token probabilities given by BP with the predictions of the autoregressive model Emu3-Gen, and the second BP pass decodes each block again with the fused distributions as priors on the information bits. On Kodak24 at 0.5 channel uses per pixel and a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 0.15 dB, the second pass removes 92% of the token errors left by token recovery, and interleaving reduces the final token error rate by 88%. At medium to high SNR, the proposed receiver exceeds deep joint source--channel coding baselines with the same channel uses by at least 1.2 dB in peak signal-to-noise ratio.

title: Equal Hamming Weights at Fixed Root Order and Applications to Constacyclic MDS Codes
abstract: For a fixed positive integer $n>1$, we study the prime powers $q$ coprime to $n$ for which all monic irreducible factors of $Φ_n$ over $\F_q$ have the same coefficient Hamming weight. Cyclotomic orbit coefficients give a finite, effective classification of these fields. Outside finitely many computable characteristics, every factor has the support of its characteristic-zero orbit polynomial; the uniform condition $p>2^{\varphi(n)}$ suffices. In each remaining characteristic, extension exponents reduce to divisors of $\ord_n(p)$, and an integer variance identity expressed by polynomial gcd degrees decides equal weight. The same coefficient data determine the full weight distribution. As an application, we prove that an MDS constacyclic code with an irreducible generator forces every irreducible polynomial of the same root order to have full support, including factors associated with different constacyclic constants. This yields a uniform gcd and norm obstruction. We develop its short-multiplier extension, give a prime-order cubic family, and establish an explicit quadratic-residue exclusion without a prime-square alphabet or a near-square length hypothesis.

title: $K_h$-Minor-Free Graphs Have Balanced Separators of Size $O(h\sqrt{n})$
abstract: We show that every $K_h$-minor-free graph with $n$ vertices has a balanced separator of size $O(h\sqrt{n})$ for any parameter $h \in \mathbb{N}$, resolving the conjecture posed by Alon, Seymour, and Thomas [AST90] in 1990. The proof is elementary, building on the combinatorial framework by Le [Le26]. A key new idea of the proof is the existence of a short hitting walk on vertex expanders: given $k$ large (not necessarily disjoint) subsets of vertices, there is a walk of length $O(k/ψ(G))$ hitting every subset, where $ψ(G)$ is the vertex expansion. This technical result substantially improves on an analogous lemma by Alon, Seymour, and Thomas [AST90] in an important parameter setting, where the previous lower bound [Kot00] does not apply.

title: CLT for the Weight of the Minimum Spanning Arborescence on the Complete Directed Graph
abstract: The minimum spanning arborescence (MSA) with a fixed boundary, defined on weighted directed graphs, is the directed analogue of the minimum spanning tree (MST). The behaviour of the MSA has been of recent interest and is known to be quite different from that of its undirected counterpart. On the complete directed graph, and for edge weights given by i.i.d. random variables with a broad class of distributions, we prove a Central Limit Theorem for the weight of the MSA with appropriate scaling. While the scaling for the CLT is similar to MST case explored by Janson, the centering required ($1$ as opposed to $ζ(3)$ for Uniform$[0,1]$ weights) and the limiting variance of the Gaussian ($1$ as opposed to $6ζ(4)-4ζ(3)$ for Uniform$[0,1]$ weights) are notably different.

title: Lorentzian entropy, subgaussian matrix concentration, and sharp functional inequalities for all matroids
abstract:
We prove complete entropy contraction for homogeneous Lorentzian laws and derive subgaussian matrix concentration and sharp functional inequalities for every matroid. Uniform retention of $\ell$ out of $r$ particles contracts matrix entropy by the optimal universal factor $\ell/r$, in every finite matrix dimension and positive field, including repeated labels. The matrix Laplace comparison retains matrix variance and arbitrary Hermitian offsets. It gives subgaussian bounds for arbitrary Hermitian observables with bounded exchange differences, and Chernoff and Bernstein bounds for basis sums.
  Every unit-edge matroid basis graph satisfies the cube's small-set and Gross inequalities, with equality classified and optimal universal complete entropy-decay rate four. Its spectrum lies in $\{0,2\}\cup[3,\infty)$, with binary direct-factor contrasts spanning the eigenspace at two. We classify extremal down-up eigenfunctions, resolving Alaniz Pintos's degree-one conjecture and the equality problem for the Feder--Mihail walk.
  For degree at least two, every matrix entropy extremizer extends uniquely from its two-particle marginal. Equality depends only on the normalized pair law, with noncommutativity confined to mutually exclusive labels. We classify power-entropy extremizers for $1<p<2$ and give a fourth-order criterion for affine equality. Retained-level Gibbs reconstruction has sharp dimension-independent stability. For multiaffine laws whose generating polynomial and complement are Lorentzian, we determine the exact simultaneous all-field quantum marginal and matrix Hölder regions and classify the sharp half-marginal fields. Connected sharp laws are determinantal through rank three; stable nondeterminantal examples exist in every higher rank.

title: Fibre factorization and automorphisms of direct products of bipartite graphs
abstract: We determine the automorphism groups of direct products of finite connected twin-free bipartite graphs whose factors are different from $K_2$. The product is generally disconnected, so the problem requires both the automorphism groups of its components and a criterion for component isomorphism. We retain the order of the bipartition classes and use the fibre product over $K_2$. An edge-relation construction, together with McKenzie's strict refinement theorem, yields unique fibre-prime factorization and a coordinate description of every specified isomorphism. After refining the original factors, component isomorphism classes are described by intersections of factor-symmetry orbits with a set of admissible labels. The stabilizer of a label acts faithfully as the fullautomorphism group of its component. These data determine the full automorphism group, including products with repeated or fibre-composite factors. For products of fibre powers of one prime graph, we compute the component groups and express their multiplicities through a subset-sum polynomial. We also obtain an explicit semidirect product for a mixed product with one nonbipartite factor and explain its relation to known stability results. An application recovers the known double-cover groups of bipartite generalized Petersen graphs.

title: A complete classification for n-species Lotka-Volterra stably dissipative systems based on a generalized AHU algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a generalized AHU algorithm based on tree isomorphism theory and applies it to the complete classification of n-dimensional stably dissipative Lotka-Volterra systems.

title: Martingalized U-statistics-based sequential inference: a blessing of degeneracy
abstract: Degenerate degree-two U-statistics have non-Gaussian limits, making sequential inference substantially more difficult than in the nondegenerate case. However, row normalization preserves the target parameter and makes the centered numerator a martingale on a harmonic variance clock, at the cost of logarithmic variance inflation. We establish a strong Gaussian approximation for this process and consistently estimate its variance through online updates, allowing spectrum-free calibration. Combining this strong approximation with Gaussian-mixture (GM) and stitched law-of-the-iterated-logarithm (LIL) boundaries yields confidence sequences with asymptotic time-uniform coverage and corresponding sequential tests for null hypotheses under which the kernel is degenerate. We further extend the framework to multi-dimensional vector-valued kernels, yielding Mahalanobis confidence ellipsoids based on consistent covariance estimation. Numerical experiments illustrate sequential type-I error control and favorable detection power in two-sample and independence testing against spectral baselines, and in three-sample homogeneity testing using vector confidence ellipsoids.

title: Free energy of 2-spin spherical vector spin glasses
abstract: We compute the limit of free energy of 2-spin spherical vector spin glasses with possibly non-convex interaction and couplings satisfying a finite fourth-moment assumption. The couplings need not be Gaussian. The limit is given by a logarithmic-determinant variational formula, equivalently by a finite-dimensional matrix Dyson equation, and its zero-temperature limit yields the ground-state energy. The limiting formulas depend only on the covariance of the couplings. We also study fluctuations: at an interior minimizer, an explicit variance bound transfers the limiting law of a logarithmic linear statistic to the free energy. For Gaussian couplings, this yields Gaussian fluctuations. At a boundary minimizer, assuming a simple regular edge with GOE Tracy-Widom fluctuations and a one-edge reduction, we transfer the edge fluctuations to the free energy.

title: Maximum principle for discrete-time stochastic recursive games driven by fractional noises
abstract: This paper investigates discrete-time stochastic recursive games driven by fractional noises, in which the cost functional is defined through a backward stochastic difference equation. By introducing discrete-time adjoint equations, we establish a maximum principle and the verification theorem for open-loop Nash equilibria in non-zero sum and zero sum stochastic recursive game problems. The effectiveness of our theorem is demonstrated through applications to two different linear-quadratic stochastic recursive games and a portfolio selection problem with a recursive utility functional.

title: Partition statistics and universal mixed mock modular forms
abstract: In this note, we construct combinatorial statistics in terms of partitions, overpartitions, and two-color partitions and relate the corresponding generating functions to the universal mock theta functions. Our framework primarily builds on two $q$-series identities of Fine.

title: Forgetting matters: when subspace optimization accelerates without the strong convexity parameter
abstract: Sequential subspace optimization (SESOP) minimizes the objective exactly over a few directions built from past iterates. It needs no problem constants, is accelerated on smooth convex functions and behaves like an accelerated method in experiments. This led to the conjecture that it is accelerated in the strongly convex case without knowing the strong convexity parameter. We show that the conjecture fails in the worst case. For every subspace method whose memory forgets slowly, namely a window of recent gradients and steps together with cumulative sums with subexponential weights, we construct a counterexample: acceleration requires a window of length of order $\sqrtκ$, where $κ$ is the condition number. SESOP and the plane form of conjugate gradients are therefore not accelerated. Memories that forget fast avoid this obstruction. Pairs of geometric filters give accelerated methods with logarithmic memory or only two stored vectors. They need neither the strong convexity parameter nor the smoothness constant, never restart the iterate and restart their memory at most $O(\logκ)$ times. Finally, the method with fixed activation times remains asymptotically accelerated on functions with Lipschitz Hessian even when each subproblem is solved by a single Newton step.

title: Sharp digirth bounds for C(k,k)-subdivisions in digraphs
abstract: For an integer $k\ge2$, let $C(k,k)$ denote the oriented cycle formed by two internally vertex-disjoint directed paths of length $k$ with the same initial and terminal vertices. We extend a problem of Picasarri-Arrieta and Rambaud [European J. Combin. 122 (2024)] on subdivisions of $C(k,k)$ to digraphs with several vertices of out-degree one. Following the sharp result of Chen et al. [arXiv:2610.38574v1 (2026)] for at most one such vertex, we determine the exact digirth threshold when at most $r\ge4$ such vertices are permitted. Specifically, for all integers $k\ge2$ and $r\ge4$, every digraph of minimum out-degree at least one, with at most $r$ vertices of out-degree one and digirth at least $r(k-1)+1$, contains a subdivision of $C(k,k)$.

title: Cutoff for Simple Random Walk on Preferential Attachment Graphs
Cube-freeness and a square formula for canonical trace ideals of Stanley--Reisner rings
abstract: Let $I$ be a monomial ideal in $S=\mathbb{k}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, and set $R=S/I$. We prove that if $I$ is $\mathbf{a}$-bounded and $M$ is a positively $\mathbf{b}$-determined $R$-module, then $\mathrm{tr}_R(M)$ is $(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b})$-bounded. For the canonical module, this gives the bound $2\mathbf{a}$. In particular, the canonical trace ideal of every Stanley--Reisner ring is a cube-free monomial ideal. We also prove that, for a Stanley--Reisner ring satisfying $(S_2)$, the canonical trace ideal is the square of its radical if and only if the ring satisfies $(G_2)$.

title: Latin cubes of order $4$ and $4320$-point quaternionic constructions in ${\mathbb R}^{16}$
abstract:
Possibly the most enduring lower-bound record for kissing numbers in dimensions greater than $8$ (excluding $24$) is $$ κ_{16}\geq 4320. $$ This lower bound is attained by a shell of the famous Barnes--Wall lattice, which was discovered in 1959. Besides this configuration, at least one alternative $4320$-point kissing arrangement is currently known.
  Recently, it was noticed that all these configurations can be described in terms of the so-called quaternionic construction, a general type of construction that was instrumental in explaining the geometry of the $841$-point kissing arrangement in ${\mathbb R}^{12}$.
  We give a simple generalization of quaternionic constructions in ${\mathbb R}^{16}$ obtained from record configurations. They are parameterized by three Latin cubes of order $4$, six permutations of $3$-element set, and are all infinitesimally jammed. Computer-aided counting shows that there are $4\,072\,728\,621$ isometry classes in this family of $4320$-point kissing arrangements.

title: Distances in the collinearity graphs of geometries related to simplex codes
abstract: Let $\cS(k,q)$ be the point-line geometry whose points and lines correspond to one-dimensional and two-dimensional subcodes of $q$-ary simplex codes of dimension $k$, respectively. We determine the complete distance relation and the diameter of its collinearity graph. For two points whose representing vectors have different sets of zero coordinates there is a common neighbour. If the representing vectors have the same zero set, then a common neighbour exists precisely when $(q-1)q^{k-2}$ of their non-zero coordinate ratios can be selected so that their product is one. To prove this, we use a generalization of Hall's result for finite abelian groups. Applying the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv theorem, we establish that the above product condition holds for $k\ge3$, which implies that the diameter is two. If $k=2$, then the diameter is one when $q=2$, two when $q=3$ and three when $q\ge4$.

title: From MHV Gravity Amplitudes and Hodges map to Pentad Varieties
abstract: We study some geometric aspects behind the Hodges matrix appearing in the context of scattering amplitudes for the $\mathcal N=8$ supergravity. Through a vector bundle construction, we show that the Hodges matrix gives rise to a canonical rational map from the two-step flag variety to symmetric matrices, called the $\textit{Hodges map}$. This construction allows to define the amplitude geometrically: its vanishing locus is a divisor - the $\textit{MHV gravity divisor}$. Inspired by the Hodges map, we introduce the notion of Hadamard ratio of two varieties. In the case relevant to gravity, this is the ratio of two Grassmannians, which we call the $\textit{pentad variety}$, connecting it to the pentad constraint from algebraic statistics. Moreover, we show that the pentad variety is closely related to the combinatorial algebraic geometry of Martin's affine slope variety, and the phirotopes of Below, Krummeck, and Richter-Gebert.

title: Power Concavity and Log-Concavity for Large-Parameter Robin 2-Hessian Problems
Efficient second-order physics-preserving schemes for incompressible flows with variable density and viscosity
abstract: This paper proposes a novel second-order prediction--filter--projection framework for incompressible flows with variable density and viscosity. In this framework, a constrained $L^2$-projection is enforced to unconditionally preserve the prescribed density bounds and discrete mass conservation, while a generalized-Laplacian reformulation combined with the D-CSAV approach is used to discretize the variable-viscosity momentum equation. In particular, a density-weighted second-order time filter is proposed, which eliminates the additional uniform-in-time bound restriction imposed on the time difference quotient of the discrete density in existing stability analyses. The resulting scheme is shown to satisfy an unconditional modified-energy dissipation law, without the viscosity-related restrictions imposed in earlier work. Then, an additional scalar auxiliary variable and its compatible temporal discretization are introduced to construct a variable-step prediction--filter--projection scheme. This scheme is also bound-preserving and mass-conserving, and satisfies an unconditional modified-energy dissipation law. Moreover, the modified energy is much closer to the ``original'' kinetic energy, differing from it only through the auxiliary-variable corrections. Based on the variable-step scheme, a reliable energy-based adaptive time-stepping strategy is developed. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy, physics-preserving properties, and efficiency of the proposed schemes.

title: Spectral Theory and Continuum Norm Resolvent Convergence of a One-Sided Discrete Dirac-Type Operator
abstract: We investigate a one-dimensional discrete Dirac-type operator $D_d$ acting on the Hilbert space $\big(\ell^2(\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C})\big)^2$, obtained from the classical continuous free Dirac operator by replacing the spatial derivative with the one-sided backward difference operator $I - S_1$, where $S_1$ denotes the right shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C})$. We establish the fundamental operator-theoretic and spectral properties of $D_d$: unlike symmetric or supersymmetric lattice discretizations, $D_d$ is bounded and non-normal for every non-zero rest mass $m > 0$, with self-commutator $[D_d, D_d^†] = -2mc^3(-Δ_{\mathrm{disc}})σ_2$, yet it is quadratically normal. We compute the exact operator norm, determine the exact spectral radius in two mass regimes, and show via Fourier--Laurent analysis that the spectrum $σ(D_d)$ is purely continuous and lies on a two-component algebraic curve in the complex plane undergoing a topological transition at $mc^2 = 2c$. Finally, introducing a lattice spacing $h > 0$ and embedding $\big(\ell^2(h\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C})\big)^2$ isometrically into $\big(L^2(\mathbb{R};\mathbb{C})\big)^2$ via Whittaker--Shannon band-limited interpolation, we prove that the scaled non-normal discrete Dirac-type operator $D_{d,h}$ converges to the continuous self-adjoint Dirac operator $D$ in the norm resolvent sense at the optimal rate $\mathcal{O}(h)$ as $h \to 0^+$, without requiring frequency cutoffs.

title: A spectral Moore problem and the Yang-Koolen conjecture
abstract: We study the maximum order $v(k,θ)$ of a connected $k$-regular graph whose second largest eigenvalue is at most $θ$. For every real $θ\geq1$, we prove that \[ T(θ) =\limsup_{k\to\infty}\bigl(v(k,θ)-2k\bigr) =2\left\lfloor1+\frac{θ^2}{4}\right\rfloor. \] In particular, $T(θ)>2θ$ for every real $θ\geq4$, disproving the Yang-Koolen conjecture. We also determine $v(k,θ)$ for all sufficiently large $k$ on explicit intervals of $θ$. We prove a jump in the second largest eigenvalue above $1$. For each fixed $1\leqθ<2$ and all sufficiently large $k$, every connected $k$-regular graph of order at least $2k+2$ whose second largest eigenvalue is at most $θ$ is the crown graph. For $θ=\sqrt2$, we prove that $v(k,\sqrt2)=2k+2$ for every $k\geq13$. Finally, we obtain two new upper bounds on $v(k,θ)$.

title: On the asymptotic distribution of the largest eigenvalue of unbalanced complex Jacobi ensembles
abstract: Let $\mathbf{A} \sim \mathbb{C}\mathcal{W}_p(I,m)$ and $\mathbf{B} \sim \mathbb{C}\mathcal{W}_p(I,n)$ be two independent complex Wishart random matrices. In this work, we investigate the asymptotic distribution of the largest eigenvalue $θ_{\max}$ of the random matrix $\mathbf{J} = (\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{B})^{-1}\mathbf{B}$. The high-dimensional regime is potentially unbalanced in the sense that, as $p \to \infty$, $m$ may grow faster than $p$, whereas $n$ grows proportionally to $p$. The asymptotic behavior of $θ_{\max}$ is characterized by means of a Riemann-Hilbert (RH) problem for Jacobi polynomials with modified Jacobi weights. We establish the type 2 Tracy--Widom asymptotic distribution of $θ_{\max}$. This provides an alternative, RH-based proof of the corresponding result of Johnstone [Ann. Statist. 36 (2008), 2638-2716] in the balanced regime, and establishes a conjecture of Jiang [Probab. Theory Relat. Fields 144 (2009), 221-246] in the unbalanced regime. In addition, we obtain an explicit correction of order $p^{-2/3}$ to the Tracy--Widom approximation, with a remainder of order $\mathcal{O}(p^{-1})$, and show exponential decay, as a function of $p$, of the upper tail of the distribution of $θ_{\max}$.

title: Congruent quotient matrix, nodal domain, and nodal count
abstract: We introduce the congruent quotient matrix along with its inequalities on inertia and demonstrate that these inequalities are the essence of the discrete nodal domain theorem, the bounds on nodal counts, and Fiedler's characterization on tree eigenvectors. Using these techniques, we also extend the existing bounds for the number of nodal domains and nodal counts.

title: Flux vector splittings and semi-implicit finite volume schemes for an isentropic two-phase flow model
abstract: We present two new semi-implicit finite volume schemes for the 1D hyperbolic and thermodynamically compatible (HTC) isentropic two-phase flow model of Romenski et al., written in terms of mixture density, volume fraction, partial gas density, mixture momentum and the relative phase velocity. In gas-liquid mixtures, the sound speed of the weakly compressible liquid is much larger than the gas sound speed and flow velocity, so the time step of fully explicit discretizations is dictated by liquid acoustic waves, even when the interest lies in the dynamics of the gas. To overcome this difficulty, the model's flux is split at the continuous level into an explicit subsystem (gas dynamics) and an implicit subsystem (liquid acoustic waves), leading to a nonlinear system for liquid pressure solved with the Newton method. In the first splitting the entire liquid phase is treated implicitly, while in the second the liquid convective terms are moved to the explicit subsystem, so only liquid acoustic waves are treated implicitly and nested Picard iterations are avoided. Thus, the time step of both schemes is restricted only by flow velocities and gas sound speed, independent of liquid sound speed. We prove and numerically confirm that both schemes exactly preserve the Abgrall condition (uniform velocity and pressure across material interfaces). For well-prepared initial data, both schemes are consistent with the volume balance of the liquid's low Mach number limit. Riemann problems, pressure equilibrium tests and acoustic tests show that in non-stiff regimes the semi-implicit schemes reproduce the results of a fully explicit scheme, while in the stiff regime they allow time steps that are up to 3-4 orders of magnitude larger, avoiding the excessive numerical dissipation of explicit schemes whose numerical viscosity is dictated by liquid sound speed.

title: A Representation Theorem for Fractional Viscoelastic Networks
abstract: We prove a representation theorem for finite series-parallel viscoelastic networks composed of springs and spring-pots of a common order $0<α<1$. The associated complex shear modulus, expressed in an appropriately chosen auxiliary variable, is rational and admits a finite partial-fraction representation with simple poles on the negative real axis and negative residues. Its reciprocal admits an analogous representation with positive residues and a possible additional pole at the origin. Inverting the corresponding Laplace transforms gives finite fractional Prony representations of the relaxation modulus and creep compliance with non-negative amplitudes. These results provide a rigorous proof of a corrected version of the Mainardi-Spada conjecture for this network class. A six-element network illustrates the construction.

title: Additive mappings of unweighted directed graphs preserving individual values of the cycle length
abstract: On the set of unweighted directed graphs on $n$ vertices, the union of graphs is defined as the union of their arc sets. A mapping of graphs is said to be additive if it preserves the union operation. In this paper, a characterization of additive mappings of unweighted directed graphs preserving a fixed value $k \geq 3$ of the cycle length is obtained.

title: Large $N$ limit of the ratio of Lukyanov integrals
abstract: We study the large-$N$ asymptotics of ratios of Lukyanov integrals for fixed real coupling $b\geq1$. Our approach uses their biorthogonal ensemble structure and vector Riemann--Hilbert techniques. Under stated analytic hypotheses, we derive the logarithmic ratio through its constant term, which is expressed by a Fredholm determinant. The expansion is locally uniform in the real parameter $α$ and is formulated separately for even and odd particle numbers. We verify the hypotheses for the correction defined by the physical ground-state thermodynamic Bethe ansatz. The relation to quantum-field-theoretic one-point functions is discussed separately.

title: $AV$-modules on affine algebraic groups
abstract: We study $AV$-modules on an affine algebraic group $G$, that is, modules that admit compatible actions of the algebra of regular functions on $G$ and the Lie algebra of vector fields. A central role in this theory is played by the Lie algebra of jets of vector fields. Our main result is the Decomposition Theorem for the Lie algebra of jets of vector fields. We apply the Decomposition Theorem to describe differentiable $AV$-modules on $G$.

title: The Self-repelling Burglar
abstract: In this paper, we study the conditional location of $X_T$ given the local time profile $L_T(\cdot)$ for two non-Markovian self-interacting processes: the polynomially self-repelling motion (PSRM) and the true self-repelling motion (TSRM). For TSRM, our novel approach yields a new proof of Dumaz's clever burglar result [Dumaz 2012].

title: Metric Correspondences and Low-Rank Deformations for Conformal and \(m\)-Modified Conformal Vector Fields
abstract: We fix a smooth vector field and a positive parameter $m$, and compare the nondegenerate metrics for which the field is conformal or $m$-modified conformal with the same prescribed smooth factor. Metrics of arbitrary signature are allowed. Passing to inverse metrics gives a linear transport equation and an explicit correspondence on the exact nondegeneracy domains. At a regular point, transverse initial data yield a signature-preserving correspondence of metric germs. For a nowhere-zero field and a Killing background in dimension at least three, every metric satisfying the modified conformal equation and differing from the background by a tensor of rank at most one has factor zero; its inverse-metric difference is $rX\otimes X$ for a unique smooth function $r$. Under a complete flow, such global deformations exist precisely when the field is null for the background and admits a smooth function $τ$ with $Xτ=1$. An auxiliary field satisfying $[X,Z]=X$ gives a second correspondence under orthogonality assumptions. Finally, for a nowhere-zero complete field, a Killing metric and a zero-factor modified conformal metric have inverse-metric difference of rank at least two whenever that rank is constant. In the rank-two case, the pair determines a unique auxiliary field. Examples distinguish the roles of dimension, completeness, constant rank, the zero-factor condition, and orthogonality.

title: On the nonvanishing of Floer lasagna modules
