abstract: In this paper, we establish several nonvanishing results for Floer lasagna modules $\mathcal{FL}(W,K)$ for a smooth compact connected oriented $4$-manifold $W$ and a knot $K\subset \partial W$, via the evaluation maps to link Floer homology. We first establish a general criterion: if a certain Heegaard Floer cobordism map associated with a smooth $4$-manifold $W$ is nonzero, then $\mathcal{FL}(W,U)\neq 0$, where $U\subset \partial W$ is a local unknot. Applications include the nonvanishing of Floer lasagna modules for $\#^m\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}$ and for knot traces $X_n(K)$ when $K$ is slice and $n$ is a non-positive integer. In another direction, we show that for every nontrivial knot $K$ and every integer $n$, the Floer lasagna module $\mathcal{FL}(X_n(K),K_n)$ is nonzero, where $K_n\subset S_n^3(K)$ is the dual knot. Moreover, if $K$ is an L-space knot, then $\mathcal{FL}(X_n(K),K_n)$ is infinite-dimensional for all integers $n\ge \max\{2g(K),1\}$.

title: Identities for generalized Bernoulli numbers from a Lie model of the 2-disk
abstract:
We define generalized Bernoulli numbers as appropriate coefficients of the Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff (BCH) product formula, extending the classical sequence of rational numbers to a 2-dimensional setting. We give an identity involving these numbers and the classical Bernoulli numbers which is equivalent to the existence of a particular complete differential graded Lie algebra modelling a cell decomposition of the 2-disk and based on the Lawrence--Sullivan model of the interval. From this identity we derive explicit quadratic relations.
  The existence of Lie models for the symmetries of the interval and the disk is related to certain properties of the BCH product and to some notable features of the classical Bernoulli numbers: the two choices for $B_1$, the vanishing of $B_n$ for odd $n\geq 3$, and the equality $B_4=B_8$.

title: A semi-parametric Bernstein-von Mises theorem at rate $n^{-3/2}$ for frequency estimation
abstract: We consider Bayesian inference for the frequency of a periodic signal of unknown shape, observed in Gaussian white noise on the interval $[0,n]$. The information about the frequency grows like $n^3$, so the frequency can be estimated at rate $n^{-3/2}$, while the shape is an infinite-dimensional nuisance parameter. We endow the frequency and the shape with independent priors, the prior on the shape being a random series in the trigonometric basis. We give conditions on the priors under which the posterior for the signal contracts at a rate that, for suitable choices, is the minimax rate for Sobolev classes of smoothness at least one, up to a logarithmic factor and adaptively to the smoothness of the shape. If, moreover, the prior keeps the shape away from shapes with a shorter period, also the marginal posteriors for the frequency and the shape contract around the truth. Under further conditions, which hold for a Gaussian random series prior conditioned to keep the shape away from shapes with a shorter period, for every true shape with smallest period 1 and Sobolev smoothness larger than $3/2$, the marginal posterior for the frequency satisfies a semi-parametric Bernstein-von Mises theorem at rate $n^{-3/2}$, which we prove by moving the origin of time, a change that leaves the posterior unchanged when the prior on the shape is invariant under time shifts.

title: Polyteam logics for quantum contextuality
abstract: We introduce logics of dependence and independence over polyteams (that is, databases with multiple relation schemes), in a similar way as in arXiv:1704.02158v3 [cs.LO]. On this basis, we develop a logical framework in which we can express (in formulas) relevant properties about the statistics of a repeated quantum experiment. In this framework, we formalize Bell's theorem, and the Kochen-Specker theorem as failure of logical entailments, as it was suggested in arXiv:2107.10817v3 [math.LO]. The key feature of polyteam logics in action here is their power to express both local and global properties, with respect to the set of possible measurements. The point of this is at least twofold. Firstly, as in arXiv:1102.0264v7 [quant-ph], it gives a high-level (information-theoretic) understanding of these physical phenomena, that is not intrinsic to the physical objects involved. Secondly, since logical entailment is often (partially) axiomatizable, this framework incites us to tackle the question of contextuality computationally. We also define semiring-weighted polyteams along with logics on them, and use them to recover the probabilistic versions of the contextuality theorems mentioned above.

title: Biunital Lie Semiheaps and Lie Triple Systems
abstract: We examine the differential geometry of Lie semiheaps that admit biunital elements. Open Ol'shanskii semigroups, which appear widely across causal geometry and harmonic analysis, provide a large class of examples. It is shown that the subset of biunits is a smoothly embedded Lie subheap. Moreover, there is a canonical Lie triple algebroid associated with any proper biunital Lie semiheap. That is, there is a vector bundle over the manifold of biunits that comes equipped with a ternary bracket that satisfies the axioms of a Lie triple system together with a compatible `higher' anchor map. Although every Lie triple algebroid associated with a proper biunital Lie semiheap is trivialisable, it is not canonically so, unlike the case of the tangent bundle of a Lie group. As concrete examples, we examine the Lie semiheap of real $n\times n$ matrices, and the conformal causal Lie semiheap associated with the Lie group $\mathrm{SU}(2,2)$, which is a double cover of the conformal group of Minkowski spacetime, and the future-directed light cone.

title: Conjectures of Bernstein and Erdős for weighted Lagrange interpolation with Hermite weight
abstract:
The classical Bernstein and Erdős Conjectures for algebraic Lagrange interpolation on a finite interval were settled in two consecutive papers by Kilgore and by de Boor and Pinkus in 1978. Extending these results to weighted interpolation on unbounded intervals has proved to be more difficult.
  In a previous work, we established the Bernstein and Erd\H os Conjectures, together with the ``modified'' de Boor--Pinkus intertwining theorem, for weighted Lagrange interpolation on the half-line with exponential weights. Here we continue this line of research by considering the Hermite weight on the whole real line. Our main result is the Hermite-weighted analogue of the Bernstein and Erdős conjectures together with the appropriate version of the de Boor--Pinkus intertwining theorem.
  A key ingredient in the classical proofs is the nonsingularity of certain derivative matrices associated with the local maxima of the Lebesgue function. This property already breaks down in the exponentially weighted setting, although the resulting difficulties can still be resolved. In the Hermite-weighted setting, however, the situation becomes more intricate, requiring a substantial refinement of the previous approach.

title: A structure-preserving finite volume scheme for the time-fractional Allen-Cahn equation with nondegenerate state-dependent mobility
abstract: We construct and analyze a fully discrete finite volume scheme for the time-fractional Allen-Cahn equation with nondegenerate state-dependent mobility. The scheme combines a standard two-point flux approximation of diffusion, the L1 approximation of the Caputo derivative on a uniform time grid, and a semiconvex splitting of the potential, and it discretizes the inverse mobility by a secant average multiplying the entire L1 derivative. The key estimate is a lower bound for the accumulated pairing of this weighted L1 derivative with the solution increments in terms of the accumulated L1 quadratic form. Using this lower bound, we derive a discrete energy estimate and the time regularity required for compactness. For twice continuously differentiable semiconvex potentials satisfying sign conditions outside $(-1,1)$ and initial data in $H^1(Ω)$ taking values in $[-1,1]$, we prove existence of at least one fully discrete solution on every admissible finite volume mesh and every uniform time grid. Every such solution satisfies the maximum bound principle and a discrete energy bound relative to the initial energy, without a time-step restriction. In up to three space dimensions, under a mesh regularity condition with a constant independent of the mesh size, we prove that any sequence of fully discrete solutions has a subsequence converging strongly in $L^2(Ω\times(0,T))$ to a weak solution of the continuous problem as the mesh size and time step tend to zero. As a consequence, we obtain existence of a weak solution in one and two space dimensions, and in three dimensions whenever such meshes exist.

title: A density theorem for non-standard irreducible cyclic codes
abstract: We prove a fixed-characteristic density form of the Berger-Charpin conjecture for non-degenerate irreducible cyclic codes: for each prime $p$, the lengths admitting such a non-standard code over some finite field of characteristic $p$ have natural density zero. Thus, for almost every length coprime to $p$, every such code over every finite field of characteristic $p$ has only the permutation automorphisms generated by the cyclic shift and the Frobenius map. The proof uses the Feng--Hollmann--Li--Xiang classification for non-standard irreducible cyclic codes, a normal form for the deriving constructions in that paper, and a theorem by Wiertelak on multiplicative orders, in the form recalled by Moree.

title: Quantum Diffusion and the Block-Size Crossover in the Block Anderson Model
abstract:
We study the block Anderson Hamiltonian \(H_L=λΨ_L+\mathcal V\) on the discrete torus \((\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z)^d\), \(d\geq2\), where \(Ψ_L\) is the nearest-neighbor Laplacian and \(\mathcal V\) consists of independent \(W^d\times W^d\) GOE blocks. In the weak-disorder limit \(λ\to\infty\), we establish an entrywise local law, a spatial scaling limit for the squared resolvent entries, time-averaged dynamical delocalization, and lower bounds on the localization length of most bulk eigenfunctions. Particularly, we allow the block size to be fixed or grow above a polylogarithmic threshold. In sufficiently large polynomial volumes, the dynamical estimates hold for \(C_δ(λ+W/λ)\leq T\leq λ^{1+κ_d^{\rm BA}-δ}\), with a dimension-dependent exponent \(κ_d^{\rm BA}>0\), and the spreading scale is \(\sqrt{(λ^3+λW)T}\). This identifies a transition at \(W\asympλ^2\) between \(λ^{3/2}\sqrt T\) and \(\sqrt{λWT}\).
  The proof combines Gaussian moment estimates with deterministic stability of a matrix Dyson equation. A partial Bloch transform handles fixed blocks, while scalar reduction controls growing blocks. A Feshbach--Schur reduction of the block \(T\)-equation separates a single scalar diffusion mode from the stable internal cell modes. A renewal expansion and exact cell counting give a positive representation of the diffusion coefficient and control the fourth moment uniformly across the block-size transition. Notably, our argument does not require an enumeration of Feynman diagrams.

title: A Parallel Adaptive Proximal ADMM for Linearly Constrained Separable Composite Optimization Problems
abstract: We propose and analyze an adaptive proximal alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), based on Jacobi-type updates, for linearly constrained separable nonconvex composite optimization problems. The objective consists of two block-separable functions, one continuously differentiable and weakly convex, and the other convex and Lipschitz continuous. The proposed method is adaptive to all problem parameters and allows inexact solutions of the block proximal subproblems. At each iteration, we solve all block subproblems in parallel, then apply a novel test to decide whether to update the Lagrange multiplier and/or the penalty parameter. Without any rank assumptions on the constraint matrices, we establish an ${\cal O}(ε^{-3})$ iteration-complexity bound for obtaining an approximate first-order stationary point. This matches the best-known complexity for cyclic proximal ADMM methods and improves the existing complexity of Jacobi-type schemes in this general nonconvex setting. Numerical experiments on a nonconvex quadratic program illustrate the proposed method's computational benefits.

title: Promotion and Extension of General Escape-Covering Duality Relationship
abstract:
Bellman's lost-in-a-forest problem, Moser's worm problem, Lebesgue's universal covering problems, and the classical 'fits and covers' questions can be organized by a common obstruction principle: an object fits a region if some admissible group action places it in the region, whereas an escape object is one for which every placement fails to remain in the interior.
  In this paper, we develop a general theory of escape-covering duality for any dimension and explore several applications. For convex translation covers of all closed planar curves of Euclidean length one, we prove $
  W \ge f(\sqrt3/9)+c_1>0.15545785378555,c_1=0.000009944944227372... $ Here $f(\sqrt3/9)$ is Wetzel's classical lower bound.
  For a rational polytopal Minkowski gauge and prescribed rational facet directions, we express universal closed-loop cover feasibility as a rational polyhedron in the facet offsets. After removing translations, minimum volume is attained at a vertex. Refining the facet directions gives explicit two-sided rational bounds for the unrestricted fixed-gauge worm constant. Four exact benchmarks recover known sharp values. The construction uses an elementary circuit--circumradius form of the established non-fitting-polygon and capacity theory. We supply its support and ledger derivation, the finite complete test family in arbitrary dimension, a cover vertex bound, and the resulting algebraicity statement.
  The surrounding escape--covering framework includes endpoint placement, attainment, gauge stability, and finite-to-continuum error bounds. For nonsymmetric gauges the objects are parametrized closed curves, so orientation-dependent length is retained. Through the published capacity identity, the improved Wetzel estimate gives a product volume--capacity factor below $1.023781939711102$ for every planar ellipsoidal gauge.

title: An exhaustion-aware product moment and zero-free half-planes for Hecke L-functions
abstract: We refine the ordinary product moment in the cubic-theta comparison by allowing a returned prime product to be exhausted. The return stops either when the positive-prime length inequality holds or when the established prime-free ordinary estimate applies. Keeping the extracted central coefficients gives a local normalization inequality on a larger domain. On the critical ordinary-length interval this yields a net first-mean gain of $1/20000$. We prove the complementary-class, short-sum and algebraic comparison inequalities directly, and obtain the endpoint $B_*-1/160000=0.87446205769353\ldots$, where $B_*$ is Liu's algebraic boundary. The zero-free conclusion is conditional on the cited general-field theta, detector, prior-bound and Mellin input theorems in their stated uniform forms. The proof includes the actual return weights, both approximate-functional-equation arms, the principal-residue normalization and descent to arbitrary number fields.

title: Real zeros of $w$-polynomials: cycles and complete cutsets
Modulus of Continuity for Finite Energy Homeomorphisms of the Circle
abstract: Given $h_o: \mathbb{S} \to \mathbb{S}$, an orientation-preserving homeomorphism of the unit circle, we seek to establish very weak conditions so as to derive a modulus of continuity for $h_o$ and its inverse $h_o^{-1}$, then use these to derive various compactness properties for families of circle homeomorphisms and solutions to Beltrami equations.

title: On subgroup perfect codes and regular sets in generalized Cayley graphs
abstract: A subset $C$ of the vertex set of a graph $Γ$ is said to be an $(a,b)$-regular set if $C$ induces an $a$-regular subgraph and every vertex outside $C$ is adjacent to exactly $b$ vertices in $C$. A $(0,1)$-regular set is called a perfect code. Let $G$ be a finite group and let $α\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ be such that $α^2=\mathrm{id}$. Let $ω_α(G)=\{α(g^{-1})g:g\in G\}$. For a subset $S\subseteq G$ satisfying $α(S)=S^{-1}$ and $S\capω_α(G)=\emptyset$, the generalized Cayley graph of $(G,α)$ with respect to $S$ is the graph with vertex set $G$ in which two distinct elements $g,h\in G$ are adjacent if and only if $α(g^{-1})h\in S$. In this paper, we prove two main results. First, let $H$ be an $α$-invariant subgroup of a finite group $G$, and let $P$ be an $α$-invariant Sylow 2-subgroup of $H$. We show that $H$ is a perfect code of $(G,α)$ if and only if $P[H,α]$ is a perfect code of $(G,α)$, where $[H,α]=\langle h^{-1}α(h):h\in H\rangle$. Second, we consider finite groups $G$ possessing a cyclic subgroup $A$ of index 2 that is invariant under an involutory automorphism $α$. We show that $ω_α(G)$ is a subgroup of $A$. Using this result, we give a complete characterization of all pairs $(a,b)$ for which an $α$-invariant subgroup $H$ of $G$ is an $(a,b)$-regular set of $(G,α)$. In particular, our characterization applies to all finite groups possessing a characteristic cyclic subgroup of index 2, for every involutory automorphism $α$.

title: On Ramanujan's cubic continued fraction, II
abstract: We show that all the periodic points with period $n \ge 3$ of the algebraic function defined by the relation $g(x,y) = x^2+2xy^2-y = 0$ are expressible in terms of values of Ramanujan's cubic continued fraction $c(τ)$. It is shown that the values $c(w/2), c(w/6), c(w/6+1/2)$ are periodic points, for specific elements $w$ in the order of discriminant $-d$ in $K = \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-d})$, with $-d \equiv 1$ (mod $8$); and all the periodic points are conjugates of these values or specific linear fractional expressions in their conjugates, times cube roots of unity. These periodic points are determined by relating them to the periodic points of the algebraic function defined by $k(x,y)= -xy^2+x^2+y^2+3x = 0$; and these periodic points (for periods $\ge 2$) generate ring class fields over $K$.

title: Entry and position statistics in alternating permutations and Young tableaux
abstract: We study entry and position statistics in alternating permutations and standard Young tableaux using linear extensions and generating functions. For alternating permutations, we give explicit formulas for the mean and variance of the first entry and of the position of any fixed value. For standard Young tableaux, we express the sum of the lower-left entries as the number of tableaux of an associated skew shape. For two-row shapes, we determine the distribution of the entry in each cell of the second row, and for the shape $(n,n)$ we give a closed formula for its sum over all tableaux, which recovers a limit formula of Stanley. Through a bijection of Lewis, the results for the shape $(n,n)$ describe the entries of a random $321$-avoiding down-up permutation of even length.

title: Noise Stability on the Hypercube: Order $7/8$
abstract: For a balanced Boolean function $f$ on the discrete hypercube, we study the $α$-stability $\mathbb{E}[(T_ρf)^α]$, where $T_ρ$ is the Boolean noise operator and $0<α<1$. Using the asymmetric Hellinger kernel estimates recently established by OpenAI, we prove that dictators minimize the $7/8$-stability in every dimension and at every correlation $0\leρ\le1$. At interior correlations they are the only minimizers. As a consequence, dictators minimize the $α$-stability for every $7/8\leα<1$, maximize the $α$-stability for every $1<α<2$, and maximize the one-sided Shannon entropy stability $\mathbb{E}[T_ρf\log T_ρf]$. This resolves a conjecture of Li and Médard and strengthens the Courtade--Kumar conjecture in the balanced setting.

title: Harmonic Quasiconformal Mappings in the BMO-Teichmüller space
abstract:
Let $\text{HQS}(\mathbb{R})$ denote the class of increasing homeomorphisms of the real line $\mathbb{R}$
  that admit harmonic quasiconformal extensions to the upper
  half-plane $\mathbb{H}$. Kalaj and Pavlović proved that a
  homeomorphism $h$ belongs to $\text{HQS}(\mathbb{R})$ if and only if $h$ is
  bi-Lipschitz and the Hilbert transform of $h'$ belongs to $L^\infty(\mathbb{R})$,
  and asked whether $\text{HQS}(\mathbb{R})$ is a group under composition.
  We give a negative answer to this question. Further, we show that the Beltrami coefficients of harmonic quasiconformal mappings of $\mathbb{H}$ can be identified with the open unit ball of $H^\infty(\mathbb{H})$.
  Finally, we study the topology of $\text{HQS}(\mathbb{R})$ and prove that
  it is contractible in the topology inherited from
  the BMO-Teichmüller space.

title: Twisting-free converse theorems for $Γ_0(32)$ and $Γ_0(36)$
abstract: We prove twisting-free converse theorems for $Γ_0(32)$ and $Γ_0(36)$ under the setting of Conrey--Farmer, namely assuming a single functional equation and a suitable Euler product, with particular shapes at ramified primes. The proofs make substantial use of the ramified primes, with methods somewhat different from the existing ones in the literature.

title: The Two-Point Inequality for $p>q$
abstract:
For $1<q<p<\infty$ we study the $L^p\to L^q$ contractivity of the two-point
  operator $T_ω(a+bx)=a+ωbx$ with a complex parameter $ω$,
  extending the Weissler two-point condition, usually discussed in the range
  $1<p\le q<\infty$, to the reversed order of exponents. For $1<q<p<2$ we prove
  that the second-order necessary condition
  $|(p-2)-(q-2)ω^2|\le p-q|ω|^2$, obtained near $(a,b)=(1,0)$, is also
  sufficient; by duality the same description applies to $2<q<p<\infty$. The
  proof uses the method of characteristic flows. In addition, for $q\le2\le p$
  the contractivity follows directly from $L^2$ contraction.

title: Well begun is half done: the computation of Eulerian paths
abstract: We characterize the uniform computational strength of finding one-way Eulerian paths in countable graphs. For both directed and undirected graphs, this problem is Weihrauch-equivalent to $\mathsf{lim}\times\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}'$, where $\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}'$ is the jump of closed choice on the natural numbers. This refines the proof-theoretical strength of the existence of an Eulerian path given by the reverse mathematics framework. The $\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}'$ component comes entirely from the difficulty of choosing a starting vertex: with a valid start prescribed, the problem is equivalent to $\mathsf{lim}$. We also study the problem $\mathsf{OrientEP}$ of orienting an undirected graph while preserving the existence of a one-way Eulerian path. We prove $\mathsf{lim}_2<_{\mathrm{W}}\mathsf{OrientEP}<_{\mathrm{W}}\mathsf{C}_{2}'\sqcap\mathsf{Sort}_2$ and $\mathsf{OrientEP}\not\le_{\mathrm{W}}\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}$.

title: On the unconstrained Allen-Cahn system and its Cahn-Hilliard limit
abstract: In [F.P. Duda et al., Meccanica, 2021] the new theory for constituent migration in solids with microstructure was developed. We consider the one-dimensional version of the basic system of this theory with generally non-zero kinetic modulus and the particular diffusivity of the "fast diffusion" type. We obtain exact traveling wave solutions for this system, and analyze several unconstraint and constraint limiting cases. We show that in unconstraint cases of Allen-Cahn type, i.e. for two independent variables, the system demonstrates broader set of possible regimes; in the constraint limit only CH-type process remains.

title: Spatial degeneracy along weak geodesics in the space of Kähler potentials
abstract: We study spatial Hessian degeneracy along weak Kähler geodesics. We construct examples in three settings: (1) On every compact Kähler manifold, the spatial form degenerates on a nonempty open set during an interior time interval, although both endpoints are smooth and strictly Kähler. (2) On ALE Kähler manifolds with a holomorphic quotient end and a decaying potential to the Euclidean metric, spatial degeneracy occurs on open regions arbitrarily far along an unbounded horn. (3) For cone and Poincaré endpoint metrics along a smooth divisor, normal spatial degeneracy occurs on open sets approaching the divisor. Both cone endpoints retain the prescribed angle. The first construction answers negatively the spatial-positivity question recorded in Darvas's survey. The ALE and divisor constructions show that weak geodesics need not preserve the asymptotic behavior of the endpoint metrics.

title: Stable solutions to $p$-Laplacian type equations with variable coefficients
abstract:
We study stable regular solutions of the variable-coefficient equation $-\operatorname{div}((A(x)
abla u\cdot
abla u)^{p/2-1}A(x)
abla u)=f(u)$ in $B_1\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, where $p>1$, $f\in C^1(\mathbb{R})$ is nonnegative, and $A$ is a locally Lipschitz, symmetric, uniformly elliptic matrix field. We prove quantitative interior Hölder estimates for $n<p+4p/(p-1)$ when $p\ge2$, and for $n<5p$ when $1<p<2$. We also obtain interior energy estimates and higher integrability of the gradient in every dimension. These estimates are given in terms of $\|u\|_{L^1(B_1)}$, with constants depending only on $n,p$, the ellipticity bounds, and a local $L^\infty$ bound for $DA$, but not on $f$ or higher derivatives of $A$. These results extend the corresponding interior estimates of Cabré, Miraglio, and Sanchón for the $p$-Laplace equation to this variable-coefficient setting. The proof uses weighted Hessian estimates to control coefficient errors and a comparison between radial and full gradient energies.

title: Boosted Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Homogeneous and Non-Homogeneous Lane-Emden Type Equations
abstract: The Lane-Emden Equation is a class of nonlinear differential equations commonly used to model phenomena in astrophysics and mathematical physics, such as stellar structure and thermal behavior in polytropic gas spheres. This study presents a novel hybrid framework that integrates Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) with boosting methods to enhance the accuracy and robustness of solutions for Lane-Emden type differential equations. Standard PINNs leverage physical laws encoded within the loss function, but their predictive performance can be constrained by optimization challenges and approximation errors. To address this, we introduce a post-processing boosting stage where the residual errors from the PINN prediction are modeled using some regression algorithms - including LightGBM, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Support Vector Regression (SVR). The outputs from these boosted models are aggregated to generate a corrected, high-fidelity prediction. The proposed methodology is systematically validated through quantitative metrics and comparative analysis against the standard PINN baseline. The results demonstrate that the boosted PINN framework significantly reduces prediction error, and improves generalization, offering a powerful and flexible approach for solving scientific and engineering problems governed by differential equations.

title: Minimal quasisections of circle bundles
abstract:
Let $E\xrightarrowπB$ be an oriented circle bundle over an oriented closed surface, and let $\mathcal E$ denote its Euler number. A \textit{quasisection} is a smooth surface $Q$, possibly with boundary, together with a generic smooth map $q:Q\to E$ such that $π\circ q(Q)=B$.
  The \textit{local formula} expresses the Euler number $\mathcal E$ of a bundle as a sum of the weights of the \textit{singular vertices} of a quasisection.
  In the present paper determine the minimal number $\mathcal N$ of singular vertices for closed and for bordered quasisections for a given circle bundle. For bordered quasisections, \[
  \mathcal N_{\mathrm b}(E\to B)
  =\left\lceil\frac{3|\mathcal E|}{2}\right\rceil. \] For closed quasisections, If $\mathcal{E}$ is even,
  \[
  \mathcal N_{\mathrm cl}(E\to B)
  =\frac{3|\mathcal E|}{2}. \]
  If $\mathcal{E}$ is odd,
  \[
  \mathcal N_{\mathrm cl}(E\to B)
  =4|\mathcal E|. \]
  We also provide examples of quasisections that realize these minimal values.

title: Weighted $L^q$-$L^r$ estimates of a generalized Oseen evolution operator in exterior domains, with applications to the Navier-Stokes flow past a rigid body
abstract: We consider a generalized Oseen evolution operator arising from time-dependent rigid motions in 3D exterior domains. Hishida and the present author established the regularity theory of the evolution operator by use of the $L^q$-$L^r$ smoothing estimates with a weight function $(1+|x|)^α$. The objective of this paper is to develop the weighted $L^q$-$L^r$ estimates globally in time. These estimates are applied to the study of the large time behavior of the Navier-Stokes flow around a time-periodic solution in weighted spaces.

title: Spectral and convex geometry of $α$-harmonic maps and sharp Morse index rigidity
abstract: We develop a weighted scalar spectral geometric description of Sacks-Uhlenbeck $α$-harmonic maps into round spheres and identify its convex geometry realization for $α$-harmonic diffeomorphisms onto the round $2$-sphere. More precisely, we establish a one-to-one correspondence, modulo orientation preserving isometries of $\mathbb{S}^2$, between orientation preserving $α$-harmonic diffeomorphisms onto the round $2$-sphere and positive Codazzi tensors satisfying a determinant bound and a compatibility condition with the prescribed metric on $\mathbb{S}^2$. These tensors are the radii tensors of auxiliary strictly convex surfaces, and the weighted scalar forms in spectral geometry equal $-α$ times the second variations of the enclosed volumes with respect to the support functions. Using these spectral geometry and convex geometry results, we prove a sharp Morse index characterization of isometric equatorial parametrizations among $α$-harmonic $2$-spheres in the round $n$-sphere. We also prove that every $α$-harmonic diffeomorphism between unit round $2$-spheres is orthogonal for all $α>1$. Equivalently, the only admissible positive Codazzi tensor whose reconstructed metric on $\mathbb{S}^2$ has Gaussian curvature $1$ is $(κ+2)^{α-1}\bar{g}$, where $\bar{g}$ is the unit round metric.

title: A posteriori error estimates for a finite volume approximation of a local sensing Keller-Segel model
abstract: A local sensing Keller-Segel model, in which cells adjust their motility to the local chemoattractant rather than its gradient, and a semi-implicit finite volume scheme for its numerical approximation are studied. Computable a posteriori bounds for the approximation error measured in terms of the $L^\infty(0, T; H^{-1}(Ω))$ and $L^2(0, T; L^2(Ω))$ norms of the cell density are derived based on a new stability estimate and suitable reconstructions of the flux and the flux potential of the numerical solution. Optimal scaling of the estimates is numerically demonstrated in 1D and 2D experiments. Moreover, an adaptive mesh refinement method steered by the estimator is proposed for the 1D case, and its efficiency is numerically verified.

title: The distribution of $απ$ modulo one in $\Fq(T)$: beyond Matomäki's exponent
abstract: Let $α$ be an element of $\Fq((1/T))$ which is not in $\Fq(T)$. We ask how small $\nrm{απ}$ can be made when $π$ runs over irreducible polynomials, and write $θ(α)$ for the largest exponent $θ$ such that $\nrm{απ}<|π|^{-θ}$ has infinitely many solutions. The analogue of Matomäki's exponent, $θ(α)\ge\frac13$, was proved by Baier and the author, and it is the natural limit of the Riemann Hypothesis. In this paper we go beyond it. For odd characteristic $p$ and $q$ large in terms of $p$ and $θ$, we prove that $θ(α)\geθ$ for every $α$ and every $θ<\sqrt2-1=0.414\ldots$, and for every $θ<\frac12$ when $α$ has bounded partial quotients. The main tools are an exact count of points in affine subspaces of $\Fq[T]$, a splitting of these subspaces into long arithmetic progressions, and the results of Sawin and Shusterman on the Möbius function along such progressions.

title: Log-Driven Semantic Tuning for Mixed Integer Programming Solvers
abstract: Automated configuration of mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers largely relies on black-box optimization. Each trial requires an expensive solver run and provides only a scalar outcome, so tuning can require many such evaluations. Human experts take a different approach. They inspect solver logs, identify performance bottlenecks, and adjust the parameters that address them. We propose Log-Driven Semantic Tuning (LDST), which uses a large language model (LLM) to automate this process. LDST extracts compact diagnostics from solver logs, uses the LLM to propose sparse edits to the current best configuration based on parameter meanings and observed solver behavior, and validates each proposal before execution. A regime-adaptive objective selects the tuning signal according to the information available from a time-limited run, while a log-based completion signal estimates completion time from branch-and-bound tree growth recorded in ordinary solver logs, so that solved and unsolved runs share one time scale. On 215 instances from five benchmark sets, LDST reduces geometric-mean loss by 43.9% on easy instances and 16.7% on intermediate instances relative to the best of SMAC3, RBFOpt, and random search. In both regimes, LDST achieves a lower loss with 10 proposals than any of these baselines achieves with 50. Configurations that LDST tunes on a single instance also transfer better than baseline configurations to unseen instances of the same family.

title: L2-contraction and Asymptotic Stability of Monotone Shock Waves for Cubic and Quartic KdV-Burgers Equations
abstract: We investigate the nonlinear stability of monotone traveling shock waves arising in the generalized Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers equation with a power-law flux, focusing on the cubic and quartic cases p=3 and p=4, respectively, in the presence of both dissipative and dispersive effects. Since shocks connecting distinct end states destroy the integrable structure of the equation, we introduce a slowly varying reference connection to establish global well-posedness for the Cauchy problem in an affine Sobolev space. A key ingredient in the stability analysis is to establish a new two-sided comparison estimate for the derivative of a monotone shock-wave profile. After a monotone coordinate transformation, this estimate allows the viscous dissipation to be compared with the natural vanishing weight arising in a shifted Poincare inequality. Together with an $L^\infty$ bootstrap controlling the higher-order relative-flux terms, this yields a global $L^2$-contraction property modulo a time-dependent shift for sufficiently small $H^1$ perturbations in the admissible parameter regimes. We obtain exponential decay of the shock profile and show asymptotic convergence to the shifted shock in $L^q(\R)$, $2<q\leq \infty$, with vanishing shift velocity.

title: A result of continuous stability for generalized persistence diagrams
abstract: We study persistence modules obtained from the $A$-fundamental groupoids of finite graphs. Moreover, we verify the categorical properties needed to form generalized persistence diagrams, and describe a quotient that identifies equivalent groupoids. A normalized linear presheaf construction places these modules in an essentially small abelian category, where Patel's Continuity Theorem gives a $1$-Lipschitz estimate in erosion distance. Explicit graph filtrations illustrate the groupoid-valued construction, and so we suggest a new approach to interpret persistence diagrams and large data sets in topological data analysis, based on recent works of A-homotopy theory of the last years.

title: Lieb-Robinson Light Cones in Long-Range Bosonic Systems
abstract: Lieb-Robinson bounds formulate emergent causality in quantum many-body dynamics. In this Letter, we study interacting bosonic systems with long-range interactions, in which both the standard assumptions of short-range interactions and uniformly bounded local energy scales are absent. We derive upper and lower bounds whose effective light-cone exponents are governed by a nontrivial interplay between the decay exponent $α$ and the bosonic interaction order $p$. The propagation protocol concentrates bosons within blocks, creating a mediating sublattice with amplified interactions. For $p\ge4$ and $2d<α\le2d+1$, the resulting exponents coincide, determining the optimal leading light-cone power. The upper bound includes $α=2d+1$ with arbitrarily small exponent loss, using a fixed-$k$ extension of the bounded-interaction result. Our results reveal that the interplay between long-range couplings and unbounded bosonic degrees of freedom gives rise to a richer light-cone structure than in either long-range bounded systems or short-range bosonic systems alone.

title: Free energy of spherical vector spin glasses
abstract: We identify the limit free energy of spherical vector spin glasses by a variational formula. The covariance function need not be convex. Using the global symmetry of the spin configurations, we introduce a family of constraint measures that gives a disintegration of the original spin distribution. We first identify the limit free energy of each constrained model and then apply the Laplace method to recover that of the original model.

title: The e-Property for Quantum Markov Semigroups
abstract: Let $(\mathcal T_t)_{t\geqslant0}$ be a quantum Markov semigroup on a von Neumann algebra and let $\mathcal A$ be an invariant Feller $C^*$-algebra. We formulate the $e$-property on the full state space and show that its quantitative defect is equivalent, within an optimal factor two, to the Hausdorff measure of non-compactness of observable orbits. We develop Cesàro and Lip-norm criteria and a generalised Doeblin minorisation by a state-space contracting positive map, including finite-dimensional and measure-prepare factorisations. When every observable has the $e$-property, the Jacobs--de Leeuw--Glicksberg decomposition identifies the reversible Choi--Effros algebra and the norm-stable sector. Expected and decoherence-free subalgebras transfer the property under norm decay of the complementary dynamics, including infinite-dimensional ultracontractive and finite-index Pimsner--Popa regimes. Finally, we establish the full comparison hierarchy among ordinary, eventual, Cesàro and pointwise eventual equicontinuity notions, reinforced by matrix Jamison and homoclinic flow counterexamples. Projection-face criteria are treated in a companion paper.

title: On Certain Congruences for Partition $k$-Tuples with $5$-Cores
abstract: Let $A_{t,k}(n)$ denote the number of partition $k$-tuples of $n$ with $t$-cores. Using fifth-order modular equations and the Atkin $U_5$-operator, we prove the congruences $A_{5,125i+21}(25n+r)\equiv 0 \pmod{5^3}$ for $r\in\{9,14,19,24\}$, $A_{5,125i+41}(25n+r)\equiv 0 \pmod{5^3}$ for $r\in\{19,24\}$, and $A_{5,125i+111}(125n+r)\equiv 0 \pmod{5^4}$ for $r\in\{39,64,89,114\}$, which were stated by Tang \cite{tang2025iterative}.

title: ALDER: A Single-Loop Augmented-Lagrangian Damped Extragradient Method for Nonconvex--Concave Minimax Problems with Nonlinear Coupled Constraints
abstract: ALDER, a single-loop augmented-Lagrangian damped extragradient method, is proposed for smooth nonconvex--concave minimax problems with nonlinear coupled inequality constraints. Within an augmented-Lagrangian framework, ALDER combines prediction--correction steps for the primal variables with explicit projected-and-relaxed multiplier updates in a single loop. The penalty parameter is fixed throughout each run, eliminating inner-loop subproblem solves and iterative penalty updates. We establish uniform boundedness of the relaxed multiplier sequence and, under an extended Mangasarian--Fromovitz constraint qualification, boundedness of the projected output multiplier. Building on these bounds, we show that ALDER finds an $\varepsilon$-KKT point within $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-7/2})$ complete first-order oracle evaluations in the strongly concave setting and $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-4})$ in the concave setting. These bounds improve upon the best known complexity bounds for multi-loop algorithms for this problem class, achieved by FAL, by removing a $\log(1/\varepsilon)$ factor, while retaining a single-loop update structure.

title: The Statistical Geometry of Latent Recovery in Hidden Markov Models
abstract: Hidden Markov models (HMMs) offer an important capability to interpret fitted latent states and transitions. When emission distributions nearly coincide, a small observation-density error does not ensure accurate estimation of the latent quantities needed for interpretation. This motivates us to characterize convergence rates for latent recovery that account for emission separation. Our main contribution lies in deriving deterministic inverse inequalities that convert Hellinger error between fitted and true densities into bounds on latent recovery errors. We develop these bounds for multivariate Gaussian HMMs with a common, known emission covariance matrix and combine them with a Hellinger estimation guarantee for the global maximum likelihood estimator to obtain latent recovery rates. Although the joint observation distribution is a Gaussian mixture with exponentially many path components, they share the same emission centers across time. Leveraging this shared structure, we show that the separation exponents are governed by the maximum number of simultaneously approaching centers rather than the number of path components. Under exact specification, the global bounds on state-sequence probability discrepancies and the 1-Wasserstein loss for latent location distributions exhibit sharp separation exponents that do not increase with the number of selected times. Moreover, sufficiently small observation-density error guarantees unique matching between fitted and true emission centers, which yields error bounds for individual emission centers and transition rows. Under over-specification, individual split-state transition rows are not necessarily identifiable, so we quantify aggregate latent recovery errors and show that state-sequence probability bounds incur larger separation exponents compared to exact specification. We conduct synthetic experiments to validate our theoretical results.

title: Parameter Bounds and Inverse Approximation for Linearized ReLU$^k$ Networks on the Sphere
abstract: We study direct and inverse approximation for linearized shallow ReLU$^k$ networks on $\mathbb S^d$ with quasi-uniform hidden parameters. For $0<α<\frac{d+2k+1}{2d}$, under the coefficient growth condition $\bigl(n\sum_{j=1}^na_{j,n}^2\bigr)^{\frac{1}{2}}\leq n^αM$, we prove that approximation at the order $n^{-\frac{d+2k+1}{2d}+α}$ is equivalent to membership in the parity-compatible Besov space $\mathcal B_{2,\infty,*}^{\frac{d+2k+1}{2}-αd}(\mathbb S^d)$. Mere convergence under the same coefficient budget does not imply this regularity. For unconstrained approximation along a nested parameter sequence, a single ridge function gives a counterexample when $α<\frac{1}{2}$, whereas for $α>\frac{1}{2}$ the endpoint Besov inverse conclusion follows from a Bernstein inequality under antipodal quasi-uniformity. The inverse conclusion is also recovered when the prescribed rate holds for two quasi-uniform parameter sequences whose union is antipodally separated.

title: Cyclotomic polynomials with trinomial irreducible factors over finite fields
abstract: We classify the pairs $(q,n)$, where $q$ is a prime power, $n>1$, and $\gcd(n,q)=1$, for which every irreducible factor of $Φ_n(x)$ over $\F_q$ has exactly three nonzero terms. The positive support exponents of these factors have a common greatest common divisor, which gives a unique reduction by a power substitution. The reduced degree is two in odd characteristic and belongs to $\{2,3,4\}$ in characteristic two; the cubic and quartic cases arise by scalar substitution from the layers of orders $7$ and $15$. This yields necessary and sufficient arithmetic conditions on $(q,n)$ and explicit factorizations. Among the classified families, precisely those arising from quartic bases have a divisor layer containing an irreducible factor with more than three terms.

title: A dual approach to $L^p$ estimates for orthogonal martingales satisfying the differential subordination
abstract: We develop a new dual approach, which can be used to establish sharp $L^p$ bounds for orthogonal differentially subordinate martingales. The method rests on the construction of a certain special function enjoying appropriate majorization properties and a novel differential condition.

title: Closed-Form Gaussian Mixture Representations of d-Dimensional Triangulated Domains
abstract: We derive a Gaussian Mixture (GM) representation of a full-dimensional subset of Euclidean space with finite volume from a finite simplicial triangulation in closed form. On each simplex, we replace the uniform probability density function (PDF) with a Gaussian PDF that minimizes the Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence, arriving at the information projection onto the family of Gaussian PDFs. By exploiting affine isomorphisms between simplices, the joint convexity and bijection invariance properties of the KL divergence, identities for Dirichlet PDFs, and a partition-of-unity argument, we establish a dimension-dependent but geometry-independent sharp upper bound on the global KL divergence between the resulting GM PDF and the uniform PDF on the original domain. Numerical examples illustrate the construction and demonstrate its potential in practical applications.

title: Auslander-type grade conditions and subcategories related to syzygy modules
abstract: The question of when a syzygy module or a module satisfying a Serre condition satisfies the cohomological vanishing conditions known as higher torsionfreeness has been extensively studied. In this paper, we address these questions using grade conditions introduced and studied by Auslander-Bridger and Auslander-Reiten. We also investigate homological conditions on Ext modules and, as an application, give a partial answer over commutative rings to a question of Auslander-Bridger concerning whether higher reflexive modules are higher torsionfree.

title: Stacked-bases Properties, maximal ideals and polynomial closures of Rings of Integer-Valued Polynomials
abstract: We study the integer-valued polynomial ring with the stacked-bases property, maximal ideals above valuation ideals, and the polynomial closure of matrices with prescribed characteristic polynomials. A content argument gives stacked-bases properties for integer-valued polynomial rings over number-field integer rings. The construction of Hagg and Mortberg provides a Bezout domain without this property. For rank-one valuation domains, maximal ideals are described by evaluations and pseudo-convergent sequences. For matrices, we give congruence-ideal and companion-lattice criteria, together with finite-level tests to characterize the polynomial closures.

title: Euler discretizations, invariant faces and brackets for lower exponents of positive switched systems
abstract: In this paper, we prove that explicit and implicit Euler discretizations yield monotone brackets for the lower Lyapunov exponent of positive switched systems. We establish convergence of the implicit bound for every Metzler family. For the explicit bound, we derive convergence criteria in reducible systems from a face formula for the uniform lower exponent on an invariant cone. The formula takes the minimum of the rates on faces that meet the cone nontrivially and are preserved by at least one mode, using only their preserving modes. For individually irreducible modes, we prove O(h) discretization errors, where h is the step size, and show that this order is sharp in general. At interior two-mode chattering optima with an irreducible optimal mixture, we obtain one-sided first-order bounds. We also construct a three-mode example in which the explicit bound converges while finite polytope lower bounds remain capped strictly below the true exponent. We prove convergence of fixed-antinorm Gripenberg brackets under individual irreducibility as the step and tolerance decrease and the search depth increases appropriately. Finally, we obtain independently verified continuous-time brackets by exact rational checks, with lower bounds that remain valid at smaller steps.

title: Relative Rouquier linearity and inverse hybrid Kazhdan-Lusztig positivity
abstract: We prove signed positivity for the expansion of a parabolic hybrid basis in the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis of a Hecke algebra. The coefficients have degree bounded by the length of the corresponding minimal coset representative. We deduce this linearity from Elias-Williamson's ordinary Rouquier linearity by a truncation argument. The result does not require the parabolic subgroup to be finite.

title: Radial conditions for global compact finite propagation for divergence-form elliptic operators
abstract: We study global compact finite propagation (GCFP) for the wave equation $u_{tt}=\operatorname{div}(A(x)\nabla u)$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, that is, the property that a disturbance starting in a compact set cannot reach spatial infinity in finite time. For smooth strictly positive matrices $A$ we show that GCFP implies $\int_1^\infty a_*(r)^{-1/2}\,dr=\infty$, where $a_*(r)$ is the minimum over the sphere of radius $r$ of $\langle Aω,ω\rangle$; the proof uses the equivalence of GCFP with completeness of the Riemannian metric $A^{-1}$, of which we prove the necessary direction for the cosine family of the Friedrichs extension. We also prove that the analogous divergence condition with $a^*(r)$, the maximum over the sphere, is sufficient, and that this holds for measurable coefficients $A\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ with $A\ge I$. Finally, we construct a locally bounded measurable matrix with $a_*=a^*$ for which GCFP holds although the integral converges, so the necessary condition is not stable under the loss of continuity.

title: Laplacian Pair State Transfer on Edge Coronas
abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with edge set $E(G) = \{e_1, \ldots, e_m\}$, and let $\mathcal{H} = (H_1, \ldots, H_m)$ be an $m$-tuple of graphs. The edge corona $G\diamond\mathcal{H}$ is obtained from the disjoint union of $G,H_1,\ldots,H_m$ by joining both end vertices of each edge $e_j$ to every vertex of $H_j$ for $1\leq j\leq m$. In this paper, we investigate Laplacian perfect pair state transfer and Laplacian pretty good pair state transfer on edge coronas. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of Laplacian perfect pair state transfer. We also derive sufficient conditions for the non-existence of Laplacian perfect pair state transfer. Further, we identify conditions under which the absence of Laplacian perfect pair state transfer guarantees the existence of Laplacian pretty good pair state transfer. Additionally, we develop constructions based on Cartesian product and tensor product to obtain a few more infinite families of edge coronas admitting Laplacian pretty good pair state transfer. Finally, we investigate the existence of Laplacian pretty good pair state transfer on the edge corona of complete graphs.

title: Regions of totally real arrangements of rational curves
abstract: We prove a plane-curve analogue of Zaslavsky's theorem for arrangements of real rational curves for which every complex singularity with more than one local branch is real and all of its branches are real. If at least one component has odd degree, the number of real regions equals the total rational Betti number of the complexified complement. We also give a formula for bounded affine regions which records the number of branches at infinity and the connected components of the real affine curve. Oriented regions generate the middle Borel--Moore homology over $\mathbb{Q}$, and they generate it over $\mathbb{Z}$ when the component degrees are coprime. The relations are described by the circles in the real normalization and, in an affine chart, by winding functions. These results imply equality of combinatorial rank and real combinatorial rank in the framework of Brown--Dupont and Sturmfels--Telen. Examples include singular rational cubics, arrangements of conics, Chebyshev curves, and the plane model of the $27$ lines on a split cubic surface.

title: When are dividend barriers optimal? A distributional characterization in renewal risk models
abstract: We study the finite-horizon optimal dividend problem in a renewal risk model with unrestricted dividend payments, examining how claim-size distributions determine barrier optimality. Under general assumptions on a fixed interclaim-time distribution, we prove that exponential claims admit a globally optimal barrier for every positive safety loading, positive discount rate and finite horizon. Conversely, within the class of claim-size distributions with continuous nondecreasing hazard, every nonexponential law admits one fixed premium--discount pair for which no barrier is globally optimal at any sufficiently long horizon. These results establish, within this distribution class, an equivalence between exponentially distributed claims and the existence of a globally optimal barrier for every parameter combination in the stated range. Numerical examples compare exponential and Gamma claims with the same mean and illustrate how the claim-size distribution changes the structure of dividend decisions.

title: Maxima of the Q-index: Forbidden an odd wheel
abstract: In 2013, Freitas, Nikiforov and Patuzzi (EJLA, 2013) proposed the problem of determining the maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius of an $n$-vertex $F$-free graph. Recently, Yuan, Zhai and Zhang (LAA, 2026) determined the maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius of graphs without wheels of sufficiently large order. In this paper, we consider the problem of forbidding a single wheel $W_{2k+1}=K_1\vee C_{2k}$. We show that, for every fixed integer $k\ge 3$ and sufficiently large $n$, the unique extremal graph maximizing the signless Laplacian spectral radius among all $n$-vertex $W_{2k+1}$-free graphs is $K_k\vee(K_2\cup(n-k-2)K_1)$.

title: Stable compatibility for model categories
abstract: By introducing the notion of stable compatibility, we provide a framework in the model category theory which addresses the existence of a stable model structure on the category of modules over a monad. Exact version of such monads have been studied in the setting of triangulated categories, separately as separable monads a la Balmer in tensor triangular geometry and non-separable monads a la Dell'Ambrogio and Sanders in stable homotopy theory. By introducing stable compatibility, we explore their properties together and produce a non-separable monad in Algebraic geometry and more.

title: Partial coactions of Hopf algebras on nonunital algebras and categories
abstract: In this paper, we introduce and investigate partial coactions of a Hopf algebra on an associative, possibly nonunital algebra and on $\Bbbk$-linear categories. We prove that every partial coaction has a globalization in a broad sense. We study in detail the case of a partial coaction on an algebra with local units; we prove that such a coaction is always induced from a global coaction, and we show that there exists a naturally associated $\Bbbk$-linear category endowed with a partial coaction.

title: Hodge theory and topology of Bogomolov--Guan manifolds
abstract: Bogomolov--Guan manifolds are simply connected, irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds that are not Kähler, yet they echo hyperkähler geometry in striking ways. We show that their Frölicher spectral sequence degenerates at $E_1$ and that their Hodge numbers are stable under small deformations. The general fibers of their natural Lagrangian fibration are rationally null-homologous, and the Beauville--Bogomolov--Fujiki form is degenerate. Despite this, in every dimension, the Euler characteristics agree with those of generalized Kummer manifolds. In dimensions four and six, we compute the full Hodge diamonds and all Chern and Pontryagin numbers. Surprisingly, these characteristic numbers are the same as the generalized Kummer ones, even though the Betti numbers differ and the Hodge diamonds are asymmetric.

title: Fermat curves and explicit class field theory for real quadratic number fields
abstract: We use Fermat curves with real multiplication and classical CM theory to construct an explicit class field theory for arbitrary real quadratic number fields. The underlying strategy is well-established in computational class field theory, our main contribution is a geometric model to realize this strategy explicitly. This approach complements the recent breakthrough works solving conjectures by Brumer, Stark and Shintani and gives an alternative constructive solution to Hilbert's 12th problem for real quadratic fields.

title: Online Autotuning of Algebraic Multigrid via Contextual Bandits and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Algebraic multigrid (AMG) methods are widely used for solving large sparse linear systems, but their efficiency depends strongly on interacting setup and solve parameters. Effective parameter choices typically depend on the problem. We develop a phase-aware online autotuning method for hypre's BoomerAMG to reduce cumulative time-to-solution over sequences of related linear systems. A LinUCB-based contextual bandit selects mixed-type parameters for AMG hierarchy construction using a shared cost model over PDE descriptors and configuration encodings. A recursive LSTDQ controller uses residual and timing observations to estimate the AMG solve time within each attempt and adapt relaxation weights between multigrid cycles. Both learners update from ongoing solves without offline pretraining. Across grids of sizes $40^3$, $60^3$, and $80^3$, the joint autotuning method reduces total runtime, including recurring learner computation, by 36.1-43.3% for diffusion problems and 19.8-31.0% for diffusion-advection problems over sequences of 5000 linear systems, relative to the reference BoomerAMG default configuration. On a variable-flow diffusion-advection benchmark comprising 30,000 systems on a $60^3$ grid, 2 systems fail to converge with joint autotuning, compared with 1677 for the reference configuration, under their respective attempt budgets.

title: Some Characterisations of the Strichartz Fourier Transform on the Heisenberg Group
abstract: Recently, Thangavelu introduced a scalar-valued Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group, built from the joint spectral theory of the sublaplacian and the central vector field. Around the same time, Krukowski characterised the classical Fourier transform on various groups from a small number of structural properties, paired with a normalisation hypothesis. In this paper, we obtain analogous results for the Strichartz Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group. Here, the spectral property is formulated jointly for the sublaplacian and the central vector field, and the translation property is based on a twisted form of left translation. The joint spectral property, paired with the twisted translation property and a normalisation at a single explicit test function, characterises the Strichartz Fourier transform on each ray of the underlying spectral set, the Heisenberg fan. The twisted translation property alone, paired with a Dirac delta property, already suffices. We also characterise the radial kernel of the transform on each ray by a Laguerre-type differential equation.

title: A matroid characterization of the combinatorially symmetric maximum nullity of a graph
abstract: The graph parameter ${\mathrm N}(G)$ is the maximum nullity among all combinatorially symmetric matrices associated to a graph $G$. The zero forcing number ${\mathrm Z}(G)$ is a well-known upper bound for ${\mathrm N}(G)$, and a zero forcing set of $G$ is exactly a set that intersects each fort of the graph. So the zero forcing number can be defined as the size of a minimum set that intersects every fort of $G$. This paper provides a similar characterization of ${\mathrm N}(G)$ that is purely combinatorial, using a connection to matroid theory and collections of forts that are compatible in a certain sense. We provide several examples highlighting subtle differences among compatible collections of forts and how they relate to full spark matrices and matroids associated to $G$.

title: From Gaussian to stable and back: Non-Pareto points in growing dimension
abstract:
We study the number of non-Pareto points in two high-dimensional models: a homogeneous Poisson point process and a fixed-size sample of independent uniform points in the unit cube. A point is non-Pareto if some other sample point is coordinatewise less than or equal to it. As the dimension grows on the logarithmic scale of the intensity or sample size, the asymptotic behavior exhibits a surprising sequence of transitions: from Gaussian to stable fluctuations, back to Gaussian, then to a Poisson limit at the sparsity threshold, followed by the eventual disappearance of non-Pareto points.
  We identify the critical thresholds, normalizations, and limiting laws in both models. Notably, the return to Gaussianity occurs while the stability index remains strictly below $2$ and is driven by a change in the dominant fluctuation mechanism. Moreover, in part of the returning Gaussian regime, the natural normalization is the square root of the expected count rather than its standard deviation. At the stable--Gaussian transition, the two mechanisms can coexist, giving rise to a sum of independent stable and Gaussian random variables.

title: A relative version of Weinstein's morphism
abstract:
We introduce a relative version of Weinstein's morphism associated to a
  Lagrangian submanifold \(L\) of a closed symplectic manifold
  \((M,ω)\). We construct a homomorphism
  \[
  \mathcal{A}^{(L,α)}\colon
  π_{1}\bigl(\operatorname{Ham}_0(M,L)\bigr)
  \longrightarrow
  \mathbb{R}/\mathcal{P}_{2}(M,ω),
  \]
  and establish its basic properties. We compute the invariant
  in several examples, including latitude circles in \(S^2\), and more generally, Lagrangian fibers in toric manifolds. These computations provide
  obstructions to Ha\-mil\-to\-nian isotopy of Lagrangian submanifolds and detect
  nontrivial, and in some cases infinite-order, elements in the homotopy
  groups of their Hamiltonian stabilizers.

title: Two types of averaging principles for multiplicative stochastic Korteweg-de Vries equations with fast oscillations
abstract: In this paper, we study averaging principles for stochastic KdV equations perturbed by a fast oscillating term generated by a stochastic reaction-diffusion equation in $H^s(\mathbb{R})$, $ s\geq 0$. When dealing with multilinear estimates of the nonlinear terms in the stochastic KdV type equation, two kinds of workspace are both effective. The classical workspace can help us prove the averaging principle in the $L_ω^2$ sense, but it has more restrictions on the noise kernel and the conservation structures. When we use a new workspace without homogeneous low frequency restrictions, only the regularity conditions and the $L_x^2$ conservation structure is needed. Correspondingly, because there is no moment estimate of the solution, we can only prove the perturbed equations converge to an averaging equation in the probability sense. Our works may have important reference value, because it not only provides a new perspective to handle dynamical problems of stochastic dispersive model, but also compare it with the classical method.

title: Impact Mechanism of a Point Interaction in the Cubic Half-Wave Equation: Well-Posedness, Constrained Energy Levels and Near-Critical Rigidity
abstract: We study the one-dimensional nonlinear half-wave equation with a logarithmically renormalized point interaction. The nonlinearity is focusing and cubic, which is mass-critical. We establish well-posedness in the energy space using a new method for unconditional uniqueness that requires no auxiliary Strichartz assumption. We reveal the mechanism by which the point interaction affects ground states. The free critical mass is the sharp threshold: fixed-mass ground states exist and are orbitally stable below it, whereas at and above it the constrained energy is unbounded from below. We also prove a near-critical rigidity result showing that bounded energy concentrating sequences converge to free ground states after rescaling.

title: Alternative Tikhonov-Type Regularization for the Calderón Inverse Conductivity Problem
abstract: This paper investigates the application of two regularization methods, classical Tikhonov and Alternative Tikhonov regularization, to the Calderón inverse conductivity problem. We develop an iterative reconstruction scheme based on linearizing the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map and approximating conductivity updates using Gaussian basis functions. The resulting linear systems are solved using both regularization methods, with particular attention given to the derivation and numerical implementation of Alternative Tikhonov regularization. We compare the performance of these methods through numerical experiments on a synthetic conductivity containing two localized regions of differing conductivity. A total of 666 reconstruction tests are performed across varying regularization parameters, damping factors, and iteration counts. The lowest relative reconstruction errors obtained are 0.064730 for Alternative Tikhonov and 0.065173 for classical Tikhonov regularization. Although both methods produce comparable reconstructions, Alternative Tikhonov achieves the lowest observed error. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of both approaches within the proposed reconstruction scheme and motivate further investigation into parameter selection, numerical stability, and reconstruction accuracy.

title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems I: The Half-Plane
abstract: In this paper, the first in a series devoted to finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in domains with boundaries, we establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse for three vortices in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}^+$. Our approach treats the boundary-induced interactions as a perturbation of the classical self-similar Gröbli collapse in the full plane. Under suitable conditions on the vortex circulations and collapse profile, we prove the existence of a one-dimensional local strong stable manifold of the augmented rescaled system, which generates exact solutions in which three distinct vortices collapse simultaneously at any prescribed interior point $z^*\in\mathbb{H}^+$. Moreover, these solutions are asymptotically self-similar, with the characteristic square-root collapse rate $O(\sqrt{T-t})$.

title: Curvature pinching for minimal Tangent-Yang-Mills hypersurfaces in spheres
abstract: We prove a rigidity theorem for closed connected minimal Tangent-Yang-Mills hypersurfaces in the unit sphere. In every dimension $n\geqslant 3$, such a hypersurface is totally geodesic if the squared norm of its Riemannian curvature tensor is at most $2n(n-1)$.

title: The Golden Quadruple: Four Reals Whose Differences Form a Geometric Progression, Rigidity of the Golden Ratio, and a Bohr Almost Periodic Cosine Sum
abstract: Let $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$. The four-point set $\{0,\varphi,\varphi^2,\varphi^3\}$ is classical: up to a dilation it consists of the two endpoints and the two crossing points on a side of the regular pentagram (Euclid, Elements XIII.8), and, by the identity $\varphi^2=\varphi+1$, its six pairwise differences are $1,\varphi,\varphi^2,\varphi^3$, with multiplicities $1,2,2,1$. We write this configuration as the golden quadruple $S=(F, F-a, F-b, F-a-b)$, where $u>0$, $a=\varphi u$, $b=\varphi^2u$ and $F>a+b$, and study its extremal and rigidity properties. We prove that it is maximal and unique: no five distinct real numbers have all their positive differences in $\{u,\varphi u,\varphi^2u,\varphi^3u\}$ (indeed, not even in the whole set $\{u\varphi^n:n\in\mathbb{Z}\}$), and every four-element set with this property is a translate of $S$. We prove that the golden ratio is forced: $\varphi$ is the only ratio $x>1$ for which some four-point set of reals has the four-term progression $\{c,cx,cx^2,cx^3\}$ as its set of distinct differences. For the analogous quadruple with base $x>1$, $x\neq\varphi$, the failure is measured by two closure residues, $(x^2-x-1)u$ and $x(x^2-x-1)u$, which along Fibonacci quotients equal $\pm u/F_n^2$ and $\pm F_{n+1}u/F_n^3$. Finally, the cosine sum $C_S(t)=\sum\cos(2πd t)$ over the six differences equals $8\cos^2(πa t)\cos^2(πb t)-2$; it is not periodic, but it is almost periodic in the sense of Bohr, with explicit almost periods $F_n/u$. For an arbitrary scale $K>0$ the golden ladder $ν_n=K\varphi^{-n}$ realises the construction with $u=ν_{203}$, so that the differences are $ν_{200},\dots,ν_{203}$; we evaluate it for $K=\sqrt{c^5/(Gh)}$. We state explicitly what is classical and what is new, in relation to difference sets, Golomb rulers, Sidon sets, Fibonacci numbers, quasicrystals and almost periodic functions.

title: Categorifications of noncrossing partitions of type B and affine type A
abstract: The lattice of wide subcategories of a tube is isomorphic to the lattice of noncrossing partitions of type B. We prove that through this categorification of noncrossing partitions, Kreweras complement is taking left perpendicular categories. With the help of this categorification and weighted projective lines, we obtain an inclusion from the lattice of noncrossing partitions of type B_n to a lattice of affine type A_n which preserves Kreweras complement.

title: Explicit Boundary-Entropy Deficits in the XX Spin Chain with arbitrary boundary fields
abstract: The exact thermodynamics of the XX spin-1/2 chain with arbitrary Hermitian boundary fields is constructed via fusion techniques. The rigorous result shows that (1) each end with a nonzero transverse field contributes $+\frac12T\ln2$ to the low-temperature free energy, whereas strictly diagonal and free ends contribute no such linear term; (2) each nondiagonal end has a characteristic temperature $T_B$, which scales as $T_B\propto h_\perp^2/J$ in the weak-field regime. For $T\ll\min\{J,T_B\}$, the boundary entropy approaches a deficit of $\frac12\ln2$ relative to a diagonal end. As the transverse field tends to zero, the boundary crossover scale vanishes and the low-temperature expansion becomes nonuniform. The present result provides a clear benchmark not only for the boundary thermodynamics of open boundary quantum integrable systems, but also for dot defects in quantum critical systems.

title: Density functionals for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian
abstract: We develop a density-functional theory for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian of nonrelativistic quantum electrodynamics in the spirit of the convex-analytic formulation of Lieb. We consider finitely many electrons, subject to external scalar and vector potentials, coupled to the full continuum of massless transverse photons with an ultraviolet cutoff. The natural basic variables are the standard electron density and a combined current density, the sum of the paramagnetic current density and a field-induced current density generated by the quantized vector potential. We prove representability results for these density-current pairs and show that the mixed-state constrained-search functional attains its infimum and coincides with the Lieb functional obtained by convex conjugation. Since arbitrarily soft photons purify mixed states at a negligible energy cost without changing their density and combined current density, the pure-state Levy-Lieb functional equals the Lieb functional and is therefore convex, even though its infimum need not be attained. In addition, we establish the zero-coupling limit, which recovers the mixed-state Vignale-Rasolt functional of current-density-functional theory. Finally, we consider the long-wavelength (dipole) limit and show that the limiting functional can be written as a constrained search for the well-known length-gauge dipole Hamiltonian.

title: Modular proof analysis and cut elimination for the Reflection Calculi $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$
abstract:
The reflection calculus with one modality is denoted by $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and its quantified generalization is known as $\mathsf{QRC}_1$. These decidable calculi are of interest since they generate the strictly positive fragments of the (quantified) provability logic for theories like Peano Arithmetic and Heyting Arithmetic.
  We introduce analytic cut-free calculi ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ and ${\mathrm{GQRC1}}$ for $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$ respectively. The new calculi derive sequents of the form $A\Longrightarrow B$ with $A,B$ strictly positive formulas. In particular, the new calculi do not use (multi)sets nor nested sequents.
  For both ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ and ${\mathrm{GQRC1}}$ it is shown that the cut-rule is admissible. As a consequence, it is proven that the calculi are deductively equivalent to $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$ respectively. The cutfree systems are used to prove uniform interpolation for the two reflection calculi.
  In addition, ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ is used to give a syntactic proof of Dashkov's Theorem to the extent that $\mathsf{RC}_1$ is the strictly positive fragment of the provability logic ${\mathsf{GL}}$.
  The paper also introduces non-analytic calculi that are conceptually easier but proof-theoretically behave badly. It is shown that even those systems allow direct cut-elimination: the benefits of the strict positivity outweigh the draw-backs of a non-analytic calculus in these cases.

title: When Pedal Shapes Come Back: a Complex Story
abstract: Under the usual nondegeneracy assumptions, repeatedly projecting a fixed point onto the side lines of an $n$-gon returns its shape after $n$ steps. We explain this classical theorem through a short complex-number identity: the multipliers of one step move cyclically around the polygon. The same calculation allows a different common angle of projection at each step. A sharp angle-dependent contraction bound identifies the incircle centre as the maximiser for tangential polygons. In space, even a regular tetrahedron can fail to recover its shape after four steps. We give an exact example, then show how concentric inscribed and circumscribed spheres restore a two-step return. Rectangular boxes provide a further four-step family.

title: Resonance varieties of Schubert arrangements
abstract: We compute the resonance varieties of the Orlik--Solomon algebras of Schubert matroids. Previously known results have been largely confined to matroids of rank $3$, and the Schubert matroids give a family of nontrivial examples of arbitrary rank. We give an expression for the cohomology of the Orlik--Solomon algebra that we show holds for Schubert matroids as well as for simple, complex-realizable rank-$3$ matroids that do not support multinets. Our proof introduces a family of matroids for which the Orlik--Solomon algebra is isomorphic to an exterior Stanley--Reisner algebra.

title: Linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant. III
abstract:
This paper is the third in the series of papers devoted to the explicit description of linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant of rectangular matrices of size $n\times k$ with entries belonging to an arbitrary ground field which is large enough.
  In this part we study the remaining case where $k = 3$ and $n \ge k + 2 = 5$ and prove that every linear map preserving the Cullis' determinant admits the same description as for the case where $k \ge 4$ and $n \ge k + 2$ obtained previously.

title: The Lorentz Threshold in Fourier Restriction
abstract: Classical Stein--Tomas restriction controls a Fourier transform on a curved surface, but the estimate changes when its values lie in a Banach space. We determine the sharp Lorentz threshold at the critical exponent $4/3$: for coefficients in $\ell_D^{4/3,q}$, the optimal Gaussian restriction constant grows like $(1+\log D)^{|3/4-1/q|}$. A multiscale wave-packet construction proves sharpness, including the delicate index $q=2$. The same threshold holds for fractional Gaussian noise, while Gaussian type and cotype alone do not distinguish the positive and negative cases. As a dispersive consequence, we establish a sharp Lorentz-channel spacetime estimate for linear capillary waves.

title: Casson invariant of knots defined by random braids
abstract: We investigate the expectation $E(v_2)$ of the Casson invariant $v_2$ for knots represented by two similar types of braids, the rosette $s$-braids which are products of $k$ factors $\prod_{1\leq 2i\leq s}σ_{2i}^{\pm 1}\prod_{1\leq 2i+\leq s}σ_{2i+1}^{\pm 1}$ and the quasitoric $s$-braids which are products of $k$ factors $σ_{1}^{\pm 1}σ_{2}^{\pm 1}...σ_{s-1}^{\pm 1}$. If $k$ is of the form $ns+1$, $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{s+1}{24}$ where $c$ is the number of crossing points of braid; if $k$ is of the form $ns-1$, $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{5-s}{24}$.\\ If we go through all $3$-braids, regardless of the shape of their diagram, we get $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{1}{8}$. \\ For knots with a checkerboard diagram, $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{1}{16}$.

title: Lyapunov functions for the Langevin equation with dissipative damping
abstract: We study the well-posedness and the large time stability of the Langevin equation in the presence of potentials and dissipative damping together with additive white noise. While the confining potential is assumed to be smooth, the nonlinear damping is allowed to have either polynomial growth or singular behaviors. We construct novel Lyapunov functions and determine the corresponding parameter regimes that lead to global well-posedness or finite-time explosion. These Lyapunov functions also allow for deriving quantitative mixing rates toward equilibrium. Our results extend existing ergodic theory established for the instance of nonlinear damping satisfying suitable integrability conditions.

title: An Incidence-Based Edge-Averaged Method for Convection-Diffusion Problems on Polytopal Meshes
abstract: We develop an incidence-based edge-averaged method for scalar convection-diffusion problems on convex polytopal meshes in arbitrary dimensions. The proposed method extends the classical edge-averaged finite-element scheme through a graph-theoretic formulation based on vertex-edge incidence matrices. We first establish this formulation on simplices in arbitrary dimensions and then extend it to convex polytopes by introducing complementary edges and generalized barycentric coordinates. A key ingredient is a matrix identity that relates the generalized Whitney edge mass matrix to a diagonal representation of the Poisson stiffness matrix, enabling an exponentially-fitted discretization expressed entirely in terms of nodal values and edge weights. We prove that the resulting stiffness matrix is a nonsingular $M$-matrix under suitable positivity and connectivity conditions, ensuring monotonicity and the discrete maximum principle.
