As an application, we derive recursive formulas for the number of topologically distinct homoclinic flows on the two-dimensional sphere and compute these numbers for flows with a small number of saddle singularities and closed orbits.

title: Asymptotic delta-like behavior of the weighted taper in Thomson's multitaper F-test
abstract: We study the weighted taper arising in Thomson's multitaper F test, which is constructed from pre-plunge discrete prolate spheroidal wave functions (DPSWF). Numerical evidence suggests that, in the asymptotic regime, the Fourier transform of this taper converges to a delta measure supported at the origin. We provide a rigorous theoretical justification for this behavior.

title: On closed symmetric monoidal enriched $\infty$-categories
abstract: We show that a closed symmetric monoidal V-enriched $\infty$-category can be described by a lax symmetric monoidal functor to V from its underlying $\infty$-category.

title: Quadratic bounds for intersecting hypergraphs: An affirmative answer to a question of Duke and Erdős
abstract: Let $m(k,b)$ denote the minimum number of edges in an intersecting $k$-uniform hypergraph in which every $(k-1)$-set of vertices is disjoint from at least $b$ edges, with $m(k,b)=+\infty$ if no such hypergraph exists. Duke and Erdős [Congressus Numerantium (1980)] asked whether $m(k,k)=o(k^4)$ is possible. In this paper, we answer this question affirmatively and determine the order of growth of $m(k,k)$ by proving that $k^2+1\leq m(k,k)\leq Ck^2$ for all sufficiently large $k$, where $C$ is an absolute constant. More generally, we show that $m(k,b)=Θ(kb)$ for all sufficiently large odd $k$ and every integer $b$ with $k\leq b\leq (k-1)(k-3)/2$, where the implied constants are independent of $k$ and $b$.

title: On cylindrical directions of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ derived from contact with spherical cylinders
abstract: We investigate the contact of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with spherical cylinders $S^2(r) \times \mathbb{R}$. We introduce cylindrical directions of these surfaces, defined by the axes of spherical cylinders having degenerate contact with the surfaces, and show that these directions capture the ridge condition of projected regular surfaces under orthogonal projection along these directions.

title: How the eigenvalue region of standardized Laplacians leaves the 2005 polygon
abstract: Let $Λ_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of $n\times n$ standardized Laplacian matrices, and let $S_n\subseteqΛ_n$ be the polygon introduced in 2005, with upper vertices $λ_0=0,\dots,λ_{n-1}=1$. It is now known that $Λ_n=S_n$, and that $Λ_n$ is convex, if and only if $n\le4$. We study how $Λ_n$ leaves $S_n$ near an edge $[λ_m,λ_{m+1}]$, $2(m+1)<n$. First, we prove a switching law for matrices having a boundary point of $Λ_n$ as a simple eigenvalue: an explicit switching function on the arcs, built from the left and right eigenvectors and the outward normal, forces maximal weight where positive and zero weight where negative; intermediate weights occur only where it vanishes. Second, we perturb the weights of the arcs $k\to k+m+1$ in the circulant digraph (arcs $k\to k+s$, $1\le s\le m$, plus these arcs with weight $τ$) that realizes the point $λ_m+τ(λ_{m+1}-λ_m)$. At second order, the first Fourier harmonic of the perturbation moves the eigenvalue beyond the line of the edge if and only if $τ<τ^*_m=\sin(πm/n)/(2\cos(π/n)\sin(π(m+1)/n))$. For even $n$ and $m$, the point with $τ=τ^*_m$ is the vertex of $S_{n/2}$ lying on this edge, and digraphs with these arcs only at even $k$ give an explicit eigenvalue path that leaves $S_n$ at $λ_m$ and, in all computed cases, ends at this vertex. Third, we give a conjectural, numerically supported picture of $\partialΛ_5$: beyond each edge of $S_5$ not incident to $0$ or $1$, $Λ_5$ forms a cap bounded by four algebraic arcs, which leaves the edge tangentially at its endpoint adjacent to $0$ or $1$ and rejoins it at $τ^*_1=(3-\sqrt5)/2$; the rest of the edge lies on $\partialΛ_5$. In computations for $n\le8$, a cap returns to its edge smoothly at $τ^*_m$, at a corner at $τ^*_m$, or at a corner beyond $τ^*_m$.

title: Omitting Types for Infinitary Real-Valued Logic: A Topological Perspective
abstract: For countable vocabularies, we extend the omitting types theorem for countable fragments of infinitary logic to Keisler's general real-valued structures by proving that the space of Henkin types of each such fragment is Čech-complete. The structures interpret function symbols arbitrarily and predicate symbols by bounded real-valued functions, while each formula carries a bound of its own. This extends the setting of Eagle's theorem from metric structures with a prescribed master metric to general structures whose vocabulary prescribes the sorts and bounds of the symbols. Following Keisler and Miller's treatment of logic without equality, we build models from closed terms. Morley's Baire category method then gives every satisfiable theory on a countable fragment a model with countable sorts omitting any countable family of types whose closed-term instances have empty interior in the space of Henkin types satisfying the theory.

title: On the Conditional Consistency of the Bootstrap
abstract: This paper focuses on the conditional consistency of the bootstrap. The target is the conditional law of a statistic given a common shock, and the bootstrap approximates it by the law of a resampled statistic conditional on the shock and the data. We call the bootstrap consistent if these laws are close in the Kolmogorov distance for almost every realization of the shock. The conditioning $σ$-algebras are allowed to be unrelated across sample sizes, and both the comparison law and the dimension of the data may vary with the sample size. We give sufficient conditions for consistency in this sense, show that they yield asymptotically correct conditional coverage for bootstrap quantiles, and provide a finite-sample bound on the coverage error. We also relate the Kolmogorov formulation to the merging of probability measures. The results are specialized to statistics depending smoothly on an estimator or on an estimated nuisance parameter.

title: Weak and Sharp Stretched-Exponential Flocking in the Kinetic Cucker-Smale Model with Noncompactly Supported Initial Data
abstract: We study the long-time behavior of the kinetic Cucker-Smale model under initial data with unbounded support in both position and velocity. Such data invalidate classical diameter-based flocking arguments and make sustained spatial cohesion difficult to establish. We prove an estimate for spatial characteristics under a finite spatial second moment and a sufficiently high velocity moment, without any requirement on coupling strength. We also prove weak flocking, i.e. control of spatial variance and integrability of velocity fluctuations in time. Under stronger assumptions on the initial tails, we establish uniform propagation of spatial exponential moments of explicitly determined order, a substantially stronger conclusion than bounded spatial variance. These estimates lead to explicit stretched-exponential rates of velocity alignment and convergence of the centered spatial distribution toward a limiting profile. Another contribution is the construction of countably atomic solutions that show optimality of the decay exponent in the spatial-tail-limited class. Together, the results clarify how initial phase-space tails govern spatial confinement and quantitative flocking for kinetic distributions without compact support.

title: A Quasisymmetric Analogue of the Bruhat Order
abstract:
We define a quasisymmetric analogue of the Bruhat order on indexed binary forests using the multiplicity-free Monk rule for forest polynomials. For the finite window $\mathcal{P}_n$ of forests supported in $[1,n]$, we construct an explicit partition into saturated chains terminating at the top rank, proving that $\mathcal{P}_n$ is strongly Sperner. We also recover the known Catalan ballot formula for its rank numbers.
  For principal lower intervals, we prove that $[\varnothing,F]$ is a lattice if and only if it is Boolean, and characterize this property by the avoidance of a bent corner in $F$, a path of three internal vertices that changes direction. This gives a forest analogue of the pattern-avoidance characterization of Boolean principal Bruhat intervals. We also conjecture that every principal lower interval is shellable, providing computational evidence and proving the conjecture for a family of hook intervals.

title: Fisher--Hartwig asymptotics and critical moments for the circular beta ensemble
abstract:
We determine the joint moments of real powers of the absolute value of characteristic polynomials in the circular beta ensemble, for every $β>0$. At fixed distinct prescribed points, the Fisher--Hartwig formula holds for every exponent greater than $-1$, with explicit constants and a relative error bounded by a negative power of the matrix size $N$. For approaching points in the same integrable range, the error is bounded by a negative power of $Nδ_N$, provided that $Nδ_N\to\infty$ and the sum of the absolute values of the negative exponents is less than two. Here $δ_N$ is the minimum distance between the prescribed points; this range includes every integrable pair of root exponents.
  For $q>0$ at the critical relation $pq^2=2β$, we prove the Keating--Wong asymptotic for the $p$th moment of the integral of the $q$th absolute power of the characteristic polynomial, for every real $p>1$. The leading asymptotic extends to every complex spatial weight in $L^p$. The proofs combine the recursion for orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle with conditional expectation identities for Gaussian multiplicative chaos and quantitative estimates for approaching singularities.

title: The real eigenvalues of the non-backtracking Laplacian
abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $N$ nodes and $M$ edges, with minimum degree at least $2$. We prove that the non-backtracking Laplacian of $G$ has at least $2M-2N+2c+2b$ real eigenvalues, counted with algebraic multiplicity, where $c$ is the number of connected components of $G$ and $b$ is the number of bipartite ones. More precisely, at least $M-N+2c$ of them lie in $[0,1)$ and at least $M-N+2b$ lie in $(1,2]$. We show that the bound $2M-2N+2c+2b$ is sharp, and that a connected $d$-regular graph attains it if and only if it is strictly Ramanujan, i.e., every adjacency eigenvalue $μ\ne\pm d$ satisfies $|μ|<2\sqrt{d-1}$. For completeness, we also show that the non-backtracking Laplacian has at most $2M-2c-2b$ real eigenvalues.

title: Graphs versus loopless digraphs with a given degree sequence, and convergence of uniformly random graphs at every density
abstract: For a degree sequence d on n vertices with M edges, let G(d) be the number of simple graphs and D(d) the number of loopless digraphs with in-degree = out-degree = d. We conjecture that G(d) >= sqrt(D(d)) exp(-C n log(2+M/n)) for every graphical d, a single inequality across all densities, and prove it up to an extra factor log n: G(d) >= sqrt(D(d)) exp(-C n log n log(2+M/n)) for every graphical d. The proof compares pairs of graphs with Eulerian digraphs by alternately colouring closed trails; the failure of injectivity is measured exactly, shared edges cancel against 2-cycles, and parity is handled by merging trails and by a parity argument on Eulerian circuits of odd components. No asymptotic enumeration and no bound on the maximum-entropy multipliers is used. When the maximum-entropy edge probabilities lie in [delta, 1-delta], the same method gives the conjecture itself, G(d) >= sqrt(D(d)) exp(-C n log n / delta). Combined with the exact identity G(d) = exp(g*(d)) pi(d), where pi(d) is the probability that the maximum-entropy beta-model has degrees exactly d, and a van der Waerden-type bound for D(d), this shows that uniformly random graphs with degree sequence d are close in the normalized cut metric to their beta-model whenever M >> n log n log(M/n), at every density, with no tameness and no cap on the degrees. We also record the conjecture in the sparse regime and, with constant 1/2+o(1), in the dense tame regime, from the asymptotic enumerations of McKay-Wormald and Barvinok-Hartigan.

title: An $L\log L$ theory of sparse graph convergence
abstract: Borgs, Chayes, Cohn and Zhao developed a limit theory for sparse graphs based on $L^p$ upper regularity with $p>1$, where Holder's inequality controls small sets. We develop the analogous theory in the Orlicz class $L\log L$, replacing Holder by the Young-Fenchel inequality for $Ψ(u)=(1+u)\log(1+u)-u$ and $Ψ^*(v)=e^v-1-v$. We prove a weak regularity lemma for upper $Ψ$-regular graphons with $4^{O(1/\varepsilon^2)}$ parts, using the modular $\intΨ$ as the energy; that upper $Ψ$-regular sequences have cut-metric convergent subsequences; that convergent sequences with $L\log L$ limits are upper $Ψ$-regular; and that $L\log L$ balls are cut-metric compact. The class strictly contains every $L^p$ class with $p>1$, and we give sparse $W$-random graphs that are upper $Ψ$-regular but not upper $L^p$ regular for any $p>1$. For graphs with a given degree sequence we prove, by Stein's method of exchangeable pairs with switchings, that if the average degree tends to infinity, the density to zero and the degree profile converges in $L^1$ to $\varphi$, uniformly random graphs converge in the normalized cut metric to $\varphi\otimes\varphi$, with no condition on the maximum degree; the sequence is upper $Ψ$-regular when $\varphi\in L\log L$. We also show that the maximum-entropy $β$-model is entrywise Chung-Lu when $d_{\max}^2=o(M)$, and that cut-closeness to it follows from a lower bound $e^{-o(M)}$ on its probability of having the prescribed degrees. Finally, $Ψ$ is the large deviation rate function of sparse Erdos-Renyi graphs up to a factor $1+O(1/\log\frac1p)$.

title: Sobolev spaces arising from the Stockwell transform on Gelfand pairs
abstract: We introduce a family of Sobolev-type spaces on Gelfand pairs, built from the Stockwell transform: a function belongs to the space of a given smoothness when its Stockwell transform, multiplied by a weight that grows with the smoothness, is square integrable. We prove that these spaces are Hilbert spaces, that they form a decreasing scale under continuous embeddings, and that an interpolation inequality controls the norm at an intermediate smoothness by the norms at the two endpoints. Under integrability conditions on the weight and on the family of analysing windows, they embed continuously into Lebesgue spaces. Under a local domination condition on the window, we show that their elements have bounded continuous representatives. On the Euclidean motion group, where the Stockwell transform reduces to a windowed Hankel transform, this gives boundedness and continuity as soon as the smoothness exceeds half the dimension, which is the classical threshold for Euclidean spaces.

title: Split Cuts in Fixed Integer Dimensions
abstract: We study how many split cuts, which include the Gomory mixed-integer cuts, are needed to reach the integer hull, and how large split closures can be. In every fixed dimension, a rational pure-integer polytope admits a polynomial-time constructible split proof of its integer hull with polynomial total encoding length; consequently, its full split rank is polynomial in the input length. This establishes the split-rank conjecture of Basu, Conforti, Di Summa, and Jiang for bounded pure-integer polyhedra in fixed dimension. Central to our approach is a preservation result: in arbitrary pure-integer dimension, an inequality whose violating points map, under an integer-affine map, into the interior of a planar lattice-free polyhedron has a polynomial split proof retaining every point already satisfying it. Whereas Chvátal--Gomory closures have polynomial-size inequality descriptions in fixed dimension, split closures need not: tetrahedra of input length $Θ(\log N)$ can have split closures with at least $2N-1$ facets, yet extension complexity $Θ(\log N)$. For the two-row system $x=f+Rs$, $s\ge0$, $x\in\mathbb Z^2$ of input length $L$, the split closure has an exact extended formulation with $O(L)$ inequalities and auxiliary variables; this bound is tight. Separation over the split closure is polynomial-time in fixed total dimension. Finally, for mixed-integer feasible rational polytopes with fixed integer dimension $p$ and any continuous dimension, we maximize a primitive integral objective on the integer variables with $O_p(G+1)$ split cuts, each removing a current optimal LP vertex, until an optimal vertex is mixed-integer feasible; here $G$ is the integrality gap of the LP relaxation, rounded down.

title: Uniqueness and radial symmetry of magnetic skyrmions
abstract:
This paper establishes radial symmetry and uniqueness of magnetic
  skyrmions as global minimizers of the simplest local micromagnetic
  energy. The strategy is to show that any radial critical point with
  strictly decreasing out-of-plane component is the unique minimizer
  in the class of general degree-one maps with the prescribed limit at
  infinity. To this end, we identify a class of null Lagrangians that
  is sufficiently flexible to contain a calibration, giving a uniform
  lower bound for the energy that is uniquely saturated on the
  critical point. Our arguments provide a blueprint for proofs of
  symmetry and uniqueness of minimizers in vectorial variational
  problems under topological constraints.

title: Beyond least-favorable distribution pairs: asymptotically instance-optimal robust hypothesis testing
abstract: When testing a composite null $\mathcal{P}$ against a composite alternative $\mathcal{Q}$, it has been known since Huber and Strassen (1973) that if a least favorable distribution (LFD) pair exists, then a version of its likelihood ratio yields a minimax optimal test, and Huber (1965) derived a similar result in the sequential setting for a specific robust testing problem that is the focus of the current paper; the same likelihood ratio is log-optimal in the worst case; its expected logarithm under the alternative equals $\inf_{P \in \mathcal{P},S \in \mathcal{Q}} KL(S\|P)$, whose inverse also determines the stopping time of the test under the alternative. These results focus on optimizing worst-case performance, but the resulting methods have lower power if the data come from simpler alternatives. This paper studies an arguably more practical goal of achieving asymptotic \emph{instance optimality} for ``power-one'' sequential tests, which remarkably may even be possible when $\mathcal{Q} = \mathcal{P}^c$. This means that when the data are drawn from any $S \in \mathcal{P}^c$, the test has power one, and its stopping time is determined by the larger information number $\inf_{P \in \mathcal{P}} KL(S\|P)$, which governs the performance of an oracle that knows $S$. To demonstrate this point, our paper focuses on the case of testing a TV ball around a discrete distribution with $d$ components, and designs a computationally and memory efficient algorithm that is also asymptotically instance-optimal. Specifically, we consider two different asymptotic settings: one is the "Wald setting", where the type-1 error level $α$ approaches zero for a fixed alternative $S$ and the second is the "Farrell setting", where $α$ is fixed and $\inf_{P \in \mathcal{P}} KL(S\|P)$ approaches $0$. Our sequential test is simultaneously optimal in both regimes.

title: Rational barycentric coordinates and low degree adjoints
abstract: We study rational generalized barycentric coordinates (rational GBCs) on polytopes. We recall their essential theory and clarify some statements from the literature. We study polytopes that admit GBCs with low degree denominators (and hence, low degree (affine) adjoint polynomials). We give a full classification of polytopes that admit polynomial barycentric coordinates (i.e. constant adjoints).

title: Characterizing $k$-Naples parking functions and refining bounds via obstructed parking functions
abstract:
The Naples parking functions are a major generalization of the classical parking functions, where cars have more options to park because they are allowed to check (and possibly park) backward up to a fixed number of spots before driving forward as in the classical case.
  In a previous work, using involutions we established an injection from the Naples parking functions to a special set of obstructed parking functions, which we referred to as \textit{left obstructed}, thereby immediately obtaining a crude upper bound on the former set. We continue that work here by identifying the image of this injection, providing a characterization of Naples parking functions as a certain (smaller) set of obstructed parking functions, which we will refer to as \textit{long left obstructed}. We also derive a formula for the number of left obstructed parking functions. These combined allow us to improve the upper bound on the Naples parking functions. In addition, we demonstrate how lower bounds for this set can be obtained. As will become clear, the long left obstructed parking functions have certain combinatorial features that are useful in estimating the cardinality of the set, which are not obvious from solely looking at Naples parking functions.

title: $M$-subgroups and normal-subgroup lattices of finite groups
abstract: Let $G$ be a group. A normal subgroup $E$ is an $M$-subgroup if $E\cap N_1\cap N_2\neq1$ whenever $N_1\cap N_2$, $E\cap N_1$, and $E\cap N_2$ are non-trivial for normal subgroups $N_1,N_2$. We characterise these subgroups as the essential or relatively uniform normal subgroups. For finite $G$, an $M$-subgroup is either trivial, contains exactly one minimal normal subgroup, or contains the socle. Consequently, every normal subgroup is an $M$-subgroup precisely when the socle has $G$-chief length at most two. We obtain an explicit $M$-closure operation and describe the minimal normal subgroups of finite direct products. For crown-based powers, we use the known comparability of normal subgroups with the socle to describe the normal lattice in terms of Boolean or subspace lattices and the quotient above the socle. We then determine when the $M$-lattice retains the normal lattice, classify normal quotients and their automorphism orbits, and characterise quotient maps compatible with $M$-closure. Finally, we compute the maximal length of chains of $M$-subgroups in terms of the chief length and socle length of $G$.

title: The local-to-global minimum problem of Calvert and Vamanamurthy: a quartic counterexample in three variables and the cubic case in all dimensions
abstract: In 1980 Calvert and Vamanamurthy asked whether a polynomial whose only critical point is a local minimum must attain its global minimum there. They gave counterexamples of every degree at least five in two or more variables and settled cubics in two and three variables and quartics in two variables, leaving open quartics in three or more variables and cubics in four or more variables. We resolve both remaining cases. First, we give an explicit quartic in three variables whose unique critical point is a nondegenerate strict local minimum, although the polynomial is unbounded below; the example extends to every dimension at least three, and its critical locus is a single point even over the complex numbers. Second, we prove that in every dimension a polynomial of exact degree three with a local minimum has another critical point, so that the cubic case holds vacuously; the proof is elementary and avoids the topological degree arguments used previously in two and three variables. Together with the results of Calvert and Vamanamurthy, this gives the complete classification of the local-to-global property by degree and dimension.

title: Minimax-Optimal Static Estimators Under Interference
abstract: We study the problem of estimating the global treatment effect in randomized experiments under interference, where a unit's outcome may depend on the treatment assignments of other units. We adopt a minimax framework, allowing an adversary to select an outcome function from a class of functions that satisfy bounded outcomes and bounded interference. We derive minimax-optimal static estimators that are robust to a wide range of interference structures, parameterized by a scalar $δ$ controlling the maximum influence of one unit's treatment on another's outcome. Under large interference, we observe two regimes. When the treatment and control groups are equally sized, the minimax-optimal static estimator is the zero estimator. When one of the two groups is larger, the minimax-optimal static estimator is a "half-zero" estimator, in which the outcomes of the smaller group are ignored, and the estimator only considers the outcomes of the larger group.

title: Covariant Calculus and Hamiltonian Flows for Nonlocal Wasserstein Metrics
abstract: In this paper, we study nonlocal metrics on smooth positive probability densities on a closed manifold, induced by symmetric jump kernels and density-dependent mobilities. First, we introduce the density-variation operator to express the density derivatives of the Dirichlet form and kinetic energy. Second, we construct density and velocity-field representations of the tangent space and prove their isometric equivalence. We use the generator's pseudoinverse to derive Levi-Civita connections and covariant differentials in both representations. Third, we establish mechanical Hamiltonian dynamics in both tangent representations; an action principle and Legendre duality identify the Hamilton--Jacobi and covariant Newton equations; smooth negative gradient flows admit a zero-energy Hamiltonian lift. Entropy diffusion, nonlocal mean-field equations, Keller--Segel dynamics, and a nonlocal Vlasov equation illustrate the resulting calculus. For geometric-mean mobility, the Hopf--Cole transformation of the nonlocal Schrödinger bridge system and the Madelung transformation of the nonlocal Schrödinger equation yield hyperbolic and trigonometric phase energies, respectively. At zero momentum, both recover the metric kinetic energy to second order.

title: The equality $s(G)=η(G)+\exp(G)-1$ fails for $G=C_2^7\oplus C_6$
abstract: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. The Erdős-Ginzburg-Ziv constant $\mathsf{s}(G)$ is the smallest positive integer $\ell$ such that every sequence over $G$ of length at least $\ell$ contains a zero-sum subsequence of length $\exp(G)$. The short zero-sum constant $η(G)$ is defined similarly, with the requirement that the zero-sum subsequence is nonempty and has length at most $\exp(G)$. It is known that $\mathsf{s}(G)\ge η(G)+\exp(G)-1.$ A conjecture proposed by W. Gao in 2003, which has been widely studied in zero-sum theory, predicts that $$ \mathsf{s}(G)=η(G)+\exp(G)-1 $$ for every nontrivial finite abelian group $G$. In this paper, we prove that this conjecture fails for the group $C_2^7\oplus C_6$.

title: The Erdős--Hajnal property for paths
abstract:
The well-known Erdős-Hajnal conjecture states that for any graph $H$, there is a constant $c=c(H)>0$ such that every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with no induced copies of $H$ contains a clique or an independent set of size at least $n^{c}$.
  In this paper, we prove that the Erdős-Hajnal conjecture holds for every path.

title: Time-Decay Rates toward Rarefaction Waves for the One-Dimensional Isentropic Compressible Navier--Stokes Equations
abstract: While the asymptotic stability of rarefaction waves for the compressible Navier--Stokes equations has been well established since the pioneering works of Matsumura--Nishihara \cite{MatsumuraNishihara1986} and Liu--Xin \cite{LiuXin1988}, the classical $L^2$ energy method yields only qualitative convergence in $L^\infty(\R)$ as $t\to\infty$ without any explicit decay rate. In this paper, we establish for the first time a standalone \(L^4\) energy estimate for perturbations of a weak rarefaction wave in the one-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes system, thereby obtaining the first explicit algebraic time-decay rates for this model. Specifically, for small initial perturbations in $H^2(\R)$ and small wave strength $δ$, we prove that $(v-V,u-U)$ decays in $L^4(\R)$ at the rate \[ \|(v-V,u-U)(t)\|_{L^4}\le C\bigl(\|(v_0-V(0),u_0-U(0))\|_{H^2}+\sqrtδ\bigr)(1+t)^{-1/8}, \] where \((V,U)\) denotes the smooth rarefaction wave, while the relative Riemann invariants \(z_\pm\) of the perturbed system decay in \(L^\infty(\R)\) at the rate \((1+t)^{-1/6}\). The proof relies on a new local quartic energy estimate for \(z_\pm\) and \(z_\pm-Q\), where \(Q=μ(v)v_x-μ(V)V_x\), as well as a nonlocal half-space wave-interaction functional for corrected characteristic modes and a weighted higher-order derivative energy estimate coupled at the scale of the one-dimensional Nash inequality.

title: Cohomology of regular spherical actions
abstract: We study regular spherical actions, namely, actions of a connected compact Lie group G on a manifold M with equidimensional orbits, some of which are spheres. These spherical orbits are diffeomorphic to homogeneous spaces G/H, and there is a list of nine possible families of pairs (G, H). The normalizer N of H in G plays an important role in our calculations, as does the Weyl group W = N/H. In fact, there are three possibilities for W, namely: Z_2, S^1 and S^3. The goal of this paper is to relate the cohomology of M to that of the orbit space M/G. We obtain a particularly simple relationship in the first case, W = Z_2. For the remaining two cases, W = S^1 and W = S^3, it is already known that the cohomology of M and that of the orbit space M/G are related by the Gysin sequence ... \to H^k(M/G) \to H^k(M ) \to H^{k-d}(M/G) \to H^{k+1}(M/G) \to ... In this work, we provide a direct construction of this sequence, avoiding the use of spectral sequences. Moreover, we give an explicit description of the connecting homomorphism as multiplication by a power of the Euler class associated with the action of the Weyl group W = S^l on the fixed-point set M^H.

title: An affine reverse Faber-Krahn inequality via information decay
abstract: We prove that every convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ admits $S\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{R})$ such that $λ_1(SK)|K|^{2/n}\le Cn$, where $C$ is universal. For origin-symmetric bodies of volume one, the bound holds in maximal Gaussian measure position. The main step is the spectral estimate \[ λ_1(D)\le C(P)\bigl(n+\sqrt{n I(ν\midγ_n)}\bigr) \] for an even isotropic log-concave probability measure $ν$ supported on a symmetric convex body $D$, with Poincaré constant at most $P$ and finite relative Fisher information. A second-order Stein estimate and an information jump under convolution give entropy decay faster than $m^{-1}$ for normalised sums. Their supports control the Gaussian measure of dilates, and a Brownian bridge expansion gives the spectral estimate. A Gaussian-weighted ground state supplies a measure whose Fisher information is bounded in terms of $λ_1(K)$. The square-root dependence then gives the bound of order $n$.

title: Projective relativistic dynamics from a quantum Lorentz algebra: time-dependent deformed Hamiltonians on (anti-)de Sitter spaces
abstract: A (non-standard) quantum deformation of the Lorentz algebra $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$ is used to construct novel time-dependent Hamiltonian systems on the (anti-)de Sitter spacetimes in $(1+1)$-dimensions. The specific deformation considered here contains, among others, the non-standard quantum deformation of $\mathfrak{sl}(2, \mathbb{R})$ and that of the `book' algebra $\mathfrak{b}_{2}$ as quantum subalgebras. The guiding idea is to apply the theory of Poisson--Hopf deformations of Lie--Hamilton systems to the Lorentz deformation, giving rise to a broad family of time-dependent deformed systems that share the same deformed Poisson--Hopf Lorentz algebra symmetry. In particular, this approach provides Hamiltonian vector fields expressed in terms of certain projective canonical variables, which, in turn, are related to the usual Beltrami variables via a canonical transformation. Under this construction, it is shown that the underlying Lorentizan spaces possess constant curvature $κ$ and the quantum deformation parameter $z$ can be identified with $κ$, such that the cosmological constant is $Λ=-z\equiv -κ$. Therefore, we deal with the anti-de Sitter, de Sitter and Minkowskian spaces for $z>0$, $z<0$ and $z=0$ (the undeformed case), respectively. Finally, as applications, we study time-dependent deformed oscillators on the (anti-)de Sitter spaces in detail, as well as time-dependent deformed Bateman and generalised coupled Caldirola--Kanai Hamiltonians.

title: Generalized Quasi-Symmetric Nets: A Constructive Approach to the Equimodular Elliptic Type and to Flexible $m \times n$ Nets
abstract: Quadrilateral meshes that flex with rigid planar faces are of interest to transformable architecture, rigid-foldable origami, and mechanical metamaterials. Their building blocks are flexible $3 \times 3$ nets, that is, Kokotsakis polyhedra with a quadrangular base, classified by Izmestiev. We study one of his types, the equimodular elliptic type, defined by three conditions on the flat angles, the third of them through Jacobi elliptic functions. We turn these conditions into equivalent algebraic ones, free of elliptic functions, which lead to the generalized quasi-symmetric nets (GQS-nets), polyhedra of this type that include the known elliptic quasi-symmetric nets. For every polyhedron of this type, we give a flexible polyhedron with the same flat angles and its flexion in closed form. From the simplest GQS-nets, we assemble arbitrarily large flexible $m \times n$ nets. Examples include nets that, at one position, form letters; further nets in the supplementary materials form digits or, seen along their rows, approximately follow the side silhouettes of a bunny and a fish. Unlike numerically computed mechanisms, these nets are exactly flexible. As an application, we design three such nets as transportable arch halls of 80 mm sandwich panels, which fold to fit through the door of a standard container or into the well of a low-bed semi-trailer, and we check them numerically under snow load and build a 1:20 model of one. Supplementary Mathematica notebooks verify the symbolic computations, a Python tool constructs the nets and checks them numerically, including for self-intersections, and further scripts recheck the halls.

title: The Ehrlich--Aberth root finder is not generally convergent
abstract:
We show that the well-known Ehrlich--Aberth root finding method is not generally convergent. More precisely, we show that there is an open subset of polynomials of any degree $d\ge 7$, and an open subset of initial conditions, such that the iteration of the Ehrlich--Aberth method converges to an attracting periodic cycle of period $4$, rather than to a vector of roots. The proof is constructive in the sense that we present explicit values for the polynomial and the $4$-cycle.
  The search is highly non-trivial: we found no attracting cycles for lower degrees/periods, and the size of the attracting domain relative to a ``unit cube'' in the space of polynomials and starting vectors is on the order of $10^{-127}$.

title: Asymptotic behavior of some strongly critical decomposable multi-type Galton-Watson processes with immigration
abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of a critical decomposable multi-type Galton-Watson process with immigration whose offspring mean matrix is triangular with diagonal entries 1. Under second-order moment conditions on the offspring and immigration distributions, we establish a functional limit theorem for the sequence of appropriately scaled processes, and describe the limit process as independent squared Bessel processes and some linear combinations of their iterated integral processes. Our work completes and extends some results of Foster and Ney (1978) for some strongly critical decomposable multi-type Galton-Watson processes with immigration.

title: The Carpenter property for subfactors of uniform infinite index
abstract: We show that if $N\subset M$ is an inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors of uniform infinite index, for instance an irreducible inclusion of infinite index, then every positive contraction $b\in N$ is of the form $E_N(p)$ for a projection $p\in M$. This gives the exact version of Popa's asymptotic result in the ultrapower, and it is a subfactor analogue of the Carpenter problem for masas. In particular, Popa's relative dimension set of such an inclusion is $[0,1]$, so the set of expectations of projections does not distinguish inclusions without corners of finite index. As applications, the Carpenter property holds for $N\subset N\rtimes G$ whenever an infinite group $G$ acts outerly on a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $N$, and for ICC groups $H\le G$ the inclusion $L(H)\subset L(G)$ has it exactly when $[G:H]=\infty$, confirming a recent conjecture. We also give examples showing that the Carpenter property does not imply uniform infinite index, and that infinite index does not imply the Carpenter property.

title: A Reider-type theorem for syzygies of cyclic covers of anticanonical rational surfaces
abstract: Let $π\colon X\to S$ be a smooth ramified cyclic cover of an anticanonical rational surface, with $κ(X)\geq0$, and let $A$ be a divisor on $S$. We prove a Reider-type theorem for syzygies: for every integer $p\ge 0$, the adjoint divisor $K_X+π^*A$ satisfies Property $\mathrm{N}_p$ provided that $A\cdot C\geq p+3$ for every curve $C\subseteq S$ with $C^2\le 1$. One ingredient is a syzygy criterion for finite covers that reduces the weight-two Koszul vanishing on $X$ to weight-one vanishing for the nontrivial character modules on $S$. The most delicate case, in which $\dim|-K_S|=0$ and $K_S^2<0$, is handled by a separate geometric argument.

title: Chain Conditions for Abelian Normal Subgroups
abstract: We investigate various chain conditions for abelian normal subgroups of groups, following Robinson (1968). We focus on the maximal condition for abelian normal subgroups, an exceptional case excluded from his results except for some counterexamples. In particular we show that a hypercentral group satisfies the maximal condition for abelian normal subgroups if and only if it is is finitely generated nilpotent.

title: The signed error-sum function of tent-map expansions
abstract: In this paper, we study the signed error-sum function of tent map base series introduced by Dai and Tang in 2011. We show that the function is discontinuous at every dyadic rational in the open unit interval, although it was asserted to be continuous. We determine its values at these points and analyze its range, differentiability, and variation. We also obtain sharp covering estimates for its graph and calculate the Hausdorff, box-counting, and covering dimensions of the graph, which are $1$, $1$, and $0$, respectively. Moreover, we show that the signed error sum agrees with Lévy's function away from dyadic rationals and that the unsigned error sum is the Takagi function.

title: Convergence Guarantees for the Broximal Point Method under Perturbations
abstract: The Broximal Point Method (BPM) of Gruntkowska et al. (2025) comes with strong guarantees for convex optimization: under convexity alone, it terminates after finitely many steps and converges linearly in function value, with bounds that do not depend on the condition number or on any other regularity property of the objective. Each iteration, however, requires the exact minimization of the objective over a ball, which is generally intractable. As a first step toward implementable variants, we study the method when these subproblems are solved only approximately. We introduce and analyze Inexact BPM, which replaces the exact broximal point by an approximation and makes no assumption on how this approximation is obtained. Under summable or sufficiently small errors, we bound the number of iterations needed to reach a neighborhood of the set of minimizers, and these bounds remain independent of the regularity of the objective. Under the weaker requirement that the errors stay below the ball radius, we prove sublinear convergence in function value for the exact broximal points underlying the perturbed iterates, valid until the target neighborhood is reached, and we recover linear rates under bounded sublevel sets or strong convexity.

title: Boundary fibers of the holonomy map for complex projective structures
abstract: We study the Morgan--Shalen boundary of holonomy representations of complex projective structures on a compact Riemann surface of genus at least two. We prove that every direction defined by a holomorphic quadratic differential with a multiple zero admits distinct projective marked length limits. Together with Dumas's uniqueness theorem for simple zeros, this gives a complete characterization of directions with unique limits. We also establish that no nonzero abelian length function can occur in the holonomy boundary of any such fixed surface, regardless of the limiting quadratic differential. Finally, we characterize all directional boundary fibers by a necessary-and-sufficient analytic condition involving valued representations and the holomorphic jet bundle underlying an oper.

title: Lieb-Robinson bounds for Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonians via path expansions
abstract: We study the transport properties of Bose-Hubbard-type Hamiltonians. Kuwahara, Vu, and Saito proved sharp bounds on (i) particle transport and (ii) the Lieb-Robinson velocity for initial states with controlled boson density. We provide simpler and shorter proofs for both results using a new set of methods. For (i), boson transport, we use a class of weighted extended particle number operators that directly enables closing the associated differential inequalities. For (ii), the Lieb-Robinson bounds, we develop a bosonic version of the Chen-Lucas path expansion technique and recover the sharp velocity bound $t^{d-1}$ up to logarithmic corrections, where $d$ denotes the lattice dimension. We also extend the transport bounds (i) to long-range hopping with a power-law exponent $α>d$. The range $α\in (d,d+1)$ corresponds to an algebraic light cone for boson transport and has not been previously covered.

title: Nonlinear adiabatic theorem for the Gross-Pitaevskii equation
abstract: We prove a nonlinear adiabatic theorem for the repulsive Gross-Pitaevskii (GP) equation with a time-dependent trapping potential $V(x,t)$. If either (i) $V(\cdot,t)$ is smooth, subquadratic in space and with uniformly bounded spatial derivatives of order $\geq 2$, or (ii) $V(\cdot,t)$ is a uniformly bounded perturbation of a fixed non-negative potential which is asymptotically $|x|^m, m\geq 2$, then the GP equation has a global solution, which remains uniformly close to the instantaneous minimizer of the time-independent GP functional, provided the initial condition is a ground state. In fact, we show that the existence of a solution of the GP equation is the real bottleneck: If existence is assumed, then adiabaticity holds under very minimal assumptions.

title: A converse theorem for GL(2) over global fields without root numbers
abstract: We prove a converse theorem for GL(2) over global fields in which the root numbers in the twisted functional equations need not be prescribed. Instead, we allow nonzero scalar factors that are invariant under unramified twists. We show that these scalars are independent of the twisting character and obtain a unique isobaric automorphic representation with the prescribed unramified local components.

title: Schwarz Lemma in Quaternionic Setting and $\mathbb C^4$
abstract:
We study a Schwarz Lemma on the matrix ball \[ \mathbb D^+=\{Z\in M_2(\mathbb C);\, \|Z\|<1\}
  \simeq U(2,2)/(U(2)\times U(2)), \] which arises naturally from the complexification of the quaternions. We prove Schwarz and Schwarz--Pick estimates on $\mathbb D^+$, construct its $U(2,2)$-invariant Riemannian Poincaré metric, and describe a Cayley transform to a tube-domain realization. The intrinsic spectral metric is the Kobayashi metric and is contracted by holomorphic maps. Comparing it with the Poincaré metric gives the sharp estimate $d(F(P),F(Q))\le \sqrt2\,d(P,Q)$ for every holomorphic self-map $F$ of $\mathbb D^+$; in general the constant $1$ is false. We also prove an infinitesimal rigidity statement and record a Burns--Krantz boundary rigidity theorem at the smooth part of $\partial\mathbb D^+$. Finally, we develop a conformally natural barycenter construction on the Shilov boundary $U(2)$. Every admissible probability measure has a unique barycenter in $\mathbb D^+$, the construction is $U(2,2)$-natural, and it gives a barycentric extension of suitable boundary maps. Under the natural admissibility hypothesis, a holomorphic self-map extending to $U(2)$ is the barycentric extension of its boundary values. Many aspects of this paper are motivated by quaternionic analysis, however, no prior knowledge of quaternionic analysis is required from the reader.

title: Zero sets in spaces of analytic functions with $p$-summable Taylor coefficients
abstract: A zero set for a space of analytic functions is a set on which some nonzero function in the space vanishes; it is exact if it coincides with the full zero set of such a function. We construct zero sets that are not exact in the classical coefficient spaces $\ell_A^p$ of functions analytic on the unit disk for every $1\le p<2$. For $1<p<2$, a single Blaschke set $W$ is a zero set for every $\ell_A^p$ in this range, but is not exact for any of them. The endpoint case $p=1$, corresponding to the analytic Wiener algebra $\ell_A^1$, requires a separate construction, yielding a non-exact zero set that accumulates at only one point of the unit circle. The proofs combine quadratic characters, finite-dimensional Clark transforms, and logarithmic estimates in zero-free regions. We also establish sharp moment duality and an exact summability criterion for a family of regular polygons. For $p>2$, we construct two disjoint exact zero sets whose union is a uniqueness set. For these exponents, suitably chosen rotations also yield a continuum-sized family of nonzero closed shift-invariant subspaces of $\ell^p$ with pairwise trivial intersections, recovering a known existence result.

title: A Unified Space-Time Variational Framework for Wave Equations on Differential Forms
abstract: We revisit a standard space--time variational formulation of the scalar wave equation in the setting of differential forms. For this, we use as spatial operator the nonnegative, self-adjoint (relative) \emph{Hodge--Laplacian} on a bounded Lipschitz domain. Its spectral decomposition reduces the wave problem in any form degree to the same family of scalar ordinary differential equations that underlies existing space-time analysis. We illustrate how this can be used to transfer results from the scalar wave equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions to other wave-type problems. In particular, we connect the framework to perfectly electrically conducting Maxwell problems.

title: Wideband Microwave Linear Analog Computer (MiLAC) for Frequency-Flat and Frequency-Selective Processing
abstract: Microwave linear analog computer (MiLAC) has been proposed as an analog processing architecture to perform efficient computation in the microwave domain. Consisting of reconfigurable impedance networks, a MiLAC can extract many of the gains of large multi-antenna systems without costly digital processing, e.g., achieving capacity in narrowband multiple-input single-output (MISO). However, the behavior of wideband MiLAC, required to support high data-rate transmissions, is widely unknown. The impedance components of MiLACs have non-trivial frequency-dependent response, requiring specific implementations to characterize it. In this work, we consider MiLAC implementations based on LC resonators with tunable capacitance, which allow synthesizing near-arbitrary passive lossless impedance matrices at individual frequencies using inductors and varactors. We characterize the mapping between optimal MISO precoding at a reference frequency, and the vector of capacitances configuring the MiLAC. We derive the degrees of freedom (DoFs) remaining after fixing such optimum precoding at the reference frequency, and show that these DoFs can be exploited to tune the frequency response of the MiLAC. We propose two techniques to exploit these DoFs: a closed-form approach for frequency-flat MiLAC processing, and a numerical approach for multi-frequency MiLAC processing, optimizing processing at frequencies other than the reference one. The frequency-flat approach shows satisfactory performance in a simulated frequency-flat millimeter-wave scenario, approaching the performance of digital processing. The multi-frequency approach can adapt to the frequency-selectivity of a simulated sub-6GHz scenario, attaining gains over frequency-flat digital processing. This constitutes the first demonstration that realistic MiLAC implementations can be configured to perform independent computations at different frequencies.

title: Generalized Ricci Solitons on Heisenberg and Oscillator Algebras
abstract: We prove that on a connected, simply-connected nilpotent Lie group, the notions of left-invariant generalized Ricci soliton, semi-algebraic and algebraic generalized Ricci soliton coincide. Moreover, every such soliton has harmonic torsion. We classify all algebraic solitons with positive definite metric on the five-dimensional Heisenberg algebra, the four-dimensional oscillator algebra and the four-dimensional split-oscillator algebra up to automorphisms and rescalings. We find that there is only a finite number of algebraic solitons, all of which have harmonic torsion.

title: Probing automorphic induction through zero correlations and secondary arithmetic terms
abstract: Zero correlations offer a way to test the cuspidal structure of an automorphic L-function, but their leading self statistics retain only coarse degree and multiplicity data. We therefore adjoin a specified cuspidal L-function as a probe and study the resulting raw mixed correlations. Assuming a factorization into cuspidal L-functions over Q, we show that a mixed pair statistic detects the probe's occurrence and recovers its multiplicity. A suitable Gevrey-order-two test eliminates the smooth-density terms and gives a subexponential error. For arbitrary smooth plateau tests, the prime number theorem of Harcos and Thorner gives an error smaller than every fixed inverse power of log T, without a self-contragredience assumption. The stronger prime number theorem of Liu and Ye gives a subexponential remainder under its stated structural assumptions, with the possible norm-twist terms made explicit. To obtain arithmetic information beyond this overlap, we compute the correlation expansion at every fixed level and inverse-logarithmic order within the original strict small-support range. We treat the pair and higher correlations separately, using Jiang's rational-field fixed-data estimates to justify the required prime-power convergence. The pair calculation identifies the mixed arithmetic finite parts and gives detailed error estimates, including the contribution of norm twists. The higher-level calculation retains connected prime-power invariants, whose first cubic contribution appears at order (log T)^{-3}. Explicit third- and fourth-level formulas and examples explain the arithmetic content of these coefficients and the limitations of self-correlations. Varying powers of the probe separates their mixed components. These formulas, together with the distinct-index sieve, provide a collection of arithmetic probe responses toward the further problem of recovering automorphic induction structure.

title: Reverse Transportation and Harnack Inequalities for Underdamped Langevin in the Non-convex Setting
Randomized Adaptive Sequential Allocation and the Limits of Bounded Exposure to Inferior Treatments
abstract: A clinical trial must learn which treatment is superior while sparing its participants from the inferior one. Kundu et al. 2025 recently showed that a purely deterministic rule, which always assigns the treatment with the larger current sample mean, achieves a strong form of this ethical goal. The smaller allocation count stays almost surely finite and has all moments bounded uniformly in the sample size. Deterministic allocation is, however, predictable, and predictability invites selection bias. We ask whether this bounded-exposure phenomenon survives once the deterministic rule is replaced by a smooth randomized one. We show that it does not. Under any fixed non-degenerate symmetric randomization, both treatments are sampled infinitely often, the adaptive sample means are strongly consistent, and the inferior treatment draws a strictly positive limiting allocation proportion. Consequently, the inferior allocation count grows linearly and its moments are unbounded. We then study annealed randomization, in which the randomization scale cools with the accumulated information, and obtain summability and divergence criteria that separate finite, sublinear, and linear exposure. A forced-exploration variant identifies the superior treatment with probability one while keeping the inferior exposure sublinear, and thereby frees the annealed guarantees from any correct-stabilization event. We also treat normalized multi-treatment rules, ties, indifference zones, unequal variances, general response distributions, and local alternatives. Finally, we develop the post-trial asymptotic inference that each exposure regime permits. The results delineate the trade-off between allocation concealment, persistent exploration, and ethical concentration on the superior treatment.

title: Moduli spaces of rank 2 sheaves on $\mathbb P^3$ via Quot schemes
abstract: We study the Gieseker--Maruyama moduli space $M_{c_3}$ of stable rank 2 torsion-free sheaves on $\mathbb{P}^3$ with Chern classes $c_1=-1$, $c_2=1$, and odd $c_3 \le 1$. Every such sheaf $E$ has reflexive hull $E^{\ast\ast}$ parametrised by $M_1$, and the quotient $E^{\ast\ast}/E$ is a 0-dimensional sheaf of length $n = (1-c_3)/2$. We prove that $M_{c_3}$ is isomorphic to the relative Quot scheme $\mathsf{Quot}_{\mathbb{P}^3 \times M_1/M_1}(\mathscr{R},n)$, where $\mathscr{R}$ is the universal reflexive sheaf over $M_1$. Our technique combines (i) Bridgeland-type wall-crossing in Donaldson--Thomas theory, (ii) the theory of good moduli spaces, (iii) deformation theory in dgla and Ext-quiver language. We deduce that $M_{c_3}$ is connected, and we analyse its \emph{smoothable component} $M_{c_3}^{\mathsf{main}}$, proving it is rational and generically smooth of dimension $4n+3$. We further prove that $\dim \mathrm{Sing} M_{c_3} \geq 4n-2$ for all $n \geq 2$. Finally, we provide a geometric characterisation for the cases $n\leq 2$. We show that $M_{-1}$ is a smooth rational projective variety of dimension 7 and compute its motive in the Grothendieck ring of varieties, while $M_{-3}$ is shown to be an integral, normal variety of dimension 11 that is regular in codimension 4.

title: Functoriality probes over number fields by mixed zero correlations
abstract: We use an automorphic L-function over one number field as a probe for the functorial structure of another automorphic L-function over a possibly different field. No automorphic induction is assumed. We first determine the mixed Euler factors arising from the explicit formula, including the residue-degree multiplicities that occur when local traces are grouped by absolute norm. This local analysis gives four probe constructions. Rational-field probes with known base change detect constituent multiplicities and, in equal rank, exact Satake equalities. Probes over a common Galois field detect conjugacy and stabilizers. Dirichlet-character probes give congruence-weighted combinations of Satake traces even when the leading overlap vanishes. A tensor-product construction realizes general different-field probes whenever the required base changes exist. We then separate the pair calculation from the higher connected calculations and work out the cubic and quartic arithmetic explicitly. In an explicit small Fourier box these expressions yield all finite secondary orders of the centered statistics; the required pair prime number theorems also give raw and distinct-index correlations. The main analytic tools are an independent fixed-data proof of Hypothesis H over number fields, a positive-margin estimate for rationally grouped coefficients, and the theorem of Harcos-Thorner for the realized Rankin-Selberg factors. This expanded version includes the full computations, local examples, and an appendix explaining the character-extension issue avoided by the proof of Hypothesis H. The resulting probes give concrete tests of functorial relationships, while recovery of automorphic induction remains a longer-term goal.

title: Extremal zero-sum sequences without elements of maximal order
abstract: Let $\mathsf D(G)$ denote the Davenport constant of a finite abelian group $G$, the maximal length of a minimal zero-sum sequence over $G$. Gao and Geroldinger conjectured that every minimal zero-sum sequence of length $\mathsf D(G)$~\cite[Conjecture~6.1]{GG99} and every zero-sumfree sequence of length $\mathsf D(G)-1$~\cite[Conjecture~4.1]{GG06} contains an element of order $\exp(G)$. We disprove both conjectures by proving a density-one theorem: for every fixed finite abelian group $H$ of exponent $M=2^ap^b$, where $a\ge2$, $b\ge1$, and $p$ is an odd prime, the set of integers $r\ge0$ for which $G_r=C_2^r\oplus H$ admits a minimal zero-sum sequence of length $\mathsf D(G_r)$ with no term of order $M$ has natural density one.

title: Tensor Products and the Isomorphic Theory of Daugavet Spaces
abstract: We construct two separable Banach spaces with the Daugavet property whose injective and projective tensor squares, respectively, fail the Daugavet property. Both examples arise from one sequence of finite-dimensional extensions. The first space is the completion of the increasing union of the extensions, whereas the second is the closed span of their coordinate functionals. We will also investigate the operator Daugavet properties of these spaces later in the paper, also highlighting natural examples of metric spaces \(M\) for which \(\operatorname{Lip}_0(M)\) has the Daugavet property but fails to have the weak operator Daugavet property. Independently of this, we will also prove that every Banach space admits a linear isometric embedding into a Banach space which is not isomorphic to any Banach space with the Daugavet property.

title: On Guarding Line Arrangements
abstract: We study the problem of guarding a set of straight lines in the plane by selecting a minimum-cardinality set of points such that every line contains at least one selected point. This problem is known to be strongly NP-hard \cite{megiddo}. We investigate approximation algorithms for the problem and analyze their performance guarantees under various structural assumptions on the underlying line arrangement. In particular, we present approximation schemes based on set-cover techniques, relaxation methods, and properties of maximal lines. We establish constant-factor bounds on the approximation ratio for several classes of arrangements and derive relationships between the guarding number and the incidence parameters of the arrangement. Connections with Dirac-type incidence results are also explored.

title: Integrating Data Center Flexibility into Power System Operations: A Framework for Temporal Redispatch
abstract: Rapid growth in data center electricity demand, driven by artificial intelligence (AI) training and inference, is expected to increase stress conditions for power grids. Operational flexibility from data centers offers a near-term lever to relieve such stresses. Existing models of data center flexibility tend to bundle economic incentives with physical constraints, obscuring the tradeoff between economic willingness to shift load and technical limitations to do so. This paper proposes a temporal-redispatch focused framework that decouples data center demand flexibility into two independently parameterized dimensions: (1) systematic flexibility, capturing the economic environment through penalties for temporal shifting of data centers' scheduled demand, and (2) operational flexibility, capturing the physical envelope through the demand shifting time window and the limit on shifted data center demand. The framework relies on a direct current optimal power flow (DC-OPF) linear program which enables annual parametric analysis at hourly resolution. The framework is studied using a synthetic grid mimicking the Texas transmission system populated with the 2026 Adjusted Forecast from ERCOT (Electric Reliability Council of Texas). Results show that operational flexibility imposes a physical lower bound on unsatisfied demand that no economic incentive can overcome; longer shifting windows and higher limits on shifted data center demand reduce operational cost with different impacts on grid utilization; and, temporal redispatch shaves system-wide net load peaks while partially compensating for localized transmission bottlenecks that emerge under modeled coal retirement scenarios.

title: The multivariate Berry-Esseen theorem with an absolute constant
abstract: We prove that the multivariate Berry--Esseen inequality for sums of independent random vectors holds with the same constant in every dimension. For independent centered random vectors $X_1,\ldots,X_n\in\mathbb{R}^d$ whose covariance matrices sum to $I_d$, we show that the distance between the distribution of their sum and $N(0,I_d)$, measured uniformly over convex sets, is at most $C_0\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb{E}\|X_i\|_2^3$ for a universal constant $C_0$. The bound requires only finite third moments and holds uniformly in the dimension, the number of summands, and their distributions. It also yields the corresponding bound for independent and identically distributed vectors. In particular, $C_0$ can be chosen to be $980$.

title: Minimal cellular resolutions of complementary edge ideals
abstract: We construct an explicit minimal cellular resolution for every squarefree monomial ideal generated in degree $n-2$ in the polynomial ring $S=K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$. Such an ideal is the complementary edge ideal $I_c(G)$ of a simple graph $G$ on $[n]$, and the resolution is supported on a labeled regular CW complex $X_G$ of dimension at most $2$. This yields closed formulas for the differentials and for the multigraded Betti numbers of $I_c(G)$ in terms of graph invariants. We then determine the $a$-invariant of $S/I_c(G)$ in terms of the vertex connectivity of $G$. Finally, when $S/I_c(G)$ is Cohen--Macaulay, we describe the canonical module and its Hilbert series, and recover the known characterizations of the Gorenstein and level cases.

title: On a hybrid trilinear Hilbert transform
abstract:
In this paper we study the boundedness properties of a \emph{hybrid} trilinear Hilbert transform characterized by a \emph{dual regime} which simultaneously exhibits 1) \emph{resonant} (zero curvature) features, \emph{i.e.}, modulation invariance properties, and 2) \emph{non-resonant} (non-zero curvature) features.
  Specifically, given $a\in(0,\infty)\setminus \{1,2\}$ and $\vecλ:=(λ_1,λ_2,λ_3,λ_4)\in (\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\})^4$ with $λ_1\neq λ_2$ and $λ_3\neq λ_4$, we provide wide-range $L^p$ bounds for the trilinear operator $$ HTHT^a_{\vecλ} (f_1,f_2,f_3)(x):= p.v. \int_{\mathbb R} f_1(x-λ_1 t)\,f_2(x-λ_2 t-λ_3 t^a)\,f_3(x-λ_4 t^a)\,\frac{dt}{t},\quad x \in \mathbb{R}\,.$$
  By combining variable multiresolution, multiscale wave-packet analysis, and Rank II LGC method, our present work establishes a common framework where the diverse methodologies of all of the following naturally converge: i) the maximal truncated bilinear Hilbert transform, ii) the Biest operator, iii) the hybrid bilinear Hilbert-Carleson operator, and iv) the non-resonant (curved) trilinear Hilbert transform.
  Ultimately, this work reveals that the hybrid trilinear transform sits on a critical intermediate scale between the purely non-resonant case and the purely resonant regime -- the latter remaining a challenging, major (open) problem in harmonic analysis.

title: Fiber-Connectivity of Almost-Toric Systems in Four-Dimension
abstract: In this paper, we study the fiber connectivity of proper almost-toric systems $Φ$ on connected four-dimensional symplectic manifolds. Using Morse--Kirwan theory, we establish three sufficient conditions for fiber connectivity. These results generalize and extend the fiber connectivity results of Pelayo, Ratiu, and Vu Ngoc (2015) by relaxing some of their hypotheses.

title: Liouville theorem for monotone solutions of the Lane-Emden system in a half-space
abstract:
The Lane-Emden system is an important model case of Hamitonian elliptic systems. We here consider the zero-Dirichlet problem in a half-space for arbitrary powers $p,q\ge1$. We prove that any nonnegative classical solution that is nondecreasing in the normal direction is necessarily trivial. No bound at infinity of any kind is assumed and this extends the known scalar monotonicity theorem.
  We also obtain the same conclusion for the scalar equation $-Δu=f(u)$ when $f\in C^1([0,\infty))$ is nonnegative, $f(0)=0$, $f\not\equiv0$, and $f(s)/s$ is nondecreasing for $s>0$. This relaxes the convexity and $C^2$ regularity requirements on $f$ in previous works.
  To prove these results we introduce a new method, completely different from the normal convexity approach from previous works, which relies on a delicate combination of techniques and could be applied to more general systems. Our basic tool is a suitable average of the linear interpolant between the solution and its normal limit on each finite strip. We next use stability estimates, combined with an energy argument for the scalar equation, or a contraction argument relying on Bessel potentials and the Schur test for the system. Increasing the strip height then forces the solution to vanish.

title: Ergodicity of geodesic flows on Aravinda-Farrell twisted doubles
abstract: The announced rank-one ergodicity theorem of Rodriguez Hertz, Rodriguez Hertz, and Wu includes the nonpositively curved metrics considered here on Aravinda--Farrell twisted doubles. For these construction metrics, a direct geometric argument identifies the singular set. Their singular geodesics are precisely those tangent to the torus sections of finitely many flat product collars, so their initial vectors have Liouville measure zero. A compact simply connected modification region cannot contain a complete geodesic; this also treats the exotic connected-sum examples. Ergodicity then follows from the classical theorem on the regular set.

title: On the representability of actions of algebras with several bilinear multiplications
abstract: We study the representability of actions in varieties of algebras with $n \geq 1$ not necessarily associative bilinear multiplications. We first prove that, for homogeneous varieties, action accessibility is equivalent to being an Orzech category of interest. For an action accessible, operadic variety we then construct the external weak actor $\mathcal{E}(X)$ of an algebra $X$, an algebra with $n$ bilinear partial operations together with a natural monomorphism encoding the actions on $X$. We characterise the algebras admitting an actor in terms of $\mathcal{E}(X)$, and we deduce an obstruction to action representability: if, for some algebra $X$ with trivial multiplications, $\mathcal{E}(X)$ does not satisfy a multilinear identity of the variety, then the variety is not action representable. Computing the external weak actor explicitly, we obtain that associative and matching dialgebras are weakly action representable but not action representable, and that Poisson algebras, left-right non-commutative Poisson algebras and matching Lie algebras are not action representable. Finally, we introduce the reduced type $(p,q)$ of such a variety and prove that, over a field of characteristic different from $2$, an operadic variety of reduced type $(p,0)$, $(0,q)$ or $(1,1)$ is action representable if and only if it is term equivalent to the variety of Lie algebras or to that of abelian algebras. For the reduced types $(p,0)$ and $(0,q)$, the arguments require no assumption on the cardinality of the field, whereas the case $(1,1)$ requires the field to be infinite.

title: Adhesive riffle shuffles: one-parameter models and mixing bounds
abstract: We compare four simple shuffles with one adhesion parameter $p$: a card-weighted sticky riffle, a block-weighted riffle, a midpoint-interpolation shuffle, and a correlated-label inverse riffle. Independent surviving contacts create contiguous blocks; no force or energy constants are fitted. We give polynomial upper bounds with explicit dependence on $p$, common adjacency-survival lower bounds, and a sharper information lower bound for interpolation. For fixed deck size $n\ge4$, the mixing time diverges as $Θ((1-p)^{-1})$ for the three cut-first models, but as $Θ((1-p)^{-2})$ for the correlated-label model. The latter distinction comes from whether one or two additional contact breaks are needed to escape cyclic rotations. For even $n$, unglued interpolation retains the lower bound $Ω(\sqrt n\log n)$ and upper bound $O(n^{5/2}\log n)$. We distinguish proved bounds from conjectured scales, recover classical riffle cutoff under sufficiently small perturbations, and explain precisely where established results on clumpy shuffles apply. The fixed-parameter asymptotic orders of the new cut-first families and their possible cutoff remain unresolved.

title: Koszul duality for boundary categories
abstract: We study how Koszul duality relates two kinds of boundary constructions associated with a smooth category and a proper category. For a smooth category with a proper Koszul-dualizing subcategory, we construct a fully faithful functor from its categorical neighborhood of infinity to the singularity category associated to the proper category. We prove that this functor is an equivalence precisely when the smooth category is reflexive, meaning that it can be reconstructed from its finite-dimensional module theory. Under a Gorenstein condition, satisfied in the Calabi--Yau setting, the functor is induced by restriction of modules. We give algebraic criteria that ensure equivalence and obtain an identification of Hochschild cohomology.

title: Convergence properties of nonlinear RLC electrical networks
abstract: Convergence properties of general electrical networks with grounded nonlinear capacitors at the nodes and nonlinear inductors and resistors at the edges are studied. It is shown how, under appropriate conditions, for every initial condition there exists a unique equilibrium to which the system converges asymptotically. Partial extensions to networks with terminals or current sources are also provided. For RC networks this is compared with the use of an alternative storage function based on the co-content functions of the resistors.

title: Generic point processes are intermittently hyperuniform and maximally rigid
abstract: We study the prevalence of hyperuniformity and spatial rigidity among translation- invariant ergodic simple point processes of fixed intensity, in a topology controlling local second moments. Hyperuniform processes are dense but meagre. We prove that intermittent hyperuniformity is residual: the number variance exhibits hyperuniform behavior along some sequences of radii and hyperfluctuating behavior along others. Maximal rigidity is also residual. Thus generic processes are maximally rigid but not hyperuniform. A local-to-global principle reduces the proofs to cross-section constructions for an arbitrary fixed essentially free ergodic $\mathbb{R}^d$-action. We also prove that processes admitting revival sequences form a residual set and exhibit near-quadratic variance along suitable van Hove sequences.

title: Calabi flow on polarized Kähler surfaces
abstract: We study global smooth Calabi flows on polarized Kähler surfaces $(M,L)$, assuming uniformly bounded Sobolev constants and the algebraic conditions $χ(\mathcal O_M)=1$ and $c_1(M)\cdot c_1(L)>0$. Using the orbifold compactness theorem, we prove a uniform Bergman estimate, construct a normal test configuration for each geometric limit, and establish uniqueness of the extremal orbifold limit up to polarized holomorphic isometry. K-polystability then identifies the limit with the original surface and gives a constant scalar curvature Kähler metric. We also prove finite-group equivariant versions of these results. Independently of the flow, we obtain a uniform Bergman lower bound for polarized cscK surfaces with bounded volume and Sobolev constants and $|S|\leq1$. We illustrate the hypotheses with nonstationary flows near a product cscK metric on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ and near Calabi's non-cscK extremal metric on the first Hirzebruch surface. Their controlled-cone energy inequalities follow from elementary calculations and continuity.

title: Entire solutions of Fermat-Type Partial Differential-Difference equations in higher dimensions
abstract:
The purpose of this paper is to investigate the finite-order entire solutions of the following Fermat-type partial differential-difference equations: \begin{align*} (P_1(z)f(z+c))^{m_1}+\left(P_2(z)f(z)+\sideset{}{_{j=1}^m}{\sum} Q_j(z)\partial_{z_j}(f(z))\right)^{m_2}=P(z), \end{align*} \begin{align*} (P_1(z)f(z))^{m_1}+\left(P_2(z)f(z+c)+\sideset{}{_{j=1}^m}{\sum} Q_j(z)\partial_{z_j}(f(z))\right)^{m_2}=P(z) \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \left(\sideset{}{_{j=1}^m}{\sum} Q_j(z)\partial_{z_j}(f(z))\right)^{m_1}+\left(P_1(z)f(z+c)+P_2(z)f(z)\right)^{m_2}=P(z), \end{align*} in $\mathbb{C}^m$, where $m_1,m_2\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $m_1+m_2>2$, $c=(c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_m)\in\mathbb{C}^m$, $P(\not\equiv 0)$, $P_1$, $P_2$ and $Q_i\;(i=1,2,\ldots,m)$ are polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^m$ such that $P(z)$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{C}^m$.
  The results established in this paper generalize those of Xu et al. \cite{Xu-Luo-Cao-2025} from $\mathbb{C}$ to $\mathbb{C}^m$.

title: Global existence and decay estimates of solutions for the compressible Prandtl type equations in Sobolev spaces
abstract: This paper addresses the global existence and large-time decay of solutions to the two-dimensional compressible Prandtl equations in Sobolev spaces. We study small perturbations around a monotone shear flow and establish global weighted Sobolev estimates together with precise time-decay rates for the solutions. The main difficulties are that the normal velocity causes a loss of one tangential derivative, the variable density gives rise to nonstandard boundary and shear-flow coupling terms, and the global-in-time argument requires sufficiently strong decay to close the time-weighted energy estimates. To overcome these difficulties, we combine the cancellation method introduced by Masmoudi and Wong~\cite{MW2015} with the good-quantity approach developed by Paicu and Zhang~\cite{PZ2021}, together with weighted shear-flow estimates and a careful treatment of the natural boundary structure. Under suitable assumptions on the density perturbation, the shear flow, and the function $f(t)$ describing the outer tangential flow, we prove the global-in-time well-posedness of solutions in weighted Sobolev spaces. In this sense, the present result may be viewed as a Sobolev-space counterpart of the recent analytic-framework result obtained by Chen, Huang and Li (J. Funct. Anal. 286 (2024), 110322)~\cite{CHL2024} for the two-dimensional compressible Prandtl-type equations, while requiring a weaker time-decay assumption on the density perturbation.

title: Volume Doubling and Geometric Inequalities on Graphs with Bakry-Émery Curvature
abstract:
We consider irreducible reversible Markov chains whose nonzero off-diagonal transition probabilities are bounded below by $ε>0$ and whose reversible measure satisfies $m_-\le m(x)\leκm_-$. Under the Bakry--Émery curvature condition $\mathrm{CD}(K,\infty)$, with $K\in\mathbb{R}$, we establish Wang's log-Harnack inequality $$
  P_t(\log f)(x)\le\log P_tf(y)
  +\frac{C\mathrm{dist}(x,y)^2}{\int_0^t e^{2Ks}\mathrm{d} s}, $$ for bounded positive $f$ bounded away from zero and all $x,y\in V$, where $C$ is a constant dependent only on $\varepsilon$. Building upon this inequality, we further prove volume doubling property: let $K_-:=\max\{-K,0\}$ $$
  \mathrm{Vol}(B(o,2R))\le C_0\exp\!\bigl(C_1\sqrt{K_-}\,R\bigr)
  \mathrm{Vol}(B(o,R)),\qquad R>0, $$ where $C_0,C_1$ depend only on $ε,κ$. If $d$ is the maximum combinatorial degree of the support graph, we further prove under $\mathrm{CD}(0,\infty)$ the sharp volume growth bound $\mathrm{Vol}(B(o,R))\le m_-CR^{\lfloor d/2\rfloor}$ for all $o$ and $R\geq 1$.

title: Federated Affine Variational Inequalities: Exact Averaging and Complexity Limits
abstract:
We study the classical Local Stochastic Extragradient method (Local SEG) for monotone variational inequalities under intermittent communication, where devices perform several local oracle calls between synchronization rounds. For affine monotone mean operators, including nonsymmetric bilinear saddle systems, we prove that equal device averaging commutes pathwise with both stages of the stochastic extragradient update. Local trajectories may therefore drift apart while their mean follows a centralized stochastic-extragradient recursion driven by averaged noise. The identity remains valid when individual oracle realizations are nonlinear and query dependent.
  Under conditionally centered oracle errors that are conditionally independent across devices within each stage, the reduction yields a restricted weak-gap rate that uses the local sequential depth for deterministic progress and the aggregate oracle budget across devices for variance reduction. When every device makes at least two local oracle calls per communication round, the bound contains no additional mixed client-drift term and is also attained by a terminal-only aggregation schedule. An affine Gaussian lower bound matches the depth and sample dependences before statistical saturation for distributed zero-respecting algorithms; its statistical component applies to arbitrary randomized algorithms. A complementary lower bound for feasible distributed zero-respecting methods shows that bounded geometry and query-dependent noise can create an additional communication-locality obstruction. These results delineate the exact-averaging regime of unconstrained affine Local SEG and a complexity boundary that arises under active feasibility constraints.

title: Uniform Dimension Theorem for SLE in Natural Time
abstract: For $0<κ<8$, we prove a uniform dimension transformation theorem for SLE in natural time: on a single probability-one event, Hausdorff and packing dimensions of every time set are multiplied by $d=1+κ/8$, and the same holds for lower and upper box dimensions of every bounded time set. The result applies to self-similar SLE with stationary increments, chordal SLE in the half-plane, and chordal SLE in bounded piecewise $C^1$ Jordan domains. In the last case, the box-dimension conclusion holds under a positive-angle endpoint hypothesis.
