The proof treats guided and continuum channels together in the edge trace and requires neither a guided metric graph nor a lower-departure estimate uniform at zero tangential momentum.

title: Extension of kappa-additive measures
abstract: We establish an extension theorem for kappa-additive probability measures, where kappa is an arbitrary uncountable cardinal. Starting from a <kappa-algebra, we define an outer measure using coverings of cardinality at most kappa and characterise measurable sets by approximation in outer measure of symmetric differences. We prove that these sets form a kappa-algebra carrying a complete kappa-additive extension of the original measure. The extension is unique on the generated kappa-algebra, and its completion is the minimal domain admitting a complete kappa-additive extension. We also establish attainment of the covering infimum and show why the closure assumption on the initial algebra is essential. Examples include a strict extension of classical Lebesgue measure under the additional hypothesis add N = aleph_1 < cov N.

title: The Covering Radius of the Reed--Muller Code \texorpdfstring{$\RM(3,8)$}{RM(3,8)} is 56
abstract: We prove that the covering radius of the third-order Reed--Muller code in eight variables is fifty-six. The proof separates even- and odd-weight inputs by moment-controlled slicing. On the even side, a transport invariant on quadratic-label stars and consistency of singleton restrictions give a compatible cubic correction. On the odd side, symmetry of the third moment yields a covariance-rank obstruction. Its rank-two exception is a quartic plus three points of a two-plane; the zero-second-moment case is a prescribed-point perturbation of a quintic. We prove that every such point perturbation has third-order nonlinearity at most fifty-five by a marked derivative identity and complete restriction-code covers. Consequently the maximum among exact-degree-eight functions is fifty-five. The structural reductions are proved analytically, and complete finite certificates verify the explicitly stated local covering and compatibility assertions. The matching lower bound follows from the published quartic relative radius.

title: Global attractor for weakly damped nonlinear parametric Klein-Gordon Schr{ö}dinger system
abstract: We consider a damped forced nonlinear Klein-Gordon Schr\''{o}dinger (KGS) system known as the parametric KGS system with Yukawa coupling. We prove the regularity of the global attractor for this infinite-dimensional dynamical system, i.e. that the global attractor is included into a smaller Sobolev space than the energy space. We prove that this global attractor has finite fractal dimension, without any assumption on the decay of the forcing terms.

title: Failure of bounded $\bar\partial$-solvability on pseudoconvex domains of finite type
abstract: We show that for every integer $n\ge3$ there is a bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$ with smooth real-analytic boundary whose maximum boundary D'Angelo $1$-type is $16$, carrying a $\bar\partial$-closed form continuous on the closure and smooth in the domain with no bounded distributional solution. On each fixed domain, we also construct a uniformly bounded sequence of smooth $\bar\partial$-closed data for which every bounded solution has norm at least $ck^{1/320}$ for all sufficiently large $k$. Each datum in this sequence and a corresponding solution extend smoothly to a neighborhood of the closure. The obstruction comes from a singular curve in two weak complex tangential directions, whose normalization admits holomorphic functions that do not extend to a neighborhood of the curve.

title: Hodge--Riemann relations for $m$-positive and generalized $m$-positive forms
abstract: We study Hodge--Riemann relations for ordinary, sequential, and weak $m$-positive real $(1,1)$-forms in complex dimension $d$. For ordinary $m$-positive forms, we prove the fully mixed relations in every permitted bidegree without assuming semipositivity, generalizing results by Xiao. As a generalization of ordinary $m$-positivity, sequential $m$-positivity is defined by the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant. We formulate a generalized mixed Hodge--Riemann conjecture for this condition and prove several cases beyond the scalar inequalities supplied by hyperbolicity. We also consider weak $m$-positivity which corresponds to the pointwise subsolution condition for the complex $m$-Hessian equation. In this setting, we prove the Hodge--Riemann relations for $p\neq q$ and in several diagonal cases, and show that the associated power map induces a pointwise diffeomorphism onto the cone of positive $(d-1,d-1)$-forms. Using Dinh and Nguyên's $L^2$ globalization method, we pass from the pointwise relations to cohomology classes on compact Kähler manifolds. Finally, we propose conjectures on a numerical criterion for sequential positivity and on solvability of the generalized $m$-Hessian equation.

title: Rigidity of the Peres-Virág class
abstract: Consider the hyperbolic Gaussian analytic function (GAF) \begin{equation*} F_{\mathbb{D}}(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty }ξ_{n}z^{n},\qquad |z|<1, \end{equation*} where the $ξ_{n}$ are independent standard complex Gaussian variables. Peres-Virág theorem tells that the distribution of the zeros of $F_{\mathbb{D}}(z)$ is provided by a Determinantal Point Process (DPP). We prove that $F_{\mathbb{D}}(z)$ is the only GAF whose zeros are determinantal with a Hermitian kernel, up to multiplication by a zero-free holomorphic function and a one-to-one holomorphic change of variable, with a \ non-degeneracy condition imposed to exclude trivial cases. The proof identifies a geometric property of GAF's with (local) determinantal zeros: the metric defined by the first intensity must have constant curvature $-4$.

title: Digital Finite Group Theory
abstract: This book develops a digital formulation of finite group theory, in which every finite group of order $N$ is represented as the alphabet $\{0,1,\dots,N-1\}$ endowed with the transported group product. Multiplication, inversion and related structure are written explicitly as integer operations on labels. The foundations treat digit functions, codes of permutations and $r$-ary operators, finite magmas, and constructions of laws from diagrams. Classical parts of finite group theory, including conjugacy classes, stabiliser chains and characters, are recast as identities between digits of codes. The book gives explicit digital laws for all groups of order at most 32, the finite quotients of the 17 plane and 230 space crystallographic groups, the symmetric and alternating groups, the finite simple groups of Lie type, and all 26 sporadic groups. For most sporadic groups the laws are obtained by chain constructions; for the Baby Monster and the Monster they are computed structurally from the 196884-dimensional representation and evaluated with the mmgroup package. The accompanying software archive reproduces the laws, tables and worked examples as verifiable integer data.

title: Perturbation Analysis of Gravitational Collapse of Gaseous Stars in the Pressureless Euler-Poisson System
abstract: The compressible Euler-Poisson system describes the full evolutionary processes of inviscid compressible gases, including compression, expansion, fluid motion, equilibrium states and gravitational collapse, under the combined effects of self-gravitation, pressure and inertial forces. It constitutes the fundamental macroscopic mathematical model for describing stellar structures, nebular evolution and gravitational collapse of gaseous celestial bodies. The system comprises mass conservation, momentum conservation, energy conservation laws coupled with the Poisson equation. Following the research in \cite{huang2022}, this paper investigates the quantitative relations among the relative perturbation amplitude of initial velocity, critical time and collapse time for gaseous stars undergoing gravitational collapse within the framework of the pressureless Euler-Poisson system. The closed-form formulas are verified against direct numerical integration, the accuracy of the asymptotic power law is quantified, and the relation between the two time scales is examined.

title: Universality of monomial square forms
abstract:
A monomial square form is a polynomial $F=\sum_{i=1}^k M_i^2$, where $M_1,\ldots,M_k$ are pairwise distinct squarefree monomials $\ne1$. We consider the problem of which of these forms are universal, i.e.\ represent every positive integer. We consider three classes of such forms:\\ (1) Forms $M_1^2+M_2^2+M_3^2+M_4^2$ ($k=4$),\\ (2) Forms $M_1^2+\ldots +M_5^2$ ($k=5$) in at most 5 variables,\\ (3) Forms where the monomials are products of consecutive variables of a fixed length:\\ $P_{m,d}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{d}(x_ix_{i+1}\cdots x_{i+m-1})^2,$ and its circular version\\ $C_{m,d}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}(x_ix_{i+1}\cdots x_{i+m-1})^2\quad(n=m+d-1,\ x_{i+n}=x_i).$ We classify which of these are universal, possibly universal, or conditionally universal on a conjecture on the form $x^2+4y^2+5z^2$. This ternary form appears repeatedly and seems to play a central role.
  For forms (1), we also show that a form is universal if and only if it represents 14, 15, 29 and 9591 (partially conditional on $x^2+4y^2+5z^2$).

title: On Higher Order Elliptic Differential Operators
abstract: In this note we examine the positive preserving properties, or the lack thereof, for Green's operators of elliptic differential operators on smooth, closed Riemannian manifolds. We will obtain the existence of elliptic differential operators on closed manifolds whose lowest eigenvalue is not simple, and the existence of a large family of elliptic differential operators on closed manifolds that only have signed eigenfunctions associated with the lowest eigenvalue. That is, we will see that there is both "good news" and "bad news" when one studies the positivity preserving properties of Green's operators associated with higher order elliptic differential operators on smooth, closed Riemannian manifolds and the eigenproblem for higher order elliptic differential operators on smooth, closed Riemannian manifolds.

title: Fluid Antenna Array-Enabled Near-Field ISAC: Joint Port Position Optimization and Transmit Beamforming Design
abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FASs) have shown that activating a single port from a densely packed antenna array can yield spatial diversity comparable to that of tens of independent antennas, a property that has substantially improved communication reliability and efficiency. The fluid antenna array (FAA) extends this concept to multi-port configurations while avoiding complex multi-dimensional spatial correlation, and offers significant geometrical flexibility under a finite aperture and a limited port budget. These attributes motivate environment-adaptive array geometry for sensing in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Although this flexibility enables adaptive array geometries that exploit near-field distance-angle information, improving multi-parameter target estimation under communication and deployment constraints remains challenging. In this paper, we propose a planar FAA-assisted near-field ISAC framework for multiuser communication and target sensing. Specifically, we derive the Fisher information matrix (FIM) and the corresponding Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) for the joint estimation of target range, zenith angle, azimuth angle, and radial velocity. Based on the derived CRB, we jointly optimize the FAA port positions and transmit beamforming to improve sensing accuracy while satisfying communication signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), transmit power, and physical deployment constraints. To solve the resulting non-convex problem, we develop a two-stage alternating optimization algorithm, in which transmit beamforming is optimized through semidefinite relaxation (SDR), while FAA port positions are successively optimized through discrete search and continuous refinement. Simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm achieves favorable sensing performance while maintaining a reasonable computational cost.

title: Local limit Theorem for Directed polymers in a random environment in the full weak disorder regime
abstract: For directed polymers in random environment, we provide a short and mostly self-contained proof of the local limit theorem in the full weak disorder phase, including the critical inverse temperature $β_c$. That is, the point-to-point partition function is well approximated by the product of two independent point-to-line partition functions (one starting from each endpoint of the system) multiplied by the simple random walk transition kernel. The approximation is valid in the $L^p$ sense for an optimal range of $p$. The result is new at $β=β_c$ and for $p>2$, and in all cases the proof is significantly simpler, technically and conceptually, than what can be found in the literature. As a consequence of the result we establish an invariance principle for the polymer measure with fixed end-point, valid for all $β\in [0,β_c]$.

title: Stability Filters for Receding-Horizon Games
abstract: In receding-horizon games, self-interested players repeatedly solve a finite-horizon generalized Nash equilibrium problem (GNEP) and apply its first-stage actions. Ensuring stability of the resulting closed-loop system, however, is a challenging task that requires careful design of the players' strategies or additional constraints. We propose a stability filter that minimally modifies the variational equilibrium of the finite-horizon GNEP to enforce a prescribed decrease of a quadratic Lyapunov function. For receding-horizon games with linear dynamics, quadratic costs, and polyhedral coupling input constraints, whose associated GNEP is strongly monotone, we show that a filter always exists such that a closed-loop equilibrium exists, the filter is always feasible, does not intervene when the equilibrium already satisfies the decrease condition, and that renders the closed loop globally exponentially stable. Moreover, the filtered strategy is an $ε$-generalized Nash equilibrium, with $epsilon$ vanishing exponentially along closed-loop trajectories.

title: Corona and Gleason problems for certain Banach spaces of holomorphic functions
abstract: We use a combination of the classical dead-end space method and the interpolation (by bounded holomorphic functions) method to affirmatively solve Corona and Gleason problems for familiar Banach spaces of holomorphic functions such as (Besov-)Lipschitz spaces of holomorphic functions on bounded symmetric domains (including the unit ball and polydisc) in $\mathbb{C}^n$, holomorphic mean (Besov-)Lipschitz spaces, (Besov-)Hardy-Sobolev spaces and some special classes of holomorphic mixed-norm (Bergman) spaces (including weighted Bergman spaces) as well as some special classes of holomorphic (mean) Besov-Lipschitz spaces on the unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^n$. Indeed, we extend our recent work on both problems for holomorphic Lipschitz algebras.

title: Efficient Numerical Evaluation of Arbitrary High-order Partial Derivatives via Algebraic Decomposition
abstract: Computing high-order partial derivatives of multivariate functions is often computationally and memory intensive. This paper addresses this problem via an algebraic approach. High-order partial derivatives of a multivariate function are expressed as linear combinations of univariate directional derivatives, which are computationally friendly. The coefficients and direction vectors are determined by the Waring decomposition of monomials, so that the number of univariate directional derivatives in the representation is minimized. Numerical experiments confirm the efficiency of the proposed method.

title: Modular L-functions and Chebyshev systems
abstract: We study real zeros of completed modular L-functions and the determination of cusp forms by their periods. Using Chebyshev systems and the Riemann-Roch theorem, we obtain bounds for real zeros, counted with multiplicity, and rank estimates for evaluation maps in terms of the dimensions of cusp-form spaces and the genera of modular curves. These estimates give criteria for finite families of periods to determine a cusp form and yield explicit dual bases in cases where the relevant quotient curves have genus zero. We also bound the dimensions of rational spans of eigenform periods.

title: Buildings governed by twisted Bruhat orders
abstract: This paper introduces the notion of a twisted building associated to a Coxeter system and an initial section of a reflection order. These are pairs of buildings and a map between them which depends on a twisted Bruhat order. It is proved that projection maps exist between components and that the common apartment property holds for a suitable notion of an apartment, generalising what is known for twin buildings. Several well-known examples are given, including a family of twisted buildings associated to an affine building and its façades.

title: Compressed Multiscale Kernel Collocation and Physics-Informed Kernel Learning for Elliptic BVPs
abstract: Kernel collocation is a meshfree method for partial differential equations whose accuracy depends on the smoothness of the kernel and of the solution. For globally supported kernels, however, the collocation matrices are dense and severely ill-conditioned. We address both issues by combining a multiscale collocation scheme with samplets, a multiresolution basis of discrete signed measures with vanishing moments. In the samplet basis, the collocation matrix has only O(N log N) relevant entries, while the multiscale scheme adapts the kernel width to the spacing of the points on every level. Since the differential operator scales the equations at the interior points differently from those at the boundary points, the rescaling alone does not bound the condition number of the level systems. We therefore solve them by a Schur-complement reduction that is invariant under this scaling. For noisy data, we consider physics-informed kernel learning, which replaces the collocation system by a regularized least-squares fit. We show that it reduces to collocation as the regularization vanishes, and we solve it by a deflated conjugate gradient method that reuses the Schur-complement reduction. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions, with exact and noisy boundary data, show that the method handles significantly more points than dense collocation.

title: The kinetic Kato square root problem
abstract: We solve the kinetic Kato square root problem for the whole-space Kolmogorov operator $$H_A=\partial_t-X\cdot\nabla_Y-\operatorname{div}_X(A\nabla_X)$$ on \(\mathrm L^2\) with Lebesgue measure, where \(A\) is a bounded measurable complex uniformly accretive matrix depending on all variables. We define its realization through a sesquilinear form and identify the square-root domains of the resulting maximal accretive operator and its adjoint with the intrinsic Sobolev space defined by one velocity derivative and half a derivative along the transport flow. The homogeneous norm equivalences depend only on the dimension and the coefficient bounds. The energy also controls a position derivative of order one third. The proof uses second-order resolvents and localized affine testing. A regularized transport symmetrizer gives hidden coercivity, while comparison with a positive Rockland operator supplies intrinsic smoothing. Commutator and dyadic approximation estimates remove the smoothing before a Carleson argument is applied. We also obtain uniform shifted square-root estimates and bounded velocity, transport and position Riesz transforms.

title: Non-simple Arrangements of Lines and Pseudolines with Many Triangles
abstract:
We study affine arrangements of an even number $n$ of lines and pseudolines with many triangles. For simple ones, Blanc's bound limits the number of triangular faces to $\lfloor n(n-5/2)/3\rfloor$. Adapting the Bartholdi-Blanc-Loisel doubling to the even case, we construct an infinite series of arrangements of $n=6\cdot2^t+2$ ($8,14,26,50,\ldots$) straight lines with two triple points and $(n(n-5/2)+1)/3$ triangles, one more than the simple bound allows.
  We obtain exhaustive enumerations of triangle-maximal pseudoline arrangements, simple or not, for even $n\le12$. For $n=6,8,10,12,14$ the maximum number of triangles, for both lines and pseudolines, is $7,15,25,38,54$; for $n=8,12,14$ every optimal arrangement has multiple points. All optimal arrangements for even $n\le12$ are realizable by straight lines, except two arrangements of 10 pseudolines, which are not stretchable. For the odd value $n=11$, no arrangement with $33$ triangles exists even with multiple points.
  We also obtain even arrangements by adding a line to odd ones. For $n\equiv2\pmod 6$ this again gives one triangle more than the simple bound, in pseudolines up to $n=44$ and in straight lines for $n=20$ and $n=32$. Doubling these pseudoline arrangements gives members of the series $18\cdot2^t+2$ and $30\cdot2^t+2$ with the same excess, up to $n=146$ and $n=242$, respectively; those with $n=38$ and $n=74$ are realizable by straight lines.
  These results lead us to conjecture that an arrangement of an even number $n$ of pseudolines has at most $\lfloor n(n-2)/3\rfloor-\lfloor n/6\rfloor$ triangles.

title: Pairs of quadrics in eleven variables over number fields
abstract: A nested version of the $δ$-method is developed for number fields $K/\QQ$ and is used to establish an asymptotic formula for the number of $K$-rational points of bounded height on non-singular complete intersections of two quadrics in $\PP^{n-1}_K$, when $n\geqslant11$.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for BD-RIS-Assisted Multi-UAV RSMA Communications
abstract: Beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (BD-RISs) extend conventional diagonal RISs by allowing controllable coupling among reflecting elements. This flexibility is attractive for aerial networks, where unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) face rapidly varying channels and strict power limits. In this paper, we study a hybrid BD-RIS-assisted multi-UAV rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) downlink, in which UAVs within favourable BD-RIS coverage use both direct and BD-RIS-aided links, whereas the remaining UAVs are served through direct links only. We formulate a network sum-rate maximization problem that jointly optimizes UAV trajectories, RSMA common-rate allocation, beamforming, BD-RIS scattering matrices, and UAV-BD-RIS association. The resulting mixed-integer non-convex problem is solved by using deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm, equipped with a constraint-preserving action layer that generates reciprocal and lossless BD-RIS responses in closed form and handles the binary association inside the environment transition. Simulation results, averaged over three training seeds under a physically consistent channel model with blocked direct links near the BD-RISs, show that the proposed design attains a sum rate comparable to SAC and higher than twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient ( TD3), proximal policy optimization (PPO), and deep Q-network (DQN), exceeds per-slot alternating optimization with fixed trajectories at about 1/65 of its per-slot runtime, and benefits mainly from RSMA, while the additional BD-RIS gain is modest.

title: Strong Borel-Cantelli laws and clusters of visits for random intermittent maps
abstract: Near the neutral fixed point of an intermittent map, a single entrance into a small target can be followed by a long run of consecutive visits, so the number of visits need not follow its mean. We study targets $[0,u_n]$ for iid random compositions of Liverani-Saussol-Vaienti maps with a bounded parameter law that is regularly varying at its minimum $α\in(0,1)$; this includes a single map. For $u_n=cn^{-g}L(n)$, where $c>0$, $0<g\leq1$ and $L$ is slowly varying, the visit count is almost surely asymptotic to its mean if and only if $\sum_n n^{-1}(nu_n)^{-(1-α)/α}<\infty$. Under the stationary law, the count divided by its mean converges to one in $L^1$ exactly when $nu_n\to\infty$. Thus clusters of visits separate these two modes of convergence.

title: Frank-Wolfe is Approximate Broximal Gradient Descent
abstract:
We show that the Frank-Wolfe method is an approximation of Broximal Gradient Descent (BroxGD), and hence of the ball-proximal method. For constrained minimization, the ball-proximal method minimizes the objective over the intersection of the feasible set with a ball around the current iterate. Linearizing the objective gives BroxGD, but the intersection can remain difficult to handle even when linear minimization over the feasible set alone is cheap. We therefore replace the intersection by a smaller copy of the feasible set, obtained by shrinking it toward the current iterate so that it lies inside the ball. Minimizing the linear model over this smaller set gives exactly Frank-Wolfe, with the shrinking factor as its step size.
  We examine what this approximation preserves and what it can lose. For smooth convex objectives on compact convex sets, Frank-Wolfe retains a linear-model decrease guarantee that gives it and BroxGD a common convergence proof, recovering the classical $O(1/k)$ bound. Among compact convex regions inside the ball chosen before the gradient is known, the smaller copy is the smallest that preserves the same linear-model decrease guarantee. Nevertheless, Frank-Wolfe can achieve much less linear-model decrease than BroxGD at the same radius. A simplex example illustrates the sparsity gained by restricting the region, while a family of triangles shows how Frank-Wolfe can lose the distance decrease guaranteed by BroxGD. We also give a computable test for recovering the distance guarantee and a refinement procedure that terminates after finitely many oracle calls on polytopes.

title: Resolution Is Not Accessibility: Coupled Minimax Risk for Reduced Statistical Experiments
abstract: A reduced experiment can have vanishing minimax risk yet lose arbitrarily much precision relative to full observation. We determine when growing reductions preserve target-specific minimax precision, their exact cost, and which omissions can remain without increasing that cost. For Gaussian sequence reductions, we give necessary and sufficient criteria for bounded relative risk and losslessness. With parameter-dependent information, sampling difficulty and unresolved target variation draw on the same parameter budget. We prove that the exact global asymptotic minimax risk is the maximum scalar interval-decision risk over their jointly attainable frontier under a Sobolev constraint. This identity shows that positive ambiguity at the inverse-square-root sample-size scale can preserve the full-observation minimax constant. Under the corresponding full-experiment risk match, a sharp boundary criterion determines when critical-order resolution suffices for losslessness. A quadratic Poisson budget yields an exact threshold and quadratic risk onset under a stated information condition. Across Poisson power budgets, separate-maxima planning incurs a diverging asymptotic coordinate-budget factor near full precision, both with a positive lossless threshold and with zero threshold but higher-order risk onset. Finite-sample calculations and conditional medical-data and classifier audits distinguish the effects of observation coverage and repeated measurement.

title: The Siegel-Shidlovskii Method Revisited
abstract: We revisit the classical Siegel-Shidlovskii method in transcendental number theory from a new perspective, in which functional relations play a central role. Within a single self-contained framework, we recover the foundational results in the theory of E-functions, including the Siegel-Shidlovskii theorem, Beukers' lifting theorem, and Andr{é}'s theorem on the singularities of the minimal differential operator annihilating an E-function. Notably, the latter is obtained without any recourse to the theory of Gfunctions. This unified approach also allows us to resolve a problem posed by Shidlovskii: we obtain a general algebraic independence measure extending the classical Siegel-Lang measure to an arbitrary algebraically independent family of E-values. We also provide a short elementary proof of a second theorem of Andr{é}, which has become an important tool in the theory of Efunctions and concerns the primality of the specialization, at a regular point, of the ideal of functional relations of a vector of E-functions satisfying a differential system.

title: Pollutant Concentration Reconstruction in Porous Media from Localized Measurements
abstract: Reliable environmental monitoring and groundwater protection heavily rely on the ability to reconstruct full pollutant concentration fields from sparse, partial field measurements. In porous media, dissolved contaminants are transported by groundwater flow while undergoing hydrodynamic dispersion and complex chemical or biological reactions. To address practical contamination challenges, this work investigates the reconstruction of pollutant distributions using water samples collected at discrete locations in unsaturated or saturated soils via sampling tubes equipped with ceramic tips. While these suction samplers provide critical local data, they inherently capture only a fraction of the subsurface environment, leaving wide areas unmonitored. Motivated by this real-world monitoring procedure, we propose steady and time-dependent advection-diffusion-reaction models to simulate contaminant transport. Our main contribution is a generalized unique continuation result demonstrating that, under appropriate physical and mathematical assumptions, two concentration fields coinciding on a non-empty observation region must match throughout the entire space-time domain, even when originating from different source configurations. We investigate this problem from both theoretical and numerical perspectives, backing our mathematical uniqueness results with numerical simulations that validate the efficiency and practical utility of our approach. The theoretical proofs combine regularity properties away from source singularities with unique-continuation principles for parabolic and elliptic partial differential equations, providing a robust framework for environmental risk assessment and site remediation.

title: McKean-Vlasov flights without moments: well-posedness, propagation of chaos and a critical threshold for law-dependent jumps
abstract: We study McKean-Vlasov equations driven by an isotropic $2s$-stable L{é}vy noise, $s\in(0,1)$, whose solutions may have no finite mean, with coefficients that are Lipschitz with respect to a bounded Wasserstein-type distance. When the jump noise is additive, we prove strong well-posedness for every initial law and every $s$, without any moment assumption, and propagation of chaos at the rate $N^{-1/2}$ for kernel interactions. When the size of the jumps depends on the law, we prove the same results for $s>1/2$, and we show by an example that uniqueness fails for every $s<1/2$. The value $s=1/2$ thus separates well-posedness from non-uniqueness; the critical case itself remains open. These results answer, for stable noise, the question of uniqueness without moments raised by Jourdain, M{é}l{é}ard and Woyczy{ń}ski and by Cavallazzi.

title: Characterization of the boundary zero set of stable polynomials in $\mathbb B_2$
abstract: Given a polynomial $p\in \mathbb{C}[z,w]$ whose zeros lie outside the unit ball $\mathbb{B}_2$ of $\mathbb{C}^2,$ we study its local Weierstrass polynomial--obtained via the Weierstrass Preparation Theorem--and provide a strong version of the Nash curve selection lemma. These results lead to a characterization of the intersection of the zero set of $p$ with the unit sphere: $\mathcal{Z}(p)\cap\mathbb{S}_{2}.$

title: The anelastic approximation and convergence rate for the compressible Navier-Stokes equations with ill-prepared data in bounded domains
abstract: We justify the anelastic approximation and establish a convergence rate for local strong solutions to the isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations in a three-dimensional bounded domain, with ill-prepared initial data and vorticity-slip boundary conditions. When the Mach and Froude numbers vanish at the same rate $ε$, the system converges to an anelastic system with nonconstant hydrostatic density. Compared with the incompressible limit, the balance between singular pressure and gravity generates a variable-coefficient acoustic operator and additional commutators. To overcome these difficulties, we introduce the pressure perturbation adapted to the hydrostatic balance and establish weighted acoustic and vorticity estimates, yielding uniform-in-$ε$ estimates. We then use the weighted Helmholtz decomposition and time-averaging technique to prove the strong convergence of solenoidal component of the momentum and obtain an error bound controlled by $ε$ and the initial error in the projected momentum. Our analysis reveals the weighted cancellation mechanism that applies to singular limits around a class of nonconstant equilibria.

title: Correlators of the Jacobi Unitary Ensemble on a General Interval and Hurwitz Numbers
abstract: We study correlators of the Jacobi Unitary Ensemble $\mathbf J(p,q,α,β,N)$ of Hermitian matrices with spectrum in an arbitrary real interval $[p,q]$. For $(p,q)=(0,1)$, Gisonni, Grava and Ruzza expressed the large-$N$ expansion of the correlators $\langle\prod_j \mathrm{tr}\,X^{λ_j}\rangle$ through triple monotone Hurwitz numbers. We extend this genus expansion to arbitrary $p,q$ with $α/N$ and $β/N$ fixed. Using the Frobenius characteristic map and the idempotent basis of the center of $\mathbb C[\mathfrak S_n]$, we also obtain an explicit formula for the Schur--Selberg type integral $\int_{(p,q)^N}χ_λ(x)\,Δ^2(x)\prod_a (q-x_a)^β(x_a-p)^α\,\mathrm{d}^Nx$ in terms of irreducible characters of the symmetric group and content products. As consequences, we describe the zero-mean ensemble, and we recover, term by term in the genus expansion, the polygon-gluing formula for the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble in the limit $c_A=c_B\to\infty$. Structurally, passing from $[0,1]$ to $[p,q]$ leaves the hypergeometric weight of the associated 2D Toda tau function unchanged and only changes the specialization of its second set of times.

title: Closed energy formulas on tensor squares of perfect crystals of types $D_4^{(3)}$ and $G_2^{(1)}$
abstract: For each integer $l\ge1$, we give closed formulas for the local energies on tensor squares of the level-$l$ perfect crystals of types $D_4^{(3)}$ and $G_2^{(1)}$, normalized to vanish at the all-zero coordinate tensors. The $D_4^{(3)}$ energy is the maximum of three defects, equivalently of nine linear forms in parameters of classical highest-weight elements. Eliminating these parameters yields the maximum of nine piecewise-linear functions of the twelve input coordinates. Tensor-compatible similarity identifies the $G_2^{(1)}$ energy at level $l$ with one third of the pullback of the $D_4^{(3)}$ energy at level $3l$, yielding the same coordinate formula. The formula has no explicit level dependence, respects natural coordinate-set inclusions between levels, and allows direct evaluation without the combinatorial $R$-matrix or crystal-graph traversal.

title: Movable Antenna-Assisted Secret Key Generation over Temporally Correlated Channels
abstract: Physical-layer key generation (PLKG) exploits reciprocal channel dynamics to generate symmetric keys, addressing the key distribution problem in wireless communications. However, strong temporal correlation in slow-fading environments limits fresh randomness and results in low key generation rates. Movable antennas (MAs) introduce spatial degrees of freedom through antenna repositioning, providing a new approach to addressing the limitation. This paper investigates MA-assisted PLKG over temporally correlated channels. A first-order Gauss-Markov process is utilized to characterize the temporal correlation of multipath gains. We characterize the full-sequence mutual information (MI) over temporally correlated channels. For fixed antenna positions and beamforming, we establish a finite-horizon approximation error bound that vanishes as both effective signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) increase. We derive a closed-form expression for the one-step conditional MI and adopt it as a tractable key-information metric. A nonconvex problem is formulated to jointly optimize antenna positions and per-slot beamforming under transmit-power and minimum-spacing constraints. We develop an alternating optimization algorithm, combining an exact principal-eigenvector beamforming solution with feasible SCA-based projected gradient position updates. Simulation results demonstrate that the MA-assisted scheme outperforms the fixed-position antenna baseline. At a high temporal correlation coefficient, position optimization achieves approximately $51\%$ higher rates than fixed antennas. Joint position and beamforming optimization provides a further $106\%$ gain over position optimization alone, demonstrating more pronounced gains under strong temporal correlation.

title: Generalized parabolic Demazure modules and the N!/2-conjecture for two-row diagrams
abstract: We study a family of generalized parabolic Demazure modules, i.e. of gl[x]-submodules of tensor products of integrable representations of the affine Lie algebra generated by tensor products of extremal vectors, and describe these modules by generators and relations. Realizing the Garsia--Haiman modules of two-row diagrams as fusion products of two local Weyl modules, we show that their y-graded components admit filtrations whose associated graded modules are isomorphic to tensor products of these generalized parabolic Demazure modules with the cohomology rings of Grassmannians. As a consequence, the Garsia-Haiman modules of two-row diagrams of a fixed size generate a distributive lattice, and the N!/2-conjecture holds for two-row diagrams.

title: Asymptotically Optimal Weighted Edge Colorings via Local Bin Packing
abstract:
We study weighted edge coloring, where each edge of a graph $G$ has a weight in $(0,1]$, and colors are assigned so that the incident weight of each color at every vertex is at most one. The objective is to minimize the number of colors, denoted by $χ'_w(G)$. This generalizes classical edge coloring (all weights are one) and bin packing ($G$ is a star). Two natural lower bounds are the maximum weighted degree $Δ_w(G)$ and the maximum local bin-packing number $\mathrm{bp}(G)$: the maximum, over vertices, of the minimum number of unit bins needed to pack the incident weights. We have $\lceilΔ_w(G)\rceil\le\mathrm{bp}(G)\leχ'_w(G)$. How closely these local lower bounds approximate the global optimum is a longstanding open problem.
  Our main result establishes an asymptotic weighted analogue of Vizing's theorem: every simple graph admits a coloring using at most $(1+o(1))\mathrm{bp}(G)$ colors. Thus local bin packings can be made globally consistent with asymptotically vanishing relative loss, even in nonbipartite graphs. Our local-to-global rounding framework coordinates feasible local packing distributions into a partial coloring, leaving only $o(\mathrm{bp}(G))$ uncolored weight at every vertex.
  For bipartite multigraphs, we prove $χ'_w(G)\le(2+o(1))Δ_w(G)$, establishing the Chung--Ross conjecture [SICOMP'91] asymptotically. For loopless multigraphs, we obtain the exact bound $χ'_w(G)\le3\lceilΔ_w(G)\rceil$. Both leading coefficients are optimal, giving weighted analogues of the classical Kőnig--Shannon bounds.
  Further upper and lower bounds show that the classical factor-$3/2$ separation does not persist with the local bin-packing benchmark. We also disprove the exact weighted-degree conjecture of Feige and Singh [ESA'08]. Our upper bounds have polynomial-time algorithms, and their existence statements are formalized in Lean 4.

title: A Note on Fractional Sobolev inequalities revisited
abstract: In this paper, we extend the analysis of homogeneous fractional Sobolev inequalities in the paper by A.D. Nguyen, J. I. Dıaz, and Q.-H. Nguyen (2020). We combine their subcritical proof with the first author's adaptation to the supercritical case to provide a short interpolation-based proof for the critical case.

title: Constructing free subgroups of matrix groups
abstract: The Tits alternative asserts that a finitely generated linear group is either solvable-by-finite or contains a non-abelian free subgroup. Given a non-solvable-by-finite subgroup G of GL(d, F), where F is the field of complex numbers or a non-archimedean local field, we present methods to construct explicitly a non-abelian 2-generator free subgroup of G in specific cases. Our implementations in the computeralgebra system Oscar are publicly available.

title: Adaptive accuracy-driven splitting in Ozaki matrix multiplication and application to block LU factorization
abstract: The Ozaki scheme for matrix multiplication computes an accurate matrix product by splitting the input matrices and evaluating a sequence of low-precision matrix products. Its accuracy and computational cost depend strongly on the number of splits. We develop accuracy-driven criteria for selecting this number in both Ozaki matrix multiplication and in block LU factorization using Ozaki trailing updates. For matrix multiplication, we derive normwise and componentwise criteria that determine how many split products are required to achieve a given accuracy requirement. For block LU, we present a fixed normwise strategy with essentially no selection cost, an LU-aware adaptive normwise strategy that can reduce the number of splits in subsequent trailing updates, and a componentwise strategy that uses information accumulated from preceding updates to guide the later selections. In the componentwise strategy, when the required number of splits exceeds a prescribed maximum, the corresponding update is instead carried out using ordinary matrix multiplication. We also provide rigorous backward error bounds for these approaches. Numerical experiments show that the adaptive normwise strategy can reduce the number of splits while preserving normwise accuracy, whereas the componentwise strategy can provide smaller componentwise backward errors when stronger local accuracy is needed.

title: Antidiagonal and square averages for amenable groups
abstract: We prove that, for commuting unitary representations $U,V$ of a countable amenable group $G$, the averages $$ D_F=\frac1{|F|}\sum_{g\in F}U_g^*V_g $$ have a common selfadjoint weak operator limit along all left and right \Folner{} sequences, with strong* convergence along two-sided sequences. This answers Bergelson's question on commuting actions. For any unitary representation $π$, we also prove that $A_F=|F|^{-1}\sum_{g\in F}π(g^2)$ converges strongly along right \Folner{} sequences to a selfadjoint central operator supported on the finite type~I part of $π(G)''$; the adjoints $A_F^*$ converge strongly along left \Folner{} sequences. This settles the convergence question for square averages posed by Bergelson and Rodríguez-Martín. For measure-preserving actions of finitely generated amenable or countable virtually FC groups, we obtain $$ \lim_n\frac1{|F_n|}\sum_{g\in F_n}μ(A\cap T_{g^2}A)>0 \qquad\text{whenever }μ(A)>0. $$ For each $\varepsilon>0$, the set $\{g:μ(A\cap T_{g^2}A)>μ(A)^2-\varepsilon\}$ meets every Bohr neighborhood of the identity in a set of positive lower density, uniformly over \Folner{} sequences. These intersections are also left and right IP$^*$ for virtually FC groups. We construct a unitary representation $π$ of a locally finite nilpotent group and a weakly mixing vector $f$ for which $\{g:\text{Re}\langleπ(g^2)f,f\rangle>-\varepsilon\}$ has upper Banach density zero for small $\varepsilon>0$. We also give a weakly mixing action of a two-generated solvable group for which the IP$^*$ conclusion fails. The recurrence results yield product sets $BB$ inside difference sets, with $B$ of positive upper density.

title: Graph splitting algorithms for inconsistent feasibility problems
abstract: In this work, we study graph splitting algorithms for feasibility problems involving closed and convex sets whose intersection may be empty. We characterize their minimal displacement vector, which is known to be the limit of the differences between successive iterates, in terms of a least-squares problem measuring disagreement between the sets according to the graph structure. We then specialize to closed affine subspaces, proving strong convergence of the shadow sequence to a solution of such a least-squares problem whenever one exists. Our analysis extends classical Douglas-Rachford results on best approximation pairs to graph splitting algorithms.

title: A Legendre-Based Modified Extreme Learning Machine for Convection-Diffusion Equations: Steady-State, Continuous-Time, and Discrete-Time Formulations
abstract: Convection-diffusion equations are fundamental models for transport phenomena, but their numerical solution becomes challenging in convection-dominated regimes due to steep gradients and sharp boundary layers. This motivates the development of accurate approaches capable of effectively resolving such features while avoiding costly iterative optimization. In this study, a modified ELM framework based on shifted Legendre polynomials is developed for convection-diffusion equations in steady-state, continuous-time, and discrete-time formulations. The proposed approach is evaluated on steady and unsteady benchmark problems with relatively high Peclet numbers, including continuous and discontinuous boundary conditions. Finite element method solutions are used as independent solution references. By exploiting the linearity of the governing equations, MELM determines the output weights through a single least-squares solve, avoiding the iterative gradient-based training required by PINNs. The shifted Legendre polynomial basis provides an effective spectral representation for resolving steep gradients and sharp boundary layers. For the DT-MELM formulation, the coefficient matrix remains unchanged across successive time levels, allowing its LU or QR factorization to be computed once and reused. A systematic comparison with PINNs that incorporate advanced training strategies demonstrates that MELM provides higher accuracy and shorter solution times for steady-state and DT-MELM formulations across the benchmark problems considered. In contrast, CT-MELM exhibits scalability limitations as the size of the space--time basis increases. Overall, the results demonstrate the effectiveness of MELM for steady-state and discrete-time convection--diffusion problems, while also showing that PINNs provide better scalability for large space--time formulations where global CT-MELM becomes computationally demanding.

title: Quasiconvexity and Lower Semicontinuity in the Riemannian Setting
abstract: We introduce a notion of quasiconvexity for integrands defined on the bundle of linear maps between the tangent spaces of two smooth, connected and complete Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$ and $(N,h)$, naturally extending the classical Euclidean notion. For continuous integrands, we prove that this Riemannian quasiconvexity is equivalent to the sequential lower semicontinuity of the associated functional $$ F(u,Ω)=\int_Ωf(du)\,dμ_g $$ with respect to the weak$^*$ convergence in $W^{1,\infty}(Ω,N)$, in the intrinsic sense adopted in the paper, for every bounded open subset $Ω\subseteq M$. We then establish the Riemannian analogues of the Acerbi--Fusco theorems for Carathéodory integrands satisfying the corresponding growth conditions, for every $1\leqslant p\leqslant+\infty$, with respect to the weak and weak$^*$ notions of convergence considered here.

title: Equivalent Graphical Conditions for Angle Rigidity and Angle-Based Network Localization
abstract: Angle rigidity theory provides a theoretical basis for characterizing the geometric shape of graphs embedded in the plane under angle constraints, and establishing global convergence of angle-based network localization algorithms. The related references, however, are largely restricted to graphs generated by triangulation or bilateration ordering, which are sufficient but not necessary for angle rigidity. This paper addresses this challenge by focusing on establishing the equivalence between angle constraints and bearing constraints. The conditions for cycle compatible frameworks (with possibly non-generic configurations) to be angle fixable are provided. Moreover, it is shown for the first time that Laman graphs equivalently characterize minimally globally angle rigid graphs, implying that a Laman graph is the simplest graph that allows a generic embedding in the plane to be uniquely determined by subtended angles. As an application, a distributed algorithm for angle-based sensor network localization is proposed, which guarantees global convergence under a much milder network topology condition than those in the literature.

title: Every tournament $T$ of order at least 3 admits infinitely many $T$-irregular oriented graphs
abstract: Let $F$ be a fixed graph. A graph $G$ is $F$-irregular if any two distinct vertices of $G$ belong to a different number of subgraphs of $G$ isomorphic to $F$. In this paper, we settle the strong conjecture about $F$-irregular oriented graphs (Dovzhenok, Lukashenko, and Filiuta, 2026) for the case of tournaments. Specifically, we prove that for every tournament $T$ of order $n \ge 3$, there exists an infinite family of $T$-irregular oriented graphs. Our proof is constructive. For $n \ge 4$, it is based on the vertex cloning method, and the underlying graphs of the constructed $T$-irregular oriented graphs are inherently $K_n$-irregular.

authors: Matheus Andrade Ribeiro de Moura Horácio
title: Rigidity of shrinking Ricci solitons with low-dimensional focal sets
abstract: We prove that, in every dimension, the focal set of the potential function of a complete gradient shrinking Ricci soliton with constant scalar curvature is totally geodesic whenever it has dimension two or three, and that every complete five-dimensional gradient shrinking Ricci soliton with constant scalar curvature is rigid. The first result follows from a Bochner identity for the covariant derivative of the Ricci tensor at the focal set. For the second, when the scalar curvature is twice the soliton constant, we prove that total geodesy implies rigidity through an integral identity on the level hypersurfaces; the case of scalar curvature three times the soliton constant is treated by a separate argument. As further applications, we combine our methods with the rigidity theorem in the recent preprint of Li, Li, Ou, Qu, Wu and Zhou to obtain rigidity in arbitrary dimension when the scalar curvature is twice or three times the soliton constant, and under integral Weyl pinching for four-dimensional focal sets.

title: Counterexamples to Relaxed Multiplication in List Coloring
abstract: Jiang and Zhu [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 137 (2019) 112--117] asked whether every $k$-choosable graph is $(km+1:m)$-choosable for every positive integer $m$. We answer this question negatively by constructing a graph with chromatic number and choice number $k$ that is not $(km+1:m)$-choosable for every $k\ge3$ and $m\ge10$. More generally, for integers $k\ge3$, $m\ge2$, and $t\ge0$, satisfying $m>8t+ε$, where $ε\in\{0,1\}$ is the parity of $m$, we construct such a graph that is not $(km+t:m)$-choosable. This also answers negatively the equivalent question of Xu and Zhu [SIAM J. Discrete Math., 36 (2022) 2585--2601] asking whether the strong fractional choice number of every graph is at most its choice number. This also indicates that, for each $k\ge3$, the supremum of the strong fractional choice numbers of graphs with choice number $k$ is at least $k+1/8$. When $t=0$, our construction yields counterexamples to multiplication for every $k\ge3$ and $m\ge2$. In particular, it yields a $3$-choosable graph on $91$ vertices that is not $(6:2)$-choosable, answering a question of Dvořák, Hu and Sereni [ Adv. Comb. (2019), Paper No. 5].

title: An optimal $χ$-bound for $\{P_7, \text{diamond}\}$-free graphs
abstract: A $\textit{diamond}$ is a graph obtained by removing an edge from the complete graph on four vertices. A graph is $\{P_7, \text{diamond}\}$-$\textit{free}$ if it contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to a seven-vertex path or a diamond. Schiermeyer (2020) asked whether there is a constant $c$ such that $χ(G)\leqω(G)+c$ for every $\{P_7, \text{diamond}\}$-free graph $G$. We answer this question affirmatively by proving $χ(G) \leq ω(G)+3$. Moreover, the bound is optimal.

title: Finite-horizon Optimal Consumption and Investment with Costly Income Adjustment
abstract: We study optimal consumption and investment for an investor who receives labor income until a fixed retirement date, can raise the income rate irreversibly at a constant price per unit of income flow, and cannot borrow against future income. A pathwise argument shows that no income is purchased during a final period before retirement whose length depends only on the interest rate and the price. Before this period the dual problem has two free boundaries: a lower one generated by the borrowing constraint and an upper one, at which income is purchased, that escapes to infinity as the final period begins. The analysis of this problem is our main mathematical contribution. During the final period it is a single obstacle problem, which we solve, together with the regularity of its free boundary, by established methods. Before that period a partial hodograph transformation straightens both free boundaries and turns the problem into a quasilinear parabolic equation with oblique boundary conditions on a fixed interval. Comparison principles, explicit barriers and regularity theory for quasilinear equations then give existence, uniqueness and smoothness. Transforming back and gluing the two constructions yields global regularity: both free boundaries are infinitely differentiable and the value function is a classical solution at every positive wealth level. A dual budget process verifies optimality. We also derive coupled Volterra integral equations for the free boundaries, prove exponential convergence to the perpetual problem under a scalar condition, and find numerically a purchase threshold that is U-shaped in the time to retirement.

title: Singular evolution of Gaussian measures under energy-critical and supercritical nonlinear Schrödinger equations
abstract:
We consider a family of nonlinear Schrödinger equations with odd-power nonlinearities and fractional dispersion in an energy-critical/supercritical regime. For a family of Gaussian measures supported on high-regularity spaces, we show that the flow immediately evolves these measures to ones that are mutually singular with respect to their initial distributions.
  In the cubic case, the threshold for singularity exactly corresponds to the energy scaling for the equation. In particular, we establish singular evolution of Gaussian measures under the flow of the energy-critical cubic NLS on the 4-dimensional torus.

title: Topological triviality of exact Lagrangian Cobordisms
abstract:
Inspired by the rigidity of exact Lagrangian submanifolds, a conjecture by P.~Biran
  and O.~Cornea asks if a simple exact Lagrangian cobordism $W$ in a tame
  exact symplectic manifold is always ``symplectically trivial'' (i.e.
  the Lagrangian suspension of an Hamiltonian isotopy).
  In this short note, we prove a topological version of this conjecture~:
  if the cobordism has dimension at least $6$, it is always topologically
  trivial. This extends a previous work of Lara Suarez who reduced the
  question to proving an injectivity result among fundamental groups.

title: Computational performance versus numerical accuracy in the acoustic terms of weakly-compressible SPH
abstract: Accurate computation of the acoustic terms in weakly-compressible SPH, including the equation of state, its inverse, and the evaluation of the local speed of sound, is essential to ensure energy conservation, robust solid boundary conditions, and correct open boundary behavior. In the classic Cole's equation of state, using values of the polytropic constant $γ\ne 1$ can lead to significant precision loss, particularly when computations are performed in single precision, as is common in GPU implementations. We extend here our previous results on the optimal choice of state variable by introducing a new higher-precision form for all three acoustic terms, denoted \texttt{explog}, and assess its numerical accuracy and computational performance across a variety of devices and test cases. We find that the new form evaluates the acoustic terms with a maximum ULP of~2 for arguments less than $0.125$, and has higher errors in less than 1\% of the arguments larger than the threshold. Combined with a rewritten expression of the pressure at solid boundary particles in the ``dummy'' model, it provides consistently more accurate results, maintaining deviations from the reference pressure profile to below 2\%, even in presence of a rough bottom terrain. Computationally, the new formulation is also faster than the naive one on GPU, and only marginally slower on CPU.

title: Quantum Private Information Retrieval on Forests
abstract: We consider the problem of graph private information retrieval (PIR) in the quantum setting. We focus on a specific type of graphs, namely the forest graphs. A forest graph is a union of disjoint trees. We consider the quantum setting where all the servers share an entangled state. Each server is allowed to send only one qudit per retrieval round. We design a scheme for the forest graphs that achieves the rate of $\frac{3}{N}$. The scheme uses a GHZ state as the initial entangled state between the servers prior to the scheme initiation. We compare our scheme with the only work done in the literature that considered the quantum setting of graph PIR. We show that our scheme is more efficient in this setting. We derive the quantum capacity for the case of $G=3K_2$, which is equal to $4/6$. $G=3K_2$ is a special case of the forest graph. We design a scheme that is specialized for this graph, achieving a rate equal to $4/6$ and provide the corresponding matching upper bound, establishing it as the capacity.

title: Lecture note on Fourier decoupling theory and its applications
abstract:
This paper is based on lecture notes taken and organized during the 17th Graduate Mathematics Intensive Training Program (Spring 2025), held at the Beijing International Center for Mathematical Research, in which Professor Shaoming Guo lectured on "An Introduction to Fourier Decoupling Theory." The main content includes an introduction to and proofs of $\ell^2$ decoupling inequality, together with its applications in number theory, harmonic analysis, and geometric measure theory.
  The writing follows Professor Guo's teaching style, proving theorems in an intuitive and heuristic manner; consequently, the text contains many figures to explain the ideas at hand, while also lacking some rigor. However, all of these geometric intuitions can be rigorously justified, albeit in a more complicated and technical way. The author hopes that readers will be able to understand, through these lecture notes, the geometric intuition hidden behind the cumbersome proofs, and thereby deepen their understanding of the relevant definitions and theorems. Rigorous proofs can be found in Professor Guo's forthcoming book, which interested readers may consult.

title: Weakly Lipschitz mappings in higher dimensions
abstract: We introduce and investigate the main features of weakly Lipschitz mappings whose pointwise Lipschitz constant is controlled from above by the derivative of a set function. The main results give conditions under which such mappings belong to $W^{1,n}_{\rm loc},$ and show that the class contains metrically quasiconformal mappings as a proper subclass. In addition, under a Rado--Reichelderfer type oscillation assumption, we derive diameter control, image-measure bounds, sufficient conditions for Lusin's $(N)$-property, and an area formula.

title: ParaDeAl: Parallel Descent Algorithms for Sparse Statistics
abstract: Best subset selection is a central problem in statistical regression, drawing increasing attention from the broader optimization and machine learning communities. Solving the hard L0 sparsity constraint directly has been computationally challenging; as a result, most existing work proposes formulations which do not enforce the constraint, but instead use a mix of L0/L1/L2 penalties to encourage sparsity. Modern methods for solving such penalized formulations are tractable for p = 100,000, but give up direct control over sparsity. In this paper, we propose a two-stage proximal gradient descent-based approach which both enforces the sparsity constraint and incorporates L1/L2 penalties, leveraging GPUs for computational acceleration to find approximate solutions. Our method, ParaDeAl, offers the user the ability to select the problem hyperparameters, solves all configurations in parallel, and obtains solutions up to 15x faster than the best state-of-the-art CPU competitors while achieving almost identical test accuracy for the same support size for large (p > 100,000) synthetic and real-world datasets.

title: Critical orthonormal Strichartz estimates for Lebesgue spaces
abstract: We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates at the critical coefficient exponent $q/2$ for fractional Schrödinger propagators. The proof for $d\geq3$ combines annular Schatten estimates with a frequency summation argument based on potential duality and Littlewood--Paley theory. In dimension two, a trace computation supplies the annular estimate needed for the global estimate. We also construct a counterexample to the global estimate with spatial $L^\infty$ and coefficients in $\ell^{q/2}$, even with a weak time norm.

title: Hyperbolic periodic orbits and optimal $1/t$ convergence of the Lax--Oleinik semigroup
abstract: Let $M$ be a closed manifold and $H:T^*M\to\mathbb{R}$ a $C^k$ ($k\geq2$) Tonelli Hamiltonian whose Aubry set consists of finitely many hyperbolic orbits, each of which is either a periodic orbit or a fixed point. We construct a $C^k$ critical subsolution that is quadratically strict outside the projected Aubry set. We then use this subsolution to establish an $O(1/t)$ rate of convergence for the associated Lax--Oleinik semigroup and the minimal action functions. This rate is optimal whenever at least one of these hyperbolic orbits is periodic.

title: High-order in-cell discontinuous reconstruction path-conservative methods for conservative systems in primitive variables
abstract: We present a path-conservative methodology for the numerical approximation of conservative systems formulated exclusively in primitive variables, the most physically relevant set of variables. The approach is designed to preserve the correct weak solution while avoiding the spurious oscillations near contact discontinuities that may arise in conservative formulations. Nonconservative products are treated through the selection of a suitable family of paths combined with an in-cell discontinuous reconstruction strategy, which is locally activated near shocks. To choose the path we introduce a compatibility condition between the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions of the non-conservative form, with the exact ones, assumed to be known. In smooth regions and across contact discontinuities, a standard path-conservative scheme is employed. The method is further extended to achieve high-order accuracy. Numerical results for the Euler multimaterial and shear interface model demonstrates correct shock-capturing property, suppression of spurious oscillations due to contact discontinuities, and convergence without using hybrid formulations.

title: An Active Flux Method for Maxwell's equations
abstract: We present a novel Active Flux method and a divergence-free method using exact evolution operators for solving Maxwell's equations in three space dimensions on Cartesian grids. The proposed methods are fully discrete, third-order accurate and rely on a truly multidimensional evolution operator based on Kirchhoff's formula for the electromagnetic wave equation. The first method is a classical Active Flux method with globally continuous reconstruction while the second method is an adaptation of the Active Flux method to a locally divergence-free reconstruction by Balsara. The applied reconstruction is built from facial degrees of freedom and is no longer globally continuous. The classical method keeps the divergence error bounded. The divergence-free method with face averages initialized by a potential keeps the constraints at round-off. We compare the accuracy of both methods for smooth and discontinuous test problems.

title: Spectral pairs of Newton non-degenerate polynomials with isolated singularities
abstract: We give a formula for the spectral pairs of Newton non-degenerate polynomials with isolated singularities. This is a revised version of a conjecture proposed by Steenbrink fifty years ago. Although this conjecture fails in the non-simplicial Newton polytope case, we can find the correction term using the intersection complexes and the primitive intersection cohomologies of toric varieties associated with non-simplicial compact faces. To verify the correctness of the formula, we provide a sample code for Singular which computes the spectral pairs and compares the output with that of sppairs in Singular for the three variable case.

title: Lossless propagation bounds for long-range fermionic interactions
abstract:
We prove propagation estimates for extensive fermionic many-body interactions with polynomial time growth, no loss of spatial decay, and an optimal threshold for the polynomial spatial exponent. More precisely, we construct local representatives of evolved fermionic many-body interactions on metric spaces with polynomial volume growth of order $d_{\mathrm{vol}}$ and suitable cell partitions. For the even Hamiltonian interaction $Φ_u$ and the even interaction $Ψ$ being evolved, we assume bounds, uniform in the site, on sums of term norms over finite supports $X$ containing a given site, with weights $e^{κ|X|}(1+\operatorname{diam}X)^a$ and $e^{κ|X|}(1+\operatorname{diam}X)^p$, respectively. Here $a>d_{\mathrm{vol}}$, $0\le p\le a$, $κ$ is sufficiently large, and the Hamiltonian bound is uniform in time. We construct local representatives whose interaction norms with weight $e^{c(1+|t-s|)^{-b}|X|}(1+\operatorname{diam}X)^p$ grow at most polynomially in $|t-s|$, for suitable $c,b>0$. In particular, $p=a$ is allowed: the Hamiltonian need not decay faster than the interaction being evolved. The threshold $a>d_{\mathrm{vol}}$ is optimal in general: uniform polynomial time bounds at $p=a$ fail for $0<a\le d_{\mathrm{vol}}$, even for smooth time-dependent two-site interactions.
  Polynomial time growth permits integration against filters with sufficiently many finite absolute moments, including those used in quasi-adiabatic constructions and quantum belief propagation. We derive consequences for filtered interactions and the dynamics they generate, providing dynamical estimates for perturbation theory with extensive perturbations, including gap stability, the principle that local perturbations perturb locally (LPPL), adiabatic theory, and response theory.
  All results also hold for quantum spin systems.

title: Beyond GNSS: Leveraging LEO Satellite Signals of Opportunity for Doppler Positioning
abstract: Large constellations of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites provide ubiquitous global connectivity; yet, their rapid motion introduces significant Doppler shift effects. While challenging for communication, these effects can be leveraged for precise user terminal (UT) positioning, particularly in GNSS-denied environments where traditional satellite-based navigation struggles. Unlike GNSS, most LEO satellites lack dedicated navigation signals, motivating signals-of-opportunity (SOPs) approaches that repurpose existing LEO signals and use publicly available two-line element (TLE) files for orbital information, although ephemeris errors can limit accuracy. This article explores the fundamental principles, challenges, and enabling technologies for LEO-based Doppler shift positioning, highlighting its advantages over conventional non-Doppler methods, and discussing future research directions. Furthermore, to facilitate realistic and reproducible performance evaluation beyond stochastic modeling, we propose SionnaNTN-RT, a ray tracing framework for non-terrestrial network (NTN) built upon Sionna, enabling end-to-end simulation of Doppler-based positioning. Simulation results demonstrate that Doppler-based positioning can achieve high positioning accuracy in both urban and open-sky environments, highlighting its promise for next-generation positioning systems.

title: Proving the Komlós conjecture slowly
abstract: The Komlós conjecture was a long-standing open problem in discrepancy theory until it was recently solved in a flurry of AI developments. We give a motivated exposition of an elementary proof of the conjecture due to Karingula and Lovett, as well as a counterexample to the strong Komlós conjecture due to Kintali, aiming to introduce the ideas in a gentle and explained manner in order to ease the understanding of the proofs. We conclude with several problems which remain open.

title: Non-Coherent Over-the-Air Distributed Consensus: Algorithm Design and Power Control Optimization
abstract: Non-coherent over-the-air (NCOTA) aggregation offers a scalable and communication-efficient approach to distributed average consensus in wireless networks, without requiring instantaneous channel state information (CSI) or phase alignment. However, persistent aggregation errors pose fundamental challenges in achieving exact average consensus under nominal distributed averaging protocols. In this paper, we develop an NCOTA consensus framework that accommodates row-stochastic mixing, without requiring the conventional average-preservation property of doubly stochastic mixing matrices. Building on a distributed optimization formulation of average consensus, we propose a decentralized projected gradient descent with row-stochastic mixing (DPGD-RS) algorithm and establish its mean-square convergence to the exact average of the agents' initial states. We further derive a closed-form upper bound on the mean-square consensus error, characterizing the effects of aggregation uncertainty, network connectivity, and mixing imbalance. Guided by this analysis, we propose a spectral-reshaping power control (SR-PC) scheme that jointly optimizes transmit powers and receive-scaling factors to accelerate convergence by balancing aggregation accuracy and network mixing. Numerical results validate the theoretical convergence guarantees and demonstrate that the proposed power control scheme significantly accelerates convergence compared with full-power transmission and spectral-radius-minimization benchmarks.

title: Scalable Fully Implicit Runge-Kutta Solvers for Time-Dependent Rayleigh-Bénard Convection
abstract: We consider the efficient numerical solution of time-dependent Rayleigh-Bénard convection governed by the incompressible Boussinesq equations. The coupled velocity-pressure-temperature system presents significant computational challenges arising from incompressibility, buoyancy coupling, convection, and the simultaneous resolution of multiple physical time scales. We present a systematic study of fully implicit Runge-Kutta methods for time-dependent Rayleigh-Bénard convection, together with scalable finite element solvers for the resulting stage-coupled systems. We employ high-order, L-stable Radau IIA methods for temporal integration and investigate Taylor-Hood and Alfeld-Sorokina finite elements in two dimensions, along with Taylor-Hood and enriched macroelement discretizations in three dimensions. The macroelement approaches offer strong local inf-sup stability and patch structures well suited to Vanka-type relaxation. In two dimensions, monolithic multigrid achieves nearly stage-independent outer Krylov iteration counts and maintains robust convergence under mesh refinement. On the same mesh with incremental pressure correction, selected Radau configurations reduce elapsed solve time by 18-32% and yield smaller sampled transient differences relative to a numerical reference solution. Three-dimensional experiments demonstrate favorable parallel scalability with Taylor-Hood elements and substantially improved discrete mass conservation with the enriched macroelement discretization. These results identify regimes in which coupled multistage fully implicit integration is computationally competitive when equipped with appropriate multigrid preconditioners.

title: A Note on the Finite-Exceedance Dependence Principle for Sum--Maximum Asymptotic Independence
abstract: Asymptotic independence between sum-type and maximum-type statistics arises repeatedly across many areas of probability and statistics, particularly in high-dimensional testing and random matrix theory. Motivated by the shared structure underlying existing proofs, which is obscured by their model-specific formulations, this note isolates a common intermediate principle. We introduce a finite-exceedance dependence principle: if the finite-exceedance dependence error vanishes at every fixed order and high-order exceedances are mildly controlled, then a finite-order Bonferroni argument yields asymptotic independence between the sum and the maximum. We further give an independent-proxy criterion for verifying this: for each finite set of exceedances, it suffices to construct an exactly independent proxy for the sum-type statistic whose approximation error is negligible in aggregate. Local deletion under dependency graphs and Gaussian regression and residualization are two examples. The framework gives modular derivations of existing sum--max independence results.

title: A counterexample concerning weighted convolution on the integers
abstract: Let $1<p<\infty$ and let $w:\mathbb{Z}\to(0,\infty)$ be a weight. When is the weighted space $\ell^p(\mathbb{Z},w)$ an algebra with respect to convolution? A well-known sufficient condition is that $(w^{-q}*w^{-q})/w^{-q}$ be bounded on $\mathbb{Z}$, where $q:=p/(p-1)$ is the index conjugate to $p$. We present an example to show that this sufficient condition is not necessary.

title: Sublinear Power-Law Growth of Level Set Diameters in Heterogeneous F-KPP Equations
abstract:
For every $α\in(1/4,1)$, we construct a heterogeneous medium $ξ$ such that the diameter of the level sets of the solution to the F-KPP equation is of order $t^α$ along a sequence of times tending to infinity. This is a natural continuation of a series of recent works establishing logarithmic lower bounds as well as linear asymptotics for the diameters of the respective level sets in random and deterministic heterogeneous media. Both results assume $\supξ> 2\infξ$; we also show that the diameter can diverge in the critical regime $\supξ=2\infξ$.
  A key ingredient is an estimate for branching Brownian motion with fixed time horizon $t$ and branching rate $1$ on the negative half-line and $2+t^{-η}$ on the positive half-line. This estimate exhibits a saturation transition: for $η<1/2$ the polynomial and logarithmic corrections to the extremal position depend on $η$, whereas for $η\geq1/2$ the extremal position becomes independent of $η$, up to an additive constant.

title: A resolution of the Steinberg module of a parabolic subgroup of GL_n
abstract: Let F be a field, G = GL_n(F), and let St be the Steinberg module of G. For a parabolic subgroup P of G, let St_P be its Steinberg module. There is a natural map rho_P: St -> St_P corresponding to intersection of a modular symbol with the Borel--Serre boundary. We construct a ZP-resolution Sh_P of St_P, the P-sharbly resolution. We also construct a P-equivariant chain map from the sharbly resolution of St to the P-sharbly resolution of St_P which enables us to compute the map induced on Steinberg homologies by rho_P. In the case when F is a number field and Gamma subset G is a torsion-free arithmetic subgroup, rho_P induces the restriction map H^(Gamma, E) -> H^(Gamma cap P, E) via Borel--Serre duality, for any coefficient module E which is flat over the base ring. If E is a vector space over Z/pZ this provides a computation of the restriction map on cohomology from Gamma to Gamma cap P in terms of sharblies, which enables the study of this restriction map in characteristic p, where Eisenstein series cannot be used.

title: Multivariable Alexander polynomials of twisted torus links via Dehn surgery
abstract: Let $T(p,q;r,s)$ be the twisted torus link obtained from the torus link $T(p,q)$ by adding $s$ full twists to $r$ adjacent strands, and let $C$ be an unknotted circle encircling those strands. For all $p$, $q$, and $r$ we compute the multivariable Alexander polynomial of $T(p,q)\cup C$ in closed form. A relation of Silver and Williams between the Alexander polynomials of a link and of its $1/n$ Dehn fillings then gives a closed formula for the multivariable Alexander polynomial of every twisted torus link $T(p,q;r,s)$, answering a question of Adnan and Park. When $\gcd(p,q)=1$, so that $T(p,q;r,s)$ is a knot, the formula is a sum of $pr$ monomials with coefficient $+1$, divided by cyclotomic factors, and its exponents are governed by an elementary counting function on the orbit of $q$ modulo $p$. Because the numerator has no cancellation, we are able to give the degree for all $s$ and a simple non-fiberedness criterion.

title: Conformal dimension of Bedford-McMullen carpets
abstract: We show that the Hausdorff dimension of a Bedford-McMullen carpet with non-uniform fibres can be lowered with a quasisymmetry, provided that the defining iterated function system does not have a full column. We prove this by constructing explicit dimension lowering metrics which are quasisymmetrically equivalent to the Euclidean metric.

title: Entropy and round-point convergence for the $σ_k$-curvature flow
abstract: We prove that every smooth closed strictly convex hypersurface in $\mathbb R^{n+1}$ contracts to a round point under the $σ_k$-curvature flow for $2\leq k\leq n-1$, without additional pinching or symmetry assumptions. After rescaling about the extinction point to mean width two, the hypersurfaces converge smoothly and exponentially in normalized time to the unit sphere. The proof is based on an entropy which is invariant under translations and dilations and admits a representation by weighted boundary areas of orthogonal projections. A strengthened Codazzi inequality yields its monotonicity. An upper bound for the entropy controls the inradius relative to the mean width, while its dissipation controls the spatial variation of the normalized speed. We also obtain two-sided curvature bounds at the natural extinction scale.

title: Global Stability and Decay for the 2D Anisotropic Navier-Stokes Equations with Fractional Horizontal Dissipation
