abstract: Although the classical Yudovich theory guarantees global existence and uniqueness of two-dimensional Euler solutions with bounded vorticity, their higher-order norms may still grow in time. This raises a fundamental question: how much dissipation we need to ensure global stability and decay? While the full Laplacian dissipation is sufficient, the stabilizing effect of weaker, anisotropic dissipation is considerably more subtle. In this paper, we investigate the global stability and long-time decay of the two-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with fractional horizontal dissipation $Λ_1^{2s}u$, where $s<1$. A central challenge is to recover sufficient decay of the second velocity component, whose weak dissipation obstruct the closure of conventional anisotropic energy estimates. Previous work by Wang-Wu-Zhu [arXiv:2601.16110] resolved this difficulty whereas the spatial weighted energy functionals must be used when $s$ approaches $1$. The main purpose of our manuscript is to remove this restriction. We introduce a hierarchy of carefully designed time-weighted anisotropic energy functionals which captures the interplay between horizontal fractional dissipation and the decay of velocity components. Under such initial assumptions, the characteristics of anisotropic dissipation is presented more straightforwardly, which also reveals the more essential intrinsic structure of fluid stability.

title: Unique Hahn-Banach extensions in Bochner $L^p$ spaces
abstract: Let $Y$ be a closed subspace of a real Banach space $X$. Let $(Ω,Σ,μ)$ be a complete finite measure space and let $1<p<\infty$. We prove that $Y$ has property-$(U)$, property-$(SU)$, property-$(wU)$ in $X$ if and only if $L^p(μ,Y)$ has the corresponding property in $L^p(μ,X)$. No Radon-Nikodým assumption on $X^*$ is required. The proofs use $w^*$-measurable representations of dual functionals and a simultaneous scalar-lifting construction. A norm-minimal representation for an element in $L^p(μ,X)^*$ is found suitable in this case. We also study the point of continuity of the identity map under different topologies on the unit sphere of $L^p(μ,X)^*$. For Bochner-integrable functionals, the pointwise $w^*-w$-continuity yields the uniqueness of the extension to $L^p(μ,X^{**})$. Examples show why arbitrary $w^*$-measurable representatives cannot replace the norm-minimal representatives in this context.

title: Renting, Owning, and Moving: Housing Tenure Choice with Transaction Costs
abstract: The wealth thresholds at which a household switches between renting and owning depend on its preferences, but the dates at which some owner sells or every renter buys do not. In our finite-horizon model, a household chooses consumption, a portfolio, and costly tenure changes while rents, ownership expenses, and transaction costs vary over time on announced dates. When financial markets span house-price risk, these dates are those of a deterministic minimum cost schedule for housing, discounted at the risk-adjusted housing carry and computed from a scalar reflected equation. Preferences, housing services, and labor income only locate the thresholds inside these timing windows, and house-price coefficients enter the dates only through the carry, because financial hedging offsets the exposure of the home. When owning costs at least as much as renting, the windows concern selling, and an anticipated selling surcharge closes the selling window before the surcharge peaks and keeps it closed for years afterwards. We also establish strong duality and the regularity of the thresholds and compute them by integral equations. Numerically, the windows disappear when short sales or borrowing are restricted but do not move with the preferences we vary under an uninsurable increase in the ownership cost.

title: Haagerup symmetries of the $E_8$ theory and conformal nets at central charge eight
abstract: A Haagerup algebra is a positive strongly rational vertex operator algebra $U$ of central charge eight with $\mathrm{Rep}(U)$ braided equivalent to the Drinfeld center $Z(\cal H_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category. Such an algebra has been proposed by Jiao, with a computer-assisted proof, and announced by Riesen and by Huang. We show that $U$ has exactly three holomorphic extensions, each isomorphic to $V_{E_8}$, and that the categories of modules over the corresponding Lagrangian algebras are the three Haagerup fusion categories of Grossman and Snyder. The extensions attached to $\cal H_2$ and $\cal H_3$ are the two lattice extensions of $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$. Along a strategy outlined by Huang, we prove a recognition theorem for $\cal H_2$ and $\cal H_3$ among unitary fusion categories of rank six with three invertible objects. For regular unitary vertex operator algebras with Tener's bounded localized vertex operators, we prove that the fusion product of two unitary modules is unitarizable when one of them integrates to the conformal net. The explicit unitary algebra $S \subset V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$ of our previous work, isomorphic to Jiao's algebra, is strongly local. Granting that Jiao's algebra is a Haagerup algebra, we deduce that the conformal net $\cal A_S$ is completely rational with $\mathrm{Rep}(\cal A_S) \cong Z(\cal H_3)$, that the Haagerup subfactor arises from $\cal A_S$, and that $\cal A_S$ solves a problem of Bischoff on generalized orbifolds. Under the same hypothesis, using a unitary structure on $V_{E_8 \oplus E_8}$ found by exact computer calculations, we prove that $S$ is completely unitary and that $\mathrm{Rep}(\cal A_S) \cong \mathrm{Rep}(S)$ through the correspondence given by smeared vertex operators. The diagonal construction and the passage to the twin algebra also show that every Haagerup algebra is completely unitary and satisfies Condition I+.

title: Vanishing-set inclusion and character degrees in finite $p$-groups
abstract: Let $G$ be a finite $p$-group and let $χ,ψ\in\operatorname{Irr}(G)$. We prove that $$\operatorname{Van}(χ)\subseteq\operatorname{Van}(ψ) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad χ(1)\midψ(1),$$ where $\operatorname{Van}(θ)=\{g\in G:θ(g)=0\}$. Consequently, two irreducible characters of a finite $p$-group with the same vanishing set have the same degree. This answers a question attributed to J. Sangroniz and recorded by Hung, Moretó, and Morotti, extending the previously known case in which one character has degree $p$. The same divisibility conclusion holds for irreducible characters of finite nilpotent groups.

title: $C^1$-rigidity of $\mathbb{H}^{p,q}$-convex cocompact representations of Gromov hyperbolic groups
abstract:
Let $p>3$ and let $Γ$ be a non-elementary Gromov hyperbolic group with $\partial_\inftyΓ\cong\mathbb S^{p-1}$. We prove that every $\mathbb{H}^{p,2}$-convex cocompact representation $$ ρ:Γ\longrightarrow \mathrm{PO}_{p,3} $$ whose proximal limit set $Λ_ρ\subset\partial_\infty\mathbb{H}^{p,2}$ is a $C^1$ submanifold preserves a totally geodesic copy of $\mathbb{H}^p\subset\mathbb{H}^{p,2}$. Consequently, $Γ/\ker ρ$ is virtually a cocompact lattice in $\mathrm{Isom}(\mathbb{H}^p)$.
  For odd $p$, we prove the same conclusion for every signature $(p,q)$ with $p>q\ge2$, under the same hypothesis $\partial_\inftyΓ\cong\mathbb S^{p-1}$.
  Our methods combine dynamics, differential topology, and representation theory. The key new ingredient is to study the radicals of the semidefinite forms induced on the tangent spaces of the limit set. They form a continuous vector bundle of constant rank. The tangent action at attracting fixed points gives a bound, in terms of the radical rank, on the number of eigenvalues of an orthogonal lift whose modulus exceeds one. We then use the topology of the sphere and the representation theory of real algebraic groups to exclude the remaining possibilities. In arbitrary signature with $p>q$, these arguments already imply that a representation with a $C^1$ limit set cannot be Zariski dense.

title: A proof of the spectral rigidity for complex projective space
abstract: We give a proof of a folklore conjecture that a compact Kähler manifold with the same scalar Laplace spectrum as complex projective space equipped with the Fubini--Study metric is holomorphically isometric to it. More generally, we prove that the spectrum of the Hodge Laplacian in any one fixed degree $p$ determines $\CP^n$ up to holomorphic isometry among compact connected Kähler manifolds, for every fixed pair of integers $(p,n)$ with $0\leq p\leq n$. Equality of a single Hodge spectrum first forces periodic geodesic flow and the integral cohomology ring of complex projective space. The ordinary first heat coefficient then identifies the total scalar curvature except on a Pell sequence of pairs. For those pairs, a clean wave-trace argument, a Krawtchouk estimate, and a mod-two projective-bundle obstruction determine the geodesic return holonomy. A canonical Kähler involution recovers a weighted first heat coefficient which is nonzero throughout the exceptional sequence. The Kobayashi--Ochiai theorem and a fixed-class second-heat-coefficient calculation complete the argument.

title: Stability of negative-regularity mixing and applications to stochastic fluids
abstract: We consider mixing for a scalar advected by random vector fields, such as solutions to stochastic fluid equations. Our main abstract result is that contraction in expectation of a negative Sobolev norm of the scalar (negative-regularity mixing) is stable under perturbations of the joint scalar-velocity process. We apply the result in three settings: mixing for a hyperviscous Boussinesq-type system where the scalar actively drives the velocity, mixing for a passive scalar advected by two-dimensional Navier-Stokes driven by smooth-in-time stochastic forcing, and a black-box proof that negative-regularity mixing implies enhanced dissipation.

title: Hyperplane Furstenberg Sets in Higher Dimensions
abstract: The hyperplane Furstenberg problem asks how small the Hausdorff dimension of $E\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ can be when a $t$-dimensional family of affine $(n-1)$-dimensional hyperplanes meets $E$ in sets of dimension at least $s$. For $0<s\le n-1$ and $0<t\le n$, we prove the sharp bound in $\mathbb{R}^n$ $\dim_{\mathrm{H}}E\ge\mathbf{F}(s,t;n,n-1)$, where $\mathbf{F}$ is Gan's Furstenberg index proposed in prime fields. We also construct examples attaining this bound for all parameters. Our main reduction theorem, Theorem 3.1, states that for $n\ge3$, $0<s\le n-2$, and $1<t\le n$, every weighted $(s,t)$ configuration $(E,H)$ at scale $δ$ produces a dual weighted $(s,t-1)$ configuration $(P,\mathcal{T})$ inside a hyperplane $H_{y_0}\cong\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$. The reduction uses radial projection and energy estimates for Frostman measures. Iterating this reduction and applying the Csörnyei--Stull incidence theorem yields the bound.

title: Zeta functions of quasi-split reductive algebraic groups over local fields
abstract: We calculate zeta functions of quasi-split reductive algebraic groups over local fields using the classification of Tits and prove a functional equation. We give explicit exam- ples of these zeta functions for non-split unitary and orthogonal groups.

title: Decomposable concordances induce closed immersions
abstract: We show that a decomposable Lagrangian concordance between two Legendrian links must induce a closed immersion between the sheaf moduli of its ends. As the main application of this criterion, we prove a conjecture of Cornwell-Ng-Sivek, showing that their Lagrangian concordance is not decomposable. This establishes the first known example of a regular Lagrangian concordance between Legendrian knots that is not decomposable. In addition, we show that even the simpler Lagrangian concordance, satelliting via the Reeb 2-copy, is not decomposable.

title: Newtonian Dynamics in Metric Spaces
abstract: We develop a variational framework for second-order, frictionless (Newtonian) dynamics in metric spaces, extending the metric theory of curves of maximal slope from gradient flows to evolutions with inertia. The construction rests on three pillars, mirroring the first-order theory. First, we introduce a class of second-order absolutely continuous curves, characterized by a geometric--variational inequality on families of tangent geodesics, and define a metric notion of acceleration. Second, we define curves of Newtonian motion as the curves achieving equality in an energy inequality involving an upper gradient--Hessian pair, which in Hilbert spaces is equivalent to Newton's equation $\ddotγ= -\nabla E(γ)$. Third, we propose a two-step predictor--corrector minimizing movement scheme and show that its discrete interpolants satisfy approximate versions of these inequalities. Under extendability and interceptor conditions on geodesics---which are satisfied, for instance, by geodesically uniformly complete, locally compact spaces with curvature bounded below---and under suitable regularity assumptions on the energy, we prove that the scheme converges, up to subsequences, to a curve of Newtonian motion. As an illustration, we recover the linear wave equation as a curve of Newtonian motion driven by the Dirichlet energy. This paper is complemented by the companion paper [Fornasier, Klemenc, Scagliotti, "A Lions Lift Framework for Gradient and Newtonian Evolutions in Wasserstein spaces"], which specifies and adapts the results to the Wasserstein metric space $(\mathcal{P}_2,W_2)$ through Lions lift, which explains Vlasov equations as Newtonian flows on spaces of probability measures.

title: Rate optimality of AFEM with maximum marking
abstract: For Poisson's equation, we prove optimal algebraic convergence rates for adaptive conforming finite element methods driven by standard maximum marking in arbitrary space dimension, for every marking parameter in $(0,1]$. Previously, instance optimality of a modified maximum marking was proved in [L. Diening, C. Kreuzer, and R. Stevenson, Instance optimality of the adaptive maximum strategy, Found. Comput. Math., 16 (2016), pp. 33--68]. The basic ingredients of our anlaysis consists of discrete reliability, discrete efficiency, overlay and closure estimates of local mesh refinement. The discrete efficiency requires a facet-interior node property of simplicial mesh refinement. The novel part of the optimality analysis is an elementary integral-sum argument that converts energy decrease into a cumulative cardinality bound of marked elements, yielding rate optimality without a contraction argument.

title: Local Limit Theorems for Heavy-Tailed Lévy Processes with Negative Drift
abstract: This paper establishes uniform local asymptotics for the first-passage time below zero and the stopped maximum of a Lévy process with negative drift and a locally regularly varying Lévy measure. We show that their probabilities of lying in distant intervals are asymptotic to the expected first-passage time multiplied by the corresponding Lévy masses, uniformly over interval widths bounded away from zero, including unbounded intervals. Although the two local events have asymptotically equivalent probabilities, their conditional overlap vanishes for fixed-width intervals. Nevertheless, we establish conditional concentration of the first-passage time and stopped maximum around their deterministic linear relation on scales dominating the fluctuations of the centered process. We further prove conditional functional limit theorems yielding a single-step process with random jump time on the original time scale and a deterministic linear descent on the accelerated scale. Finally, we identify the joint limiting distribution of the unscaled pre-passage position and terminal overshoot, distinguishing continuous passage from passage by a downward jump.

title: Centralizers of maps as automorphism groups of Yang--Baxter solutions
abstract: For a partition $X = Y \sqcup Z$ of a set $X$ and an arbitrary map $g \colon Y \to {\rm Hom}_{\rm Set} (Z, \, Z)$, we construct a solution $R_g \colon X \times X \to X \times X$ of the braid equation. We characterize intrinsically the solutions which are isomorphic to some $R_g$ and we give a necessary and sufficient condition for two solutions $R_g$ and $R_{g'}$ to be isomorphic. Consequently, the number of isomorphism classes of the solutions $R_g$ on a set with $n$ elements is $1 + \sum_{k = 1}^{n-1} \widetilde{o} (n - k, \, k)$, where $\widetilde{o} (m, \, k)$ is the number of orbits of the symmetric group $S_m$, acting by conjugation, on the set of multisets with $k$ elements of maps $\{1, \ldots, m\} \to \{1, \ldots, m\}$. This construction is then used to obtain a solution of the braid equation whose automorphism group is exactly the centralizer ${\rm Aut} (f_1, \ldots, f_k)$ of a given family $f_1, \ldots, f_k \colon X \to X$ of maps, $k \geq 1$. For $k = 2$, combined with a result of Agore, Chirvasitu and the author, this gives another proof of the fact that any group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a solution of the braid equation (equivalently, of the set-theoretic Yang--Baxter equation).

title: First- and second-order constrained optimisation for inverse homogenisation of unidirectionally varying microstructure
abstract: This paper is concerned with inverse homogenisation problems that aim to identify microstructure features of a body from macroscopic measurements. The unknown microstructure is assumed to vary macroscopically in one spatial direction and affects the effective tensor in an elliptic partial differential equation that governs the behaviour of the body on the macroscale. We establish the well-posedness of the PDE-constrained minimisation problems that model the task of identifying the microstructure, derive first-order necessary optimality conditions, and prove the convergence of a gradient-projection algorithm for the studied problem class in an infinite-dimensional setting. We moreover demonstrate that recently obtained results on generalised differentiability properties of solution maps of bilateral obstacle problems make it possible to set up and analyse a novel semismooth Newton method in the considered situation. The functional analytic setting that we use for our investigation is chosen such that it covers various elliptic PDEs simultaneously (classical second-order equations, bi-Laplace problems, linear elasticity, etc.) and explicitly exploits the problem structure to obtain global convergence guarantees for the studied solution algorithms in terms of the Lipschitz constants of the involved operators. Our analysis is accompanied by numerical experiments which show that the new semismooth Newton approach requires far less expensive projection evaluations than the gradient-descent method and, thus, offers a significant speedup.

title: Optimal bounds for design curves on the torus
abstract:
A closed rectifiable curve on the torus $\mathbb T^d=\mathbb R^d/\mathbb Z^d$ is a $t$-design curve if normalized arclength integration is exact for trigonometric polynomials $e^{2πi \langle m,x\rangle}$ with frequencies $m\in\mathbb Z^d$ satisfying $\|m\|_\infty\le t$. For the arclength $L$ of such curves, we establish the sharp lower bound \begin{equation}\label{eq:abs} L\geq \Big(\frac{(t+1)^{2d}-1}{t(t+2)}\Big)^{1/2}. \end{equation} Equality is attained by the family of Korobov curves described in \cite{Kunis,Lindblad}.
  For even $t$, we also derive an explicit lower bound on the length of total-degree $t$-design curves, defined by the frequency condition $\|m\|_1\leq t$. This bound is sharp for $t=2$ in every dimension and for every even $t$ in dimension two.
  We determine the minimum length of hyperbolic cross $t^2$-design curves in dimension two. For $d\geq3$, we establish lower bounds of optimal order for the length of hyperbolic cross $t^d$-design curves.
  Finally, we obtain lower bounds of optimal order for the length of $t$-design curves associated with sparse frequency sets.

title: Frame Properties of Effective Stationary Sequences
abstract: The Kaczmarz algorithm is an iterative projection method for reconstructing vectors in a Hilbert space from inner product data. However, sequences that are effective for this algorithm need not be frames and may lack standard frame reconstruction properties. We investigate these properties for stationary effective sequences, which were classified by Kwapień and Mycielski according to their spectral measures. In particular, we show that the corresponding Kaczmarz reconstruction series always converge unconditionally if and only if the spectral measure is atomic with finitely many point masses. We show that if the spectral measure is atomic, the stationary effective sequence and its auxiliary Parseval frame can be interchanged in the Kaczmarz reconstruction formula. Finally, we construct two stationary effective sequences with singular continuous spectral measures, one of which can be interchanged with its auxiliary Parseval frame in the reconstruction formula, and one of which cannot be interchanged.

title: On Landau's "local method" for obtaining zero-free regions
abstract: We extend Landau's local analytic method for the deduction of zero-free region to a very general setting, and as a particular consequence, obtain a zero-free region and corresponding Prime Number Theorem for Beurling number systems with well-behaved integers. We also discuss the sharpness of the method and prove estimates for the local number of zeros, as well as a clustering result, which roughly put says that zeros close to the 1-line cannot be isolated but must occur in clusters.

title: The Universal Nilpotent Cone and a Canonical 1-form
abstract: We construct a canonical Du Bois 1-form on the nilpotent cone in the dual Lie algebra of any reductive group. Using this 1-form we give an intrinsic construction of Nadler and Yun's universal global nilpotent cone. In particular, we obtain a moduli interpretation of the universal nilpotent cone.

title: Free energy of the Hopfield model
abstract: We identify the limit of the free energy of the Hopfield model with independent symmetric Bernoulli patterns, for every temperature and loading ratio. A Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation reduces the problem to that of identifying the limit free energy of a bipartite spin glass with $\pm 1$ and spherical spins. One key difficulty is that the patterns, which become the coupling coefficients in the bipartite model, are Bernoulli instead of Gaussian, and the limit free energy is sensitive to the law of these coefficients. We show that the model is in fact equivalent to one involving Gaussian patterns and also subject to a finite number of Bernoulli random fields. We then solve this model by adapting the techniques recently introduced to identify the limit free energies of spin glasses with either $\pm 1$ or spherical spins.

title: Anderson localisation in infinite and finite resonator crystals with long-range interactions
abstract: We establish Anderson localisation for random capacitance operators and quantify concentration of individual modes of finite capacitance matrices for clusters of subwavelength high-contrast resonators. The underlying geometry is fully periodic in dimensions $d=2,3$, with one resonator per cell, and the inverse material factors are independent and uniformly distributed. We retain the full capacitance interaction, whose coefficients decay exponentially with lattice separation. Under coordinate reflection symmetry, spectral and dynamical localisation hold near the upper spectral edge for every fixed positive disorder strength. At weak disorder $W$, we obtain an explicit localisation window of energy width proportional to $W$; prescribed positive intervals are localised at sufficiently large disorder. A variational boundary comparison and a material-variable eigenvalue-spacing estimate transfer localisation from truncated matrices to individual modes of the finite capacitance matrix. In a bounded sample of cell size $\varepsilon$, with probability tending to one, all except for $O(\varepsilon^{1-d}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ modes in the localisation interval concentrate within radii $O(\varepsilon\log(1/\varepsilon))$. The estimates are uniform for the contrast-dependent capacitance family at small contrast. We also prove a common limiting density of states for the truncated and finite matrices and illustrate concentration numerically.

title: Quadrature Perturbations and High-Order Time Discretization for Prescribed-Feature Evolutionary GTransNet Galerkin Systems
abstract: In this paper we study quadrature perturbations and high-order time discretization for a prescribed-feature evolutionary generalized transferable neural network (Evo-GTransNet) Galerkin method for linear self-adjoint parabolic equations. Assembly quadrature, together with truncated singular value decomposition, is used to select a numerically resolved trial space and obtain coordinates with an identity mass matrix. Since this normalization depends on the assembly quadrature, the retained functions are also evaluated using a separate comparison quadrature, which is finer in the numerical experiments. For the two resulting semidiscrete systems, we derive an exact equation for the difference between their trajectories and an energy estimate that separates errors arising from the effective operator, load vector, and initial projection. The estimate is conditional on the trial space selected by the assembly quadrature. The retained rank, discarded mass, cross mass, and principal angles are used to assess this selection step. Refining the comparison quadrature yields stable retained spaces for the reported configurations, whereas deliberate underintegration leads to much larger perturbations. On the fixed retained systems, the temporal convergence of implicit midpoint, BDF, Radau IIA, and Gauss--Legendre methods is consistent with their classical orders over the resolved refinement ranges. The experiments distinguish the retained-coordinate error from the total solution error; the latter is measured against the PDE solution in the $L^2$ norm, with the error integrals evaluated by sufficiently fine quadrature. They also illustrate the importance of suitable starting values for BDF3 and show how the performance of IMEX-BDF schemes depends on the operator splitting and time step size.

title: The strong fractional choice number can exceed the choice number
abstract:
Erdős, Rubin and Taylor asked whether every $(a,b)$-choosable graph is $(am,bm)$-choosable for all positive integers $a,b,m$. Dvořák, Hu and Sereni disproved this by constructing a $4$-choosable graph that is not $(8,2)$-choosable, and asked whether a $3$-choosable graph can fail to be $(6,2)$-choosable. As a weakening, Li and Zhu asked whether every $k$-choosable graph is $(kb+1,b)$-choosable for all positive integers $k,b$. Equivalently, Xu and Zhu asked whether $\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G)\le\operatorname{ch}(G)$ for every graph $G$. Here $\operatorname{ch}(G)$ is the choice number of a graph $G$, and $\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G)$ is the strong fractional choice number of $G$, which is defined as the infimum of the real numbers $r$ such that $G$ is $(a,b)$-choosable for all positive integers $a,b$ with $a/b\ge r$.
  In this paper, we prove that, for all integers $t\ge0$ and $b\ge7t+2$, there is a planar graph $G$ with choice number three that is not $(3b+t,b)$-choosable. For $(b,t)=(2,0)$, our construction gives an affirmative answer to the question of Dvořák, Hu and Sereni. This family answers the questions of Li and Zhu and of Xu and Zhu negatively, and shows that the supremum of $\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G)-\operatorname{ch}(G)$ over graphs of choice number three is at least $1/7$. We further prove that, for all integers $k\ge4$, $t\ge0$ and $b\ge3t+2$, there is a graph $G$ with $\operatorname{ch}(G)=k$ that is not $(kb+t,b)$-choosable. For every $k\ge4$, this establishes the stronger lower bound $1/3$ on the supremum of $\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G)-\operatorname{ch}(G)$. The latter construction also produces simpler versions of the counterexamples of Dvořák, Hu and Sereni. It is worth mentioning that the core gadgets in both constructions are very simple. The former is an eight-vertex graph, and the latter is the six-vertex wheel $W_5$.

title: Hammock coordinates for silting subcategories of derived-discrete algebras
abstract: We introduce hammock coordinates to study the combinatorial structure of partial silting configurations in the bounded derived category of a derived-discrete algebra $Λ(r,n,m)$. By extracting exact integer inequalities from the Bobiński--Geiß--Skowroński Hom-hammock formula, we establish a closed-form criterion for pairwise partial silting both within any $\mathcal Z$-component and across distinct components. Using this coordinate framework, we establish three primary results. First, we prove the universal upper bound $|S| \le n+m$ on the cardinality of any partial silting configuration $S$ of $\mathcal Z$-objects ---both globally via Bongartz completion in the silting-discrete setting, and combinatorially within a single component via a $Σ^r$-invariant staircase argument. Second, we prove that this bound is universally sharp by constructing an explicit L-shaped partial silting configuration of size $n+m$ for every $Λ(r,n,m)$, alongside specialized diagonal configurations. Third, we show that the configuration lattice carries a faithful action of the cyclic group $\mathbb Z/g$ where $g = \gcd(r+m, n-r)$. We conclude by showing a structural obstruction to local determination: pairwise partial silting of consecutive objects in the lattice ordering does not imply global partial silting, due to the strict additivity of a coordinate defect along chains.

title: Good rational functions up to degree six
abstract: Locally recoverable codes (LRCs) are fundamental to the architecture of modern distributed storage systems. The Tamo-Barg construction of optimal LRCs was revolutionized by the introduction of good polynomials, which group evaluation points into local recovery sets. However, polynomial constructions are constrained by their inherently large Galois groups, which limit the number of totally split rational places. Recent advances have generalized this paradigm to good rational functions, which leverage the geometry of the projective line to achieve minimal Galois groups and subsequently codes with greater length. In this paper, we complete the classification of good rational functions of degree up to $6$ in characteristic $2$. By embedding the problem into algebraic function field theory, we explicitly determine the minimal arithmetic and geometric Galois groups for these low degrees. Furthermore, we move beyond asymptotic Hasse-Weil estimates by proving that the exact number of totally split places over extension fields obeys a linear recurring sequence (LRS). This gives an efficient method for computing the exact lengths and dimensions of the corresponding optimal LRCs and, in many cases, yields parameters beyond those obtainable from good polynomials.

title: Higher dimensional Kleinian groups of small Hausdorff dimension are classical Schottky groups II
abstract: This is the higher dimensional continuation of our works on Hausdorff dimension of Kleinian groups \cite{Hou2010}, \cite{Hou2020}. In this paper we prove that for all $r\ge 2$ there exists $λ_r>0$, which is independent of the dimension $N$ of the hyperbolic space, such that any finitely generated non-elementary torsion-free Kleinian group of $\Isom(\mathbb{H}^N)$ generated by $r$ elements with limit set of Hausdorff dimension $<λ_r$ is a classical Schottky group. For two generators the bound can be taken to be $1/3$. The proof relies on our previous works in \cite{Hou2010}, \cite{Hou2020} and on a metric carrier graph reduction. Our result can also be considered as the complete converse to the well-known theorem of Phillips-Sarnak \cite{PS} for spaces of any dimension $N$.

title: The 1-2-3 Conjecture for Borel Combinatorics
abstract: The 1-2-3 Conjecture asserts that every finite graph without isolated edges admits edge weights from $\{1,2,3\}$ such that the sum function forms a vertex coloring. We study its Borel analogue for locally finite Borel graphs without isolated edges, proving that five weights suffice in general and four suffice for regular graphs. We obtain three weights for acyclic graphs admitting a Borel selection of a nonempty finite set of ends from each component. We also obtain $μ$-measurable and Baire measurable vertex-coloring $3$-edge weightings from $3$-colorings of the same definability, under probability measure-preserving and Baire quasi-invariance conditions, respectively.

title: A height transportation approach to the quantitative Prékopa--Leindler inequality
abstract:
We give a new, simpler proof of sharp stability for the Prékopa--Leindler inequality. In contrast to the main arguments from Figalli, van Hintum and Tiba~\cite{FigalliVanHintumTibaPL}, our proof hinges mostly on the sharp stability theory for the Brunn--Minkowski problem, developed by the same authors \cite{figalli2024BM}, and on the idea of using a height transportation approach in order to match level sets.
  As a by-product of our techniques, we are able to prove the sharp dependency on $τ= \min\{λ,1-λ\}$ in the Prékopa--Leindler stability constant whenever one of the inputs is logarithmically concave, producing a new, simplified proof of two of the main results from~\cite{FigalliVanHintumTibaPL}.
  Finally, in the same fashion as Kristály and Pîrvuceanu \cite{kristaly2026quantitative}, we are able to obtain new stability results for the Bakry-Emery log-Sobolev inequality and for the Talagrand inequality. Due to the sharpness of the inputs, these results are optimal in terms of exponents. We moreover show that the $L^1$ nature of the distance in such results \emph{cannot} in general be improved to any other $L^p$ distance, where $p>1.$

title: Selection principle for Weak KAM solutions on $\mathbb{R}^n$ via large deviation principle for diffusions
abstract: Stationary Hamilton-Jacobi equations generally admit many weak KAM solutions. The question is how to select one weak KAM solution that reflects a meaningful physical principle. In this paper, we propose a selection principle for Hamilton-Jacobi equations arising from the large deviation principle of general drift-diffusion processes on $\mathbb{R}^n$ based on the exponential asymptotics of invariant measures. We first characterize the Aubry set as the finitely many equilibria of the drift, using an action estimate from the orthogonal decomposition of the drift. For any boundary data on the Aubry set compatible with the Peierls barrier, we construct the unique coercive weak KAM solution with these boundary data, which is also the maximal locally Lipschitz viscosity solution. The Freidlin-Wentzell graph formula then provides the boundary data on the Aubry set that select the unique weak KAM solution. The selected solution is exactly the rate function in the large deviation principle for invariant measures in the zero noise limit. We also show that this rate function is the vanishing viscosity limit, to which the viscous approximations converge locally uniformly. Finally, under additional regularity assumptions, we show that the long-time and zero-noise limits commute for suitably prepared initial densities.

title: Characterization of the group Fourier transform of Hilbert space Valued functions
abstract: A remarkable theorem of S. Alesker, S. Artstein-Avidan, and V. Milman characterizes the Fourier transform on $\mathbb{R}^n$ as, in essence, the unique transformation on the space of tempered distributions that exchanges convolution with pointwise multiplication. In this paper, we extend this perspective to the setting of the Heisenberg group $\He$, focusing on functions taking values in a separable Hilbert space $\Hi$. We establish a characterization of the group Fourier transform on $\He$ in terms of convolution. More precisely, we characterize the group Fourier transform on $L^1(\He,\Hi)$ and $L^2(\He,\Hi)$. In addition, we obtain a similar characterization for the group Fourier transform of $\Hi$-valued Schwartz class functions on the Heisenberg group.

title: Kernelized Stable Fluids for simulating physically accurate solutions
abstract: The Stable Fluids algorithm is a fractional step method for solving the incompressible Navier-Stokes (NS) equations in an unconditionally stable way. It was initially developed for visual effects and allows real-time simulations because of its low computational complexity. The method solves the advection step by using the method of characteristics which is implemented via linear interpolation. This results in excessive diffusion of vorticity and is one of the main reasons for the physical inaccuracy of the algorithm. We propose Kernelized Stable Fluids with Sparse Cholesky Preconditioning (KSF-Chol) in order to address this shortcoming and make the algorithm thereby suitable for engineering problems and scientific computing. The algorithm is modified by replacing the linear interpolation approach with kernel interpolation in the advection step. We accelerate the computationally expensive kernel interpolation by using sparse Cholesky preconditioning and a near-/far-field approach and optimize both methods for computations on a uniform Cartesian grid. KSF-Chol achieves per time step a near-linear computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}(N\log^d(N/\varepsilon_{\mathrm{chol}}))$ in space and time. We test KSF-Chol against reference solvers and numerical reference data on multiple 2D and 3D benchmarks and demonstrate a significantly reduced numerical diffusion as well as a competitive accuracy concerning the computation of relevant flow quantities.

title: Persistence of $C^2$ regularity for aggregation patches
abstract: We prove persistence of $C^2$ boundary regularity for patch solutions of the two-dimensional aggregation transport equation, in contrast with the known $C^2$ ill-posedness of Euler vortex patches. More generally, we consider transport equations with kernels of the form $L(\nabla N)$, where $N$ is the fundamental solution of the Laplacian and $L$ is a linear map. We show that $C^2$ regularity persists for every $C^2$ initial patch if and only if $L$ is a scalar multiple of the identity. Our approach builds on the curvature formulation introduced by Kiselev and Luo.

title: Microscopic Origin of the Equation of Motion for Open Thermodynamic Systems
abstract: In my previous work (arXiv:2609.07810) \cite{Aydiner_2026}, I derived a second-order equation of motion for open thermodynamic systems from the First Law of Thermodynamics and established its dynamical equivalence with mechanical oscillators and electrical RLC circuits. In the present study, I independently recover the same mathematical structure of the equation of motion from a mesoscopic model of particle transfer between two reservoirs connected by a channel. Starting from collective momentum balance, particle conservation, and reservoir chemical-potential response, I derive the inertial--dissipative--restoring dynamics and obtain explicit expressions for its effective coefficients in terms of the physical parameters of the system. The resulting equation predicts distinct damping regimes, characteristic relaxation time scales, and resonance under periodic driving. The natural frequency and resonance conditions are explicitly determined by the physical parameters of the particle-transfer system. In the slow-transport limit, the model recovers the conventional Onsager-type linear flux--force relation. The independent emergence of the same dynamical structure from two distinct physical approaches provides theoretical support for the previously proposed thermodynamic equation of motion. By identifying the physical mechanisms underlying its effective coefficients, the present study strengthens the physical foundations of the proposed framework and supports the possibility of describing open thermodynamic systems within a common dynamical framework shared with mechanical and electrical systems.

title: Human Variations on AI Mathematics
abstract: This article is motivated by the OpenAI manuscripts "Minimal metrics and interior injectivity for nef adjoints" and "Log abundance in characteristic zero". We establish a jet comparison for metrics with minimal singularities and use it to prove a dlt-type extension theorem. Combined with geometric arguments from the latter manuscript, this yields an alternative analytic proof of its Theorem~3.1.

title: A Stieltjes representation of order $p$ for $ \mathrm{tr}[(A+tB)^{-p}]$: Heinävaara's measure, B-splines, and Stahl's theorem
abstract: For $A$ positive definite, $B$ positive semidefinite and $p\ge1$ we show that $\mathrm{tr}[(A+tB)^{-p}]=\int(1+t\ell)^{-p}\,dρ_p(\ell)$ for a positive measure $ρ_p$ on the spectral interval of $L=A^{-1/2}BA^{-1/2}$, and we identify the measure: it has atoms $\mathrm{tr}[(P_sA^{-1}P_s)^p]$ at the eigenvalues of $L$ and a continuous density, an integral of Heinävaara's tracial joint spectral measure along rays. For integer $p$ the positivity of $ρ_p$ follows from the positivity of Heinävaara's measure alone, and the density is a sum of Curry-Schoenberg B-splines; for real $p$ the representation is obtained by inverting Heinävaara's transform. For $0<p<1$ the function is a Stieltjes function of order $p$ only if $[A,B]=0$, but a positive representation of order one holds, with an explicit density. Along $A_p=pI+A_0$, $p\to\infty$, the measures converge to the measure of Stahl's theorem (the Bessis-Moussa-Villani conjecture) for $\mathrm{tr}\,e^{-(A_0+tB)}$.

title: Nonparametric Intensity Estimation for Covariate-Driven Poisson Processes Using Deep Learning
abstract: We consider nonparametric maximum likelihood estimation of the intensity function of a Poisson process, allowing the intensity to depend on observed covariates. Such models describe how event rates vary with external conditions, including conditions under which the intensity becomes arbitrarily small or vanishes. However, risk analysis based on the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence typically requires the true intensity to be bounded away from zero, a restrictive assumption in applications. We develop a unified approach that avoids this assumption and derive an oracle inequality for the covariate-averaged Hellinger distance between the true intensity and the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE). As an application of the oracle inequality, we establish convergence rates for NPMLEs based on deep neural networks (DNNs). Our results show that, as in nonparametric regression, the ability of DNNs to capture underlying structure leads to improved convergence rates. Specifically, DNN-based NPMLEs mitigate the curse of dimensionality when the true intensity has a compositional structure and automatically adapt to a low-dimensional Riemannian manifold structure of the event space. For intensity functions with a compositional structure, DNN-based NPMLEs achieve nearly minimax-optimal convergence rates without explicitly incorporating this structure into the network architecture. Simulations demonstrate that DNN-based estimators outperform kernel estimators in most settings, while manifold kernels remain competitive in some designs. Finally, we analyze stimulus-evoked neural spiking using data from the Allen Brain Observatory Visual Coding Neuropixels project. DNN-based NPMLEs provide better out-of-sample performance than a conditional kernel estimator, as evaluated by held-out log-likelihood.

title: An information-geometric formulation of distributed computation
abstract: Understanding how complex systems perform computations, i.e. how they store, transmit, and transform information across their components, is a major goal across the natural sciences. However, characterising genuinely collective computations across multiple inputs and outputs that cannot be reduced to contributions from individual components remains an open problem. In this work, we introduce $Φ\text{ID}^{IG}$, a geometric theory of information dynamics that captures irreducible collective phenomena and enables a complete decomposition of multi-input multi-output operations into interpretable computational modes, providing a complete informational profile of a system. We first validate our framework to identify and quantify distinct computational modes in discrete and Gaussian systems with known ground truth. We then apply it to uncover the computational architecture of complex systems across synthetic and real-world scenarios, including chaotic maps, where distinct universality classes are associated with characteristic modes of computation; brain anatomy of over 100 mammalian species, revealing an evolutionary shift towards more distributed computation in the human neocortex; and financial markets, where collective computations recover the modular organisation of market sectors. Overall, our results show how complex systems can be quantitatively investigated through multidimensional computational portraits derived from the geometry of their underlying probability distributions.

title: Koopman-von Neumann formalism meets contact Hamiltonian systems
abstract: The present work develops a Koopman--von Neumann (KvN) formulation of contact Hamiltonian dynamics on the Hilbert space defined by the contact volume. The resulting generator includes the divergence correction required for unitary evolution. We establish symmetry and, for complete contact Hamiltonian vector fields, essential self-adjointness and a strongly continuous unitary evolution; we also describe covariance under contactomorphisms. For completely integrable contact systems with complete flows, it is possible to recover an invariant direct-integral decomposition and strongly commuting KvN generators. We further relate contact KvN dynamics to the KvN formulation of its symplectization.

title: Gradient flow formulation and discrete approximation of reaction-cross-diffusion systems with size exclusion
abstract: We characterize a class of possibly degenerate nonlinear reaction-cross-diffusion systems with size exclusion as (non-metric) gradient flows in continuity-equation format driven by entropy. We then establish a connection between these systems and discrete reaction networks by proving an EDP-type lower limit inequality for the associated gradient systems. In the non-degenerate case, we show a chain rule identity that allows us to identify minimizers of the corresponding energy-dissipation functional as weak solutions to the PDE system. In conjunction with the lower limit, this yields an alternative proof of existence of weak solutions and their approximability by solutions to the proposed discrete ODE systems. Finally, we generalize our results to models including drift terms by extending the established framework to tilted energy landscapes.

title: Efficient congruencing in $\mathbb Z[t]$ modulo $t^2$
abstract: We develop an analogue of nested efficient congruencing applicable in the ring $\mathbb Z[t]/t^2\mathbb Z[t]$ so as to estimate mean values related to that of Vinogradov. Let $k$ be a natural number, and suppose that $\varphi_j(u)\in \mathbb Z[t,u]$ $(1\le j\le k)$ is a system of polynomials having Wronskian $W(u;\boldsymbol \varphi)=\det ({\rm d}^i\varphi_j(u)/{\rm d}u^i)_{1\le i,j\le k}$ with respect to $u$. Consider the number $Υ_{s,k}(X;\boldsymbol \varphi)$ of integral solutions of the system of equations \[ \sum_{i=1}^s \bigl( \varphi_j(u_i+v_it)-\varphi_j(u_{s+i}+v_{s+i}t)\bigr) \equiv 0 \pmod{t^2}\quad (1\le j\le k), \] with $|u_i|\le X$ and $|v_i|\le X$ $(1\le i\le s)$. We show that when $W(u;\boldsymbol \varphi)\not\equiv 0\pmod{t}$ and $1\le s\le k(k+1)/2$, then $Υ_{s,k}(X;\boldsymbol \varphi)\ll X^{2s+\varepsilon}$. Our conclusions extend to number fields and function fields, as we outline. We describe several consequences of our results, including forthcoming work establishing the main conjecture for certain systems of equations not possessing translation-dilation invariant properties.

title: A nearly tight bound on the probability $G(n,p)$ is even-degenerate
abstract: A graph is even-degenerate if we can order its vertices as $v_1,\dots,v_n$ so that the number of edges from $v_i$ to $v_1,\dots,v_{i-1}$ is even for all $i>2$. We show that the probability $G(n,p)$ is even-degenerate is $e^{-Ω(n/\log\log n)}$, which is only a factor of $\log\log n$ away, in the exponent, from the trivial lower bound $2^{-O(n)}$.

title: Spectra of Beurling algebras of abelian groups
abstract:
We give a complete classification of all sets which are spectra of Beurling algebras of any locally compact abelian group, parametrizing them by compact convex sets in the dual of a certain locally convex vector space generated by the group.
  Hence, for example, a finitely generated free abelian group may enjoy a more complicated range of such spectra than the does rational numbers.

title: On Farah ideals and beyond
abstract:
An ideal $\mathcal{I}$ on $ω$ is called Farah if there are hereditary closed subsets $C_n$ of $\mathcal{P}(ω)$, for $n\inω$, such that $\mathcal{I}=\{A\subseteqω:\ \forall_{n\inω}\ \exists_{k\inω}\ A\setminus k\in C_n\}$. Farah asked in [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 356 (2004), no. 6] if every $\mathbf{F_{σδ}}$ ideal is a Farah ideal. We show that this is false by providing both tall and non-tall counterexamples. Moreover, we show that there is an antichain in the sense of Katětov order of length $\continuum$ consisting of $\mathbf{F_{σδ}}$ non-Farah ideals.
  We also investigate a closely related problem concerning sets of ideal limit points. We show that if $\mathcal{I}$ is an $\mathbf{G_{δσδ}}$ ideal on $ω$ and $x\in X^ω$ is a sequence in an uncountable Polish space $X$, then \[ Λ_x(\mathcal{I})=\left\{p\in X:\ \exists_{A\notin\mathcal{I}}\ x\restriction A\text{ converges to }p\right\} \] is $\mathbf{F_σ}$. This answers [Top. App. 312 (2022)] (partially) and [J. Symb. Logic, DOI: 10.1017/jsl.2026.10181]. Earlier it was known to be true only in the case of Farah ideals.

title: Normalizers in the category of topological groups
abstract: We show that the category of morphisms of topological groups admits split extension classifiers and hence the category of topological groups admits normalizers. We give explicit descriptions of both normalizers and of split extension classifiers of morphisms of topological groups in terms of split extension classifiers of topological groups.

title: Higher-order many-sorted categorial algebras via generalized hep-derivors
abstract: Higher-order many-sorted categorial algebras are many-sorted algebras whose carriers are strict higher-order categories and whose operations are higher-order functors. They admit a homogeneous and a heterogeneous presentation, both by partial algebras whose operation domains are given by existence equations. To relate these presentations and their dimensions, we introduce generalized hep-derivors between hierarchical equationally partial signatures. A generalized hep-derivor selects carriers by existence equations in one variable and interprets operation symbols by terms, with operation domains evaluated recursively in the transformed algebra. Every generalized hep-derivor induces a functor between categories of many-sorted partial algebras. The values of this functor satisfy the domain conditions wherever their operations are defined, and we characterize when the operations are defined exactly where these conditions hold. The functor induced by a composite receives a natural inclusion from the composite of the induced functors; this inclusion, which can be strict, makes the induced functors a normal lax indexed category. In finite dimensions, generalized hep-derivors realize graduation and unification as an equivalence between the homogeneous and heterogeneous presentations, and discretization as a left adjoint to truncation. In dimension $ω$, we reconstruct the categories of $ω$-categorial algebras as projective limits of their finite-dimensional truncations and obtain unification by a quotient construction; we also establish algebraic squares and compatibility with change of signature. Finally, for nonempty sets of sorts, we show that the finite-dimension condition in the homogeneous $ω$-presentation is not axiomatizable by quasi-existence equations on its fixed signature.

title: Wasserstein accelerated proximal gradient algorithms
abstract: We propose accelerated proximal gradient methods for composite optimization problems on the quadratic Wasserstein space of probability measures, including Kullback--Leibler divergence minimization. The objective function consists of a smooth geodesically convex functional and a possibly nonsmooth regularizer that is convex along generalized geodesics. The convexity and smoothness conditions on the smooth component are imposed only on the feasible set. As a preliminary result, we establish the equivalence between geodesic convexity of the smooth functional on the feasible set and convexity of its Hilbert-space lift on the corresponding feasible set. Assuming exact proximal steps, we prove an $O(k^{-2})$ convergence rate for the objective gap when the smooth component is geodesically convex and accelerated linear convergence when it is geodesically strongly convex. We also describe particle approximations of these algorithms.

title: Quantitative finiteness for maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of non-arithmetic ball quotients
abstract: We prove that the number of maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of a smooth finite-volume non-arithmetic ball quotient is bounded linearly by its volume, with a constant depending only on the complex dimension. This gives a quantitative strengthening of the finiteness theorems of Bader--Fisher--Miller--Stover (Invent. Math., 2023) and Baldi--Ullmo (Ann. of Math., 2023).

title: Sharp bounds and asymptotic profiles for Lane-Emden systems at the Serrin threshold
abstract: We classify isolated singularities of $p$-Laplace and $k$-Hessian Lane--Emden systems on their Serrin critical curves without radial symmetry. Our approach reconstructs a radial profile from the source measures through a truncated Wolff potential, providing a nonlinear counterpart of spherical averaging. For upper inequalities at equal powers, we determine the sharp joint logarithmic lower bound on the zero-mass singular branch. A radial pair attains this bound while both normalized components oscillate between zero and infinity. For exact systems at equal powers, we obtain a common second-order profile with a shared phase and a sharp two-term logarithmic expansion of the component difference. At unequal powers, we establish power--logarithmic asymptotics with explicit leading constants. These asymptotics hold uniformly in direction.

title: Lattice Green's functions for Poisson problems with two unbounded and one periodic direction
abstract: Fourier-based Poisson solvers treat periodic directions spectrally and unbounded ones by the Hockney--Eastwood convolution with a free-space kernel. With two unbounded and one periodic direction, the setting of vortex tubes, wakes and jets, the kernel used so far by these solvers combines the two-dimensional kernel on the zero periodic mode with the symbol of the operator sampled on the doubled grid on every other mode. We show that the second ingredient is not exact: the error is the field of the periodic images of the source and independent of the mesh size. While the period $L_z$ is not much longer than the unbounded extent $L_x$, it is of order $\exp(-2πd/L_z)$, with $d$ the distance to the nearest image; beyond, it grows like $(L_z/L_x)^2$. The error is thus small on cubic domains, but larger than the solution itself on elongated ones. We remove the approximation by extending the integral representation of the exact second-order kernel of Hou and Colonius: the screened kernel of each mode is evaluated in closed form along one unbounded direction and by Gauss--Legendre quadrature along the other, for the high-order dimension-split and Mehrstellen stencils, at a one-off cost of about one solve. The kernels, implemented in the open-source library \flups{}, are verified by comparison with independent quadratures, by a padding test sensitive to the boundary condition enforced, and by convergence at the order of each stencil on an axially modulated tube source, on domains up to $64$ times longer than wide and up to $2.7\times10^{11}$ unknowns.

title: Open problems from the Length Optimization event at MDS 2026
abstract:
During the Minisymposium on Length Optimization as part of the International Conference "Mathematics Days in Sofia - 2026", the participants collected the following open problems:
  1. Find any non-trivial upper and lower bounds for the degree of a branching point in the Gilbert-Steiner problem with cost-function $c(x) = x^p$ in the metric space $X = \mathbb{R}^d$ for large $d$ and fixed $p > 1/2$ (see Section 1).
  2. Determine whether a typical trajectory of a given branched optimal traffic plan has bounded length. To find the optimal transport plan between the Dirac measure in the center of a circle and the Lebesgue measure on the circle (see Section 2).
  3. To find the maximal distance minimizers for any explicit compact sets (see Section 3).
  4. What is the minimal $C$ such that for any set of $n$ points in the three-dimensional unit cube, there is a tour through all these $n$ points with the sum of the cubes of its edge lengths at most $C$ (see Section 4).
  5. To explore parallels between tropical caustics and Steiner trees: do caustics really need convexity (see Section 5).

title: Specification LASSO and a Flexible Characteristics-Based Asset Pricing Model
abstract: This paper studies a partially linear semiparametric additive model that allows for interactions among variables in high-dimensional settings. We propose the Specification LASSO (S-LASSO), a two-step method that integrates LASSO and Adaptive Group LASSO to simultaneously perform variable selection and model specification. Theoretically, we establish that S-LASSO possesses oracle properties in terms of selection consistency and asymptotic normality. Monte Carlo simulations confirm that S-LASSO outperforms existing alternatives across a variety of scenarios. Empirically, we apply S-LASSO to a characteristics-based asset pricing model, exploring the linear and nonlinear effects of asset-specific characteristics on cross-sectional returns, as well as their interactions with firm size.

title: Maximizing Crossword Grids with a Fixed Minimum Clue Length
abstract: In an American-style crossword puzzle, the grid must be connected, 180-degree symmetric, and have minimum word length 3. Ferland and Pratt construct $n\times n$ crossword grids with many clues satisfying these conditions and prove their construction is maximal when $n\equiv 1$ or 3 $\pmod{4}$. In this paper, we explore American-style crosswords in which the minimum word length is 4. Jacobs computed the maximal $15 \times 15$ grid with minimum word length 4. In this paper, we construct grids with a maximal number of clues for all $n \not \equiv 0 \pmod{5}$.

title: Geometrization of Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer and Vogan's conjecture on local Arthur packets
abstract: We give a geometric analogue of Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer for a general class of reductive groups over p-adic fields with cyclic component groups of trivial or prime order. We prove that this geometric transfer coincides with Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer, adapted to the language of disconnected groups, assuming the local Langlands correspondence satisfying certain desiderata, including the Kazhdan-Lusztig hypothesis for the ambient group and its endoscopic groups. As an application of this geometrization, we prove Vogan's conjecture on local Arthur packets over p-adic fields: for quasisplit classical groups and their pure inner forms, all local Arthur packets are ABV-packets, and the distributions attached to these ABV-packets of Arthur type satisfy Arthur's local conjectures on twisted endoscopic character relations. This demonstrates the following general principle: for any reductive group G over a local field, an Arthur packet should be defined as an ABV-packet of Arthur type, equipped with the endoscopic pairing calculated by traces of actions on vanishing cycles or microlocalizations.

title: Separatrix splitting in a multiferroic neuromorphic oscillator: toward Arnold diffusion
abstract: Prototype magnetic neuromorphic systems, in essence, are based either on ferromagnetic or antiferromagnetic materials as key elements for conventional neuromorphic setups. In this work, we propose a novel neuromorphic system based on a ferromagnetic disk and a ferroelectric layer coupled via the magnetoelectric effect. We study a magnetoelectrically coupled ferromagnetic--ferroelectric oscillator as a candidate element for neuromorphic devices. A local reduction of conservative Landau--Lifshitz dynamics identifies a magnetic coordinate--momentum pair, which is coupled to an inertial ferroelectric polarization mode. We derive the action--angle description of the resulting double-well--harmonic-oscillator Hamiltonian, obtain the quartic-well frequency map and Fourier coefficients in terms of elliptic functions, and establish monotone in-well twist. In the autonomous two-degree-of-freedom model, isoenergetic nondegeneracy supports KAM confinement on regular compact domains. Periodic electric forcing introduces a third effective frequency, although the harmonic magnetic sector leaves the unperturbed resonance loci parallel. An explicitly specified nonlinear magnetic extension produces transverse resonance intersections. We calculate leading resonant widths and local homoclinic splitting, and derive a damping-dependent splitting threshold for a stated scalar reduction. These results identify analytical structures relevant to transport and explain possible polarization-based electrical readout. Establishing Arnold diffusion in the coupled model requires additional connecting-orbit analysis or controlled long-time evidence; neither a diffusion law nor Nekhoroshev stability of the driven model is inferred from the present finite-time calculations.

title: Homological reduction and entropy of discontinuous interval maps
abstract: We develop a homological approach to the topological entropy of discontinuous interval maps with arbitrary branch orientations. Relations among the one-sided images of discontinuities reduce the kneading determinant, while symmetries yield further simplifications. We determine the smallest possible dimension of this reduction for each orientation pattern and show that this minimum can coexist with maximal entropy. The general theory is applied to maps with increasing or decreasing branches, extending earlier results for bimodal maps and yielding exact formulas for entropy and periodic-orbit counts.

title: Statistics of the Shepp $p$-product
abstract: In 1962, Shepp famously discovered a product of normal random variables that preserves normality. The Shepp product, which takes the form $XY/\sqrt{X^2 + Y^2}$, has since been thoroughly studied and has found numerous connections to other areas of statistics. Among other things, it has an extension to $n$ normal variables, gives a multiplicative analogue of the central limit theorem, and applies rather unexpectedly to genomics as a test statistic for alignment-free sequence analysis. The Shepp product is evidently the $p =2$ special case of $XY/\sqrt[p]{X^p + Y^p}$ that we call the Shepp $p$-product. We will show that the Shepp $p$-product, particularly when $p = 1$ and $p = \infty$ (the latter in a limiting sense), is no less fascinating and applicable than the original $p = 2$ case. Just as the Shepp $2$-product preserves normal distributions, the Shepp $1$-product preserves Cauchy distributions, and the Shepp $\infty$-product preserves exponential distributions. In fact, the converse is also true in an appropriate sense, allowing us to characterize the Cauchy, normal, and exponential distributions as the unique distributions preserved by the Shepp $p$-product for $p =1,2,\infty$, respectively. We will study the multiplicative analogue of infinite divisibility with respect to the Shepp $p$-product, establish an asymptotic theory for the Shepp $p$-product of $n$ i.i.d.\ random variables, and estimate the rates of convergence in Kolmogorov distance. Some of our results are new even for the $p=2$ case. We will also discuss new applications of the Shepp $p$-product in statistics, computational biology, and statistical physics. In particular, our new test statistic for exponentiality based on the Shepp $\infty$-product is more powerful, both theoretically and empirically, than the rule-of-thumb Kolmogorov--Smirnov test based on the relative efficiency.

title: On a Class of Non-Local Elliptic-Transport Systems in Score-Guided Probability Flow on $SE(3)$: Score-Singularity Resolution, Space-Time ADN Shift, and Markov Mean-Field Games
abstract: We establish mathematical foundations for optimal spatiotemporal vector fields governing continuous score-guided probability flows over bounded submanifolds $M \subset SE(3)$ on the Special Euclidean group $SE(3) \cong \mathbb{R}^3 \times SO(3)$. Modeling dynamic density evolution via a score-perturbed Lie-algebraic continuity equation under zero-flux boundary conditions, we resolve the non-local score drift singularity $s(g,t) = \nabla_{SE(3)} \log ρ(g,t)$ as $ρ\rightarrow 0^+$ via weighted parabolic flux dissipation bounds. Using left-invariant exponential group mollifiers, we derive boundary-preserving DiPerna--Lions commutator estimates tracking structure constants $\{c_{ij}^k\}$. Second, interpreting the optimality system as a 7D space-time elliptic operator $L_{7D} = -Δ_{SE(3)} - \partial_t^2$ with zero-order corner compatibility on $\partial M \times \{0,T\}$, we establish Agmon--Douglis--Nirenberg $W_p^2(Q_T)$ shift estimates tracking Lie algebra constants, boundary geometry $\|\partial M\|_{C^2}$, and Ricci curvature $\|Ric_{SE(3)}\|_{L^\infty}$, yielding a full $C^\infty(\overline{Q}_T)$ Schauder bootstrap expansion. Third, we extend this system to non-cooperative Markov Mean-Field Games (MFGs) on $SE(3)$, establishing score-guided Nash equilibria via Schauder--Tychonoff fixed points. Crucially, the constant diagonal Ricci curvature $Ric_{SE(3)} = \mathrm{diag}(0,0,0,1/2,1/2,1/2)$ from $SO(3)$ induces a sharp Bochner--Weitzenböck spectral gap boost $λ_1(-Δ_{SE(3)}) \ge λ_1(-Δ_{\mathbb{R}^3}) + 1/2 > 0$. This positive rotational curvature enhances the Lie-algebraic Poincaré coercivity constant, demonstrating that intrinsic group curvature stabilizes score-guided flows against dispersion and expands the critical Nash uniqueness horizon $T_{SE(3)}^*$ beyond flat Euclidean limits.

title: A complete description of the algebraic structure of pseudocompact abelian groups
abstract: We solve a major open problem from [D. Dikranjan, D. Shakhmatov, Algebraic structure of pseudocompact groups, Memoirs AMS 633 (1998)] by describing abelian groups which admit a pseudocompact Hausdorff group topology. First, we prove that an abelian group G can be equipped with a pseudocompact Hausdorff group topology iff it can be decomposed into a direct sum G=B\oplus H of a bounded torsion group B and agroup H satisfying |nH|=|H| for all positive integers $n$, such that both B and H admit a pseudocompact Hausdorff group topology. Second, for an unbounded abelian group G, we denote by m the minimal positive integer n such that |nG|=|kG| for all integers k\ge n. Then G admits a pseudocompact group topology iff both G[m]={g\in G: mg=0} and mG\cong G/G[m] admit a pseudocompact Hausdorff group topology.

title: Anticyclotomic Iwasawa theory at potentially ordinary primes
abstract: We study anticyclotomic Iwasawa theory for self-dual twists of $p$-ordinary modular forms of weight two with nebentype $ε^2$, where $ε$ is a non-trivial Dirichlet character of conductor $p$. Under a generalized Heegner hypothesis and suitable residual hypotheses, we prove one divisibility in the anticyclotomic main conjecture in both the definite and indefinite settings. The prime $p$ may split, remain inert, or ramify in the imaginary quadratic field. Our proofs use a compatible bipartite Euler system of Heegner classes and theta elements, together with a comparison with the $p$-adic $L$-functions of Kohen--Pacetti. In the definite case, we prove cotorsion of the Selmer group and the characteristic-ideal divisibility by the $p$-adic $L$-function. In the indefinite case, we prove a rank-one statement and the corresponding divisibility in terms of the Heegner class. We also discuss criteria for equality and their relation to Kolyvagin's conjecture. Specialization gives finite-level Bloch--Kato Selmer bounds with local terms, and applications to Mordell--Weil ranks and $p$-primary Tate--Shafarevich groups for elliptic curves that have potentially ordinary reduction at $p$ satisfying our hypotheses.

title: Harnessing Mutual Coupling in Cell-Free mMIMO
abstract: This letter investigates a cell-free massive MIMO system with $L$ access points (APs), each employing a small fixed-form-factor, uniform linear array of $N$ potentially closely spaced antennas. Utilizing multiport communication theory, we analyze the impact of mutual coupling on uplink and downlink spectral efficiency (SE) under various impedance-matching strategies. We compare two deployment regimes: ($i$) increasing $N$ while $L$ is kept fixed, and ($ii$) increasing $N$ while fixing the total antenna count $M = NL$. Numerical results show that, with a full matching network, mutual coupling itself becomes beneficial when an AP serves several user equipments, which is the typical operating regime of user-centric cell-free networks. Furthermore, with full matching, antenna densification can enhance SE or allow for a reduction in the number of APs without performance loss. Since full matching networks remain of manageable size in the small arrays of distributed APs, unlike in large centralized arrays, cell-free networks offer a natural setting for exploiting mutual coupling.

title: Two-level additive Schwarz preconditioners with GDSW coarse spaces for high-order discretizations in 3D
abstract: Overlapping Schwarz methods are among the most successful domain decomposition preconditioners for large-scale finite element simulations. In this work, the Generalized Dryja-Smith-Widlund (GDSW), GDSW$^*$, and Reduced GDSW (RGDSW) coarse spaces are studied for three-dimensional high-order finite element method (FEM) and virtual element method (VEM) for the Poisson equation and the equations of linear elasticity. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study of GDSW-type coarse spaces for polynomial degrees $k\ge 3$ in three dimensions, for either discretization. In 3D VEM, the face degrees of freedom (DOFs) are moments instead of point values. The kernel of the differential operator, which defines the interface values of the GDSW coarse basis functions, must be represented through these moments. The construction is therefore no longer purely algebraic and, without this correction, the coarse level loses its effect for $k\ge 3$. FEM and VEM are tested on hexahedral meshes, and VEM is additionally tested on polyhedral ones. Polynomial degrees up to $k=5$ and runs on up to $4\,096$ subdomains and parallel cores are included in the numerical study. Numerical experiments show scalable iteration counts for all coarse space variants for the Poisson problem, illustrating the expected trade-off between the coarse space size and robustness. Further experiments for linear elasticity confirms that the moment-based construction extends naturally from the scalar to the vector-valued problem.

title: Rank stability of elliptic curves over prime cyclic extensions of function fields
abstract: Let $\ell$ be an odd prime number. Let $E$ be a non-isotrivial elliptic curve defined over the global function field $K = \mathbb{F}_q(t)$ such that $(q, 6) = 1$ and $q \equiv 1 \mod \ell$. We show that as $q$ grows arbitrarily large, both analytic and algebraic ranks of $E$ do not grow upon base change to $100\%$ of $\mathbb{Z}/\ell \mathbb{Z}$ Galois extensions over $K$. One of the applications we obtain is that over a positive proportion of $\mathbb{Z}/\ell \mathbb{Z}$ Galois extensions $L$ over $K$, the Tate--Shafarevich group of $E$ over $L$ is non-trivial. To obtain these results, we incorporate several geometric and probabilistic techniques which were studied in previous literature. These include the construction of desired auxiliary abelian varieties by Mazur--Rubin--Silverberg, the theory of middle convolution and big monodromy results by Katz and Hall, uniform Chebotarev density theorem by Kowalski, and distribution of prime Selmer groups of auxiliary abelian varieties by Klagsbrun--Mazur--Rubin and Park.

title: The proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: a detailed exposition and an extension to rotation systems
abstract: The Harary--Hill conjecture states that the crossing number $\ucr{K_n}$ of the complete graph $K_n$ is $Z(n):=\frac{1}{4}\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\rfloor$ for all $n\ge 3$. In October 2026 OpenAI uploaded to GitHub a proof of this conjecture. The proof is very short, but it relies on polynomial methods that are not part of the standard techniques used by many combinatorialists, and it is written with very little motivation or explanation. Since we found the proof very hard to follow, we decided to write this paper, which contains a complete proof of the conjecture written for mathematicians who are more familiar with combinatorics than with polynomial methods. In fact we prove a more general result on rotation systems of $K_n$, from which the Harary--Hill conjecture easily follows. Namely, we show that for every rotation system $Π$ of $K_n$ the number of $4$-vertex subsystems of $Π$ realizable as drawings of $K_4$ with one crossing, plus three times the number of non-realizable $4$-vertex subsystems of $Π$, is at least $Z(n)$. The statement and proof of our result are purely combinatorial and do not involve drawings at all.

title: Gaussian Products and an Order Dichotomy for Principal Ideals
abstract: We identify the algebraic principal ideal generated by a Gaussian product of two Hilbert--Schmidt operators. Its deterministic generator is obtained by multiplying the square tails of their singular-value sequences; in a fixed diagonal basis, one probability-one event gives the identity for all decreasing square-summable weights. For the induced operation on principal ideals, we prove an order dichotomy for arbitrary families of strictly positive probes. A family jointly determines every inclusion if and only if its tail stable-rank profiles have no common eventual upper bound. Equivalently, each prescribed countable input system admits one probe from that family reflecting all inclusions. If the condition fails, one common fibre contains a copy of $\mathcal P(\mathbb N)/\mathrm{Fin}$ preserving finite sums and intersections. Its generators are continuously parametrized and arbitrarily close in Hilbert--Schmidt norm, while their deterministic output ratios tend to one at any prescribed rate. The order dichotomy follows from a bound on all probes that lose one noninclusion and a separated block construction under a scalar tail budget. Further consequences include generic separation under every positive summable envelope and exact cardinal thresholds for joint detection and single-probe separation.

title: Structured Neural Network Models for Anisotropic Magnetic Constitutive Laws
abstract: High-performance electrical steel used for iron cores of power transformers and generators exhibits complex material behavior. While modeling and simulation of isotropic nonlinear response is well understood, the incorporation of magnetic anisotropy remains challenging. This work proposes to utilize a structured neural network architecture to systematically describe the anisotropic nonlinear anhysteretic magnetic material response of electrical steel sheets. By constructing a convex and smooth co-energy density with dedicated behavior at infinity, we can ensure thermodynamic consistency and correct physical behavior and further guarantee basic mathematical properties which provide well-posedness of corresponding magnetic field problems and efficient numerical solvers. Numerical tests demonstrate the capability of the proposed method to describe strongly anisotropic behavior as well as its robust convergence in finite-element simulations.

title: Symbol-based residual certification of reduced and neural surrogates for tempered-fractional CGMY pricing
abstract: We certify reduced and neural approximations of European-put price trajectories under the Carr--Geman--Madan--Yor model by residual bounds for the spline Galerkin discretisation of the tempered-fractional pricing equation. The Galerkin matrices are Toeplitz sections of an explicit periodised Fourier symbol; summing the alias series to a stated tail makes the assembled system exact to $10^{-8}$. A Lévy--Khintchine argument gives the parameter-explicit bound $λ_{\min}(S_I)\ge r\,m_{\min}$ for the symmetric part, valid for $Y\in(0,2)\setminus\{1\}$, replacing numerical spectral estimates. A banded comparison norm built from the mass and stiffness symbols yields a rigorous certificate at $O(N)$ cost with explicit effectivity, and empirical interpolation of the symbol makes the operator affine in about 36 terms with a rigorous error transfer, so a reduced model is certified at a cost independent of $N$; a three-stage rule escalates to the full-order bounds only when needed. At the resolution that prices the whole parameter box to one cent ($N=1024$), the full-order certificate costs 6% of a direct solve, and the certified POD--Galerkin model of rank 80 costs 3% of it and settles 99.8% of $10^4$ queries without touching the full space. No false accept occurs on any query with a reference solution (150 inside the parameter box, 264 outside), and outside the box the certificate accepts 193 of the 210 queries on which the reduced model is still within one cent. The neural reduced models trained here miss the one-cent tolerance by a factor of at least 46; the certificate detects this at every query in a few milliseconds and explains it as a trade-off between temporal smoothness and coefficient accuracy. A residual certificate for the American put is proved as an outlook.

title: Radial Symmetry and Nondegeneracy for Singular Liouville Systems with Small Singular Exponents
abstract: We extend the classification (Lin and Zhang, Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Anal. Non Linéaire \textbf{27}, 2010) to finite-mass singular Liouville systems with sufficiently small positive singular exponents. For symmetric, entrywise nonnegative, irreducible and invertible coupling matrices, every solution whose mass vector lies near a fixed compact subset of the regular mass surface is radial about the singular point and is uniquely determined by its component masses up to dilation. We also establish nondegeneracy modulo dilation. To overcome the failure of the moving-plane argument for positive exponents, we use compactness and a local reduction based on integral identities. The results also hold for nonzero nonnegative exponent vectors and for small mixed-sign vectors satisfying an explicit integral inequality.
